_comment: Programme detail researched from official awarding-body sources and applied by the programme_details stage. Only empty record fields are filled; a value already present is never overwritten here.
_rules: Every record must carry verification.source_citations, or the stage skips it entirely. An amount with nothing to check it against is worse than no amount, because it looks researched.
fully_funded is applied only when tuition_coverage is true, so a stipend can never be recorded as though it were a tuition waiver.
Official facts live in official_details; guidance derived from them lives in applicant_utility. They are stored apart and must never be merged.
A field the awarding body does not publish stays null. Absence of evidence is an answer, not a gap to be filled by inference.
deadline_central is the programme's own closing date. deadline_institutional is any earlier university date, stored separately.

official.application_cycle: 2026 call for applications (universities had to submit institutional applications by 16 November 2025 for the 2026 call)
official.deadline_central_display: 16 November 2025 (university institutional applications deadline for the 2026 call)
official.deadline_note: This is an institutional programme: French higher education institutions submit the applications, and 2026 dates have now been published. As at 1 October 2026 the 2026 institutional call has closed and the next award round is being prepared, so no new candidate deadline is open.
official.status_note: The page states: 'In light of the publication of the 2026 call for applications, the 2025 calls have closed.' The 2026 call has since been published with institutional deadlines in November 2025.

official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship funds tuition fees and a monthly allowance, but Campus France is explicit that it does not cover all fees: 'The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship does not cover all the costs related to your stay in France (health insurance, housing, transport, etc.)'
official.funding_label: France Excellence Eiffel - EUR 1,181 per month for master's, EUR 1,426 per month for doctoral, plus tuition fees
benefits: Master's and doctorate: EUR 1,181 per month (11% of the annual social ceiling) on top of tuition fees
Doctorate: EUR 1,426 per month (18% of the annual social ceiling) on top of tuition fees
Direct payment of tuition fees to the institution rather than to the student
Health insurance at the preferred rate for foreign students
eligibility: Be enrolled in or applying to a French higher education institution in an eligible programme
Be under 25 for a master's award, or under 30 for a doctoral award, on 1 January of the year of the award
Hold the nationality of a non-European Economic Area country (the award is also open to candidates from non-EUA candidate countries for master's/doctoral studies)
Be nominated by the French institution rather than applying directly
Not be a French national, and meet the 25/30 age limits
official.citizenship_residency: 'Students from non-European Economic Area countries' are eligible. The scholarship is not open to EEA nationals.
official.international_eligibility: Explicitly for students from non-European Economic Area countries studying in France; EEA nationals are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The award targets candidates whose profile and projects have a significant link with the priorities of the scheme: economics, management, political science, humanities, law, education, sustainable development, research, innovation and technology, development, geopolitics, digital transition, health and sciences, etc. Health and sciences are at the heart of the France 2030 investment plan.
official.application_method: The scholarship cannot be applied for directly. You must be nominated by a French institution (universities, grandes écoles or comparable institutions) that submits the application to Campus France through the online platform. Each institution is responsible for selecting its candidates. Applications are shortlisted, assessed and ranked by the institution, which creates a master list of excellence of up to three candidates per scheme and discipline.
requirements: Be enrolled in or applying to an eligible French institution
Be under 25 (master's) or under 30 (doctoral) on 1 January of the award year
Hold a nationality from outside the European Economic Area
Be nominated by the institution, not applying directly
Be shortlisted by the institution into its master list of excellence (up to three candidates per scheme and discipline)
documents: Institutional nomination on the Campus France online platform
Institutional master list of excellence
Supporting documents defined by the nominating institution
official.english_requirement_note: The Campus France scholarship pages publish no English language requirement; the award can be for French-language or English-language programmes depending on the institution.
selection_criteria: Excellent academic record (institution selection is based on excellence)
A significant link between the candidate's profile and the scheme's priorities
Institutional shortlisting into a master list of excellence of up to three candidates per scheme and discipline
official.selection_weighting: The weighting is institutional by design: each institution selects and creates a master list of excellence, and Campus France reviews nominations with an Ethics Committee.
official.duration: 12 months for master's; 18 to 36 months for doctoral
award_holder_conditions: Must be nominated by a French institution - direct applications are not accepted
Campus France pays tuition fees directly to the institution
The scheme does not cover health insurance, housing, transport or other living costs
supplements_or_initiatives: Two distinct schemes: France Excellence Eiffel scholarship (general) and the France Excellence Eiffel scholarship for excellent foreign students (Missions)

official_contacts.general: Campus France; contact via https://www.campusfrance.org/en/contact

official.description: The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship is a French Ministry of Foreign Affairs programme managed by Campus France that funds tuition fees plus a monthly allowance for students from non-European Economic Area countries studying in France at under 25 (master's) or under 30 (doctoral). Candidates are selected and nominated by French institutions, which build a master list of excellence of up to three candidates per scheme and discipline. Campus France makes the payments, and the scheme does not cover housing, health insurance or transport.
official.coverage: Covers tuition fees and a monthly allowance of EUR 1,181 (master's) or EUR 1,426 (doctoral), but not housing, health insurance or transport.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is outside the European Economic Area
Check you are under 25 (master's) or under 30 (doctoral) on 1 January of the award year
Apply to an eligible French institution and let them nominate you - you cannot apply directly
Build a profile that clearly links to one of the scheme's priority areas
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to Campus France instead of being nominated
Being over the age limit
EEA nationality
Missing the institution's internal nomination deadline, which is earlier than Campus France's
Not reaching the institution's master list of excellence, which caps entries at three per scheme and discipline
estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing
Health insurance beyond the preferred student rate
Transport
Visa costs
Everyday living costs beyond the monthly allowance
document_audit: Confirm the institution has actually submitted your nomination on the platform
Have a profile and project statement that maps to a scheme priority
Track your own age against the 1 January cut-off

alerts.message: Each institution can nominate at most three candidates per scheme and discipline, so competition inside your institution is the real filter.
Institutional deadlines are in the previous year (November 2025 for the 2026 call), so plan roughly a year ahead.

submission_workflow: Choose an eligible French institution in a priority area
Apply for admission through that institution's own process
Ask to be considered for an Eiffel nomination
Submit the nomination by the institution's internal deadline
Wait for the institution's master list of excellence and Campus France's decision

official.application_cycle: Annual, coordinated with the applicant university (typically applications open in the spring/summer preceding the study year)
official.deadline_central_display: No central date. The Deutschlandstipendium is coordinated by the applicant university, and each university sets its own application period, which it publishes on its own website.
official.deadline_note: The official site is explicit: 'You will find the current application period on the website of the university where you want to apply.' There is no central closing date; admission office deadlines differ by university and are published locally.
official.status_note: The programme is running for the 2026/27 cohort, with universities running their own application rounds. The official site shows the scheme is live but publishes no single open/closed state.
official.funding_period: per month
official.funding_duration: 12 months, up to 24 months for master's courses
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Deutschlandstipendium is a monthly stipend only. The official FAQ addresses this directly: it is a scholarship for excellent students and does not include tuition fees or a travel allowance. The FAQ recommends checking the financing options of the chosen university and other bodies for help with study and travel costs.
official.funding_label: Deutschlandstipendium - EUR 300 per month for 12 months (up to 24 for master's)
benefits: EUR 300 per month for the duration of the scholarship period
12 months normally, extendable to 24 months for master's courses
One year of funding may be extended by up to two years for master's students
Insurance contributions for health insurance, care insurance, accident insurance and long-term care insurance are paid for the scholarship holder
eligibility: Have been accepted by a German university or a university recognised in the Federal Republic of Germany (for master's courses: have been admitted or will be enrolled)
For higher education students, general university entrance qualification plus a qualifying examination for the specific course of study
For master's students, a bachelor's or equivalent degree
Have a school or university leaving certificate that qualifies for higher education in Germany
Migrate to Germany specifically to study (not for employment or family reunification), and take up the study in Germany
Have a qualifying school-leaving certificate, and (for master's students) a bachelor's degree or equivalent
official.citizenship_residency: Nationality is not a criterion: eligibility depends on being accepted by a German university and migrating to Germany to study. The official FAQ states the applicant must be a foreigner who has been admitted to a German university or a university recognised in Germany. No nationality restriction is published.
official.international_eligibility: Explicitly for international students: applicants must be able to migrate to Germany to study, and the scheme is funded by the German Foreign Office together with partner institutions and private donors.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Coordinated by the applicant university, which also defines subject priorities; the German Foreign Office provides the funding.
official.application_method: Apply through the university. Two variants are described: the university selects the scholarship holders (Auswahlverfahren der Hochschule), or the university forwards suitable students and the DAI decides (Dai procedure). The application forms are not issued by the Deutschlandstipendium website; the university publishes them.
requirements: Apply to the university where you want to study and follow its application process
Be admitted, or be admitted and enrolled, by the end of the scholarship period
Meet the subject-specific requirements of that university
Be ranked according to study and examination achievements, to a degree that enables a successful degree

Have a personal commitment to positively shape the development of their home country after the studies in Germany - and prove this through voluntary commitment or previous engagement in civil society organisations
documents: Application form published by your university
School-leaving certificates
Proof of admission or enrolment at the German university
Proof of your commitment to contribute to the development of your home country after the studies
official.english_requirement_note: The official FAQ does not publish an English test requirement. The page is in German and concerns a German-language study context.
selection_criteria: Subject-specific study and examination achievements that make a successful degree possible
Score, grade or grade-related achievements
The university's own subject-specific assessment criteria, including particular subject priorities and a defined procedure
official.selection_weighting: The official site states the assessment is made according to study and examination achievements, and that the criteria are subject-specific, including particular subject priorities of the university and a defined procedure. It gives no percentage weighting.
official.duration: 12 months, extendable to 24 months for master's courses
award_holder_conditions: Must be admitted, or admitted and enrolled, by the end of the scholarship period
Must not change to another university or the award is revoked
Must be enrolled, with a change of university causing revocation
Must report changes in circumstances, and the DAI can end the scholarship or require a refund in the case of false information about the personal or academic situation
May be subject to a selection of courses of study outside the subject-specific award, and the university may restrict the number of courses of study chosen
supplements_or_initiatives: Insurance contributions (health, care, accident, long-term care) paid for the scholarship holder

Frequently asked questions notes there is currently no Deutschlandstipendium offered by tuition-free public schools (no fee-based public schools) that is not covered by a scholarship - i.e. no tuition-fee supplement exists

official_contacts.general: not published on the official site

official.description: The Deutschlandstipendium is funded by the German Foreign Office with around 900 scholarships for excellent international students each year. It pays EUR 300 per month for 12 months, extendable to 24 months for master's students, plus insurance contributions. Applications are made directly to the university, which publishes its own application period, forms and subject-specific criteria, and either selects the scholars itself or forwards candidates for the DAI to decide. Eligibility requires being admitted to a German university and migrating to Germany to study.
official.coverage: A EUR 300 monthly stipend for 12 months (up to 24 for master's) plus insurance contributions; it does not cover tuition fees or travel.
official.funding: Partial - EUR 300 per month (EUR 150 federal + EUR 150 from private donors), income-independent and in addition to BAfoG, for at least two semesters and at most to the end of the standard period of study

application_readiness_checklist: Get admitted to a German university first, or at least apply to it
Find your university's own Deutschlandstipendium page for the application period and forms
Confirm the scheme requires you to migrate to Germany to study
Prepare evidence of your commitment to contribute to your home country's development after graduation
Check whether your university selects scholars itself or uses the DAI procedure
common_rejection_risks: Applying through the Deutschlandstipendium website instead of the university
Not being admitted or enrolled by the end of the scholarship period
Changing university after the award
Weak study and examination results against the university's own subject criteria
Not being able to evidence the commitment to contribute to their home country
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees at public universities in many states
Travel to and from Germany
Study materials
Living costs beyond EUR 300 per month
document_audit: Save your university's own application form and deadline
Gather all school-leaving certificates and proof of admission
Document civil-society engagement or a written commitment, as the FAQ asks for proof
Confirm the insurance elements offered on top of the stipend

alerts.message: Every university sets its own period. Check your university's page rather than relying on a national date.
The DAI can end the scholarship or demand repayment if information about your personal or academic situation was false.

submission_workflow: Research which universities offer the Deutschlandstipendium and their own criteria
Apply for admission at the chosen university
Follow the university's own Deutschlandstipendium application route and forms
Submit within the university's published application period
If the university uses the DAI procedure, wait for their shortlist

purpose: A scholarship program for privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who are enrolled in undergraduate schools, graduate schools, junior colleges, colleges of technology, specialized courses in specialized training colleges, university preparatory courses or Japanese language institutes in Japan and are facing financial difficulties.

Japanese-language official statement: a programme that pays the MEXT Foreign Students Learning Encouragement Allowance to privately-financed international students who are excellent in both academic performance and character and who cannot study for financial reasons.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or development-goal requirement is published. The programme is described only as support for privately-financed international students who are excellent in studies and character and who face financial difficulty in continuing their studies ('学業、人物ともに優れ、かつ、経済的理由により修学が困難である者').
study_type: Full-time enrolment as a regular student in a graduate school in Japan
Enrolled as a research student at graduate level holding at least an undergraduate degree
Full-time enrolment as a regular student in an undergraduate school, junior college, college of technology (3rd year or above) or specialized course in a specialized training college
Full-time enrolment as a regular student in an advanced course (specialised post-graduate course) in an undergraduate school, junior college, college of technology or specialized training college
Full-time enrolment as a regular student in a preparatory Japanese language programme in an undergraduate school or junior college
Full-time enrolment as a regular student in a university preparatory course at an educational institution, with the objective of entering a university

Enrolment in a Japanese language institute with the objective of advancing to an undergraduate school, graduate school, junior college, college of technology or specialized course in a specialized training college
official.degree_award: No degree. This is a stipend paid to students who are already enrolled in a Japanese educational institution; it is not a degree-granting award.
official.deadline_central_display: No central application deadline is published. JASSO publishes only: 'Method of application: Please ask the staff at the educational institution in which you are enrolled.'
official.deadline_institutional: Set by the enrolled educational institution only ('Please ask the staff at the educational institution in which you are enrolled'). The published page gives no date.
official.tuition_rule: There is no tuition waiver. The award is a monthly stipend only. The published allowance test explicitly excludes enrollment fee and tuition fee from the amount considered, i.e. tuition is not met by this scholarship and remains payable by the student.
official.home_tuition_rule: Not published. JASSO states no rule on host-country or home-country tuition during the award. The enrolment fee and tuition fee of the Japanese institution remain payable by the student and are explicitly excluded from the allowance test, so no tuition is met by this scholarship.
official.host_institution_fee: Enrollment fee and tuition fee are payable to the enrolled educational institution. They are named as excluded from the allowance calculation and are not paid from the scholarship.
official.tax_status: Not published. The JASSO programme page states no tax treatment for the monthly stipend.
covered_expenses: Monthly stipend of 48,000 yen for graduate school / undergraduate level
Monthly stipend of 30,000 yen for Japanese language institutes
not_covered_or_excluded: Tuition fees
Enrollment fees
Any support that would breach the published income test: allowance received by the candidate (excluding enrollment fee, tuition fee etc.) must not exceed an average of 90,000 yen per month
Awards to students who are receiving a scholarship whose concurrent receipt with the Honors Scholarships is restricted
Support under JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program (Overseas Study Support System)
No airfare, travel allowance or relocation cost is mentioned anywhere on the published page
general_eligibility: The candidate must be a privately-financed international student: enrolled in a Japanese educational institution and NOT a grantee of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship or of any foreign government scholarship, and holding the residence status 'Student'.
The candidate must be enrolled full-time (as a regular student) in one of the published eligible course types.

The candidate must meet the grading criteria specified in the application guidelines (Japanese-language guidelines specify a grade point average of 2.30 or above at graduate, undergraduate and Japanese language institute level, expected to be maintained during the scholarship period, or an equivalent judgement of excellence where a GPA cannot be used).

The candidate must meet the published language requirement (Japanese: JLPT N2 or above, or EJU Japanese score of 200 points or above, or a language level separately recognised by JASSO; English: CEFR B2 or above). The language condition does not apply to candidates in a preparatory Japanese language programme, a university preparatory course or a Japanese language institute.
The candidate must be willing to cooperate with JASSO's career path survey, conducted through the enrolled institution or other methods, after the scholarship is granted.
The candidate must not be receiving a scholarship whose concurrent award with the Honors Scholarship is restricted.
The candidate must not be receiving support under JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program.
ineligibility_conditions: Grantees of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship
Students sent by any foreign government scholarship
Candidates whose allowance (excluding enrollment fee, tuition fee etc.) exceeds an average of 90,000 yen per month
Candidates with a financial supporter in Japan whose annual income is 5 million yen or more
Candidates receiving a scholarship restricted from concurrent award with the Honors Scholarships
Candidates receiving support under JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program
Candidates whose previous year's grade point average is below the published threshold, or who are not expected to maintain it during the scholarship period
Students at institutions that are currently suspended from applying to this scholarship (JASSO states none are suspended at present)

undergraduate: Stipend: 48,000 yen per month
Full-time regular enrolment required in an undergraduate school, junior college, college of technology (3rd year or above) or specialized course in a specialized training college
Japanese/English language requirement applies (not a preparatory programme)
masters: Graduate level: 48,000 yen per month, same rate as undergraduate
Full-time regular enrolment required in a graduate school in Japan
Japanese/English language requirement applies
phd: The published page states only 'graduate school' and does not separate master's and doctoral levels; both fall under the graduate level rate of 48,000 yen per month
A candidate holding at least an undergraduate degree and enrolled as a research student at graduate level is also eligible
Japanese/English language requirement applies

host_requirements: The candidate must already be enrolled at the educational institution that recommends them - the institution, not the applicant, submits.

The number of students an educational institution can recommend depends on the number of international students enrolled in it; JASSO warns that depending on the educational institution the applicant may not be able to apply at all.
The candidate must sign the sheet designated by JASSO every month at the international students' office in the enrolled educational institution.
documents: No document list is published on the JASSO programme page. The binding source is the application guidelines (募集要項) of the educational institution in which the candidate is enrolled, which set the grading criteria and the required supporting documents.
The institution, not the applicant, submits the recommendation to JASSO, so the documents it collects are institution-defined.
document_format_rules: No file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published by JASSO for this programme. The institution's application guidelines govern all format rules.

Post-selection, the payment forms are handled through the JASSO scholarship payment system using the manual edition published for the current financial year (April 2026 edition manuals for the learning encouragement fee system).
official.selection_notes: There is no open competition and no published assessment rubric. Selection is by nomination: JASSO states the programme determines selected students 'by recommendation from the university or school' (Candidate selected by recommendation of the university or school). Candidates must additionally meet the grading criteria and language condition specified in the application guidelines issued by the institution. JASSO publishes selection results (the 2026 selection results are posted as a Japanese-language PDF, dated 5 June 2026).
application_steps: Contact the staff in charge at the educational institution in which you are enrolled ('Please ask the staff at the educational institution in which you are enrolled').
The educational institution selects and recommends candidates to JASSO. The applicant cannot apply directly.
If recommended, the candidate signs the JASSO-designated sheet every month at the international students' office of the educational institution.
applicant_submission_route: Institution-mediated only. The published route is: applicant -> enrolled educational institution (international students office / staff in charge) -> JASSO.
official.application_portal: No application portal for the scholarship itself. Post-selection administration runs through the JASSO scholarship payment system (留学生給与等給付システム); the student log-in page for the bank account details form is https://www.sas.jasso.go.jp/abr/ and log-in ID and password are issued by the enrolled school's staff, with the current edition manual (April 2026) published on JASSO's system page.
arrival_rules: The candidate must already be enrolled at the Japanese educational institution; this is not a pre-arrival award and JASSO publishes no arrival, visa or relocation support
The grant period starts in April (12-month award) or October (6-month award), so the student must be enrolled and resident in Japan before the payment period begins
Residence status must be 'Student' (留学) throughout the grant period
JASSO publishes no rule on a maximum permitted period of stay before or after the award
timeline_rules: Scholarship period: 12 months (April to the following March) or 6 months (October to the following March), as a rule.
Payment is monthly and is tied to a monthly signature on the enrolment confirmation sheet at the institution.
JASSO posted the 2026 selection results on 5 June 2026 (PDF, Japanese only).
The programme runs two intake types - an April-start 12-month period and an October-start 6-month period - but the published page gives no submission dates for either.
official_application_route: Candidate -> enrolled educational institution's staff in charge -> JASSO (recommendation-based selection)

official.duration: 12 months (April to the following March) or 6 months (October to the following March), as a rule (原則として).

official.living_cost_coverage: Not established as living-cost funding. The published award is a fixed monthly stipend of JPY 48,000 (JPY 30,000 at Japanese language institutes). official.description: JASSO pays a monthly stipend to privately-financed international students who are already enrolled at a Japanese educational institution and hold the residence status 'Student'. The published rates are JPY 48,000 per month at graduate and undergraduate level and JPY 30,000 per month at Japanese language institutes, for 12 months (April-March) or 6 months (October-March). It pays nothing else: enrolment fee and tuition fee remain payable by the student, there is no airfare, accommodation allowance or arrival support, and the award is means-tested (other allowance excluding tuition must not average more than JPY 90,000 per month). Selection is entirely institution-mediated - the enrolled institution recommends the candidate within a quota based on its number of international students, and JASSO publishes no deadline, document list or format rules.

important_advice_for_students: Do not apply directly to JASSO. JASSO states the method of application is 'Please ask the staff at the educational institution in which you are enrolled'. Nothing you submit to JASSO will be considered.

Check first whether your institution can even recommend candidates. JASSO warns that the recommendation quota depends on the number of enrolled international students and that depending on the institution you may not be able to apply.
Budget on the stipend alone. This is 48,000 yen (or 30,000 yen at a Japanese language institute) per month. Tuition and enrollment fees are yours.

Pass the income test before anything else: your allowance excluding enrollment fee and tuition fee must not exceed an average of 90,000 yen per month, and any financial supporter in Japan must earn under 5 million yen a year.

Check that you are not on the grant of a Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship or any foreign government scholarship, and that you are not already on JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program - all three are explicit disqualifiers.
Get your language evidence ready early: JLPT N2+, EJU Japanese 200+, or CEFR B2+. These tests are scheduled and booked months ahead.
Note that the published English page does not give the GPA number; the Japanese page specifies a grade point average of 2.30 or above and expects it to be maintained during the award.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your institution actually recommends candidates for this scholarship this year - JASSO states the quota depends on the number of international students enrolled and that 'depending on your educational institution, you may not be able to apply'.

document_audit: JASSO publishes no document list and no format rules for this programme - no file size, file type, translation or date-of-issue rule exists on the official page. The binding document rules are in your institution's application guidelines (募集要項).

Ask the institution in writing for: the required documents, accepted file formats and sizes, whether a certified translation is accepted for documents not in Japanese, and how recent each document must be.

The published evidence items you will need to produce are: proof of enrolment as a full-time regular student, your previous year's grade report showing GPA 2.30 or above, a JLPT certificate / EJU score report or CEFR B2+ English evidence, and evidence of allowance received and of any financial supporter's income.
Monthly signature is the one published signature rule: you must sign the JASSO-designated sheet every month at the international students' office.

After selection, the bank account details form (振込口座届) is submitted through the JASSO scholarship payment system; the log-in ID and password come from the institution's staff, so request them at selection, not before.
submission_workflow: 1. Ask the staff at your enrolled educational institution whether they recommend candidates for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship and what the quota is.
2. Obtain the institution's application guidelines and their internal deadline - JASSO publishes none.
3. Prepare the evidence listed in the document audit and submit to the institution's international students office by its internal deadline.
4. The institution selects and recommends candidates to JASSO. You submit nothing to JASSO directly.
5. If selected, the institution issues you a log-in ID and password for the JASSO scholarship payment system (留学生給与等給付システム).
6. Submit the bank account details form (振込口座届) at https://www.sas.jasso.go.jp/abr/ following the current edition manual.
7. Sign the enrolment-confirmation sheet every month at the international students' office so that payment continues.

purpose: The objective of Doctoral Networks is to implement doctoral programmes by partnerships of organisations from different sectors across Europe and beyond to train highly skilled doctoral candidates, stimulate their creativity, enhance their innovation capacities and boost their employability in the long-term.

These doctoral programmes respond to well-identified needs in various research and innovation areas, expose the researchers to the academic and non-academic sectors, and offer research training as well as transferable skills and competences relevant for innovation and long-term employability.

REA framing: to train entrepreneurial, innovative and resilient doctoral candidates able to face current and future challenges and to convert knowledge and ideas into products and services for economic and social benefit.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or development-goal requirement is published. Green research is treated as an encouragement rather than a criterion: projects are 'strongly encouraged to adopt sustainable practices in line with the MSCA Green Charter', must report on their efforts, and sustainability 'may even be considered as a criterion to decide between otherwise ex-aequo proposals'.
study_type: Research employment (fellowship) within a doctoral programme run by an international consortium
Standard Doctoral Networks - international, interdisciplinary and inter-sectoral cooperation to train PhD candidates

Industrial Doctorates - train PhD candidates who wish to develop their skills and step outside academia, in particular in industry and business; individual participants must be enrolled in a doctoral programme and jointly supervised by the academic and non-academic partners

Joint Doctorates - highly integrated international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary collaboration leading to a joint doctoral degree or multiple doctoral degrees; PhD candidates must be enrolled in a joint programme and be jointly supervised
official.degree_award: Full doctoral degree. The researcher must be enrolled in a doctoral programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree in at least one EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country; a beneficiary based in a non-EU, non-Associated third country can be the sole degree-awarding institution. Joint Doctorates lead to a joint or multiple doctoral degree awarded by the participating institutions.
official.deadline_central_display: The MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026 call will open on 28 May 2026 and will close on 24 November 2026, 17.00, CET.
official.deadline_institutional: None for individual doctoral candidates. Each funded project advertises its own deadline on its EURAXESS vacancy, so the operative date is per institution and per project. The 24 November 2026 date applies only to consortium proposals.
official.funding_period: Each researcher is employed for a period of a minimum of 3 months and a maximum of 36 months; up to 48 months in the case of Joint Doctorate fellowships. Doctoral Network projects themselves can last up to 4 years, up to 5 years for Joint Doctorate projects.
official.tuition_coverage: No tuition waiver is described. The published rule is only that the researcher must be enrolled in a doctoral programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree in at least one EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. Whether the enrolling institution charges doctoral fees to the employed researcher, and whether those fees are charged to the grant, is decided by the beneficiary and is not published on the pages read.
official.travel_coverage: A mobility allowance is one of the four published per-researcher components of EU support. No separate airfare, relocation or travel-cost reimbursement figure is published on the pages read, so no travel budget is asserted.
official.tuition_rule: No tuition waiver is published. MSCA does not describe any fee waiver for enrolled doctoral candidates; the published requirement is only that the researcher be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project, and the fellowship is delivered as employment by the recruiting beneficiary rather than as a study-fee waiver. Whether a host charges doctoral enrolment fees to an employed researcher is not addressed on the published pages read and must be confirmed with the host.
official.home_tuition_rule: Not published. MSCA states no rule on the researcher's fees in their country of origin before recruitment, and no rule on any fees owed there during the fellowship.
official.host_institution_fee: No fee payable to the host is published in respect of the fellowship. The recruiting beneficiary is the employer and bears salary and national employment contributions; whether a doctoral programme charges an enrolment fee to an employed researcher is a host-institution matter that the published pages do not address.
official.tax_status: Not published. The published pages state that EURAXESS provides advice on visas, pensions, taxation and recognition of qualifications, i.e. tax treatment is a host-country matter and no EU tax rule is published.

general_eligibility: Doctoral Networks are open to international consortia of universities, research institutions and infrastructures, businesses including SMEs, and other socio-economic actors from different countries across Europe and beyond

The consortium must include at least three independent legal entities, each established in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and with at least one of them established in an EU Member State
On top of this minimum, other organisations from any country in the world can also join, either as beneficiaries or as associated partners depending on the status of the country

phd: This action funds doctoral candidates only. The researcher must be enrolled in a doctoral programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree in at least one EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
The researcher must not have a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.
Employment period: minimum 3 months, maximum 36 months; maximum 48 months for Joint Doctorates.

Mobility rule: must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date.
Industrial Doctorates: must spend at least 50% of time outside academia and must be jointly supervised by the academic and non-academic partners.
Joint Doctorates: must be enrolled in a joint programme, jointly supervised, and awarded a joint or multiple doctoral degree.
Secondments may be carried out during up to one half of the duration of research training activities, except in Industrial and Joint Doctorates where the limitation does not apply.

host_requirements: All beneficiaries must recruit at least one doctoral candidate.
Beneficiaries are required to host recruited researchers at their premises and supervise them, or use associated partners linked to them to do so.
Each MSCA Doctoral Network should have a clearly identified supervisory board co-ordinating network-wide training, research and in particular supervision activities.
The network must establish a career development plan for each recruited doctoral candidate jointly with their supervisor.
Selected projects must publish and advertise vacancies as widely as possible, including on the EURAXESS Jobs Portal.
Offer attractive working conditions in line with the European Charter for Researchers.

Joint supervision of the researchers is mandatory for Industrial and Joint Doctorates; Joint Doctorates additionally require a joint governance structure with joint procedures for recruitment, admission, supervision and evaluation of doctoral candidates.
document_format_rules: No file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published on the MSCA pages read for this action.

Proposal submission rules for organisations are governed by the online manual of the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal and by the call templates, which are published on the call page rather than on the action page.
For individual candidates, all document rules (formats, sizes, translation, dates, signatures) are those stated on the EURAXESS vacancy by the advertising institution.
official.selection_notes: Two separate selection processes exist. (1) Proposal level: the European Research Executive Agency checks whether the proposal meets the call's eligibility criteria; all eligible proposals are evaluated by external experts - the REA how-to-apply page states MSCA proposals are evaluated by at least 3 independent external expert evaluators against the award criteria defined in the work programme. The evaluation phase lasts up to 5 months from the call deadline. Applicants are informed by email and can check results in the 'My area' tab of the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal. Successful applicants are then invited to sign a grant agreement; generally the parties sign within 3 months. (2) Researcher level: selected projects must select doctoral candidates from all over the world in an open, transparent and merit-based process. Sustainability may be considered as a criterion to decide between otherwise ex-aequo proposals.
application_steps: Choose the funding modality that matches the project: Standard, Industrial Doctorate or Joint Doctorate.

Build the consortium: at least three independent legal entities in three different EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries, with at least one in an EU Member State; find partners via the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal 'Partner Search', the MSCA Matchmaking platform or the European Enterprise Network.
Create a profile on the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal (EU Login account) and register the organisation to obtain a PIC number.

Read the guidance documents on the dedicated call page: MSCA Work Programme and general annexes, guide for applicants, specific FAQs, proposal template and instructions, MSCA-specific evaluation forms, and the Horizon Online Manual.
Draft the proposal and complete all administrative forms and annexes; partners may contribute to their parts.
Get further guidance from the National Contact Point in your country and check eligibility with peers.
Submit through the Electronic Submission Service before the deadline; submit early to avoid last-minute problems. You can update, download or withdraw the proposal up until the deadline.
Receive an 'acknowledgement of receipt' e-mail for each submission.
After the deadline: REA eligibility check, external expert evaluation, notification of results.
If successful, sign the grant agreement with the REA.
applicant_submission_route: Grant route (organisations): consortium -> Electronic Submission Service on the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal, signed by the coordinator's authorised representative.

Doctoral candidate route (individuals): PhD candidates apply directly to the funded Doctoral Network project or host institution, using the vacancies the projects advertise internationally, including on EURAXESS.

arrival_rules: No arrival date, arrival deadline or relocation rule is published for recruited researchers on this page. The start of the fellowship is agreed between the researcher and the employing beneficiary.

EURAXESS is published as the source of advice on visas, pensions, taxation and recognition of qualifications, i.e. arrival formalities are a host-country matter and MSCA publishes no arrival requirement.
Beneficiaries may organise secondments for recruited researchers anywhere in the world, which implies travel but publishes no travel or relocation budget rule.

official.duration: Doctoral Network projects can last up to 4 years, and up to 5 years in the case of Joint Doctorate projects. Each individual fellowship lasts between 3 and 36 months, and between 3 and 48 months in the case of Joint Doctorate fellowships.
official.application_cycle: Annual call cycle for proposals: applications can be submitted at any time from the opening date of the chosen call until its specified submission deadline. The 2026 call HORIZON-MSCA-2026-DN-01 opened on 28 May 2026 and closes on 24 November 2026. For individual doctoral candidates there is no EU-level cycle at all - vacancies are advertised internationally and on EURAXESS, which is updated daily, so openings are continuous.
official.deadline_note: The published 24 November 2026 date (17.00 CET) is the proposal submission deadline for organisations and consortia under call HORIZON-MSCA-2026-DN-01. Doctoral candidates are not applicants to that call; they apply to funded projects after selection.
official.funding_label: EU support for each recruited researcher, delivered as salaried employment by the recruiting beneficiary: a living allowance, a mobility allowance and, if applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances. At project level, funding is also provided for research, training and networking activities and for management and indirect costs. No per-researcher monetary figure is published on this page.
official.living_cost_coverage: A living allowance is one of the published per-researcher components of EU support, but no rate is published on this page. It reaches the researcher as salary from the employing beneficiary under national employment law; country coefficients and the gross/net split are set in the MSCA Work Programme and the MSCA Financial Guide, not on this page.
benefits: Employment by the recruiting beneficiary, so the fellowship is paid as a salary under national employment law rather than as a scholarship paid directly to the student
Access to secondments, which the beneficiary may organise for recruited researchers anywhere in the world
Participation in funded research, training and networking activities at project level
For Joint Doctorates, a joint doctoral degree or multiple doctoral degrees awarded by the participating institutions
eligibility: Researchers funded by Doctoral Networks must not have a doctoral degree at the date of their recruitment
Researchers can be of any nationality
Researchers should be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project
Researchers should spend at least 50% of their time outside academia, for Industrial Doctorates

Researchers should comply with the mobility rules: in general, they must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before their recruitment date
Doctoral Networks are open to international consortia of universities, research institutions, businesses, SMEs and other non-academic organisations

A consortium should include at least three independent legal entities, each established in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country, with at least one of them established in an EU Member State
On top of this minimum, other organisations from any country in the world can also join; specific conditions apply to Industrial and Joint Doctorates
As from 2022, resubmission restrictions apply for applications that received a score below 80% the previous year
official.citizenship_residency: Researchers funded by Doctoral Networks can be of any nationality; no nationality or residency condition is published for the recruited researcher. The only residency condition is the mobility rule: the researcher must not have resided or carried out their main activity in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before their recruitment date.
official.international_eligibility: Open to doctoral candidates of any nationality worldwide who do not hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment, enrol in a doctoral programme during the project and satisfy the mobility rule. At consortium level the minimum is three independent legal entities in three different EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries with at least one in an EU Member State, with additional partners from any country in the world able to join.
requirements: Must not hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment
Must be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project
Must comply with the mobility rule (no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in the recruiting country in the 36 months before recruitment)
Industrial Doctorates: must spend at least 50% of their time outside academia and be jointly supervised by the academic and non-academic partners
Joint Doctorates: must be enrolled in a joint programme and be jointly supervised, leading to a joint or multiple doctoral degree
Each beneficiary must recruit at least one doctoral candidate
At consortium level: at least three independent legal entities in three different EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries, at least one in an EU Member State
documents: For organisations and consortia (published list of call documents on the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal): MSCA work programme 2026-2027 and its general annexes, guide for applicants, specific FAQs, application and evaluation forms, and the online manual on how to submit an application

For individual doctoral candidates: no MSCA document list is published. The published position is that candidates 'will find the full requirements of the position you are interested in' on the EURAXESS vacancy and 'be able to apply directly to the institution or project of your choice', so the document list is set by the advertising institution.
selection_criteria: The published objective doubles as the published standard the action is designed to meet: to train highly skilled doctoral candidates, stimulate their creativity, enhance their innovation capacities and boost their long-term employability, through doctoral programmes answering well-identified needs in research and innovation areas and exposing researchers to academic and non-academic sectors
Organisations: REA checks whether the proposal meets the call's eligibility criteria, and eligible proposals are evaluated by external experts. No scoring scale is published on this page.

Individual candidates: there is no MSCA competition. Selection of a researcher is made by the institution or project advertising the vacancy, and the published rule is that candidates apply directly to that institution or project.
Applications that scored below 80% in the previous year are subject to resubmission restrictions (in force since 2022)
application_method: Organisations and consortia: find the open or forthcoming call on the MSCA funding page, find partners and apply through the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal

Read the call documents published on the dedicated call page: MSCA work programme 2026-2027, general annexes, guide for applicants, specific FAQs, application and evaluation forms, and the online manual
Submit the completed proposal including all annexes through the portal's submission service before the call's specified submission deadline
Individual doctoral candidates: monitor the vacancies published internationally and on EURAXESS (updated daily), then apply directly to the institution or project of your choice

Use EURAXESS for advice on visas, pensions, taxation and recognition of qualifications, and use the MSCA National Contact Point in your country for help preparing an application or questions about a specific funded job offer
award_holder_conditions: Enrolment in a doctoral programme during the project is a published condition of the fellowship
Compliance with the mobility rule throughout the fellowship
Must not hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment
Industrial Doctorates: at least 50% of time outside academia, with joint academic and non-academic supervision
Joint Doctorates: enrolment in the joint programme with joint supervision, leading to the joint or multiple degree
Secondments organised by the beneficiary may take place anywhere in the world

official_contacts.general: European Research Executive Agency (REA) - the main source of information on the application and evaluation process (https://rea.ec.europa.eu/index_en). MSCA National Contact Points in your country - for help preparing an application or questions about the specific requirements of funded job offers (https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/support/ncp). Research Enquiry Service - the main contact point for all questions about participation in the MSCA and the EU Research Framework Programmes (https://ec.europa.eu/info/research-and-innovation/contact/research-enquiry-service_en). Published contact page: https://marie-sklodowska-curie-actions.ec.europa.eu/contact (last updated 21 April 2026). For a specific PhD position the contact point is the institution advertising the vacancy on EURAXESS.

official.program_type: EU research fellowship - Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Networks, a grant awarded to a consortium that employs recruited researchers as salaried staff
official.region: European Union and Horizon Europe Associated Countries (minimum three consortium entities in three different such countries, at least one in an EU Member State), with additional partners from any country in the world; recruited doctoral candidates can be of any nationality
coverage: A living allowance for each recruited researcher
A mobility allowance for each recruited researcher
A family allowance, if applicable
A long-term leave allowance, if applicable
A special needs allowance, if applicable
At project level: research, training and networking activities
At project level: management costs and indirect costs
official.description: MSCA Doctoral Networks pay for doctoral researchers indirectly: the European Commission funds a consortium of at least three organisations, and each beneficiary employs at least one researcher for 3 to 36 months (up to 48 for a Joint Doctorate) as salaried staff. Each recruited researcher receives a living allowance and a mobility allowance plus, where applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances, paid as salary by the employing organisation under national law; MSCA publishes no per-researcher figure on the action page. The award funds doctoral study only, requires enrolment in a doctoral programme during the project, and excludes anyone who already holds a doctoral degree at recruitment or who fails the 12-month-in-36-months mobility rule. There is no application to the European Commission for a fellowship - candidates apply directly to the institutions advertising vacancies on EURAXESS, each with its own deadline.
official.funding: Fully Funded - per recruited researcher a living allowance, a mobility allowance and (where applicable) family, long-term leave and special needs allowances, plus research/training/networking activities and management and indirect costs

important_advice_for_students: You cannot apply to the European Commission. MSCA Doctoral Networks money goes to a consortium; you get a job as a recruited researcher inside a funded project.
Your real entry point is a funded project vacancy. Search the EURAXESS jobs list, which is updated daily, and apply directly to the institution or project.

Test your mobility eligibility first. If you have lived or worked/studied in the recruiting country for more than 12 months in the past 36 months, you are ineligible. This is the most common hard fail.
You must not already hold a PhD at the recruitment date.

Check the funding type before you commit. Standard, Industrial Doctorate and Joint Doctorate carry different rules - Industrial Doctorates require at least 50% of your time outside academia and mandatory joint supervision; Joint Doctorates run up to 48 months and lead to a joint or multiple degree.
Read the individual vacancy advertisement, not just the MSCA name. Conditions, salary and start date are set by the recruiting organisation and vary by country.

Overall indicative budget for the 2026 call is 593.03 million - that is the call total, not your fellowship. No per-fellowship salary figure is published on the MSCA pages read, so do not assume a number.

referee_tracking.instructions: MSCA does not publish a referee or reference-letter requirement for doctoral candidates. Selection is an open, transparent and merit-based process run by each funded network, so referees, if any, are set by the individual vacancy advertisement and the host institution's own process. Check the vacancy text.

post_award_requirements: Enrolment in the doctoral programme is a condition of the fellowship and must continue during the project.
Comply with the mobility rule throughout the fellowship.
For Industrial Doctorates, spend at least 50% of time outside academia.
Participate in network training, research and networking activities and follow the network's supervisory board arrangements.
Work to a career development plan agreed jointly with the supervisor, covering training, teaching, publication planning and conference participation.
Report on green / sustainable practices adopted by the project.
Abide by the grant agreement signed with the European Research Executive Agency and by the beneficiary's own employment contract.
questions_to_ask_host: Is the doctoral programme enrolment fee-free for employed researchers, or do I pay tuition to the host institution?
What is the gross and net monthly salary under national law, and which MSCA allowances (living, mobility, family, long-term leave, special needs) apply to my case?
Which country coefficients apply to my host country and family situation?
What is the exact employment start date, contract type and duration, and is the contract with the host institution or a partner?
Which secondment opportunities are paid, and how much funding is left for them?
What are the selection criteria, the assessment timeline, and does the process include an interview?
Which documents do you need, in which format, and by what internal deadline - which is earlier than the MSCA project start?
Is a reference letter or referee report required, and who contacts referees?
common_rejection_risks: Failing the mobility rule (more than 12 months in the recruiting country in the 36 months before recruitment).
Already holding a doctoral degree at the recruitment date.
Not enrolled in a doctoral programme leading to a degree in an EU Member State or Associated Country.
For consortium applicants: fewer than three independent legal entities in three different EU Member/Associated Countries, or none in an EU Member State.
For Joint Doctorates: fewer than three entities entitled to award doctoral degrees, or no degree-awarding institution in an EU Member State or Associated Country.
For Industrial Doctorates: an individual research plan that does not reach 50% time outside academia.
Resubmitting a proposal that scored below 80% the previous year - a resubmission restriction applies.
Late submission - the Electronic Submission Service will not accept a proposal after 17.00 CET on 24 November 2026.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Doctoral enrolment or tuition fees at the enrolling institution, if charged - the MSCA pages read do not state that these are covered; confirm with the host.
Visa, residence permit and relocation costs - not published as covered by MSCA.
Any salary component not covered by the living, mobility, family, long-term leave or special needs allowances.
Costs during secondments beyond the funded period, and personal costs not permitted under the grant.
document_audit: At EU level the published documents are for organisations, not individual candidates: guide for applicants, MSCA Work Programme and general annexes, proposal template and instructions, MSCA-specific evaluation forms, and the Horizon Online Manual.

No file size limits, accepted file types, translation rules or date-of-issue rules for individual candidates are published on the MSCA pages read; these are set by each vacancy advertisement and by the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal upload rules.
For the organisational route, the Electronic Submission Service is the only accepted submission system - proposals sent by email are not admissible.

alerts.message: Read the call page and the guide for applicants as soon as the call opens; consortium formation takes longer than applicants expect.
Hard submission deadline for proposals. Submit early; you can update, download or withdraw only up until the deadline.
If you are a doctoral candidate, monitor the EURAXESS list of MSCA-funded vacancies, which is updated daily.
Re-run the mobility check against your actual travel history in the past 36 months.

application_readiness_checklist: You cannot apply to the European Commission. The 24 November 2026 deadline belongs to consortium proposals; you apply to institutions advertising funded vacancies on EURAXESS.
Check you do not already hold a doctoral degree at the recruitment date - this is an absolute disqualifier.
Check the mobility rule: no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in the recruiting organisation's country in the 36 months before your recruitment date.
Confirm the advertised position states that you will be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project.
For an Industrial Doctorate, confirm the position commits you to at least 50% of your time outside academia and joint supervision.
For a Joint Doctorate, confirm the advertised programme is a joint doctoral programme with joint supervision and a joint or multiple degree.
Prepare to be recruited as an employee: you will need identity, nationality, address, bank and tax-residence documents under the host country's employment law.
Use EURAXESS early for visa, pension and tax advice - MSCA publishes no arrival rules and the host country sets them.
submission_workflow: 1. Search the EURAXESS vacancy list for MSCA-funded doctoral positions (the MSCA filter covers EU-funded and MSCA-funded posts, updated daily).
2. Check the mobility rule for each advertised country before applying - a country you have lived in for over 12 months in the last 36 months will disqualify you.
3. Read the full requirement list published in the vacancy; it is set by the advertising institution, not by the EU.
4. Prepare the documents the vacancy asks for, using EURAXESS guidance for visa, pension, taxation and qualification-recognition issues.
5. Apply directly to the institution or project - you submit nothing to EURAXESS and nothing to the European Commission.
6. If shortlisted, expect an interview and reference checks by the host; agree your start date, salary and any secondment plan in writing before signing.
7. On appointment, the host enrols you in the doctoral programme and employs you, then claims the MSCA allowances through the beneficiary's reporting.

official.application_cycle: Annual; applications possible between 1 June and the stated application deadline, with funding beginning in 2027 (usually 1 October 2027, or earlier if a German language course is taken first)
official.deadline_central_display: Applications for this scholarship programme are possible between 1 June and the stated application deadline.
official.deadline_note: DAAD does not publish a single date on the programme page. It states that application deadlines are updated annually in the second quarter and are usually in the same period as the previous year, and that the portal is only accessible during the current application period. The page also shows 'Currently you cannot apply for this programme', so the specific day must be taken from the current annual call.
official.status_note: The programme page states 'Currently you cannot apply for this programme', because applications are only possible between 1 June and the annual deadline and that period has passed for the current cycle. The page describes funding that must begin in 2027.
official.funding_period: per month
official.funding_duration: 10 to 24 months, awarded for the standard period of study for the chosen programme up to a maximum of 24 months
official.tuition_coverage_note: DAAD states plainly that it does not cover tuition fees. The scholarship covers living costs, insurance, travel and study allowance, and you are separately responsible for admission to and enrolment at the German host university, including any semester contribution.
official.funding_label: EUR 992 per month plus insurance, travel allowance and an annual EUR 460 study allowance
benefits: Monthly scholarship payment of EUR 992
Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, on application only
Annual study allowance of EUR 460
On application after the start of funding: a monthly rent subsidy, a monthly allowance for accompanying family members, and a subsidy for justified additional costs of a disability or chronic illness
Payment of fees for an online German language course after receipt of the Scholarship Award Letter
A German language course of 2, 4 or 6 months before the start of the study visit if needed, which is compulsory if the study programme is taught in German
An allowance for a personally chosen German language course during the scholarship period
Reimbursement of the fee for a TestDaF or DSH test
Green Mobility Top Up for climate-friendly travel, or reimbursement of carbon offset payments for air travel
eligibility: Have completed a first degree (for example a Bachelor's or Diplom) at the latest by the time the funding period begins
Your most recent university degree should generally not date back more than 6 years at the application deadline
Not have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline
Have been admitted to, or apply separately for admission to, a suitable postgraduate or Master's programme at a state or state-recognised university in Germany
Be pursuing a Master's programme that has not already begun in Germany, since funding is only available for degree programmes starting in the winter semester of the following year
Applications from artistic disciplines and architecture are directed to separate DAAD scholarship programmes
official.citizenship_residency: The DAAD portal requires you to select your status and country of origin, and only programmes for which you are eligible are shown. The page does not publish a nationality restriction for this programme.
official.international_eligibility: This is a DAAD scholarship for international students applying from outside Germany; applications are not possible from within Germany, and the programme is for students who have completed a first degree abroad. Eligibility depends on the applicant's status and country as shown in the DAAD portal.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to all academic disciplines except artistic disciplines and architecture, which have their own DAAD scholarship programmes (Architecture, Fine Art/Design/Film, Performing Art, Music).
official.application_method: Apply online through the DAAD Portal. After registering, complete the online application in full and upload the documents in the 'Attachments' section. Scanned, non-certified documents are accepted, and DAAD reserves the right to request certified copies. Request the recommendation form in the portal, send it to your university teacher to complete, and upload it back.
requirements: Register in the DAAD Portal during the application period and use a desktop computer, as the portal is only usable to a limited extent on mobile devices
Have completed your first degree by the start of the funding period, and normally within the last 6 years
Submit your own application for admission to the German host university by its deadline; you are responsible for the university admission requirements and for entry regulations into Germany

A Scholarship Award Letter is only valid if you have been admitted to study at the host university named in your application, so admission must be notified before the funding period begins if it has not been received at application time
Provide proof of proficiency in the language of instruction of your chosen programme, which must be no older than 3 years
Not have been resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline

If the programme includes a period of study or work placement outside Germany, it is usually funded only if it is essential to the scholarship objective, is not in your home country, and is no longer than a quarter of the scholarship period (up to 50% for joint and double-degree programmes if specified in the study regulations)
documents: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form, maximum 3 pages
Statement about academic and personal reasons for the planned study project in Germany (letter of motivation), 1 to 3 pages, uploaded under 'study project/motion'
Letter of admission to the study programme at the host university in Germany, or notification of admission before the funding period begins
Form 'Information about your preferred master programmes', if planning a second degree or Master's programme in Germany, uploaded under 'course profile'
Proof that credits acquired in Germany will be recognised by the home university, if spending a study year in Germany as part of a degree completed abroad
Current overview of grades or transcript of records with individual grades, uploaded under 'university degree certificates'
University degree certificate indicating final grades, to be submitted by the start of funding if not yet completed at application time
Proof of knowledge of the language of instruction in the chosen programme, no older than 3 years
One recent supporting letter of recommendation from a university teacher, using the DAAD-generated form
Optional: other relevant documents such as employment certificates and proof of extracurricular engagement
official.english_requirement: Proof of proficiency in the language of instruction of the chosen programme, no older than 3 years
official.english_requirement_note: The programme page states that the language of instruction in German programmes is German, while international programmes are taught in English, or German and English, and that you must provide proof of your level of proficiency in the language of instruction. For English-taught programmes the page lists Cambridge English, Cambridge Business, IELTS, ISE, TOEFL iBT, TOEFL Essentials, TOEIC, PTE Academic, onSET English and Duolingo English Test as certificates that can be submitted, but it publishes no minimum score. Country-specific certification requirements are listed by country in the application documents section.
selection_criteria: Academic qualification: academic achievements, school leaving certificate if applicable, course of studies, knowledge of the language of instruction or working languages, and relevant internships and work experience

Quality of the study project: quality of the study project and of the preparation, including preliminary information, choice of degree programme, host university and establishment of contacts, and integration of the project into the academic career path

Potential of the applicant: academic and personal motivation for the stay in Germany, German language skills if different from the working language, prospects and significance of the stay for development, and extracurricular commitment and social engagement
Due consideration is given to aspects of equal opportunities, on which applicants can provide information in the application form
official.duration: Between 10 and 24 months depending on the length of the programme. Scholarships are awarded for the standard period of study for the chosen programme, up to a maximum of 24 months. After the first year, academic achievements are assessed, and if this shows the applicant will complete the programme within a reasonable period the scholarship continues as planned.
award_holder_conditions: Funding must begin in 2027, usually on 1 October 2027, or earlier if you take a German language course first
You must be admitted to the host university named in your application, or the Scholarship Award Letter is not valid
Participation in a German language course is compulsory if the study programme is taught in German
DAAD does not cover tuition fees
Funding is only available for degree programmes starting in the winter semester of the following year, and not for a Master's programme already begun in Germany
supplements_or_initiatives: Green Mobility Top Up for climate-friendly travel or reimbursement of carbon offset payments
Separate DAAD scholarship programmes for Architecture, Fine Art/Design/Film, Performing Art and Music

official_contacts.general: DAAD Scholarship Portal: portal@daad.de; technical hotline +49 (0) 228 882-8888; funded by the German Federal Foreign Office

official.description: DAAD's Study Scholarships - Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines fund a postgraduate or Master's degree, or one study year in Germany as part of a degree completed at the applicant's home university. The scholarship pays EUR 992 per month, insurance contributions, a travel allowance on application and an annual EUR 460 study allowance, for 10 to 24 months, with funding starting in 2027. DAAD does not cover tuition fees, and applicants must separately secure admission to a German university. The programme is funded by the German Federal Foreign Office, and artistic disciplines and architecture have separate DAAD programmes.
official.coverage: Covers a EUR 992 monthly living allowance, insurance, a travel allowance and a EUR 460 annual study allowance, plus optional rent, family and disability supplements; it does not cover tuition fees, which DAAD states explicitly, nor semester contributions or the cost of a second visa.
official.funding: Partial to Full - EUR 992 per month, an annual study allowance of EUR 460, payments towards health/accident/personal liability insurance and a travel allowance; duration 10-24 months. DAAD explicitly does not cover tuition fees.

application_readiness_checklist: Check that your status and country of origin are selectable in the DAAD portal, since only eligible programmes are shown
Complete your first degree by the start of the funding period and normally within the last 6 years
Secure admission to a state or state-recognised German university separately, and apply by that university's deadline
Pick a programme starting in the winter semester, since no other start is funded

Missing the host university admission deadline, which invalidates the award letter
A degree completed more than 6 years ago without a documented reason
More than 15 months of residence in Germany at the deadline
Applying under an artistic or architecture discipline, which needs a different DAAD programme
Assuming the scholarship pays tuition fees
estimated_uncovered_costs: All tuition fees at the German university
Semester contribution and any compulsory fees
Costs above the EUR 992 monthly allowance, unless the rent or family supplements are granted
Language test fees, which are not reimbursed even though a TestDaF or DSH fee can be reimbursed
The portion of a study year not recognised by the home university
document_audit: Keep the CV to 3 pages maximum and the motivation letter to 1 to 3 pages
Upload the recommendation form under 'Letter of Recommendation' after the teacher completes it
Upload the study programme form under 'course profile' if you are planning a second degree or a Master's in Germany
Upload the transcript under 'university degree certificates'
Have the admission letter or proof of recognition of credits ready, both of which are mandatory items

Choose a German university and programme, and apply for admission there independently

Complete the online application and upload all required documents as PDFs
