official.description: The GKS Exchange Students Program pays KRW 630,000 per month for four months (one semester) plus round-trip economy class airfare at actual cost, and NIIED's programme overview adds accommodation, settlement and insurance. It does not pay tuition: on the same official portal the degree programme's benefit list includes tuition and the exchange programme's does not, so any tuition charged by the participating university stays with the student. Around 500 students a year are funded, but the quota is explicitly subject to budget changes and only at universities NIIED has selected for the year. Selection is entirely institutional - your home university nominates you, the participating Korean university recommends you, and NIIED picks from those recommendations - and neither NIIED nor Study in Korea publishes an application deadline, document list or format rule for this programme.

important_advice_for_students: Do not confuse this with the GKS Degree Program. The exchange programme is 4 months, pays KRW 630,000 per month plus round-trip economy airfare, accommodation, settlement and insurance - it does NOT list tuition, and the quota (~500) and route are completely different.

Your real task is institutional. You cannot apply to NIIED. Your home university must have an agreement with a NIIED-affiliated Korean university that has been selected to run the programme, and the Korean university must recommend you.
Check you are applying to only one Korean university at a time. Multiple simultaneous applications are disallowed.
You must be in a degree exchange programme. A Korean language course placement does not qualify.
You need 80% overall academic performance at your home university. Have your transcript ready with that figure provable.

If you have ever held a Korean government scholarship, you are ineligible. If you currently study in Korea, you are ineligible. If you hold Korean citizenship, including dual citizenship, you are ineligible.
There is no published extension: recipients who have completed one semester (4 months) cannot apply for a scholarship extension.
Budget on KRW 630,000 per month. Study in Korea notes the monthly allowance may vary based on stay and semester end date, so the final month can differ.

referee_tracking.instructions: NIIED's published selection procedure is 'NIIED reviews and selects scholarship applicants recommended by the selected universities' - it names no referee, transcript assessor or interview panel. Any reference or recommendation letter required is set by your home university and the participating Korean university, not by NIIED. Ask both before nominating.

Return to your home university at the end of the exchange - the award is round-trip airfare and a single 4-month period; no continuation or second placement is published.
Any reporting to the participating university or NIIED is set by that institution; NIIED publishes no post-award reporting rule on the pages read.

submission_workflow: 1. Obtain NIIED's participating-university list for the current year from the Study in Korea GKS Exchange section and pick one university that has an agreement with your home university.
2. Apply to your home university for the exchange place, using its exchange-application process for students nominated under that bilateral agreement.
3. Meet your home university's internal deadline - this is the only deadline that exists; NIIED publishes none.
4. Submit to your home university the academic evidence it requires, including proof of 80% or above overall academic performance, for onward nomination.
5. The participating Korean university selects you from the nominations and forwards its recommendation to NIIED.
6. NIIED reviews the recommendations and announces the scholarship selection; keep an eye on your home and host university for the notification, since NIIED publishes no results date.

7. After selection, confirm with the participating university what the accommodation, settlement and insurance components mean in practice, and book travel against the actual round-trip economy fare only.

purpose: The Australia Awards Fellowships program is a competitive grants program providing short-term development opportunities in Australia that develop influential networks to advance development outcomes in partner countries by increasing the capacity of mid-career and senior officials in the region who are positioned to lead priority development and foreign affairs outcomes in partnership with Australia, and by developing and strengthening institutional partnerships and people-to-people links across the region and beyond between Australian and overseas counterpart organisations.

Fellowship activities aim to provide access to high-quality training, exchange of expertise, skills and knowledge, and opportunities to enhance networks on issues of shared interest. Activities can include a combination of short-term study and/or training, research, professional attachments, and networking.
The program is designed to complement Australia's individual bilateral and regional development programs and long-term scholarships.
sdg_requirement_details: No Sustainable Development Goal requirement is published. Alignment is instead required to one of six published DFAT development priority areas: (1) Climate change, adaptation, resilience and green energy transition (including critical mineral mining); (2) Health; (3) Gender equality, disability equity and social inclusion; (4) Digital Economy, cyber resilience, and media engagement; (5) Maritime and the Blue Economy; (6) Infrastructure and connectivity.
study_type: Short-term study and/or training
Research
Professional attachments
Networking

Any combination of the above; the programme is a short-term development opportunity of 2 to 52 weeks, commencing in Australia and followed by in-partner country activities focused on implementation and exchange of expertise, skills and knowledge
official.degree_award: No degree. This is a short-term fellowship / professional development placement (2 to 52 weeks), not a degree-awarding programme.
official.deadline_central_display: Round 21 is now closed for applications. Key dates for Round 21: 3 November 2025 - applications for Round 21 open; 10 November 2025 - Industry Information Session held; 16 January 2026 (11:59pm AEDT) - applications for Round 21 close; from August 2026 - Round 21 Outcome, successful and unsuccessful notifications made to all applicants. Key dates for Round 22: applications are expected to open in the final quarter of 2026. No Round 22 closing date is published.
official.deadline_institutional: Not published as a separate institutional deadline. Applications are submitted by the Australian Organisation, and the page publishes only the DFAT round opening and closing dates. An Australian Host Organisation may set earlier internal deadlines; these are not published by DFAT.
official.tuition_coverage: Not published as a component. Fellowship activities 'can include a combination of short-term study and/or training, research, professional attachments, and networking', but the page publishes no tuition-fee component; the award is stated as 'up to $34,500 per Fellow' without a tuition breakdown.
official.living_cost_coverage: Not itemised. DFAT publishes a single figure - funding of up to $34,500 per Fellow - plus a mandatory Australian Host Organisation co-contribution. No stipend, living-cost rate or per diem breakdown is published on this page.
official.travel_coverage: Not itemised as a separate component. DFAT states it will 'only fund and provide visa support letters for individual Fellows, not their family members', so Fellow travel is inside the funded scope, but the page does not break out airfare from the up-to-$34,500 figure. What the grant pays for is set in the round guidelines documents.
official.tuition_rule: No tuition-fee component is published. Fellowship activities can include short-term study and/or training, but DFAT identifies no tuition item; the up-to-$34,500 per Fellow is a single total grant for the Fellowship, and any course or programme fee charged by the host or a training provider is not identified as covered. Tuition is therefore not established as met, and the host's co-contribution is not defined as a tuition payment.
official.home_tuition_rule: Not published. The Fellow continues in their home-country role and returns home to implement the Fellowship; no rule on home-country salary or study fees continuing during the Fellowship is published.
official.host_institution_fee: Not published as a fee. The published requirement is that Australian Host Organisations must demonstrate commitment to the program and ongoing collaboration by providing a co-contribution to the Fellowship costs (in-kind and/or financial). No fee payable to the host is specified.
official.tax_status: Not published. Tax treatment is a personal matter under Australian law and the Fellow's home-country law; DFAT publishes no tax rule for this fellowship.

Short-term study and/or training, research, professional attachments and networking activities in Australia

not_covered_or_excluded: Family members of the Fellow - DFAT will only fund and provide visa support letters for individual Fellows, not their family members, and the Fellow must be able to travel without family members
Individual applicants - 'Individuals cannot apply'; the applicant must be a legal Australian entity with a current ABN

general_eligibility: Australian Organisations in partnership with Overseas Counterpart Organisations (OCOs) in eligible developing countries are eligible to apply.

Australian Organisations must be able to demonstrate links with OCOs in eligible countries and must demonstrate commitment to the partnership and Fellowship program through an in-kind and/or financial co-contribution.

Applicants must be Australian Organisations who are legal entities with a current Australian Business Number (ABN). Examples include private sector, research centres, higher education providers, vocational education and training providers, peak bodies, Australian chambers of commerce, community groups, non-government organisations, media organisations, professional associations and industry bodies; and Australian Government departments (Federal, State/Territory and local), government agencies, statutory authorities, and Government Business Enterprises.
The OCO must operate and reside in an eligible country; OCOs cannot be individuals.
New or emerging partnerships with OCOs will be considered.
The Fellowship must align with one of the six published development priority areas.
A minimum of two weeks is delivered in Australia, and the in-Australia activity duration must be longer than the in-partner country activity duration.
ineligibility_conditions: Individual applicants - individuals cannot apply.
The applicant being an OCO rather than an Australian legal entity with a current ABN.
The applicant organisation not having a current Australian Business Number (ABN).
The submitting officer not being an employee of the Australian Organisation.
The applicant organisation having already exceeded six applications.
Applications covering more than 15 DFAT-funded Fellows.
Applications covering ineligible countries only.
Applications without an Australian Organisation co-contribution.
Applications with no in-partner country activity.
Proposals that do not align with one of the six development priority areas.
Fellowships with less than two weeks in Australia, longer than 52 weeks in total, or where in-Australia activity duration is not longer than in-partner country activity duration.
OCO(s) not from an eligible ODA-listed country.
OCO(s) that are an international arm or branch of the Australian organisation, or under the same overarching international organisation or international consortium.
Applicant organisations listed in the National Redress Scheme (institutions that have not joined or signified their intent to join the Scheme).

Fellows who are Australian citizens or applying for Australian citizenship, including dual citizenship where one citizenship is Australian.
Fellows who hold or are applying for Australian permanent resident status.
Fellows who are current serving military personnel.

Fellows who have not been working in their country of citizenship or residency, and in an area relevant to the Fellowship activities, preceding the proposed commencement date.

phd: Not applicable by academic level. The programme targets senior officials and mid-career professionals who, in the short to medium term, will be in a position to advance priority development and foreign affairs issues on their return home. No academic degree threshold is published; the only published academic-style condition is the English language ability requirement.

host_requirements: The Australian Host Organisation (AHO) must be a legal entity with a current Australian Business Number (ABN).
The AHO must demonstrate links with the Overseas Counterpart Organisation in an eligible country.
The AHO must demonstrate commitment to the partnership and the Fellowship program through an in-kind and/or financial co-contribution.
The AHO must ensure all nominated Fellows meet the published general eligibility requirements.

The AHO is responsible for ensuring Fellows have an adequate level of English language ability, or must implement appropriate measures to enable Fellows to fully participate in and benefit from the Fellowship activities (for example, translation services).

The AHO must ensure the proposed Fellowship can be participated in by the Fellow for the full duration proposed, except in exceptional circumstances approved by the Australia Awards Global Support Unit (GSU) and DFAT.
The Fellowship must deliver a minimum of two weeks in Australia, with in-Australia activity duration longer than the in-partner country activity duration, and total duration between 2 and 52 weeks.
The AHO must nominate no more than 15 DFAT-funded Fellows per application.
document_format_rules: No file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published on the DFAT HTML pages read.

The 'specified format' is defined in the round guidelines and application template for that round. An application that fails to provide all information in the specified format does not pass the mandatory compliance gate and is never assessed, so format compliance is a pass/fail condition rather than a scored one.

Language: DFAT publishes no translation rule for the application. It does require the Fellow to have adequate English to participate fully, and notes that AHOs are responsible for ensuring Fellows' English ability or implementing measures such as translation services - with the specific warning that translation services should not be used for Multi-country Fellowships where they would compromise learning outcomes.
Applications are lodged by the Australian Organisation's submitting officer as an employee of that organisation, which is a signature and authority condition as well as an eligibility one.
official.selection_notes: Selection is not an open individual competition. Australian Organisations submit a competitive application that is screened against the published mandatory Application Compliance Criteria - an application that fails any of them cannot progress to the assessment stage. Compliance criteria include: provide all information in the specified format; submitted by a legal Australian Entity with a current ABN; applicant is not an individual/OCO; submitting officer is an employee of the Australian Organisation; the Applicant Organisation has not exceeded six applications; the application cannot exceed 15 DFAT-funded Fellows; the application only covers eligible countries; a co-contribution from the Australian Organisation is included; in-partner country activity is included; the proposal aligns with one of the development priority areas; a minimum of two weeks is delivered in Australia; the Fellowship is between two and 52 weeks in total; in-Australia activity duration is longer than the in-partner country activity duration; the OCO is from an eligible ODA-listed country; OCO independence rules; not listed in the National Redress Scheme; and not listed in the proscribed lists. Successful and unsuccessful notifications are made to all applicants - from August 2026 for Round 21.
application_steps: Identify the priority area the Fellowship will align with and confirm the OCO is from an eligible country and is independent of the Australian Organisation.
Confirm the Australian applicant is a legal entity with a current ABN, has not exceeded six applications, and is not on the National Redress Scheme or the proscribed lists.
Build the Fellowship plan: total duration 2-52 weeks, at least two weeks in Australia, in-Australia duration longer than in-partner country duration, in-partner country activity included.
Secure the Australian Organisation's in-kind and/or financial co-contribution.

Verify each nominated Fellow against the published general eligibility requirements, including age 18+, non-Australian citizenship and permanent residency status, residence in an eligible developing country, not current serving military personnel, and the spouse/partner restriction.
Prepare the application in the specified format using the round guidelines for the current round (Round 21 guidelines are published).
Submit the application as an employee of the Australian Organisation within the published round window (Round 21: 3 November 2025 to 16 January 2026, 11:59pm AEDT).

applicant_submission_route: Australian legal entity with a current ABN (the submitting officer must be an employee of that organisation) -> DFAT via the Australia Awards application process. The OCO and the individual Fellow do not submit.
official.application_portal: Not published as a URL on this page. DFAT directs applicants to the Australia Awards website (australiaawards.org) and publishes the round guidelines documents for the relevant round; enquiries to fellowships@australiaawards.org.
arrival_rules: The Fellowship commences in Australia. The published sequence is activity in Australia first, followed by in-partner country activities, so the Fellow travels to Australia and then returns to the OCO country during the Fellowship itself.
At least two weeks must be delivered in Australia, and the in-Australia activity must be longer than the in-partner country activity.
Total duration is 2 to 52 weeks inclusive of in-Australia, online and in-partner country activity.
The Fellow must be able to satisfy all Department of Home Affairs visa requirements; DFAT provides a visa support letter for the individual Fellow only.
Family members do not travel with the Fellow - DFAT only funds and supports the individual.
timeline_rules: Round 21: applications opened 3 November 2025; Industry Information Session held 10 November 2025; applications closed 16 January 2026 (11:59pm AEDT); outcomes and notifications to all applicants from August 2026.
Round 22: applications expected to open in the final quarter of 2026. No closing date published.

Fellowship duration: 2 to 52 weeks, commencing in Australia, followed by in-partner country activities. The duration of in-partner country activities must not exceed the duration of activities in Australia.
An Australia Awards Fellowships Pre-Departure Guide is published by DFAT for the successful round, so pre-departure requirements exist but are set out in that guide rather than on this page.

official_contacts.general: Australia Awards. Website: Australia Awards (australiaawards.org). Industry Information Sessions are held each round.

official_application_route: Australian Organisation (legal entity, current ABN; submitting officer is an employee) prepares and lodges the application with DFAT under the Australia Awards Fellowships round.
DFAT selects Australian Host Organisations; AHOs then nominate individual Fellows from their OCOs, and AHOs must ensure each Fellow meets the general eligibility requirements.
Enquiries: fellowships@australiaawards.org. Round guidelines, FAQ, budget tables and the Pre-Departure Guide are published as official resources for each round.
degree_levels: Not defined by academic level. The programme targets senior officials and mid-career professionals, and no undergraduate, master's or doctoral level is specified anywhere on the published pages.
official.duration: 2 to 52 weeks per Fellowship. The Fellowship commences in Australia and is followed by in-partner country activities focused on implementation and exchange of expertise. The duration of the in-partner country activities must not exceed the duration of the activities in Australia. The mandatory compliance criteria add that at least two weeks must be delivered in Australia and that the total cannot exceed 52 weeks, counting in-Australia, online and in-partner country activity together.
official.application_cycle: Annual competitive grants round administered by DFAT. Round 21 opened 3 November 2025 and closed 16 January 2026 (11:59pm AEDT), with outcomes notified to all applicants from August 2026. A DFAT visa support letter for the individual Fellow

official.international_eligibility: Restricted to nationals and residents of DFAT's published list of eligible developing countries: Pacific (Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna); Southeast Asia (Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Vietnam); South Asia and Middle East (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Mongolia, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Iraq, Jordan, State of Palestine); Africa (Botswana, Democratic Republic of Congo, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe); Caribbean (Belize, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Haiti, Jamaica, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Suriname); and Europe (Ukraine). Individuals from other countries, and all Australian citizens and permanent residents, are outside the programme. Individuals cannot apply at all - the applicant is always the Australian Host Organisation.

documents: No applicant document list is published on the DFAT HTML pages read. The only published document requirement is the mandatory compliance criterion that the application must 'provide all information in the specified format'.

selection_criteria: Mandatory compliance gate: the application must satisfy every published Application Compliance Criterion or it does not progress to the assessment stage - specified format; legal Australian entity with a current ABN; applicant not an individual or OCO; submitting officer an employee of the Australian Organisation; no more than six applications by the organisation; no more than 15 DFAT-funded Fellows in one application; eligible countries only; a co-contribution from the Australian Organisation included; in-partner country activity included; alignment with one development priority area; a minimum of two weeks in Australia; total duration of 2 to 52 weeks; in-Australia duration longer than in-partner duration; OCO from an eligible ODA-listed country and not an arm/branch or sister body of the Australian organisation; not listed in the National Redress Scheme; not on the ADB, World Bank, terrorist-organisation or Consolidated List proscribed lists

The Fellowship must align with one of six published development priority areas: (1) Climate change, adaptation, resilience and green energy transition (including critical mineral mining); (2) Digital Economy, cyber resilience, and media engagement; (3) Maritime and the Blue Economy; (4) Infrastructure and connectivity (plus the further priority areas listed on the same section of the page)
Funding is offered 'on a competitive basis' - DFAT publishes no scoring scale, weighting or pass mark on this page, so any ranking model would be invention
Individual Fellows are not assessed competitively by DFAT: the Australian Host Organisation selects the Fellow and must ensure the Fellow meets all general eligibility requirements
New or emerging partnerships with OCOs are stated to be considered

Confirm the applicant is a legal Australian entity with a current Australian Business Number, and that the submitting officer is an employee of that organisation

Check the mandatory compliance criteria before drafting anything: the six-application cap, the 15 DFAT-funded Fellow cap, the 2-52 week duration, the minimum two weeks in Australia, and the in-Australia duration exceeding the in-partner country duration
Agree the co-contribution (cash and/or in kind) with the Australian Host Organisation and reflect it in the application
Prepare the application using the current round's guidelines and budget table, in the specified format, including the in-partner country activity and the priority-area alignment
Check the applicant organisation against the National Redress Scheme and the published proscribed lists before submitting

DFAT selects the Australian Host Organisations, which then confirm the individual Fellow; enquiries go to fellowships@australiaawards.org

Travel without family members; DFAT funds and provides visa support letters for the individual Fellow only
Complete in-partner country implementation activity as part of the Fellowship, with that activity shorter than the in-Australia activity
Complete the Fellow's Completion Survey at the conclusion of the Fellowship

Not hold, and not apply for, Australian permanent residency during the Fellowship

official.program_type: Government grants programme - Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade competitive grants to Australian Host Organisations, which host individual Fellows nominated from Overseas Counterpart Organisations in eligible developing countries
official.region: Australia (host country). Fellows are citizens of and residents of DFAT's published eligible developing countries: Pacific, Southeast Asia, South Asia and Middle East, Africa, Caribbean, and Ukraine
coverage: Up to $34,500 per Fellow, offered on a competitive basis
DFAT visa support letter for the individual Fellow
Short-term study and/or training, research, professional attachments and networking activities in Australia and in-partner countries, of 2 to 52 weeks
A mandatory co-contribution from the Australian Host Organisation toward the Fellowship costs
official.description: Australia Awards Fellowships is a DFAT competitive grants programme in which an Australian organisation - never an individual - applies for funding to host a Fellow nominated by an overseas counterpart organisation in an eligible developing country. The grant is up to $34,500 per Fellow for a single Fellowship of 2 to 52 weeks, and the Australian Host Organisation must add a mandatory cash and/or in-kind co-contribution; DFAT publishes no tuition component, no living-cost rate and no separate airfare figure. Every application must first clear a mandatory compliance gate - correct format, current ABN, no more than six applications per organisation, no more than 15 DFAT-funded Fellows, at least two weeks in Australia, in-partner country activity, and alignment with one of six development priority areas - or it is never assessed. The Fellow must travel without family, cannot hold or be seeking Australian permanent residency, and must be a citizen of and resident in one of DFAT's listed eligible countries; Round 21 closed on 16 January 2026 and Round 22 is expected to open in the final quarter of 2026 with no date published.
official.funding_label: Funding of up to $34,500 per Fellow, offered on a competitive basis, plus a mandatory co-contribution from the Australian Host Organisation in cash and/or in kind. This is a single capped grant for a Fellowship of 2 to 52 weeks - not a periodic payment and not a per-item breakdown. DFAT publishes no separate tuition, living-cost, airfare or visa-fee component; the only other funded item named on the page is the visa support letter for the individual Fellow.

important_advice_for_students: You cannot apply for this as an individual, and you are very unlikely to be the right applicant. The applicant must be an Australian legal entity with a current ABN; students apply only as the nominated Fellow inside someone else's application.

Your realistic route is: be employed by an Overseas Counterpart Organisation in an eligible country that already has or can build a partnership with an Australian organisation, and be nominated as a senior official or mid-career professional.

Check the eligible country list first. The programme is limited to listed ODA-eligible countries in the Pacific, Southeast Asia, South Asia and the Middle East, Africa, the Caribbean and (Europe) Ukraine.

The hard personal disqualifiers are worth checking early: any Australian citizenship including dual citizenship, any Australian permanent residency or an application for it, being current serving military personnel, and being married or engaged to (or in a de facto relationship with) anyone who holds or is eligible to hold Australian or New Zealand citizenship or permanent residency.

Budget carefully. The published figure is 'up to $34,500 per Fellow' and the Australian Host Organisation must add an in-kind and/or financial co-contribution. Treat $34,500 as a ceiling, not an entitlement.
DFAT funds only the individual Fellow. Family members are not funded and no visa support letters are issued for them - if you need family to travel, that cost is not covered.

English ability is a real requirement, not a formality: the Fellow must have 'an adequate level of English language ability to be able to fully participate in the program, including an ability to complete the Fellow's Completion Survey at the conclusion of their Fellowship'.
Watch the calendar. Round 21 closed on 16 January 2026 and Round 22 is expected to open only in the final quarter of 2026, so this is not a programme to start assembling in December.
If your OCO is an international branch of the Australian organisation, or sits under the same overarching international organisation, it does not qualify.

referee_tracking.role: No individual Fellow referee or reference process is published
referee_tracking.instructions: DFAT publishes no referee requirement for the Fellow. Selection happens at application level, assessed by DFAT against the mandatory Application Compliance Criteria, and the Fellow is vetted by the Australian Host Organisation against the published general eligibility requirements. Any reference or supporting statement is an Australian Host Organisation requirement under the round guidelines, not a DFAT-published Fellow requirement.

post_award_requirements: Participate in the nominated Fellowship activities for the full duration proposed by the Australian Host Organisation, except in exceptional circumstances approved by the GSU and DFAT.
Travel without family members - DFAT funds and provides visa support letters for the individual Fellow only.
Complete the Fellow's Completion Survey at the conclusion of the Fellowship (the English requirement is written around this).
Deliver the in-partner country component focused on implementation and exchange of expertise, skills and knowledge; the in-partner country duration may not exceed the in-Australia duration.
Follow the Australia Awards Fellowships Pre-Departure Guide, which DFAT publishes for each round.
Deliver the minimum two weeks in Australia as planned - the design of the placement is assessed on that basis.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the Australian Organisation's co-contribution in cash and in kind, and how is it valued?
How much of the up-to-$34,500 will actually be available for me, and what does the budget table for the round allow me to spend it on?
Is airfare, accommodation, per diems and visa costs inside the grant or additional? The DFAT page does not break this down.
Do I pay any fees to the host institution, and are there tuition or course costs for the study/training components?
What are the internal nomination deadlines, and who in my OCO signs the application?
What are the exact document requirements, file formats and page limits set out in the round guidelines?
Does the Fellowship include any onward in-partner country funding, and is that funded by DFAT or by my OCO?
What happens if my circumstances change mid-Fellowship - who do I notify, and what does the GSU approval process require?
common_rejection_risks: Applying as an individual, or as an OCO rather than an Australian ABN-holding entity.
An OCO that is an international arm/branch of the Australian organisation or sits under the same overarching international body.
An OCO in a country not on the eligible list.
Failing any mandatory compliance criterion - these are stated as pass/fail gates to reach assessment.
No co-contribution from the Australian Organisation, or no in-partner country activity.
Less than two weeks in Australia, total duration outside 2-52 weeks, or in-Australia duration not longer than in-partner country duration.
Exceeding six applications as the Australian Organisation, or proposing more than 15 DFAT-funded Fellows.

A nominated Fellow with Australian citizenship, Australian permanent residency, an application for either, or a partner who holds or is eligible to hold Australian or New Zealand citizenship or permanent residency.
A nominated Fellow who is current serving military personnel, or who cannot travel without family members.
Insufficient English to participate fully, including completing the Completion Survey.
An applicant on the National Redress Scheme or a proscribed list.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Family travel and related costs - DFAT funds only the individual Fellow.
Any cost above the up-to-$34,500 per Fellow ceiling.
Whatever the Australian Host Organisation does not cover from its required co-contribution.
Personal expenses, and any costs of extending the placement beyond the approved duration.
document_audit: DFAT publishes no document list, file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule or date-of-issue rule on this page. document_format_rules is therefore deliberately empty.

The binding format source is the current round guidelines - DFAT has published 'Australia Awards Fellowships guidelines round 21' and round 20 guidelines and round 20 budget tables as DOCX and PDF. Get the guidelines for the round you are applying to and work from its document checklist.

Compliance items to have ready: current ABN of the Australian Organisation; confirmation the submitting officer is an employee; the Organisation's application count to date; confirmation of non-listing on the National Redress Scheme and the four proscribed lists; the OCO's country of operation and residence; a per-Fellow eligibility checklist (age, citizenship, residency status, service status, partner status).

alerts.message: Round 22 is expected to open. Watch the Australia Awards site and the DFAT page for the published opening date and closing deadline.
Attend the Industry Information Session - Round 21's was held in the week after opening and is where DFAT walks through the compliance criteria.
Re-run the mandatory Application Compliance Criteria list. Failing any one of them means the application does not reach assessment.
Check the spouse/partner restriction and the Australian citizenship / permanent residency restriction. Both are absolute disqualifiers.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are applying through an Australian legal entity with a current ABN - individuals and OCOs cannot apply, and the submitting officer must be an employee of that entity.

Confirm your country of citizenship and your country of residence both appear in DFAT's published eligible-country list; citizenship and residence may be different countries but both must be eligible.
Confirm you have held no Australian permanent resident status and are not applying for it.
Confirm you are not current serving military personnel.

Confirm you are not married, engaged or in a de facto relationship with anyone who holds or is eligible to hold Australian or New Zealand citizenship or permanent residency - this is a hard exclusion and is widely missed.
Confirm you can obtain a visa satisfying Department of Home Affairs requirements for the whole Fellowship.
Confirm you have been working in your country of citizenship or residency, in a field relevant to the Fellowship, before the proposed start date.
Confirm you can travel without family members and can be away for 2 to 52 weeks.
Confirm your English is good enough to take part fully and to complete the Fellow's Completion Survey at the end.
Have the Australian Host Organisation's co-contribution (cash and/or in kind) agreed and quantified before drafting.
Build the Fellowship so that at least two weeks sit in Australia, the in-Australia block is longer than the in-partner country block, and the total stays within 52 weeks.
Align the proposal to exactly one of the six development priority areas and say so explicitly.
Check the Australian organisation is not listed on the National Redress Scheme and is not on the ADB, World Bank, terrorist-organisation or Consolidated List proscribed lists.
Confirm the Australian organisation is within its six-application cap and that the proposal is within the 15 DFAT-funded Fellow cap.
Download the current round's guidelines and budget table and use their exact templates - format failure means no assessment at all.
submission_workflow: 1. Choose the one development priority area your Fellowship aligns with and settle the eligible-country question for the OCO.
2. Agree the Fellowship shape with the Australian Host Organisation: total 2-52 weeks, minimum two weeks in Australia, in-partner country activity included and shorter than the Australian block.
3. Agree and value the Australian Host Organisation's co-contribution in cash and in kind.
4. Download the current round's guidelines and budget table from the DFAT round resources and build the application in the specified format.
5. Run the mandatory compliance criteria against your draft - all of them, because one failure removes the application from assessment.
6. Have the submitting officer, who must be an employee of the Australian Organisation, lodge the application with DFAT before the published round closing date and time zone.
7. After DFAT selects the Australian Host Organisation, the host confirms the individual Fellow's eligibility and arrangements, and DFAT issues the visa support letter for the Fellow only.
8. Follow the DFAT Pre-departure Guide once the Fellowship is confirmed.
