purpose: The Australian Government provides funding to eligible higher education providers through the RTP to support their training of domestic and overseas students undertaking research doctorate and research masters degrees (collectively higher degrees by research, HDRs).

Published objectives of the RTP: provide flexible funding to support training domestic students and overseas students undertaking HDRs at Australian higher education providers; deliver graduates with the skills required to build careers in academia and other sectors of the labour market; support collaboration between higher education providers and industry and other research end-users.

The RTP is a research block grant program: Australian Government funding is provided through annual block grants to eligible Australian higher education providers in accordance with section 46-20 of the Higher Education Support Act 2003 and the Higher Education Support (Commonwealth Scholarships) Guidelines 2025. 2026 RTP grant amounts allocated to eligible providers are based on a formula reflecting each provider's relative performance in attracting research income and supporting students to complete HDRs.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or development-goal requirement is published. The published alignment test is with three RTP objectives: provide flexible funding to support training domestic and overseas students undertaking higher degrees by research at Australian higher education providers; deliver graduates with the skills required to build careers in academia and other sectors of the labour market; and support collaboration between providers and industry and other research end-users.
study_type: Accredited research doctorate (PhD) - higher degree by research
Accredited research masters degree - higher degree by research
At least two-thirds of the student's time must be spent on research at the eligible Australian university
Full-time or part-time student load (the Guidelines do not restrict part-time students, but providers may award to part-time students only in specific circumstances)

RTP industry internship pathway: an eligible industry internship of at least 3 months and 60 full-time equivalent days of engagement, agreed in writing between the student, the provider and the research end-user, attracts an additional weighting of 2.0 in the provider's funding allocation
official.degree_award: Full research degree (research doctorate or research masters) at an eligible Australian university. Coursework degrees such as a bachelor or masters coursework degree do not qualify as an HDR and are excluded from RTP eligibility.
official.deadline_central_display: No Commonwealth deadline exists. Published wording: 'Universities are responsible for the application, selection and offer processes and deadlines for RTP scholarships.' and 'If you are a prospective higher degree by research (HDR) student interested in applying for an RTP scholarship, you will need to contact your chosen eligible higher education provider (HEP) directly. RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education.'
official.deadline_institutional: Set by each eligible Australian university and published in its RTP scholarship policy, which students are directed to view on the university's webpage. No Commonwealth or provider-wide date is published.
official.travel_coverage: Not published as a travel or airfare component. The published allowances assist with 'the ancillary costs of a HDR', with examples given as relocation costs to undertake a HDR, HDR thesis printing and academic publication costs, and Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) costs for international students and their dependents. No airfare or travel budget figure is published.
official.tuition_rule: A tuition fees offset is a published component of the scheme, but it is not automatic. The page states that students 'can be offered RTP scholarships for one or more of the following: tuition fees offset; a stipend for general living costs; allowances related to the ancillary cost of HDRs'. The choice of components is the HEP's, so a specific recipient may hold a stipend without a fees offset. No page on education.gov.au publishes a rule on whether tuition owed to an overseas institution continues during the award.
official.home_tuition_rule: Not published. The page addresses only the Australian tuition fees offset and says nothing about fees payable to a home-country institution during the award.
official.host_institution_fee: Not published as a student fee. Australian Government funding reaches eligible providers as block grants under section 46-20 of the Higher Education Support Act 2003 and the Higher Education Support (Commonwealth Scholarships) Guidelines 2025, with 2026 allocations calculated by a published formula reflecting each provider's research income and HDR completion performance. The page publishes no HEF/SAF statement, no course-fee amount and no student contribution.
official.tax_status: Published: 'Full-time RTP stipends are considered tax exempt, provided they meet the additional criteria outlined by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO). Part-time RTP stipends are taxable.' Students are referred to the ATO's scholarship payments webpage for further information.
covered_expenses: Fees offset - full offset of the higher degree by research tuition fees applicable for the student
Stipend to assist students with their living costs while undertaking a HDR
Allowances to assist with the ancillary costs of a HDR
Relocation costs to undertake a HDR (published as an example of an allowance)
HDR thesis printing and academic publication costs (published as examples of allowances)
Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) costs for international students and their dependents (published as an example of an allowance)
not_covered_or_excluded: Bachelor degrees and masters coursework degrees - coursework degrees do not qualify as a HDR and are excluded from RTP eligibility
HDRs undertaken at an overseas university - eligibility requires enrolment at an eligible Australian university
RTP fees offset for a student already receiving an equivalent Australian Government award or scholarship designed to offset HDR fees

For a fees-offset recipient, an RTP fees offset where the student is in receipt of another Commonwealth award or scholarship for the purpose of paying HDR tuition fees (subsection 17(2) applies to domestic students)
Any support beyond the maximum period of support - eligible universities cannot provide extensions beyond the stated maxima

No published list of excluded purchases applies to the stipend itself; use of funds is not restricted in the published Guidelines, but providers set their own policy and any paid-employment restrictions
general_eligibility: Be a domestic or international student enrolled in an accredited research doctorate or research masters degree (an HDR) at an eligible Australian university.
Spend at least two-thirds of your time on research at the eligible Australian university.
For an RTP fees offset specifically, not be receiving an equivalent award or scholarship from the Australian Government that is designed to offset HDR fees.

Meet the eligibility criteria specified in the Higher Education Support (Commonwealth Scholarships) Guidelines 2025 (which replaced the Commonwealth Scholarships Guidelines (Research) 2017 on 3 December 2025).

International students are eligible, but the university in administering RTP scholarships may only spend up to 10% of its RTP funding per grant year on providing scholarships to international students.
Applications may be made to more than one university, or more than once at the same university.
ineligibility_conditions: Enrolling in a bachelor or masters coursework degree - coursework degrees do not qualify as a HDR
Undertaking the HDR at an overseas university rather than an eligible Australian university
Receiving an equivalent Australian Government award or scholarship designed to offset HDR fees, which bars an RTP fees offset
For domestic students in receipt of another Commonwealth award or scholarship for the purpose of paying HDR tuition fees, which bars an RTP fees offset under subsection 17(2)
Not enrolled at an eligible Australian higher education provider
Failing the provider's own additional selection criteria (the Guidelines do not bar a student the provider's criteria bar)

masters: Research masters degrees only (higher degree by research). Masters coursework degrees are explicitly excluded.
Full-time: up to 2 years of support, with no minimum published. Part-time: up to 4 years.
Stipend rate for part-time students is 50% of the full-time rate offered by the university.
Part-time RTP stipends are taxable; full-time RTP stipends are considered tax exempt provided the additional ATO criteria are met.
phd: Research doctorate degrees only (higher degree by research).
Full-time: minimum 3 years, maximum 4 years. Part-time: minimum 6 years, maximum 8 years.

Support must be provided for at least 3 years and up to 4 years full-time; these durations are doubled for part-time students. Eligible universities have discretion to award any period within these ranges and cannot provide extensions beyond the maximum.

The maximum period of support is calculated from the student's HDR course commencement date, which may or may not have occurred at a previous university and may or may not have been supported through the RTP. Support is not reset or extended on transfer to a different university.
Stipend rate for part-time students is 50% of the full-time rate offered by the university.

host_requirements: The university must be an eligible higher education provider receiving research block grants (published as a separate list by the Department of Education).
The university must administer RTP scholarships itself, including the application, selection and offer processes and deadlines.
The university must publish an RTP scholarship policy on its webpage detailing its application, selection and offer process.

The university must clearly distinguish, in all communications about student selection (including websites and direct communications), between the student eligibility criteria specified by the Guidelines and any additional selection criteria it sets.
The university must provide information regarding suspensions of RTP scholarships in its RTP scholarship policy.
The university must provide a stipend rate at least equal to the base full-time RTP stipend rate and no more than the maximum full-time RTP stipend rate, using RTP funding.
The university must inform students of the estimated value of each type of RTP scholarship support awarded in the RTP offer letter.
The university must include in its RTP scholarship policy the circumstances in which it will not approve a student to undertake work outside their HDR, including any restrictions on hours worked.
The university must include information on both outgoing and incoming transfers of RTP scholarships in its RTP scholarship policy.
In administering RTP scholarships a university may only spend up to 10% of its RTP funding per grant year on providing scholarships to international students.
documents: No document list is published on the Department of Education page, because the Department does not receive RTP applications.
Documents are those required by the specific HEP for its own application and selection process; those requirements sit on the HEP's own scholarship page, not on education.gov.au.
document_format_rules: No file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published by the Department of Education, because the Department does not receive applications.
All format rules are the provider's own and differ between providers; obtain them from the HEP's RTP scholarship page before preparing anything.
One published output-format rule does exist and is scheme-wide: any acknowledgement of RTP funding must include the RTP DOI (doi.org/10.82133/C42F-K220) in the published form of words.
official.selection_notes: Selection is institutional, not Commonwealth. Published: 'Universities have the discretion to award RTP scholarships as a result of a competitive selection process, the nature of which is determined by the university.' In determining its selection process a university may take into consideration previous study, relevant work experience, research publications, referee reports and other research experience, and may give priority to students undertaking research in a particular discipline or emerging area of research strength, students who achieved specific marks in their previous degree(s), students undertaking a research degree for the first time, or students studying on campus and/or in person. No Commonwealth assessment rubric, score or interview requirement is published. The Guidelines deliberately place only a floor under eligibility (for example, first class honours is not required, and holding a research degree from an overseas university, having previously completed an HDR, or having withdrawn from a previous RTP are not bars), leaving the rest to the provider's published policy.
application_steps: Identify eligible Australian higher education providers (the Department of Education publishes the list of higher education providers eligible for research block grants).
Read the chosen university's published RTP scholarship policy, which must detail its application, selection and offer process.
Contact the university's postgraduate research office directly to discuss how to apply and whether RTP is available to international students.
Check the university's internal deadline - the university sets it and the Commonwealth publishes none.
Apply through the university according to its published process (including any English language or IELTS requirement the university sets).
If offered, read the RTP offer letter, which must state the estimated value of each type of support awarded (fees offset, stipend, allowances).
On acceptance, acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution in research publications using the required wording and the RTP DOI, and add the DOI to your ORCID profile if you have one.
applicant_submission_route: Student -> chosen eligible Australian university (postgraduate research office / its RTP scholarship application process). The student applies at the university level; RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education.
official.application_portal: No Commonwealth portal. Each eligible Australian university runs its own application process, which must be detailed in its RTP scholarship policy published on the university's webpage.
arrival_rules: No arrival rule is published. The page states no arrival deadline, no enrolment-timing condition, no visa or travel support and no relocation assistance for RTP scholarship holders.
Overseas students are inside the scope of the scheme, but no airfare, travel or arrival component is published as part of the RTP.
Any arrival or visa conditions come from the provider and Australian student visa law, not from the RTP programme page.
timeline_rules: RTP base and maximum stipend rates are indexed each year, effective from 1 January; the base and maximum rates for the following year are announced by 1 October each year.

Published full-time stipend rates (AUD per year): 2025 - base 33,511, maximum 52,352; 2026 - base 34,315, maximum 53,608; 2027 - base 35,550, maximum 55,537. The announced rates apply to all RTP stipend payments made in the relevant year, not only to new recipients.

Period of support: research doctorate full-time minimum 3 years / maximum 4 years; research doctorate part-time minimum 6 years / maximum 8 years; research masters full-time up to 2 years; research masters part-time up to 4 years.

A student's period of support will not be increased for periods of paid recreation leave or personal leave approved by the provider, but will be increased by the length of any RTP Scholarship Suspension, additional paid personal leave, paid parental leave, paid partner leave, or paid family and domestic violence leave approved by the provider.

Industry internship weighting: the written internship agreement must be made within 18 months of course commencement for a full-time student or within 36 months for a part-time student, extended by any HDR period of suspension in the first 18 months or any increase to the period of support.

From 3 December 2025 the Higher Education Support (Commonwealth Scholarships) Guidelines 2025 apply, replacing the Commonwealth Scholarships Guidelines (Research) 2017. The former rule that a student must not receive income from another source related to the course of study and greater than 75% of the RTP stipend rate was removed with the new Guidelines.
The RTP digital object identifier is doi.org/10.82133/C42F-K220.

official_contacts.general: Department of Education research block grants enquiries. Additional routes published: your university's postgraduate research office or scholarship office; Services Australia for the Child Care Subsidy; the Department of Home Affairs for visa questions.
official_contacts.email: RBGrants@education.gov.au (enquiries about the RTP, per the published Enquiries section of the Research Training Program page)

official_application_route: Direct to the chosen eligible Australian university - contact its postgraduate research office and apply under the process in its published RTP scholarship policy. RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education.
A student may apply to more than one university, or more than once at the same university; the provider decides the process.

Transfers: a student may transfer from one eligible Australian university to another subject to the new university accepting them and agreeing to continuation; there is no transfer of funding between universities and the new university must have sufficient RTP funds available.
degree_levels: Research masters (higher degree by research masters)
official.duration: Research doctorate: a minimum of 3 years and up to a maximum of 4 years at the discretion of the higher education provider for a full-time student load, and a minimum of 6 years up to a maximum of 8 years for a part-time student load. Research masters: up to 2 years full-time and up to 4 years part-time. A student's period of support is not increased for periods of paid recreation leave or personal leave approved by the provider; it is increased by the length of any approved RTP suspension, or any additional approved paid personal leave, paid parental leave, paid partner leave, or paid family and domestic violence leave.
official.application_cycle: Continuous and institution-administered. There is no Department of Education round: RTP scholarships are administered by individual higher education providers, each of which has its own application and selection process, and RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education. Prospective students may apply for an RTP scholarship at more than one provider, so intakes follow each provider's own HDR recruitment cycle.
official.deadline_note: No central deadline exists, by design. The page states that a prospective higher degree by research student 'will need to contact your chosen eligible higher education provider directly', that 'RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education', and that each HEP 'has their own application and selection processes'. Every deadline is the provider's own and varies between providers and between intakes.
official.funding_label: RTP scholarships are offered by providers for one or more of: tuition fees offset; a stipend for general living costs; and allowances related to the ancillary cost of HDRs. Stipend rates are indexed each year, effective 1 January, and the base and maximum rates for the following year are announced by 1 October each year. Published full-time rates: 2027 base $35,550 and maximum $55,537; 2026 base $34,315 and maximum $53,608; 2025 base $33,511 and maximum $52,352. Because the scheme publishes a base and a maximum rather than a single rate, and because the provider decides which components a given scholarship comprises, no single funding amount applies.
official.funding_period: per year - the base and maximum RTP stipend rates are indexed each year, effective from 1 January, and the following year's rates are announced by 1 October each year
benefits: A choice of published components: a tuition fees offset, a stipend for general living costs, and allowances related to the ancillary cost of HDRs

Flexibility on duration within the published band: 3 to 4 years full-time or 6 to 8 years part-time for a research doctorate, and up to 2 years full-time or 4 years part-time for a research masters, at the provider's discretion
Extensions to the period of support for approved paid parental, partner, personal, family and domestic violence leave, and for approved scholarship suspension

Recognition through a dedicated persistent identifier: the RTP has its own DOI (doi.org/10.82133/C42F-K220), which must be used to acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution and added to an existing ORCID profile
For research doctorate students, an eligible industry internship can attract an additional weighting of 2.0 in the provider's RTP funding allocation
eligibility: Enrolled in, or applying to, a research doctorate or a research masters degree (a higher degree by research) at an eligible Australian higher education provider
Either a domestic student or an overseas student - the scheme supports the training of both
Study at an HEP eligible for research block grants, which the Department publishes as a list
Meet the eligibility and selection criteria of the specific HEP offering the scholarship, including its academic and English-language requirements

For the industry internship weighting only: complete an eligible industry internship of at least 3 months and 60 full-time-equivalent days, agreed in writing between the student, the HEP and the research end-user within 18 months of course commencement (full-time) or 36 months (part-time)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to both domestic and overseas students. The page publishes no nationality list, no country-of-origin restriction, no passport or residency condition and no quota; it funds eligible HEPs 'to support their training of domestic and overseas students undertaking research doctorate and research masters degrees'. Any citizenship-based selection is the HEP's own policy, not a scheme rule.
official.international_eligibility: Overseas students are explicitly inside the scheme's scope: the three published objectives include 'provide flexible funding to support training domestic students and overseas students undertaking HDRs at Australian HEPs'. The page publishes no nationality, passport, English-language, age, field-of-study or prior-degree restriction. Eligibility and selection are entirely the provider's, and the provider decides whether a fees offset, a stipend and ancillary allowances are offered.
requirements: Contact the chosen eligible higher education provider directly; RTP scholarship applications cannot be made through the Department of Education
Apply through that provider's own application process and meet its selection criteria and deadline
Be undertaking, or intending to undertake, a research doctorate or research masters degree (HDR) at an eligible provider
Study at the student load the scholarship is awarded for, since the published period-of-support bands differ between full-time and part-time loads
From 3 December 2025, acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution in material relating to the HDR project, using the published form of words with the RTP DOI
If you hold an ORCID profile, include the RTP DOI in that profile; there is no requirement to create an ORCID profile if you do not already have one
Agree the period of support with the provider - it is not extended for paid recreation leave or approved personal leave, only for approved suspension and additional approved paid leave

For the industry internship weighting, have the written internship agreement in place between the student, the HEP and the research end-user within 18 months of commencement (full-time) or 36 months (part-time), with an eligible research end-user at the time the agreement is made
selection_criteria: No selection criteria are published by the Department of Education. Each HEP runs its own application and selection process and publishes its own criteria; the Department page contains no ranking, weighting, pass mark or assessment panel.

The published scheme-level constraints that shape any selection are: the degree must be a research doctorate or research masters; the provider must be eligible for research block grants; the period of support must sit inside the published band for the degree and student load; and the scholarship may comprise one or more of the three published components.

Published incentive rule that affects provider behaviour: an additional weighting of 2.0 within the RTP funding allocation formula is applied to each research doctorate student reported from 2022 as completing their course having undertaken an eligible industry internship.

Published allocation rule that affects how generous a provider can be: 2026 RTP grant amounts are allocated on a formula reflecting each provider's relative performance in attracting research income and supporting students to complete HDRs.
application_method: Identify an eligible higher education provider from the Department's published list of HEPs eligible for research block grants
Contact that provider directly - applications cannot be made through the Department of Education
Apply through the provider's own application portal, in the provider's own format, by the provider's own deadline
You may apply to more than one provider, and each runs its own selection process independently
For scheme-level questions read the RTP Frequently Asked Questions for students, in particular FAQs 3, 5 and, where applicable, 28-30
If offered the scholarship, accept the provider's conditions and note the acknowledgement obligation and the ORCID DOI requirement that apply from 3 December 2025
award_holder_conditions: Remain enrolled in the research doctorate or research masters degree at the offering provider, at the student load for which the scholarship was awarded

Keep the period of support inside the published band for the degree and load: 3-4 years full-time or 6-8 years part-time for a research doctorate; up to 2 years full-time or 4 years part-time for a research masters

Note that the period of support is not increased for paid recreation leave or approved personal leave, and is increased only by an approved RTP suspension or additional approved paid personal, parental, partner, family and domestic violence leave

From 3 December 2025, acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution in any material produced through the RTP-supported HDR study, using the published wording with the RTP DOI (doi.org/10.82133/C42F-K220)
If you hold an ORCID profile, add the RTP DOI to it; you are not required to create an ORCID profile if you do not have one

If an industry internship is to count towards the provider's weighting, it must be at least 3 months and 60 full-time-equivalent days, with a written agreement between the student, the provider and the research end-user inside the published 18-month (full-time) or 36-month (part-time) window, and with an eligible research end-user at the time of the agreement
official.program_type: Government research scholarship - Australian Government Research Training Program, funded through annual block grants to eligible higher education providers under section 46-20 of the Higher Education Support Act 2003 and the Higher Education Support (Commonwealth Scholarships) Guidelines 2025, and administered by each provider
official.region: Australia (host country). Open to domestic and overseas students; the Department publishes no eligible-country list
coverage: Tuition fees offset
A stipend for general living costs
Allowances related to the ancillary cost of higher degrees by research
official.description: The Research Training Program is Australian Government funding that flows to eligible universities as block grants, which those universities then use to offer scholarships to students doing a research doctorate or research masters. A scholarship may comprise one or more of three published components - a tuition fees offset, a stipend for general living costs, and allowances for the ancillary costs of a higher degree by research - and it is the university, not the Department, that decides the mix, applies, selects and sets the deadline. Stipend rates are indexed annually and published as a base and a maximum (2027: $35,550 base, $55,537 maximum), so the amount you receive depends on your provider and your stipend level rather than on a national figure. Support runs 3 to 4 years full-time for a research doctorate, or up to 2 years full-time for a research masters, and from 3 December 2025 recipients must acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution using the RTP's own DOI and add it to any ORCID profile they hold.

important_advice_for_students: There is no Commonwealth application and no Commonwealth deadline. Everything - application, selection, deadline, documents, English test - is set by the university, and it must publish that in its RTP scholarship policy. Read the policy before you spend anything on applications.

As an international student you are eligible, but your university may only spend up to 10% of its RTP funding per grant year on international students. Ask the postgraduate research office directly whether any RTP places are available to internationals before you invest in a research proposal.

Check the exact combination you are being offered. A university may give you a fees offset only, stipend only, allowance only, or a combination, and the fee offset amount varies by university and research area. The offer letter must state the estimated value of each component.

Budget on the range, not a number. The stipend must be at least the base full-time rate and no more than the maximum: for 2027 that is AUD 35,550 to AUD 55,537 per year; 2026 was AUD 34,315 to AUD 53,608. Part-time is 50% of whatever the university offers and is taxable, whereas full-time stipends are tax exempt if you meet the ATO criteria.
If you are an international student, ask whether an OSHC allowance is included. It is listed as a valid allowance use, but it is not automatic.

Do not assume a scholarship you must not combine still blocks you. The old rule barring other income related to the course of study above 75% of the stipend was removed on 3 December 2025. But if you already hold a Commonwealth award for HDR tuition fees, that bars an RTP fees offset - so check before you accept a second offer.

Plan your period of support carefully. It is counted from your HDR commencement date, including any time done at a previous university, and it is not reset if you transfer. Support cannot be extended beyond the maximum (4 years FT doctorate, 8 years PT doctorate, 2 years FT masters, 4 years PT masters).
Check whether your provider restricts paid work. The provider must publish the circumstances in which it will not let you work outside your HDR, including any hours cap.
You will have to acknowledge the Commonwealth in publications, and add the RTP DOI to your ORCID profile if you have one.

referee_tracking.role: Referee reports - at the provider's discretion, not a Commonwealth requirement
referee_tracking.instructions: The Commonwealth Guidelines do not name a required number of referees. FAQ 4 and FAQ 8 both state only that 'in determining its selection process for RTP scholarship, a university may consider previous study, relevant work experience, research publications, referee reports, and other factors'. The number of referees, who may be contacted, and the form of the report are set in the university's RTP scholarship policy and its HDR admission requirements. Check both, and contact referees early - academic referees can be slow.

post_award_requirements: Acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution in research publications using the required wording: 'This research was supported by the Commonwealth through an Australian Government Research Training Program Scholarship [DOI: https://doi.org/10.82133/C42F-K220] .' This applies to recipients of an RTP fees offset, stipend or allowance.
Include the RTP DOI in your ORCID profile if you already have one (the Funding section is described as appropriate). There is no requirement to create an ORCID profile if you do not have one.
Meet the provider's rules on work outside your HDR, which the provider must publish in its RTP scholarship policy.
Follow the provider's published suspension process; the provider must publish how suspensions operate.

Accept the provider's conditions on paid recreation leave, personal leave, additional personal leave, parental leave, partner leave and family and domestic violence leave, and note which of these extend the period of support.
Maintain enrolment and progress in the HDR; the provider administers the scholarship.
questions_to_ask_host: Do you offer RTP to international students this year, and how many places are left under your 10% cap?
Which combination will I receive - fees offset, stipend, allowances - and what is the estimated value of each, as stated in my offer letter?
What stipend rate will I be paid, and is it the base rate or above? Will the rate be re-indexed each 1 January?
Will the award be full-time or part-time, and does a part-time load halve the stipend?
Is an OSHC allowance included for me and my dependants, and is a relocation allowance available?
What is your internal closing date, and what documents, formats and referee reports do you require?
What English language or IELTS requirement applies to international applicants in your RTP process?
What restrictions do you place on paid work, and do I need approval before taking any work?
What is your policy on suspending the scholarship, and on transferring to another university without resetting my period of support?
How does the RTP industry internship weighting work for my research doctorate, and what is the deadline for the written internship agreement?
common_rejection_risks: Missing the university's internal deadline - the Commonwealth publishes none, so all timing risk sits with the provider.
Applying for a coursework degree (bachelor or masters coursework) instead of a research degree.
Applying for an HDR at an overseas university rather than an eligible Australian provider.
The provider having no international-student RTP places available under its 10% cap.
Holding another Commonwealth award or scholarship for HDR tuition fees, which bars an RTP fees offset.

Missing the provider's additional selection criteria - first class honours is not required by the Guidelines, but marks, discipline, first-time-research status and on-campus study are all things providers publish as priorities.
Failing the provider's English language or IELTS requirement.
Assuming the maximum stipend rate. The provider sets a rate within the base-to-maximum band.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any part of the HDR tuition fee not covered by the fees offset - the offset must fully cover applicable HDR fees, but the student must check the estimated value in the offer letter because it varies by university and research area.
Living costs above the stipend actually offered. The stipend is a band, not a fixed amount.

Everything not covered by an allowance: the published allowance examples are relocation, thesis printing, academic publication and OSHC. Books, equipment, conference travel and living-cost shortfalls are not named as covered.
Living costs for dependants beyond any OSHC allowance.
For part-time students, the difference between 100% and 50% of the full-time rate, and the tax payable on the part-time stipend.
Unpaid research-related costs if the provider offers fees offset only with no stipend and no allowances.
document_audit: The Commonwealth publishes no RTP document list for students. Required documents are those of the university's RTP scholarship application process and its HDR admission requirements, published in the university's RTP scholarship policy.
No file size limits, accepted file types, translation rules, date-of-issue rules or signature rules are published centrally. document_format_rules is therefore deliberately empty.

What is certain from the published sources: referee reports may be required (the provider's discretion); the offer letter must state the estimated value of each type of support; if an industry internship weighting is being claimed, the written agreement between student, provider and research end-user must be in place within the published 18-month (full-time) or 36-month (part-time) window.

For international students, the Australian visa application's funding section is a separate Department of Home Affairs matter; both the Department of Home Affairs and the university's postgraduate research office may assist.

alerts.message: New base and maximum RTP stipend rates for the following year are announced (effective 1 January). The new rates apply to all RTP stipend payments made in that year, not only to new recipients.
Open the chosen university's RTP scholarship policy. The Commonwealth application, selection criteria, deadline, documents and English requirement are all in that document.
Check the offer letter lists the estimated value of each support type, and check you are not in receipt of another Commonwealth award for HDR tuition fees.
Track your period of support from the HDR commencement date. It is not reset by a transfer and cannot be extended beyond the maximum.
Include the required acknowledgement sentence and the RTP DOI 10.82133/C42F-K220, and add it to your ORCID profile if you have one.

application_readiness_checklist: Pick your provider from the Department's published list of higher education providers eligible for research block grants - an ineligible provider cannot offer an RTP scholarship.
Go to that provider, not to the Department of Education. There is no Department application route and no national deadline; applications are the provider's own.
Confirm your proposed degree is a research doctorate or research masters, not a coursework degree.
Ask the provider exactly which components it will include - fees offset, stipend, ancillary allowances - because the scheme is 'one or more of' and providers differ.
Ask for the stipend rate you would get and whether it is the base rate or the maximum rate for your award.
Check the period of support against your intended load: 3-4 years full-time for a research doctorate (6-8 part-time), up to 2 years full-time for a research masters (up to 4 part-time).

Budget for the fact that leave does not extend your funding: paid recreation leave and approved personal leave do not add to the period of support, and only approved suspension and additional approved paid parental, partner, personal, family and domestic violence leave do.
You may apply to multiple providers, but each runs its own independent selection - there is no advantage in holding offers from two providers and no national ranking.
If you already have an ORCID profile, be ready to add the RTP DOI (doi.org/10.82133/C42F-K220) to it; you are not required to create one.
Plan to acknowledge the Commonwealth's contribution in any output from the project, using the published wording with the RTP DOI.

If you might do an industry internship, note the published eligibility: at least 3 months and 60 full-time-equivalent days, written agreement within 18 months of commencement full-time or 36 months part-time.
submission_workflow: 1. Read the RTP FAQs for students on the Department page first, especially FAQs 3, 5 and 28-30, so you are not surprised by scheme-level rules.
2. Choose an eligible provider from the Department's published list of HEPs eligible for research block grants.
3. Contact that provider's HDR or scholarships office directly about RTP scholarship applications - this is the only application route that exists.
4. Obtain that provider's application form, document list, format rules, deadline and selection criteria; none of these come from the Department.
5. Submit the application to the provider by its deadline, and repeat for any other provider you choose to approach.
6. If shortlisted, expect the provider's own assessment process and offer; check the component mix, stipend rate, student load and period of support in writing before accepting.
7. After accepting, meet the acknowledgement obligation: use the published wording with the RTP DOI in outputs, and add the DOI to your ORCID profile if you have one.

verification.cycle_verified: Research Training Program scheme page as published on education.gov.au, page last modified 22 July 2026, read from the Wayback Machine capture of 17 September 2026 because the live education.gov.au host did not respond to any fetch attempt on 2026-10-01. The page carries no application round: RTP is continuously administered by providers, so there is no cycle to confirm.
official_fields_confirmed: RTP objectives: flexible funding for domestic and overseas students undertaking HDRs; graduates with skills for academia and other sectors; collaboration between HEPs and industry and other research end-users
The three published scholarship components: tuition fees offset, stipend for general living costs, allowances related to the ancillary cost of HDRs - offered as 'one or more of'
Periods of support by degree and student load: research doctorate 3-4 years full-time, 6-8 years part-time; research masters up to 2 years full-time, up to 4 years part-time

purpose: Established in 2023, the Scholarship was generously donated by the Estate of Annie Farrand in memory of Annie Farrand and her mother Annie Elizabeth Farrand.
The Scholarship is awarded to exceptional international students from diverse priority markets studying the Bachelor of Agricultural Science degree or degrees at the University of Sydney.

The published selection basis is academic merit as assessed from the applicant's application for admission, awarded on the nomination of the Dean of the Faculty of Science or their nominated delegate.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or development-goal requirement is published. The only targeting language is 'exceptional international students from diverse priority markets', which is a market-diversity objective rather than a development-goal criterion, and no priority market is named on the page.

official.degree_award: A full undergraduate degree award, not a short-term award. The Scholarship is attached to the Bachelor of Agricultural Science degree or the Honours degree and is tenable for up to 3 years at a full-time load.

official.tuition_rule: No tuition waiver. The Scholarship is a cash award of $20,000 per annum, the terms add that 'No other amount is payable', and nothing in the terms describes a fee offset or a credit against tuition. official.description: The Farrand Scholarship in Agricultural Science is an endowed University of Sydney award created in 2023 from the Estate of Annie Farrand that pays $20,000 per annum for up to three years of full-time study in the Bachelor of Agricultural Science or Bachelor of Agricultural Science (Honours). It is a cash award, not a fee offset: the terms state that no other amount is payable, and it does not cover tuition, living costs or travel. There is no application at all - every international student holding an unconditional offer for the full-time degree is considered automatically, merit is assessed from the admission application, and the award is made on the nomination of the Dean of the Faculty of Science. The published close date is 01 December 2025, the open date is published as N/A, and the award is expressly subject to the availability of funds.

important_advice_for_students: Do not spend time looking for a form or a scholarship portal. There is no application; the open date is literally published as N/A.
Put your effort into the admission application instead, because that is the only thing assessed for merit.
Check the $8,300 per annum interaction before you accept anything else from the University - it is the most commonly missed trap in these terms.
Treat this as a partial award on top of a fee-paying degree, not as a funded place. Budget tuition and living costs yourself.
Do not assume a third year. The award is up to 3 years at a full-time load and the terms publish no renewal.
Confirm with the Faculty of Science that funds are still available for the year you are applying, because the award is expressly subject to the availability of funds.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply for the Bachelor of Agricultural Science or Bachelor of Agricultural Science (Honours) in the Faculty of Science and get to an unconditional offer - that offer is the only thing that triggers consideration.
Confirm you are an international student at the time you apply. If you become a domestic student before the semester census date, the award is terminated.
Plan for a full-time load only. There is no part-time version of this award.
Do not look for a Scholarship form, portal or email address. There is none; the published open date is N/A.

Check every other scholarship you hold or are offered. Accepting a University of Sydney scholarship valued at $8,300 per annum or more for the same purpose - including the Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarships Scheme - terminates this one.
Understand the merit test is your admission application, so admission-test scores and any selection for the degree carry more weight than a separate statement would.
Plan your enrolment fees: the award pays you cash after each census date and does not pay tuition, so you must have funds for fees and living costs from other sources.
Target a semester average mark of at least 65 in every semester and keep every fee paid - both are conditions of the award, not advice.
If you plan an exchange during the award, make sure you can achieve a Satisfied Requirements grade for that period, or your next payment is at risk.
Check whether the Faculty of Science is still advertising the award and whether funds remain, because the terms state the Scholarship is offered subject to the availability of funds.
common_rejection_risks: Not holding an unconditional offer by the published close date of 01 December 2025 - the open date is N/A, so the unconditional offer is the only trigger and there is no late route.
Being a domestic student, or becoming one before the semester census date.
Enrolling part-time. The award is full-time load only.
Enrolling in a degree other than the Bachelor of Agricultural Science or Bachelor of Agricultural Science (Honours) in the Faculty of Science.

Low academic merit in the admission application - this is the only published selection criterion and it is assessed from your admission material, so a weak admission result is fatal and cannot be argued around.
Accepting a competing University of Sydney scholarship worth $8,300 per annum or more for the same purpose, including VCIS, which terminates the award.
Falling below a semester average mark of 65, or letting fees go outstanding.
Providing false or misleading information in the Scholarship application - this is a termination ground and the University reserves the right to require repayment of funds already paid.
Failing to resume study after approved leave.
Assuming the award renews beyond three years or survives a change of faculty - neither is possible under the published terms.
estimated_uncovered_costs: All tuition fees - this is a cash award and no fee offset is described in the terms.
Living costs, rent, food, transport and course materials - no component of any kind is published, and $20,000 per annum is the entire award.
Visa, airfare to and from Australia, and any relocation or settling-in cost - no travel or visa component is published.
Health cover beyond what the University requires of all students.
Anything the University of Sydney requires for enrolment that is not the Scholarship itself, since the terms state that no other amount is payable.
Lost income if deferral is refused, since deferral is not permitted without the Dean's prior permission.

No file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published for this Scholarship. Documentation rules come from the University of Sydney admission process, not from these terms.

submission_workflow: 1. Apply for admission to the Bachelor of Agricultural Science or Bachelor of Agricultural Science (Honours) in the Faculty of Science at the University of Sydney.
2. Progress the admission to an unconditional offer by the published close date of 01 December 2025.
3. Confirm your status is international student at the time of application.
4. Do nothing else. There is no Scholarship application to submit; the published position is that all eligible students with an unconditional offer are automatically considered.
5. Your admission application is assessed for academic merit.
6. If selected, the award is made on the nomination of the Dean of the Faculty of Science or their nominated delegate, subject to the availability of funds.
7. On enrolment, maintain a semester average mark of at least 65 and keep all fees paid; the instalment is paid after each semester census date.

purpose: The Humphrey Fellowship Program is funded by the U.S. Department of State and administered by the Institute of International Education (published footer statement).

The programme's published framing is a leadership development model: Humphrey Fellows who meet the eligibility requirements apply through their Binational Fulbright Commissions or the Public Affairs Section of the U.S. Embassy in their home countries, and the programme's own alumni structure is organised into six regions - East Asia and Pacific, Middle East and North Africa, South and Central Asia, Europe and Eurasia, Sub-Saharan Africa, and the Western Hemisphere (published site structure).
A distinctive published component is the Global Policy Dialogues, presented as a key component of the programme, and an annual Global Leadership Forum at which Humphrey Fellows meet (published).
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or development-goal requirement is published. The programme publishes four Impact Areas - Human & Institutional Capacity, Rights & Freedoms, Sustainable Lands and Thriving Communities - each with a list of Fields of Study. These are subject areas rather than development goals, and no SDG or cross-cutting development objective is stated.
study_type: Non-degree, self-defined programme of independent non-degree study at a leading U.S. university (ten months)

official.degree_award: No degree. The published structure is Academic Enrichment - course work at the host university 'without the expectation of meeting specific degree or diploma requirements' - plus a Professional Affiliation placement. Fellows do not receive a degree or diploma from the host university.

official.funding_period: Ten-month Fellowship programme. official.travel_coverage: Published as a component. Round-trip international travel to and from the United States is funded as part of the fellowship, together with health insurance. No airfare class, allowance ceiling or family-travel rule is published on the page read.

The fellowship is funded by the U.S. Department of State and administered by the Institute of International Education, and the host relationship is with a university in the programme's published network of host universities. Transcript authenticity: transcripts must be official, valid documents, and must list the courses taken and the grades received. A document that omits courses or grades does not satisfy the published rule.
Conditional documentation: diplomas need only be uploaded if the transcript does not show proof of the degree, so the documentation set depends on what the transcript evidences.

official.selection_notes: Selection runs in three published stages. Second, independent review committees in the United States review those nominations. Third, the J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board determines final candidate approval. The published merit signals available to an applicant are the six eligibility requirements, the essay prompt, the employer letter, and the transcript. The programme publishes no weighting, no pass mark, no interview format and no appeals route, and it does not publish the number of Fellows or the number nominated by country. The decision is communicated back through the national post.

Await status notification from your Embassy or Binational Commission after Board approval.

official_contacts.general: The Humphrey Fellowship Program is funded by the U.S. Department of State and administered by the Institute of International Education. Applicants apply through their country's Binational Fulbright Commission or the Public Affairs Section of the U.S. Embassy, and the programme directs applicants to contact that body for application information and deadlines. The programme publishes dedicated pages for U.S. Embassies & Commissions, a country eligibility list with a 'Check Eligibility' tool, and a Frequently Asked Questions section. Regional alumni and programme structure is published across six regions: East Asia and Pacific, Middle East and North Africa, South and Central Asia, Europe and Eurasia, Sub-Saharan Africa, and the Western Hemisphere.

official.description: The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program is a U.S. Department of State programme, administered by the Institute of International Education, that takes mid-career professionals from eligible countries to the United States for ten months. It is a non-degree leadership and public-service award: Fellows undertake academic enrichment at a leading U.S. host university without any expectation of meeting degree or diploma requirements, plus a six-week Professional Affiliation placement with a host organisation, and the published funding components are round-trip international travel, health insurance and a living allowance. Eligibility is strict and country-based - citizenship of an eligible country, an undergraduate degree, at least five years of full-time professional experience, demonstrated leadership and a record of public service, limited experience in the United States, and English ability - and applicants cannot apply directly: they apply through their country's Binational Fulbright Commission or the U.S. Embassy's Public Affairs Section on a country-specific deadline. Nominations are then reviewed by independent committees in the United States and final approval is made by the J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board, with status communicated back through the national post.
official.duration: Ten months, the published Fellowship Period, comprising the academic enrichment component at a host university and the six-week Professional Affiliation placement. The programme starts in the United States between August and September in the year following the March selection announcement. The fellowship is a single ten-month period with no published extension or renewal mechanism.
official.funding: Fully Funded - funded by the U.S. Department of State and administered by the Institute of International Education. Note: the programme website publishes NO award figures or component breakdown; amounts are set per country mission.

important_advice_for_students: This is a leadership and public-service award, not an academic scholarship. The published criteria are five years of professional experience, leadership, public service and limited U.S. exposure. A strong transcript will not compensate for thin professional or civic record.
'Limited experience in the United States' is the requirement most applicants misread as a strength. Substantial prior U.S. study or work disqualifies you.

You cannot apply directly. The route is your Binational Fulbright Commission or the U.S. Embassy, which run their own country process on their own deadline. Treat the national post as your employer in this process and keep them engaged.
The transcript rule is precise: official, valid, in English, and listing courses and grades. A certificate or a transcript without grades does not comply.
The essay has a published bar rather than a scoring scale - it must thoroughly address the prompt. Thin essays are the most likely avoidable rejection at the national stage.
One of your two referees must be your current employer. Do not assume two academic referees will do.
Budget around a ten-month non-degree year with a Professional Affiliation placement, and expect to be in the United States from late August or September.

There is no published appeals route. The national selection, the U.S. review committees and the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board are sequential and final, so the only leverage you have is the quality of the national application.

referee_tracking.instructions: The published rule is that two letters of recommendation are required in English and that one must be from the applicant's current employer. This is a hard content requirement, not a suggestion. Request it with enough lead time for a referee writing in English, and give the employer a specific account of your public service and leadership, since those are the published merit signals the letter is being read against.

referee_tracking.role: Second referee - one further letter of recommendation, in English
referee_tracking.instructions: The published rule requires two letters in total, one of which must be the current employer, so the second may be academic, professional, civic or from a previous employer, provided it is in English. Choose the referee whose view of your leadership qualities and record of public service is strongest, since those are the published selection signals, and brief them on the programme's criteria.

post_award_requirements: Take up the place in the United States for the ten-month Fellowship Period, starting between August and September in the year of selection.

Participate in both published components: academic enrichment at the host university, taken without the expectation of meeting degree or diploma requirements, and the six-week Professional Affiliation placement with a host organisation.
Note that the fellowship is non-degree: no degree or diploma is conferred, so any academic credit is subject to the host's own policy and is not guaranteed by the programme.
Observe the terms of your national post's nomination, since that is the route through which the fellowship was awarded.
Participate in the programme's community components, including the Global Policy Dialogues and the annual Global Leadership Forum, which the programme publishes as key components.
Maintain eligibility conditions that the programme publishes for Fellows, and meet any conditions your national post or the Institute of International Education sets at award stage.
questions_to_ask_host: Is my country on the eligible list for this cycle, and does my Binational Fulbright Commission or Embassy have a country-specific quota?

What does my post weigh most - the essay, the professional experience and public service record, or the academic transcript?
Is there a second-round interview or assessment at national level, and who conducts it?
How many candidates does my country nominate, and how does that change if my post is selective?
What is the Professional Affiliation placement process, and can the host organisation influence the placement?
What is the fellowship's commencement and completion timetable, and how does the Professional Affiliation placement fit inside the ten months?
What does the fellowship cover exactly for my host - health insurance, travel, books, and any costs the programme does not name?
common_rejection_risks: Not a citizen of an eligible country.
No undergraduate degree.
Fewer than five years of full-time professional experience, or part-time experience only.
More than three years of prior US residence or activity without the required four years back home at professional level.
Incomplete answers to questions, or essay responses in English that do not thoroughly address the prompt.
Only one letter of recommendation, or missing the letter from the current employer, or letters not in English.
Non-official, invalid, or incomplete transcripts, or transcripts not in English, or missing diploma where the transcript does not show proof of the degree.
Missing the post's internal deadline so the post cannot nominate you before its mid-September submission to Washington.
Expecting a degree or expecting to choose the host university - the programme is explicitly non-degree with assigned placement.

Anything you commit to at home that conflicts with a rigorous ten-month schedule with considerable time away from the host campus.

application_readiness_checklist: Check your country first. Citizenship of an eligible country is the first published requirement, eligibility is country-by-country, and the programme publishes a country eligibility list and a 'Check Eligibility' tool. Everything else is wasted effort if you are not on that list.

Confirm the six published requirements: eligible-country citizenship, an undergraduate degree, at least five years of full-time professional experience, demonstrated leadership and a record of public service, limited experience in the United States, and demonstrated English language ability.
Count your professional experience properly - five years of full-time is the floor, and the public-service and leadership evidence is assessed alongside it.
Think carefully about your U.S. exposure. The published requirement is limited experience in the United States, and long prior U.S. study or work is a disqualifier, not a strength.

Contact your Binational Fulbright Commission or the U.S. Embassy's Public Affairs Section immediately. There is no central deadline and no direct application; the post sets the internal deadline and it varies by country.
Arrange two English letters of recommendation early, and make sure one is from your current employer. That is a published hard requirement, not a preference.
Order official English transcripts that list courses taken and grades received. If the transcript does not show the degree, you must also upload the diploma.
Write the essay in English and address the prompt thoroughly. The published requirement is that essay responses 'thoroughly address the prompt', alongside complete answers to all questions.

Check the four Impact Areas and their Fields of Study before you invest in the essay, because your national post will be assessing fit against the programme's structure: Human & Institutional Capacity; Rights & Freedoms; Sustainable Lands; Thriving Communities.
Plan for ten months, not a degree. There is no degree or diploma at the end, so if you need a credential this is the wrong programme.
Do not wait on the central programme office for news. The status is communicated to you by your Embassy or Commission after the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board approves.
submission_workflow: 1. Use the published country eligibility list and the 'Check Eligibility' tool to confirm you are a citizen of an eligible country.

2. Verify the six published eligibility requirements: undergraduate degree, at least five years of full-time professional experience, leadership and public service, limited U.S. experience, and English language ability.

3. Identify your Field of Study within one of the four Impact Areas - Human & Institutional Capacity, Rights & Freedoms, Sustainable Lands, Thriving Communities - and note the specific field, because your national post will be working to that structure.
4. Contact your Binational Fulbright Commission or the Public Affairs Section of the U.S. Embassy for the application pack and the internal deadline, which varies by country.
5. Order official English transcripts that list courses taken and grades received, and add a diploma only if the transcript does not show the degree.
6. Request two English letters of recommendation, ensuring one is from your current employer.
7. Draft the essay in English so that it thoroughly addresses the prompt, and complete every question in the application.
8. Submit to the national post by that country's deadline. There is no central deadline and no direct submission to the programme.
9. If nominated, the file goes to independent review committees in the United States, and final approval is made by the J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board.
10. Wait for status from your Embassy or Commission, which will inform you after the Board's approval.

official.description: The Wien International Scholarship Program (WISP), established at Brandeis University in 1958, is described by Brandeis as "a first-of-its-kind program bringing undergraduate students from every corner of the globe to campus and engaging the entire community to be active global citizens." Since its inception it has brought over 894 scholars from 115 countries to Brandeis. Brandeis identifies Wien Scholars "not only by their academic achievement, but for their contributions inside and outside of the classroom prior to, during, and after their years at Brandeis." The official programme page does not publish any award amount, funding components, application route, deadline, document list or selection procedure; those details are not stated on any Brandeis page that could be read.

official.description: The Global Excellence Scholarship is a competitive, merit-based award of USD 10,000 per year as a non-resident tuition waiver for international freshmen and transfer students on an F-1 visa at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities. It runs for four years for entering freshmen and three years for transfers, and there is no separate application: every international applicant who applies for admission by the deadline is automatically assessed. Renewal requires 30 credits by the end of year one, 60 by year two and 90 by year three, at least 13 credits per semester, consecutive enrolment, satisfactory progress and continued F-1 status.
official.coverage: Covers USD 10,000 per year of non-resident tuition for the duration of the award; the University explicitly states it offers no full tuition waiver and expects international students to fund the remainder of their education, and the award cannot be used for study abroad.

official.tuition_coverage: Partial and conditional. Merit scholarships are awarded on academic merit without regard to need, and no tuition-only waiver mechanism is published. The top award, the Presidential Scholarship, 'covers the full costs of tuition, as well as on-campus housing and meals, for the four years of undergraduate study' - but Clark states that recipients 'are responsible for additional costs totaling approximately $12,000-$15,000 per year'. For other international applicants Clark states explicitly that while it provides merit and need-based aid, 'it may not cover all educational expenses', and that because resources are limited 'we can't offer admission to international students who require full funding.'
official.tuition_rule: There is no tuition-waiver instrument. Aid works in three published channels. (1) Merit: 'Merit scholarship decisions are made solely based on information presented in the admission application without consideration of financial need', and admitted students who receive a merit-based scholarship are notified at the time of admission. (2) Need-based: offered based on family financial circumstances as institutional or government grants that do not need to be repaid, or federal loans; students must reapply annually. (3) External/private: if you receive a private scholarship you must inform the Clark University Office of Financial Assistance in writing, and private scholarships are counted as part of your aid package rather than added on top. A Federal Work-Study award, where the student qualifies, is included in the financial aid offer letter.
official.home_tuition_rule: Not published. Clark publishes nothing about fees at, or continuation of study at, the applicant's previous school.
official.host_institution_fee: The host institution is Clark University and the published fees are its own: Student Activity & Programming Fee USD 460, Orientation Fee USD 400, Health and Wellness Fee USD 680 (2026-2027), plus estimated Books USD 900, Miscellaneous USD 800, Transportation allowance USD 250 and Health Insurance USD 2,833. In Massachusetts State Law terms, Clark requires all matriculated full-time and three-quarter-time students to participate in the Student Health Insurance Plan unless proof of comprehensive comparable coverage under a policy filed and approved in the U.S. is provided. Which of these fees any individual merit or need-based award covers is not published.
official.tax_status: Not published. Clark publishes no tax treatment for merit or need-based awards paid to an F-1 student.

general_eligibility: Be an applicant to Clark University's undergraduate programme (first-year or transfer; both have published deadlines and aid deadlines).
Have demonstrated exceptional academic performance and personal qualities during secondary school years - this is the published basis of merit consideration.

For a need-based award, file the CSS Profile with the application by the admissions deadline.

If an international student, complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form. It can only be completed after the applicant has applied, on their applicant status portal, and it serves as the certification of financial resources for students not requesting aid and as the application for Clark-funded assistance for students who are.

If English is not the applicant's native language, provide an official TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Pearson PTE score report. Clark states it has no specific minimum scores but publishes general indicators of the minimum English proficiency for studying at Clark, and notes that meeting these indicators does not guarantee admission.

US citizens and US permanent residents are not treated as international students for this route - they use the FAFSA instead (Clark's FAFSA code 002139).

document_format_rules: No file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published on the pages read.

Format rules are therefore those of the underlying platforms and of Clark's own admissions systems: the Common Application, the Coalition Application with Scoir, the Transfer Common App and the Clark Transfer App each impose their own requirements, and the Clark University International Student Aid Application, the transcripts, the recommendations and the aid forms are governed by the University.

The only published format constraint on evidence is the word 'official' applied to the English proficiency report: an official TOEFL, Duolingo or IELTS score report is required where English is not the applicant's native language.
official.selection_notes: There is no separate scholarship competition with a published rubric. Scholarship and admission decisions are bundled by round, which makes round choice the main lever an applicant controls: Early Decision is binding but publishes a materially better scholarship position, while Early Action and Regular Decision are non-binding and therefore risk-free. For international applicants, English proficiency is assessed holistically rather than by a single published minimum, and an interview is treated as especially important for non-native English speakers - so the interview is a realistic differentiator despite being optional. With roughly 5% of the student body international, no country or nationality weighting is published.
application_steps: Choose a round: Early Decision I (application Nov 1, notification late December), Early Action (Nov 1, mid-January), Early Decision II (Jan 15, early March) or Regular Decision (Jan 15, late March) - as an international applicant you follow the same deadlines as all other applicants. Transfer applications are rolling.
Submit the Common Application, or the Coalition Application with Scoir. There is no application fee.

Upload transcripts covering the last three years of education (via the application portal, preferably, or by email to intadmissions@clarku.edu), with certified English translations if the originals are not in English.
Arrange two letters of recommendation - one school counselor and one teacher (or two academic teachers where there is no counselor).
Submit an official English proficiency score report (TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Pearson PTE) if English is not your native language.

File the CSS Profile with your application by the admissions deadline if you want to be considered for a need-based award. Apply for financial aid early - Clark states the FAFSA and any other required financial aid materials are due by the same deadlines as the admission application.
After submitting your application, watch for the applicant status portal access (a few days after submission) where the online checklist shows whether scores and materials have been received.
Complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form on the applicant status portal (all international students must).

Optionally schedule an interview - in person, virtual, via InitialView or Vericant, or by emailing intadmissions@clarku.edu to request a virtual slot. For international students the interview can also serve as a supplementary measurement of English proficiency.
If admitted and seeking aid, report any private or external scholarship to the Office of Financial Assistance in writing.

Clark's own portal is the Undergraduate Admissions 'Connect with Clark' and 'Request information' route plus the Office of Financial Assistance route, not a scholarship application system.

timeline_rules: Admissions rounds (international applicants follow the same deadlines as all other applicants): Early Decision I - application November 1, notification late December; Early Action - November 1, notification mid-January; Early Decision II - January 15, notification early March; Regular Decision - January 15, notification late March.

Clark states it is a good idea to apply for financial aid right after applying for admission so that the admission decision and financial aid offer can be provided at the same time.

Early Decision I and II are binding: if admitted you must enrol at Clark and withdraw your applications to other schools.
The International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form becomes available only after the applicant has submitted an admissions application.

Cost of attendance figures published are for 2026-2027. Clark states figures such as the average aid package without a year, and the two official pages give different averages (USD 50,755 and USD 49,545).

official.description: This record covers Clark University's institutional undergraduate scholarship portfolio rather than a single named award. The headline award is the Presidential Scholarship, which covers the full cost of tuition plus on-campus housing and meals for the four years of undergraduate study, with recipients still responsible for additional costs of roughly $12,000 to $15,000 per year; a second named award, the Davis United World College Scholars Program, is a need-based grant of up to $15,000 per year. There is no separate scholarship application: scholarships are decided inside the admissions process, bundled with the admission decision and made more generous in the binding Early Decision rounds, which publish decisions before Thanksgiving alongside more scholarship funding and a higher admission rate. Underneath the named awards sit institutional need-based aid that Clark reports as reaching 99% of first-year students with 98% of aid in the form of non-repayable grants, while international students are reported as typically paying around $40,000 per year after aid against a total cost of attendance of approximately $85,000.

Transfer fall semester start: rolling 1 February to 1 June, notification rolling within 4 weeks. Transfer spring semester start: rolling 1 September to 1 November, notification rolling within 4 weeks. Spring admission is also published for first-year and transfer students, with over 50 such students admitted each year.

common_rejection_risks: Applying as an international student who needs full funding - Clark states it cannot offer admission in that case. This is a hard institutional limit, not a competitiveness judgement.
Indicating a financial need greater than Clark can offer. The admissions process is need-aware and the application may be denied on that basis.
Missing the CSS Profile deadline - the CSS Profile must be filed by the admissions deadline, so a late filing forfeits need-based consideration entirely.

Forgetting the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form, which all international students must complete and which only becomes available after applying.
Submitting only two years of educational data. Clark cannot review an application with only two years of credentials, and 6-3-3 systems need an extra middle school year.
Sending the Duolingo English Test score as a screenshot or scan - it must come directly from the Duolingo portal.
Non-English documents with no certified translation.
Missing an optional-looking deadline that is not optional, such as senior-year records that do not yet exist in your system.
Assuming a Presidential Scholarship means the whole cost - even that award leaves approximately USD 12,000-15,000 per year payable by the recipient.
Assuming a private scholarship will be added on top of Clark's package - it must be declared and is counted within it, and an undeclared external award can change your package.
Early Decision applicants who are admitted but then enrol elsewhere, breaching a binding agreement.

Estimated books (USD 900), miscellaneous expenses (USD 800) and a transportation allowance (USD 250).
Health Insurance (USD 2,833 in the 2026-2027 published cost) unless you can evidence comprehensive comparable coverage under a policy filed and approved in the U.S.
Anything beyond Clark's published aid capacity, which is why an applicant who needs full funding cannot be admitted at all.

alerts.message: Decide whether your family's resources can cover roughly USD 40,000 per year after aid. If you need full funding, Clark will not admit you. This is the single most important filter in the whole application.
