Get the FAFSA done - it is on the published application checklist and it is what establishes need.

If you are an international aid applicant, complete the separate Clark University International Student Aid Application as well. This is a published, distinct requirement and it is the step international applicants most often miss.
If English is not your native language, book the official TOEFL, Duolingo or IELTS test early enough to have the report in hand - an official score report is required.

Book the interview. It is officially optional, but Clark states it is especially important for applicants who do not speak English as a native language, and it is the most credible differentiator available to you.
Line up one teacher recommendation and a counselor recommendation - both are on the published checklist.

Model the real cost, not the headline. Even the Presidential Scholarship leaves you responsible for approximately $12,000-$15,000 per year, and international students are published as typically paying around $40,000 per year after aid against roughly $85,000 total cost of attendance.
Compare the two official Clark pages that publish the average aid package before you rely on either number - they disagree, and neither states a year or population.
Be clear on what you are applying for: this is an institutional portfolio, not one scholarship, so ask which named award you would be considered for and what its individual conditions are.
If you are a transfer applicant, note the rolling windows (1 February - 1 June for fall start, 1 September - 1 November for spring start) and the roughly 4-week rolling notification.
important_advice_for_students: There is no scholarship application. Every dollar of merit aid is decided inside the admissions process, so the strength of your admission file and your round choice are the scholarship strategy.
Early Decision is the only round with a published scholarship benefit. If Clark is genuinely your first choice, the binding commitment is buying you a materially better funding position.
Do not read 'full tuition, housing and meals' as fully funded. Clark itself says the Presidential Scholarship recipient is still responsible for approximately $12,000-$15,000 a year.

International applicants: the International Student Aid Application is a separate published requirement on top of the FAFSA, and English proficiency evidence is mandatory unless English is your native language.

Sit the interview even though it is optional. Clark flags it as especially important for non-native English speakers, and Clark assesses English proficiency holistically rather than by a published minimum.

Be sceptical of single figures. Clark publishes two different average aid-package numbers on two official pages, and international cost figures that do not reconcile with the total cost of attendance. Read the Cost of Attendance page and the Office of Financial Assistance page together.
document_audit: The published application checklist is: Common Application or Coalition Application with Scoir; transcript(s); optional interview; counselor recommendation; one teacher recommendation; FAFSA application. Treat that as the minimum set.
Add the Clark University International Student Aid Application if you are an international applicant seeking aid - it is published as required, and it is not on the general checklist.

Add an official TOEFL, Duolingo or IELTS score report if English is not your native language. 'Official' is the only format word Clark publishes for it, so use an official report rather than a home-printed score sheet.

Transfer applicants must use the Transfer Common App or the Clark Transfer App, not the first-year application, and Clark flags additional transfer requirements on a separate page - get those from the transfer applicant guidance rather than assuming they mirror the first-year list.

No file size, file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published. Format rules come from the Common Application, Coalition Application, Scoir, Transfer Common App and Clark Transfer App platforms, and from Clark's own admissions and financial-aid systems. Ask Financial Aid for the current rules rather than assuming.

referee_tracking.role: High school counselor / school official - published as 'Counselor recommendation' on the application checklist
referee_tracking.instructions: A counselor recommendation is a published checklist item. Ask your counselor early in the application cycle, and check whether the Common Application or the coalition application routes the counselor submission automatically or whether Clark requires a separate form.

referee_tracking.role: One teacher - published as '1 teacher recommendation' on the application checklist
referee_tracking.instructions: Exactly one teacher recommendation is published. Choose a teacher who can speak to sustained academic performance and personal qualities, since Clark says consideration is given to students 'who have demonstrated exceptional academic performance and personal qualities during their secondary school years'. Confirm the deadline with the teacher in weeks, not days, and check the platform's due date.

submission_workflow: 1. Choose your round and note its deadline: 1 November for Early Decision I and Early Action, 15 January for Early Decision II and Regular Decision, or the rolling transfer window for your intended semester.
2. File the FAFSA, and add the Clark University International Student Aid Application if you are an international aid applicant.
3. Request an official TOEFL, Duolingo or IELTS score report if English is not your native language.
4. Ask your counselor for a recommendation and one teacher for a recommendation, and agree dates with both.
5. Submit the Common Application, or the Coalition Application with Scoir. Transfer applicants use the Transfer Common App or the Clark Transfer App.
6. Upload transcript(s) and complete the essay and activities sections.
7. Sit the interview - optional, but strongly encouraged and specifically flagged as important for non-native English speakers.
8. Submit before your round deadline. There is no separate scholarship submission at any point.
9. Review the award letter against the published Cost of Attendance, Merit-Based Aid and Need-Based Aid pages before accepting, and confirm in writing any condition not stated on the pages.
post_award_requirements: Confirm in writing the academic standing required to keep the award. Clark publishes no threshold, so this must come from Financial Aid in writing at award stage.

Confirm the renewal or continuation position. Only the Presidential Scholarship has a published term - four years of undergraduate study - and no renewal or extension condition is published for any award.

Confirm the year-by-year amounts, because the published average aid-package figures differ between two official Clark pages and the top award still leaves roughly $12,000-$15,000 a year to the recipient.
If you received Early Decision, note that you are bound to enrol at Clark and had to withdraw your other applications.

If you are an international student, maintain the immigration status required for your programme and meet any separate terms of the Clark University International Student Aid Application - neither is published on the pages read.
Re-check the total cost of attendance at each renewal point: Clark publishes no tuition-increase protection, so treat the four-year published figures as current-year figures, not guarantees.
questions_to_ask_host: Which named scholarship would I be considered for, and what are that award's individual conditions, amount and renewal terms?
Is the award I am being offered a gift or a loan, and does it have an academic threshold, a conduct condition, or a repayment trigger?
For the Presidential Scholarship, how is the approximately $12,000-$15,000 per year of remaining cost calculated, and what does it cover?
How do Clark's named scholarships stack with need-based aid, and can a merit award be reduced if my need changes in a later year?
What is the current academic standing required to retain my award, and what happens if I fall below it for one semester?
For international students, does the Clark University International Student Aid Application cover the full four years, and what happens to my award if my family's financial situation changes?
Is there any award for international students comparable to the Davis United World College Scholars Program, and what is its cap?
If I am offered Early Decision funding, does the binding commitment change if my aid package changes before enrolment?

official.description: The LSE Excellence Scholarship is an award for exceptional applicants joining a Postgraduate Taught programme at LSE in 2026 in one of thirteen named departments, with a total value of £20,000 and £10,000 per year on two-year programmes. It is decided inside the admissions process: there is no financial support application at all, awardees are identified from the admission application, and awards are made on a rolling basis during the application cycle until all awards are allocated. LSE publishes no component breakdown, so it is not stated whether the £20,000 applies to fees, living costs or travel, and no renewal, deferral, continuation or arrival condition is published.
official.duration: The total value is £20,000. For two-year programmes the value is £10,000 per year, so the same £20,000 total is spread across two years rather than reduced. LSE publishes no programme lengths on this page and no minimum or maximum award duration beyond the one-year and two-year funding patterns.
official.application_cycle: Rolling, inside the main LSE postgraduate application cycle for entry in 2026. There is no separate scholarship round: LSE publishes that 'Awards will be made to candidates on a rolling basis during the application cycle, until all awards are allocated.'
official.deadline_note: No scholarship deadline is published, and none can exist, because there is no scholarship application. LSE publishes only that awards are made on a rolling basis during the application cycle until all awards are allocated. The operative constraints are therefore the LSE postgraduate application deadline for the 2026 entry year (already carried in this record's institutional deadline fields) and the exhaustion of the award pool: once all awards are allocated, the scheme is effectively closed for that cycle even while applications are still open.
official.funding_label: The total value of the scholarship is £20,000. For two-year programmes, the scholarship value is £10,000 per year. LSE publishes no component breakdown at all - there is no statement of how much goes to tuition fees, how much to living costs, and no travel, books or equipment element. The figure is a total award value, not a stipend and not a fee-waiver percentage.
official.funding_period: one-off total award; for two-year programmes it is paid as £10,000 per year across two years, so the total does not change with programme length
official.living_cost_coverage: Not established as living-cost funding. LSE publishes a single total value of £20,000 with no breakdown by fee, living cost, travel or any other component, no rate, no per diem and no cost-of-living standard. It is not described as a living-cost allowance, and the amount is small relative to LSE's fees and London living costs.
benefits: A total award value of £20,000 for an applicant judged exceptional on academic ability and potential

Apply early within the cycle. Awards are made on a rolling basis until all awards are allocated, so the pool of competing applicants grows as the cycle proceeds and the same academic file carries a weaker position at the end.
Target entry in the 2026 cohort if you are following this record; LSE publishes the award for 2026 joiners only and does not state that it will repeat.

important_advice_for_students: This is an admissions award, not a funding application. Everything you do to be admitted is what wins it, and there is no scholarship essay to write.

Check the department list first. It is the cheapest way to find out whether you are eligible at all, and it is easy to assume any LSE master's qualifies.
Do not model this as a fee waiver. LSE publishes a total value with no breakdown, and £20,000 does not cover LSE fees plus London living costs.

official.deadline_note: There is no single central deadline. Merit-based scholarships require no separate application, since all applicants admitted to HEC Paris Master's programmes are automatically considered, and results are emailed within one week of the publication of the admission results. Need-based scholarships have per-round deadlines set to match each admissions round, with Round 1 at 12pm noon on 26 October 2026. The Equal Opportunity Scholarship requires the form to be submitted through the HEC Paris Applicant Space.
official.status_note: The Round 1 need-based deadline of 26 October 2026 at 12pm noon is after today's date of 1 October 2026, so it is upcoming. Merit-based consideration happens automatically on admission, with no separate application.

Individual amounts published include the Equal Opportunity Scholarship at up to 35% of tuition fees, the Excellence Scholarship and the Six Excellences Scholarship at up to 15,000 euros, the Stan Schwab Scholarship at 10,000 euros, the AVENIR Scholarship as a separate Eiffel programme, and the Garzouzi award as 15,000 euros deducted in M1 plus a possible further 15,000 euros in M2.
official.travel_coverage_note: The AVENIR Scholarship, which is the Eiffel scholarship administered by HEC Paris, includes a monthly allowance of EUR 1,200 and covers one international return ticket, plus social security and cultural activities. official.description: Esade's Scholarship Program funds academically excellent students with limited financial resources. MSc and MBA Talent Scholarships (published as Esade Need-based Scholarships) cover 50% to 85% of the programme tuition fee and are assessed on talent and financial need. Esade also runs Excellence Awards, which are talent-only, range from 10% to 50% of MSc tuition, and are limited to one award per candidate. Living costs are handled separately through Lodging, Living, Exchange and SUD grants.
purpose: The Esade community is entirely committed to supporting talent and diversity. Esade believes that having that talent and diversity in their classrooms is fundamental to be able to enrich students' educational experience, providing them with ever greater learning opportunities and favoring progress and social justice at the same time.
To help support and develop the best talent, Esade strives to attract the most outstanding students, regardless of their financial situations, origins, cultural backgrounds and religious beliefs.

Esade's Scholarship Program offers talented students with excellent academic track records from diverse socio-economic backgrounds the opportunity to study at Esade. All Esade scholarships are possible thanks to the generosity of its community, so that academically excellent students with limited financial resources can study at Esade.

Talent Scholarships cover between 60% and 100% of recipients' tuition fees for their entire undergraduate or double-degree programs, all based on the individual candidates' academic results and their financial need.

official.description: The Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship is NTU's premier doctoral scholarship, granted by the University President, for candidates taking a full-time PhD at NTU. It pays the full annual tuition fee plus a monthly stipend (S$5,300 for Singapore Citizens, S$4,800 for Singapore Permanent Residents, S$4,300 for International Students, revised with effect from January 2026) and separate book, IT, thesis and overseas conference allowances. There is no bond attached.
purpose: The Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship (NPGS) is a competitive and prestigious scholarship scheme designed to encourage outstanding graduates or final-year students to take their first step towards a leading research career by studying for a full time PhD at NTU.

application_readiness_checklist: Be on a full-time PhD at NTU. NPGS is not available for Master's programmes.
Have, or be on track for, an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree or equivalent â€” if your degree is unfinished, get written confirmation from your university now, because this is a hard gate.
Line up a supervisor before you submit. It is highly recommended; if you cannot, NTU will appoint one based on your research interests, but you lose control of that match.
Assemble resume, educational certificates and transcripts, test scores and recommendation letters per the Research Programmes Admission Guide 'How to Apply â€“ Supporting Documents' list.
Check every test score's date: scores must be within 5 years or less from the date of your application.
If your prior study was in English and you want a test waiver, request a medium-of-instruction letter from your home university.
Apply in the October/November to December window and tick interest in the 'NTU Scholarship' in the application â€” there is no separate scholarship form.
Plan for the final interview at university level; outcomes land roughly 3 to 6 weeks after it.
Have a Singapore bank account ready and update your details in GSLink by the 15th of the semester commencement month.
important_advice_for_students: There is no bond. NTU states plainly that there is no bond attached to the scholarship, so you are not locked into returning to your home country.
Do not read 'priority will be given for campus accommodation' as free housing. It is a queue preference; you still need to budget for rent, and priority does not guarantee a place.
Budget in Singapore dollars and by citizenship tier. Your stipend is S$5,300 (Citizen), S$4,800 (PR) or S$4,300 (International), and only Citizens get the CPF contribution on top.
Renewal is not automatic in name: it is renewable 'subject to good progress', up to 4 years, and the school also weighs availability of research funding. Keep your progress reports clean.
As an International Student you will be required to do teaching or laboratory supervision under the Graduate Assistantship Programme. Factor that workload into your research time.
NTU reserves the right to vary the stipend at any time and states that coverage and award terms are subject to change â€” do not build a fixed budget on today's figure.
If you are an existing student on a higher stipend rate, NTU says your stipend remains the same; the revised rates apply from January 2026.
The conference allowance is capped and runs on a financial-year basis (April to March), so plan conference travel against the S$5,000 cap and the April-to-March window.
You do not need a separate scholarship application. The single most common administrative mistake is simply forgetting to indicate the 'NTU Scholarship' in the programme application.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a Master's programme â€” NPGS is only for PhD.
Not holding, and not being able to evidence being on track for, an Honours (Highest Distinction) degree or equivalent.
Failing to supply the official university documentation confirming on-track status when the undergraduate degree is incomplete.
Missing the October/November to December application window, or submitting before the period for the academic year is announced.
Submitting an incomplete application â€” consideration happens on submission of a complete application within the period.
Forgetting to indicate interest in the 'NTU Scholarship' in the programme application.
Submitting GRE/GMAT scores older than 5 years from the application date.
Requesting a test waiver without the home university medium-of-instruction letter.
Not attending or not preparing for the final interview at university level.
Failing to update GSLink bank details by the 15th of the semester commencement month, which delays stipend payment.
Applying for the wrong NTU entity â€” NIE runs a separately announced application period.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation and rent â€” the award gives only priority for campus accommodation; it does not pay for housing.
Airfare to Singapore and any relocation cost â€” no travel or relocation allowance is published.
Anything beyond the S$5,000 per financial year Overseas Conference Allowance cap.
Personal, medical and day-to-day living costs above what the monthly stipend and the book, IT and thesis allowances cover.
Costs arising if the award is not renewed: renewal is subject to good progress and to the school's determination and availability of research funding, so plan for an unpaid final period.

application_readiness_checklist: Sit UGC-NET (or the UGC-CSIR joint test) and qualify in the Junior Research Fellowship category â€” this is the only entry route UGC publishes.
Confirm you qualified under the JRF category, not the 'Assistant Professor + Ph.D.' category or the 'Ph.D. only' category; neither carries the fellowship.
Secure an M.Phil. or Ph.D. research place at a University, Institution or College.

Work with your institution's research/admissions office immediately: UGC says the M.Phil/PhD registration is made by the institution, and it must happen within two years of your result or award letter.

Check which contingency you are eligible for â€” Contingency A if you are in Humanities or Social Sciences (including Languages), Contingency B if you are in Science. The rates differ and are not interchangeable.
Budget against Rs. 37,000 per month for the first 2 years, then Rs. 42,000 per month, knowing the tenure ends at 5 years or thesis submission, whichever comes first.
Do not assume tuition is paid: UGC publishes the fellowship and contingency only, with no tuition-fee statement.
important_advice_for_students: There is no separate fellowship application form at UGC. The only thing you apply for is the qualifying test. The fellowship follows from the result plus an institutional registration.

The two-year clock is the real deadline and the institution holds it, not you. UGC says registration for the M.Phil/PhD is made by the University/Institution/College within two years of the declaration of result, issue of the award letter, or joining the fellowship. Chase your institution in writing.

Your qualifying category is worth as much as your score. NTA is explicit that the 'appointment as Assistant Professor and admission to Ph.D.' category does not carry the JRF award, and 'admission to Ph.D. only' does not carry either.
Do not budget the fellowship as covering tuition. UGC's published financial assistance is the monthly fellowship plus a contingency allowance, with no mention of fee payment.

Note the two-tier contingency. Humanities and Social Sciences scholars get Contingency A (Rs. 10,000 pa as JRF, Rs. 20,500 pa as SRF); Science scholars get Contingency B (Rs. 12,000 pa as JRF, Rs. 25,000 pa as SRF). Science scholars receive more.
Plan for the step-up at 2 years: your rate rises from Rs. 37,000 to Rs. 42,000 and your contingency also steps up, so year three onwards is better than years one and two.

If you are a foreign national, resolve your eligibility before anything else. NTA frames UGC-NET as determining 'the eligibility of Indian nationals' for the JRF award, and the UGC scheme page publishes no foreign-national provision. Do not assume you can sit the test and claim the fellowship.
common_rejection_risks: Qualifying under 'appointment as Assistant Professor and admission to Ph.D.' or 'admission to Ph.D. only' rather than the JRF category.
Never sitting, or not passing, NET-JRF or the UGC-CSIR joint test.
The host institution failing to lodge the M.Phil/PhD registration within the two-year stipulated period.
Joining the fellowship without a confirmed M.Phil. or Ph.D. registration.
Expecting the fellowship to pay tuition fees, which UGC does not state it covers.
Applying for the wrong contingency band by misidentifying the discipline as Science versus Humanities/Social Sciences.
Assuming a Research Associateship is a separate UGC scheme that can be applied for directly â€” UGC's Student Corner lists only two fellowships and does not publish an RA scheme page.
Missing the UGC-NET cycle dates, which are set by NTA rather than by the fellowship page.
estimated_uncovered_costs: M.Phil./Ph.D. tuition and programme fees â€” no tuition payment or waiver is published under this scheme.
Living costs beyond the monthly fellowship of Rs. 37,000 (first 2 years) or Rs. 42,000 (thereafter).
Travel, relocation and fieldwork costs â€” no travel allowance is published.
Medical insurance and health cover â€” not published as covered.
Costs after the fellowship ends: tenure is 5 years or thesis submission, whichever is earlier, and no extension is published.
document_audit: UGC publishes no document list for this scheme on the scheme page, so documents is recorded as empty rather than filled from assumption.
UGC publishes no file format, size, translation or signature rules, so document_format_rules is an empty list.

Practical note: the documents that matter procedurally are your UGC-NET result and award letter, because UGC's two-year registration clock is measured from the date of declaration of result, the date of issue of the award letter, or the date of joining the fellowship. Keep certified copies of all three dates.
Get your institution's written confirmation that the M.Phil/PhD registration has been made and the date it was made â€” that is the only evidence that satisfies UGC's two-year condition.

official.description: The TWAS-CSIR Postgraduate Fellowship Programme, run jointly by India's Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and UNESCO-TWAS, funds foreign scholars from developing countries to pursue research toward a PhD in CSIR laboratories and institutes in India. It is restricted to researchers aged 35 or under on 31 December of the application year, nationals of developing countries other than India who hold no residency visa in India or a developed country, holders of an MSc who are employed with a research assignment at home, and who can secure an official acceptance letter from a CSIR host. The fellowship pays a monthly stipend for living costs, food and health insurance plus subsidised accommodation, for up to 4 years full-time or 6 months to 3 years as a sandwich fellowship. The 2026 call closed on 3 June 2026 after an extension from 20 May.
official.program_type: South-South research fellowship (TWAS-CSIR, co-funded programme for PhD research in India)

official.coverage: The fellowship pays a monthly stipend covering living costs, food and health insurance plus subsidised accommodation, but the stipend amount is not published, is not convertible into foreign currency, and accompanying family members are the fellow's financial responsibility, so it is not stated as full funding.

official.description: The Netaji Subhas - ICAR International Fellowship (NS-ICAR IF) funds a three-year Ph.D. in agriculture and allied sciences in identified priority areas, for both Indian candidates studying abroad and overseas candidates studying at Indian Agricultural Universities in the ICAR-AU system. Thirty fellowships are available each year. The award pays a monthly stipend plus a contingent and preparatory lump sum and provides a to-and-fro economy class air ticket, but host institution fees, medical insurance and medical fitness are all paid by the fellow.
purpose: In its continued efforts towards enhancing and sustaining the standards, quality and relevance of higher agricultural education in the country, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has instituted International Fellowships with dual purpose of (i) human resource development in cutting edge technologies, and (ii) demonstrating the strength of Indian agricultural system abroad.

The objective is to develop competent human resource that are trained in the identified best laboratories in the world (for Indian candidates) and similarly expose overseas candidates to the best Indian Agricultural Universities (AUs) in the ICAR-AU system (comprising of State Agricultural Universities, Central Agricultural University Imphal, ICAR-Deemed Universities, Allahabad Agricultural Institute-DU, Central Universities having agricultural faculty) for creating a pool of scientist-envoys for enhanced future co-operation.

The NS-ICAR IFs are available to support Indian/overseas nationals for pursuing doctoral degree in agriculture and allied sciences, in the identified priority areas, to the Indian candidates for study abroad in the identified overseas Universities/Institutions having strong research and teaching capabilities, and to overseas candidates for study in the best Indian AUs in the ICAR-AUs system.
The Netaji Subhas-ICAR International Fellowships are available in frontier areas of Agriculture and allied sciences at the recognized agricultural universities/institutions in India and abroad.
study_type: Doctoral (Ph.D.) research in agriculture and allied sciences
Must be within the Council's identified priority areas of research, which are notified one year in advance
Priority areas span Crop Sciences, Horticulture, Biotechnology and nanotechnology, Animal Sciences, Natural Resource Management, Agricultural Engineering and Fisheries
official.degree_award: Full doctoral degree â€” the fellowship supports a Ph.D. degree programme in agriculture and allied sciences. The fellow is designated an "NS-ICAR International Fellow". It is explicitly not a training or short-duration research award.
official.duration: Three years. "The NS-ICAR IFs are available to Indian candidates as well as overseas candidates for a period of three years." The tenure of fellowship will not be extended in any case, in so far as the Council support is concerned. If the fellow is not able to complete the degree during this period, he/she will use his/her own resources for completing the degree.
official.application_cycle: Annual. "Applications for NS-ICAR IFs will be invited on annual basis through announcements published in Indian national newspapers and the notification on ICAR website 'http://www.icar.org.in'. Indian diplomatic missions in foreign countries will also be informed through e-mails." The Council will identify and announce the priority areas of research and the list of institutions for admission one year in advance. For the year 2026, thirty (30) fellowships for a duration of three years are available, split between Indian and overseas candidates according to the availability of good candidates in the identified priority areas.
official.deadline_central_display: The application should be submitted by September 25, 2026, to ADG (HRD) at adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com, mentioning the "Application for NSIF: Name of Applicant and contact number" in the subject line of the mail. Last date for submission of the application is September 25, 2026.
official.funding_label: Ph.D. Amount payable to the International fellowship candidates: Indian fellows going abroad â€” US$ 2,000/- per month, plus lump-sum payments towards contingent and preparatory expenses of US$ 1,000/- per year. Overseas fellows in India â€” INR 40,000/- per month, plus lump-sum payments towards contingent and preparatory expenses of INR 25,000/- per year. Plus a to-and-fro economy class air ticket provided by the Council.
official.funding_period: Three years of fellowship support, with the first six months released as the first installment and subsequent releases conditional on certified academic progress reports. Two currency tracks are published (US$ for Indian fellows going abroad; INR for overseas fellows in India), so no single amount is recorded.
official.living_cost_coverage: Monthly fellowship of US$ 2,000/- per month for Indian fellows going abroad, or INR 40,000/- per month for overseas fellows in India, plus a lump-sum payment towards contingent and preparatory expenses of US$ 1,000/- per year or INR 25,000/- per year respectively.
official.travel_coverage: To-and-fro, economy class air ticket for international travel, by the shortest route, from the airport nearest the residence/work place of the candidate to the airport nearest the destination University, in respect of both Indian and Overseas candidates (air tickets to be provided by the Council). Overseas fellows are additionally entitled to economy-class travel cost reimbursement from the port of arrival in India to the destination University in India and back.
official.tuition_rule: "All fees chargeable by the host institution where the fellow is enrolled will be paid by the fellow himself out of the fellowship grant or from his/her own resources." The fellowship does not pay host institution fees.
official.host_institution_fee: All fees chargeable by the host institution where the fellow is enrolled must be paid by the fellow out of the fellowship grant or from his/her own resources.

official.selection_notes: Candidates are evaluated on a parameters/weighted scale covering the relevance of the area of study, the proposed research plan, academic records, achievements and past work experience. Selection is then made on the basis of the evaluation score and a subsequent interview by a Selection Committee constituted by the Council and duly empowered to judge the suitability of the candidate with regard to the importance of the area of study and the proposed research plan. The Committee may also decide to conduct a telephonic/teleconferencing interview, and the overseas candidates may even be interviewed by experts as identified by the Council who may be based in their home country. The two referees may be directly contacted by the Council for comments in the prescribed format on the candidature. At the time of interview the applicants must furnish a letter of acceptance for their admission in the respective degree programme at the University. The allocation of the thirty fellowships between Indian and overseas candidates depends on the availability of good candidates in the identified priority areas. The Secretary, ICAR and the Additional Secretary DARE are the final authority in resolving and taking decision on any situation/case of conflict, and that decision is binding on all parties concerned. For any dispute, the applicable law is Indian law under the jurisdiction of Courts in Delhi only.

arrival_rules: For overseas fellows whose research experiments and data collection must be at Indian SAUs/Institutes located in India: they may be allowed for a maximum period of one-and-a-half-year as per their research plan, and during the stay in India they are eligible for fellowships @ Rs. 40,000/- per month plus contingent and preparatory expenses @ Rs. 25,000/- per annum.

Interim visits to India by overseas fellows are permitted only with the consent of their Advisor and prior approval of ICAR, on their own resources â€” ICAR will not provide any financial support on travelling for the purpose.
The period of absence from the host university and the stay in an Indian university/institute must be authenticated/verified by the identified Advisor and Co-Advisor respectively.
timeline_rules: Applications are invited annually, published in Indian national newspapers and notified on the ICAR website; Indian diplomatic missions in foreign countries are informed by email.
Priority areas of research and the list of institutions for admission are identified and announced one year in advance.
Last date for submission of the 2026 application: September 25, 2026.

The first installment equals the first six months of the fellowship and is released on the Council receiving the fellow's acceptance for the fellowship and the admission letter from the host University.
Thereafter the fellowship amount is released after the Council receives the academic progress report from the fellow, duly certified by the concerned advisor/supervisor/head of institution.
Progress reports are submitted to the Council every six months.
Tenure: three years, not extendable in any case so far as Council support is concerned.

In case the fellow is not able to complete even after 2 years of the prescribed duration of the programme for which the fellowship was sanctioned, the Council may take necessary steps for the recovery of the fellowship paid.
Completion report (copy of dissertation/thesis plus a brief report) is due within 15 days of completion of the programme.

Once selected, candidates must register for the programme within one year from the date of issue of the letter of fellowship award; in case of delay the offer terminates automatically and no separate cancellation communication is issued by the Council.
The first installment to the Indian fellow is paid in Indian Rupees only.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your Master's is in agriculture/allied sciences with OGPA 6.60/10.0 or 65% marks or equivalent â€” this is a hard numeric gate.
Check the age gate against the last date for receipt of applications: 35 for fresh candidates, 40 for in-service candidates.
Check the freshness gate: as a fresh candidate your Master's must have been completed not more than two years before the specified date in the year of admission.
As an in-service candidate from India, confirm you are employed in the ICAR-AU system and that you can get deputation approval from your Director/Vice-Chancellor.
Choose a research topic inside the Council's identified priority areas â€” they are published one year in advance and a proposal outside them is not eligible.
Pick a host from the published lists: identified overseas institutions for Indian candidates, identified Indian Agricultural Universities in the ICAR-AU system for overseas candidates.
Apply to the host yourself and get the acceptance letter â€” ICAR makes you obtain it 'at their own level' and you must have it in hand at interview.
Write the research plan and give it a title; the form asks for discipline, degree programme, session and year of admission, prescribed duration, proposed area of study and the host's contact person.
Nominate two referees with email addresses â€” one your current supervisor (if employed) and one an expert in your area. ICAR will contact them directly.

Assemble the certified pieces early, because they take longest: the doctor's physical fitness certificate with seal, and â€” for overseas applicants â€” the Indian Diplomatic Mission certificates with office seal.
Attach copies of your academic documents, a recent photograph, supporting documents for achievements, and copies of research papers for publications above NAAS 4.0.
If you are an Indian candidate, have your Aadhar number ready â€” it is mandatory to receive the fellowships.
Email the whole pack to adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com with the subject exactly as "Application for NSIF: [your name] and [contact number]" by the deadline.
Plan your financial buffer: host fees, medical insurance and medical fitness come out of your own pocket or out of the fellowship.
important_advice_for_students: This is not full funding. ICAR states plainly that 'All fees chargeable by the host institution where the fellow is enrolled will be paid by the fellow himself out of the fellowship grant or from his/her own resources', and that all other costs including medical insurance come from the fellowship or your own resources. Model the host tuition fee before you commit.

You get the air ticket, and it is genuinely generous: a to-and-fro economy class ticket provided by the Council for both Indian and overseas candidates. But for Indian candidates, getting to the departure airport in India and from the arrival airport to the overseas university is on you or your sponsor.
For overseas fellows in India, the Council also reimburses economy-class travel from the port of arrival to your university and back â€” worth claiming.

Budget for three years and no more. The tenure 'will not be extended in any case'. If you are slow, you finish on your own money, and if you are two years past the prescribed programme duration the Council may recover the fellowship paid.

The stakes on conduct are high. Unsatisfactory performance or conduct probation terminates the fellowship immediately and makes you pay for the rest of the programme. Indian Fellows who do not return to India face recovery of the entire amount paid plus 10% overhead, and the Indian Embassy in the host country may be informed.

Do not move or change your research direction. You must sign an undertaking that you will neither change the place of work nor deviate from the broad research area, and progress is certified every six months by your advisor.

If you are an overseas fellow and your work needs Indian field trials, you may spend up to one-and-a-half-year in India and you keep the same fellowship rate during that time â€” but interim trips beyond that need your Advisor's consent and prior ICAR approval, and ICAR funds no travel for them.

Prepare for the money mechanics. The first six months are released only after ICAR receives your acceptance and your host's admission letter, and the first installment to an Indian fellow is paid in Indian Rupees only.

Indian fellows must put up an irrevocable US$ 10,000 bank guarantee in favour of the Secretary, ICAR for the whole programme. Foreign national fellows instead have Rs. 2,00,000 recovered from their grant (Rs. 1,00,000 each from the first two installments), refunded at final release. These are different mechanisms â€” know which applies to you.
The interview may not be a video call you choose. The Committee can use teleconferencing, and overseas candidates may be interviewed by Council-identified experts based in their home country.

ICAR shares in your IP. The Council takes an appropriate share on patents and knowledge generated under its IP Management bulletin, and any other IP agreement you sign must be shared with ICAR. Acknowledge ICAR support in all publications.

Note the 30-fellowship cap: allocation between Indian and overseas candidates depends on the availability of good candidates in the priority areas, so a strong topic matters as much as a strong record.
common_rejection_risks: Master's degree below OGPA 6.60/10.0 or 65% marks or equivalent.
Over the age limit on the last date prescribed for receipt of applications (35 fresh, 40 in-service).
As a fresh candidate, having completed the qualifying degree more than two years before the specified date in the year of admission.
As an in-service candidate from India, not being employed in the ICAR-AU system.
Proposed research outside the Council's identified priority areas.
No acceptance letter from the host â€” you must have one, and you must produce it at the interview.
Naming a host that is not on the identified list, or a host without the required research and teaching capability and faculty/infrastructure strength.
Only one referee, or two referees who do not meet the published composition (current supervisor plus an expert in the area).
Missing, unsealed or unsigned certificates â€” the physical fitness certificate needs a doctor's seal, and overseas applicants' certificates need the Indian Diplomatic Mission's office seal.
Missing the Certificate from the Candidate including the return-home undertaking.
Missing supporting documents: academic document copies, recent photograph, achievement documents, or copies of research papers for NAAS-above-4.0 publications.
An in-service candidate who cannot produce deputation approval, or an Indian in-service candidate who will not execute the three-year service bond.
No Aadhar number for an Indian candidate, which ICAR states is mandatory to receive the fellowships.
A wrong or missing email subject line â€” ICAR specifies "Application for NSIF: Name of Applicant and contact number".
Missing the deadline. For the 2026 cycle the last date was September 25, 2026.
estimated_uncovered_costs: All host institution fees where the fellow is enrolled â€” explicitly the fellow's own responsibility, out of the grant or own resources.
Medical insurance â€” explicitly excluded; the fellow meets it from the fellowship or own resources.
The medical fitness test â€” at the fellow's own cost.
For Indian candidates going abroad: travel from residence/work to the port of departure in India, and from the port of arrival to the destination University overseas.
Interim visits to India by overseas fellows â€” ICAR provides no financial support on travelling for the purpose.
Completion costs if the Ph.D. is not finished within the three-year tenure, or recovery of the fellowship paid if it is not finished two years beyond the prescribed programme duration.
For Indian fellows: the working capital tied up in the US$ 10,000 irrevocable bank guarantee held for the whole programme.
For foreign national fellows: Rs. 2,00,000 withheld from the grant until final release.
Books, equipment, fieldwork and consumables beyond the annual contingent and preparatory lump sum of US$ 1,000 (Indian fellows abroad) or INR 25,000 (overseas fellows in India).
document_audit: Completed application form in the prescribed ICAR proforma, signed with date and place.
Recent photograph of the applicant â€” a stated form item.
Copies of documents for every academic qualification from the graduate degree onwards, showing university/institution, degree, year, subjects and marks/grades/OGPA.
Supporting documents for professional work experience and achievements: awards/honours/scholarships (Gold Medal, Best Thesis, NTS, JRF), NET, ARS, research/teaching experience.

Publications above NAAS 4.0 only, in the prescribed four-column format (authors and title, name of journal, journal ID, NAAS score against the NAAS list of Science journals 2025), with copies of the research papers attached.
Acceptance letter for admission from the Host University â€” copy to be attached.
Copy of the research plan â€” YES/NO indicated and the copy attached.
Deputation permission from the parent organisation for in-service candidates.
Certificate from the Candidate: truth declaration, agreement to the guidelines/terms and conditions, and the undertaking to complete the Ph.D. and return to their country. Signed.

Certificate from the Indian Diplomatic Representative (overseas applicants only): permanent domicile certification, the return-to-country-of-domicile undertaking, and certification that the entries were checked against original documents and the application is complete, with scanned copies of relevant certificates enclosed. Must carry signature, name, designation, OFFICE SEAL, address, date and place.

Certificate of Physical Fitness by an authorized Medical Doctor: medical history, physical examination, lungs, summary, the doctor's view on ability to carry a full course of study involving long hours of work, health rating (EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR), vaccination record and general remarks. Must carry signature, address, date and DOCTOR's SEAL.

Certificate of Proficiency in English (overseas applicants only): whether the applicant is proficient/not proficient in written/spoken English and/or has/has not passed the English Proficiency Test, naming the conducting authority, under the SEAL of the Indian Diplomatic Mission.
Referee comment forms, one per referee, in the prescribed FORMAT: referee's name, designation, affiliation, contact phone, email; the three declarations; signature and date.
Passport details (number, date of issue, place of issue, date of expiry) and, for Indian candidates, the Aadhar number.
Fresh/in-service tick, with the Master's completion year for fresh candidates or the employer's name, address, head of organization and position held for in-service candidates.

Health advisory to action on: those planning to study in India are strongly advised to get vaccinated against typhoid/cholera before coming to India; those proceeding for overseas studies may get appropriate vaccination as per the host country's requirements.
Publication check: ICAR's document publishes no file size limit, accepted file extension or translation rule, so those remain to be confirmed with the ADG (HRD) at ICAR before you send.

referee_tracking.instructions: One of the two referees should preferably be the applicant's supervisor in the current occupation (if employed). The applicant supplies the referee's name, address, contact phone number and e-mail address; the Council may contact the referees directly to obtain comments in the prescribed format. The referee completes the 'FORMAT FOR REFEREE COMMENTS ON THE SUITABILITY OF CANDIDATE FOR NETAJI SUBHAS-ICAR INTERNATIONAL FELLOWSHIP', which asks them to state whether they are well acquainted with the applicant's work and achievements, whether they are satisfied the applicant has the sincerity, zeal and capacity to complete the Ph.D. programme applied for with funding support under the fellowship, and whether they would recommend the applicant without hesitation â€” then signs and dates it.

referee_tracking.role: Referee 2 â€” expert in the area
referee_tracking.instructions: The second referee should be an expert in the area and well acquainted with the candidate's work. The applicant supplies the name, address, contact phone number and e-mail address, and ICAR may contact this referee directly using the prescribed referee comment format, with signature and date.

Not a referee in the assessment sense, but the host's advisor/supervisor/head of institution certifies every academic progress report that the fellow submits to the Council, and those certified reports are the condition for each subsequent release of the fellowship.

A certifying authority rather than an academic referee. The mission certifies that the applicant is permanently domiciled in the named country and will return to the country of domicile on completion of studies in the host country; certifies that the entries in the application form, particulars about examinations passed, marks obtained, subjects studied and syllabi covered have been checked with original documents and that the application is complete in all respects; and confirms the applicant has enclosed scanned copies of relevant certificates, diplomas or degrees. Requires signature, name, designation, office seal, address, date and place.

Completes the Certificate of Physical Fitness, including medical history, physical examination, lungs, summary, an explicit statement on whether the applicant is or is not physically able to carry on a full course of study involving long hours of work in a college/university/institution in India or abroad, a health rating, the small pox vaccination record, and whether there is evidence of communicable disease, fatigue or physical defects. Requires signature, address, date and doctor's seal.

official.description: The IIT Kanpur Office of International Relations page for how to apply sets out admission to MTech, MS (By Research), MDes, M.Sc. and PhD programmes for candidates who are not citizens of India and are not OCI/PIO card holders. Those candidates are treated as Foreign Nationals, apply through the Pingala portal or by emailing the admissions office, may be funded through six routes (ICCR, Study in India, AARDO, ASEAN-DIA, India Bhutan Friendship Scholarship, or the Institute Fellowship), and are charged a fee structure that separates a USD tuition component from an INR 17,495 hostel fee component.
purpose: To set out how candidates who are NOT citizens of India (by birth or naturalized) and/or are OCI/PIO card holders â€” treated as foreign nationals â€” apply for admission to IIT Kanpur's MTech, MS (By Research), MDes, M.Sc. and PhD programmes.
IIT Kanpur offers all foreign degree students a monthly fellowship at par with Indian students. Only those students who do not receive any other funding will be eligible for the Institute Fellowship.

The page routes foreign applicants to the scholarship and fee-concession schemes through which the Government of India and partner bodies fund them, and publishes the tuition and hostel fee structure and the annual application windows.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are not an Indian citizen by birth or naturalization and do not hold an OCI/PIO card â€” otherwise this route does not apply to you.
Register on the Study in India (SII) portal. IIT Kanpur calls this mandatory and says it is also linked to issuance of your study visa, so do it before anything else.

Pick one funding route and meet its own condition: ICCR, Study in India, AARDO (AARDO member country, MTech only), India Bhutan Friendship (Bhutanese, MTech), ASEAN-DIA (currently on hold), or the Institute Fellowship (no other funding).
Match your degree to a published programme and department, and check that department's eligibility minimum â€” the published figures are absolute minimums and departments may add more.

Assemble: passport/citizenship card, applicant photo, applicant signature, proof of date of birth, qualifying degree certificate (original/provisional), GATE score card if you have one, and the mark/grade sheet of the qualifying degree as a single PDF file.
Add the NOC only if you are a sponsored, part-time or external candidate.
Apply in the right window: Autumn 20 March â€“ 15 April, or Spring 1 September â€“ 31 October for PhD only.
Submit through Pingala, or use the Foreign National email route with IIT Kanpur's offline sample form if the portal has closed.
Do not pay the application fee â€” it is waived for the Foreign National category, and you are asked to ignore the Pingala payment prompt after submitting.
Do not let a missing GATE score stop you â€” the GATE requirement is waived for the Foreign National category.
Be ready for a video-conferencing interview if shortlisted, and accept that departmental committees make the final admission decision.
important_advice_for_students: Do not read 'Institute Fellowship at par with Indian students' as full funding. Foreign students pay a published fee structure on top: USD 250 to USD 4,000 in tuition depending on programme and SAARC status, plus INR 17,495 hostel fee. Budget for that.

The single exception on tuition is the AARDO Fellowship, which waives tuition and gives free accommodation plus airfare to and from New Delhi â€” but it is for MTech only and for AARDO member countries in Asia and Africa.
The cheapest route to a scholarship may be Study in India: apply there, sit the PRAGATII exam, and meritorious students are selected for up to USD 3,200 covering tuition, accommodation and mess.
If you already hold another scholarship, you lose the Institute Fellowship â€” it is explicitly limited to students who receive no other funding. Do not count on both.
The Study in India registration is not paperwork you can defer. IIT Kanpur links it to your study visa, so a missing registration can block your visa and therefore your admission.

Two real advantages: the application fee is waived and the GATE requirement is waived for the Foreign National category. Do not let a missing GATE score stop you, and do not attempt to pay a fee you do not owe.

Watch the two-stage assistantship structure if you are a PhD candidate: Rs. 37,000/- per month for the first two years, then Rs. 42,000/- for another three years. The rate steps up, so your later years are better funded.

If you want the assistantship, you must be a regular candidate. M Tech/MS (By Research) in Cybersecurity is explicitly for sponsored/part-time/external candidates and carries no financial assistantship.

Be practical about the assistantship duty: MTech, MDes and MS (By Research) assistants are assigned 8 hours of work per week, and the institute states you are expected to carry out the assigned duties during the programme.

The email route for foreign nationals has its own, later deadline than the portal. For 2026-27 the portal closed April 15 at 02:00 PM but foreign nationals could still email until April 30, 2026 â€” do not assume the portal and email deadlines coincide.
Applications to ICCR are usually April-June, which is a different calendar from IIT Kanpur's own windows. If you are routing through ICCR, you are managing two deadlines.
ASEAN-DIA is on hold. If that was your plan, it is not available right now, and the ASEAN portal is a different route hosted at IIT Delhi.
Departments can set requirements above the published minimums, so treat the eligibility table as a floor and confirm with your target department before you invest effort.
common_rejection_risks: Applying as an Indian citizen or OCI/PIO card holder through the foreign-national route, where those candidates are not treated as foreign nationals.
Missing the mandatory Study in India registration, which is also linked to study visa issuance.
Applying outside the published windows (Autumn 20 March â€“ 15 April; Spring 1 September â€“ 31 October for PhD).
Missing the Foreign National email deadline because you assumed it matched the Pingala portal closure date.
Splitting the qualifying mark/grade sheet into multiple files when it must be a single PDF file.
Applying for the assistantship while sponsored, part-time or external â€” assistantship is limited to regular students.
Applying for M Tech/MS (By Research) in Cybersecurity as a regular candidate â€” it is sponsored/part-time/external only and carries no assistantship.
Counting on the Institute Fellowship while also holding another scholarship â€” it is limited to students with no other funding.
Relying on the ASEAN-DIA fellowship, which is published as currently on hold.
Applying for the India Bhutan Friendship Scholarship as a non-Bhutanese student, or for AARDO from a non-member country.
Being below the department's actual requirement, where the department has set a bar above the published absolute minimum.
Failing to prepare for, or attend, the video-conferencing interview that decides the final selection of shortlisted FN candidates.
Attempting to pay the waived application fee on the Pingala Portal after submission.
Not sending the required testimonials with the emailed Foreign National application.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees for every route other than the AARDO Fellowship: USD 250 (PhD SAARC), USD 500 (PhD Non-SAARC), USD 500 (MTech SAARC), USD 750 (MTech Non-SAARC), USD 2,000 (MBA SAARC) or USD 4,000 (MBA Non-SAARC).
The hostel fee of INR 17,495 in every row of the fee structure table, except under the AARDO Fellowship which includes free accommodation.
Books, equipment, travel and everyday living costs beyond the monthly fellowship or assistantship and the annual scheme-specific items.
The gap between the India Bhutan Friendship Scholarship's 'fully funded' description and any cost not named in it â€” IIT Kanpur publishes no itemised coverage for that scholarship.
Any cost attached to the Study in India route above the capped USD 3,200 scholarship.
Travel to and from India for everyone except AARDO beneficiaries, for whom airfare to and from New Delhi is published.
Medical insurance and other personal costs â€” not published as covered by any of these schemes.

submission_workflow: Confirm foreign-national status (not an Indian citizen by birth or naturalization; no OCI/PIO card).
Register on the Study in India portal and keep the confirmation, since it is linked to your study visa.
Select the funding route that fits your circumstances and complete that scheme's own conditions.
Check your target programme and department's eligibility minimums, including any departmental requirement above the published floor.

Prepare the document set: passport/citizenship card, photo, signature, proof of date of birth, qualifying degree certificate, GATE score card if available, and the mark/grade sheet as a single PDF; add the NOC only if sponsored, part-time or external.
Apply within the correct window â€” Autumn 20 March â€“ 15 April, or Spring 1 September â€“ 31 October for PhD.

Submit through Pingala for M.Des / MS (By Research) / PhD, or email the complete application with the required testimonials to admissions_ir@iitk.ac.in (cc admissiondesk@iitk.ac.in) as a Foreign National candidate.
Do not pay the application fee; skip the GATE requirement.
Prepare for the video-conferencing interview if shortlisted.
On admission, separately apply to the external scheme you are using, on that scheme's own portal and calendar (ICCR is usually April-June).
Register for and complete the assistantship or Institute Fellowship award formalities once admitted.
post_award_requirements: Keep the Study in India registration current, since it is linked to study visa issuance.

For Institute Assistantship holders: carry out the assigned duties during the programme â€” 8 hours of work per week for MTech, MDes and MS (By Research) assistants â€” and remain a regular (non-sponsored/non-part-time/non-external) student.
Pay the published tuition and hostel fee charges unless covered by a scheme that expressly waives them (only the AARDO Fellowship is published as waiving tuition).
Do not combine the Institute Fellowship with other funding; if other funding arrives, the Institute Fellowship does not apply.
No return-home, deferral, renewal or clinical obligation is published by IIT Kanpur for these schemes.
questions_to_ask_host: What are the specific eligibility requirements my department applies on top of the published absolute minimum?
Does my department require a GATE score despite the Foreign National waiver, and will the waiver be honoured for my programme?
Is the assistantship or Institute Fellowship available to me given my candidate category, and at what monthly rate for my programme and year?
What is the exact total fee I will owe, in USD and INR, for my programme and my SAARC or non-SAARC status, and when is it payable?
Is campus hostel accommodation guaranteed at INR 17,495, or is it first-come first-served?
What is my department's real interview process, and how long should I allow for the video-conferencing shortlist?
Which funding scheme do you recommend for my nationality, and does IIT Kanpur have any fee concession for me beyond the published table?

verification.source_conflict_rule: Two IIT Kanpur offices publish on this route and they are not identical in scope: the Office of International Relations (OIR) 'How to apply' page owns foreign-national status, the funding-route menu, the fee structure, the document list and the annual windows, while the Dean of Academic Affairs (DOAA) PG Admissions pages own the application mechanics (Pingala and email routes, portal dates), the Foreign National concessions (fee waiver, GATE waiver, video-conferencing interview) and the programme-level eligibility minimums. Where they overlap, the DOAA pages govern the mechanics of applying and the OIR page governs who qualifies as a foreign national and what is charged. Where the OIR page's programme list is labelled to a past intake (July 2025 semester) while the DOAA pages carry 2026-27 dates, the DOAA dates are used and the mismatch is flagged rather than silently reconciled.
verification.source_freshness_rule: This page is a live admissions page with no publication date, so its fee table, windows, funding-route menu and programme list are valid only for the cycle it currently reflects. The Pingala closure date and the Foreign National email deadline change every year, and the ASEAN-DIA 'currently on hold' note can change without notice. Re-read both the OIR 'How to apply' page and the DOAA foreign-students, apply-online and eligibility-requirement pages before each cycle, and read the fee-concession order at https://surl.li/fjpdiq for anything beyond the published fee table.

official.application_cycle: Annual cycle for first-year fall entry. Counselor, teacher and community organisation nominations open 15 September and close 30 November; the applicant's own application does not have to be Early Decision but should be submitted by 1 December; finalist interviews take place in mid-February; awards are decided with the admission cycle.

official.deadline_institutional: The applicant's own University of Rochester application does not have to be submitted as Early Decision but should be submitted by 1 December, and financial aid documents must be completed. Renewal requires applying for financial aid annually by 15 March.
official.deadline_note: Two different deadlines belong to two different actors. Third-party nominations - the route by which a candidate enters the scholarship - open 15 September and close 30 November, and the University states it does not accept nominations from students or parents. The applicant's own admission application 'does not have to be submitted as Early Decision, but should be submitted by December 1'. Separately, award holders must apply for financial aid annually by 15 March to renew. The date recorded is the nomination closing date.
official.status_note: Read on 1 October 2026. Nominations are open from 15 September, so the nomination window is open today, and the applicant application deadline of 1 December is still ahead.

official.funding_duration: four years, or up to eight semesters, until the first bachelor degree requirements are met, whichever comes first
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'A four-year scholarship to the University of Rochester in the amount of the cost of attendance. Health insurance is covered if applicable.' official.description: The Alan and Jane Handler Endowed Scholarship is the University of Rochester's premier award, funded from a permanently endowed fund created in 2007 with an ultimate commitment of $25 million. Handler Scholars receive assured, complete financial support - tuition, fees, housing, food, books, personal expenses and transportation - for the duration of the regular four-year academic program, with health insurance covered if applicable, plus an enrichment fund of up to $5,000. Selection is based on academic excellence, outstanding potential to be future leaders, demonstrated mastery of complex challenges and substantial financial need shown on the CSS Profile and FAFSA, and international students are selected each year.

official.coverage: The Handler Scholarship provides complete financial support for four years - tuition, mandatory fees, housing, food, books, personal expenses and transportation, up to eight semesters or until first-degree requirements are met - with health insurance covered if applicable, plus an enrichment fund of up to $5,000; it excludes Rocky Bucks/Flex Account funds, individual non-course-required fees such as dorm damage and parking tickets, and off-campus housing costs above the standard allowance.
official.funding: Fully Funded — four-year scholarship equal to the full cost of attendance (tuition and fees, housing and food, books and supplies, personal and transportation) plus an enrichment fund of up to $5,000; health insurance covered if applicable

official.description: Duke University's Karsh International Scholars Program, founded in 2010 through a gift from Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh, recognises a cohort of international undergraduates who have demonstrated financial need. There is no separate application: candidates apply to Duke University and request financial aid. The award covers tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, any demonstrated need exceeding those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships and other opportunities that advance the student's academic career.
purpose: In honor of the exceptional contributions international scholars make to Duke University, the Karsh International Scholarship was founded in 2010 thanks to a generous donation from Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh.

Karsh International Scholars comprise an intellectually and civically engaged cohort of international students who promote interdisciplinary inquiry, academic research, and scholarship in the service of society.
International applicants must have demonstrated financial need to be eligible for this scholarship.
study_type: Full-time undergraduate study at Duke University
Undergraduate degree programme (A.B. or B.S.); applicants who already hold a B.A. or a B.S. degree cannot be considered
official.degree_award: Full undergraduate degree at Duke University (A.B. or B.S.). The scholarship is need-based financial aid attached to enrolment; it is not a standalone short-term award.
official.duration: Four years. Duke University issues four-year aid awards for international applicants; once the aid award is complete, it is automatically renewed for the applicant's subsequent years at Duke. The award also includes three summers of funding.
official.application_cycle: Annual, tied to Duke's undergraduate admissions cycle. International applicants seeking aid are considered in a separate admission pool alongside Duke's Early Decision and Regular Decision rounds, with the CSS Profile due by November 3 (Early Decision) or February 1 (Regular Decision) for the 2026-27 CSS Profile year, which becomes available to complete online by October 1. Aid is re-applied for annually while the student is at Duke.
official.deadline_central_display: There is no separate Karsh Scholarship deadline. The operative deadline is the Duke admission decision-plan deadline for the CSS Profile: November 3 for Early Decision and February 1 for Regular Decision. As at the 2026-10-01 verification date the next binding date is November 3, 2026 (Early Decision); the Regular Decision CSS Profile deadline is February 1, and the CSS Profile is available to complete online from October 1.
official.deadline_note: The two institutional CSS Profile deadlines are Early Decision by November 3 (aid estimate issued with the offer of admission in December) and Regular Decision by February 1. Duke states that if your aid application is not complete by the deadline your total eligibility for aid will not change, and that applications continue to be processed as they arrive â€” but it urges you to submit as soon as possible to receive your aid offer with your offer of admission. The February 1 date is used for deadline_institutional because the November 3 Early Decision date is carried in deadline_central as the next binding date.
official.funding_label: Karsh International Scholars Program â€” covers your tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need that exceeds those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships, and other opportunities that will advance your academic career. Need-based: the amount is set from the applicant's demonstrated financial need and Duke's cost of attendance, not a fixed scholarship figure.
official.tuition_rule: The award covers tuition. Duke's published estimated cost of attendance before aid shows Tuition of $70,265, and the Karsh award covers tuition in full together with mandatory fees of $2,907. The award also covers demonstrated need that exceeds those costs.
official.host_institution_fee: Mandatory fees are covered by the award. Duke's published estimated cost of attendance before aid lists Estimated Fees of $2,907.

The financial aid interest box is the single most consequential checkbox in your application. Duke states that international applicants admitted with "no financial aid interest" are ineligible to apply for financial aid for any year of undergraduate study â€” that decision is effectively irreversible.
You are pooled separately. International applicants who indicate interest in financial aid are considered in a separate admission pool, so applying with aid interest changes who reads your file.

Missing the CSS Profile deadline does not destroy eligibility, but it delays the aid estimate. Duke says total eligibility will not change and it keeps processing applications as they arrive â€” but your aid award may arrive after your admission letter rather than with it.
Late documents are the real risk, not the deadline. If the College Board requests foreign tax forms or employer statements and you are slow, your award slips.

Get the translations right the first time. Duke requires official English translations, both the original and the translated copy, and the currency conversion into US dollars as part of the translation.
Airfare and visa costs are not in this award. Duke's published cost of attendance includes only domestic transportation of $582, varying by home address. Budget your own flights, visa and SEVIS fee.

Renewal is favourable for international students. Duke issues four-year aid awards to international applicants and automatically renews them for subsequent years â€” but you still submit a new aid application each year with updated income and asset information.

If next year's cost of attendance rises, your grant aid rises with it. Duke states that where you qualified for need-based grant aid and the 2026-27 cost of attendance is higher than the current year, it will increase your grant aid to cover the difference.
Plan around the June funding step and the arrival session. Aid steps arrive by email in June once you enrol, and you must attend a financial aid session on arrival before aid is applied.
The award includes three summers of funding for research and unpaid internships. That is a genuine extra: use it for unpaid opportunities you could not otherwise afford.
common_rejection_risks: Holding dual U.S./other-country citizenship.
Already holding a B.A. or B.S. degree.
Failing to demonstrate financial need â€” international applicants must have demonstrated need to be eligible.
Leaving the financial aid interest box unticked, or failing to have it changed through the Office of Undergraduate Admissions.
Being admitted in the "no financial aid interest" pool, which makes the applicant ineligible for aid in every year.
Missing the CSS Profile deadline (November 3 Early Decision, February 1 Regular Decision) and receiving a delayed aid estimate.
Not completing the CSS Profile at all, which removes you from institutional aid consideration.
Not completing both parents' CSS Profiles where both parents contribute, leaving Duke unable to calculate the Expected Family Contribution.
Being slow to respond to a College Board request for foreign tax forms or employer income statements.
Submitting translations that are not official, or omitting the original-language copy, or omitting the currency conversion into US dollars.
Skipping the FAFSA when required â€” only students who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents may skip it.
Failing to attend the mandatory financial aid session on arrival at Duke.
Failing to submit a new aid application in later years, or leaving income and asset information out of date.
estimated_uncovered_costs: International airfare to the United States â€” Duke's cost of attendance lists only domestic transportation of $582, varying by home address.
US visa application fee, immigration paperwork and the I-901 SEVIS fee â€” none is published as covered.
Anything above your demonstrated financial need: the award is explicitly need-based and is sized to demonstrated need, so a change in your family's circumstances could leave a gap.

Books, course materials and supplies beyond the demonstrated-need calculation if your circumstances change after award â€” Duke requires a new aid application each year with updated income and asset information.
Costs during a leave, withdrawal or a year in which your family's income rises materially, since the award is recalculated annually from the CSS Profile.
Expenses incurred by current students that Duke's cost of attendance does not itemise, such as travel home or non-Duke study-abroad costs.
document_audit: CSS Profile (2026-27) â€” required for all aid applicants, available online from October 1; a separate profile is completed by each contributing parent.
FAFSA â€” required for U.S. citizens and permanent residents; students who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents may skip this step.
Family's current year or most recent foreign tax forms â€” only if requested by the College Board.

Non-filer form from the Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support â€” for parents who are not employed or are self-employed; documents that they do not file taxes and reports yearly income in the box provided.
Official English translations of all documents and earnings statements, plus the original-language copies.
Currency conversion from the original monetary values into US dollars, provided as part of the translation.
Routing check: additional documents go through the College Board's online IDOC service following emailed instructions â€” not by email to Duke.
Publication check: Duke publishes no file size limits, accepted file extensions or signature requirements beyond the translation, dual-copy and IDOC routing rules recorded above.

submission_workflow: Verify your eligibility: non-U.S. citizen, no dual U.S. citizenship, no existing B.A. or B.S., and genuine financial need.
Choose Early Decision (CSS Profile by November 3) or Regular Decision (CSS Profile by February 1).
Apply to Duke University, ticking "yes" in the financial aid interest box; if already applied without it, contact the Office of Undergraduate Admissions to change it.
Register for the CSS Profile from October 1 and complete it for the 2026-27 cycle by your round's deadline.
Have each contributing parent complete a separate CSS Profile.
Complete the FAFSA if you are a U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
Monitor email, including College Board email, for an additional-documentation request.

If requested, assemble foreign tax forms, employer income statements from both parents (or the non-filer form), official English translations, original copies and the currency conversion into US dollars.
Upload everything through the College Board IDOC service as instructed.
Receive your admission letter and aid award; if no additional documentation was requested, Duke states it has enough information to award aid at the time of admission.
Decide to enrol and complete the funding steps from the June email.
Attend the mandatory financial aid session on arrival at Duke so the aid is applied.
post_award_requirements: Attend the mandatory financial aid session upon arrival at Duke in order for the aid to be applied.
Complete the enrolment and funding steps Duke emails in June once you decide to enrol.
Submit a new financial aid application every year at Duke with updated income and asset information.
Keep your financial circumstances documented and be ready to supply translated documentation again if requested.
Contribute to the cohort Duke describes: Karsh International Scholars promote interdisciplinary inquiry, academic research, and scholarship in the service of society.
Plan your three funded summers for research, unpaid internships and other opportunities that advance your academic career.
No return-home, deferral or clinical obligation is published by Duke for this scholarship.

Citizens of any country outside the U.S. can be considered; dual U.S./other-country citizenship cannot

Aid award issued with the letter of admission; June email with funding steps after enrolment
