verification.source_conflict_rule: Three Duke sources cover this record and each owns a distinct layer. The Office of University Scholars and Fellows page owns the programme's identity, rationale, cohort, coverage and FAQ. The Undergraduate Admissions Financial Support page owns the international applicant's application mechanics, including the aid-interest box, the separate admission pool, the CSS Profile and FAFSA deadlines, the IDOC document set, the translation rules and the four-year award with automatic renewal. The Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support pages own the aid calendar and the domestic process. Where they overlap, the international-specific instructions on the Admissions Financial Support page govern an international applicant, and the OUSF page governs what the scholarship is and what it covers. The named 'Karsh' coincidence between two different Duke offices was resolved by function, not by name: OUSF administers this programme, the Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support administers need-based aid.
verification.source_freshness_rule: These pages carry no publication date, so treat every figure as valid only for the cycle shown and re-check before each cycle. Duke itself warns that estimates are based on the prior year's cost of attendance and are revised in the spring, so an award figure quoted from one page may be superseded weeks later.

official.description: Harvard College's financial aid programme is entirely need-based and, by Harvard's stated policy, international students are eligible for exactly the same aid as American students. Harvard publishes two principles â€” need-blind admissions and 100% need-based aid â€” and states that it meets 100% of students' demonstrated financial need. An aid package is built by first establishing the parent contribution, then factoring in student employment and any outside awards, with scholarship funds (grant-based, never repaid) covering the remaining need. Prospective students submit a CSS Profile and an IDOC Packet for the 2027-2028 school year.
purpose: Harvard College provides need-based financial aid that allows us to bring the best students to Harvard, regardless of their family's ability to pay.

"We know that paying for college is a big concern for many families, and we're committed to making a Harvard education â€“ and the opportunities that come with it â€“ possible for more students than ever. International students are eligible for exactly the same aid as American students."

"Because we want to bring the best people to Harvard regardless of their financial circumstances, we follow two important principles: 1. Need-blind admissions. Your financial need and your aid application will never affect your chance of being admitted to Harvard. 2. 100% need-based aid. We base aid awards on need, not on merit. This means that financial aid supports the students who will benefit from it the most. Furthermore, we meet 100 percent of our students' demonstrated financial need."
"We want to make Harvard accessible and affordable for everyone who gets inâ€”no matter what."

"Financial aid is always available to your family - whether for your first year or your senior year. Our knowledgeable financial aid officers are here to help you navigate the financial aid application process."
study_type: Full-time undergraduate study in the Faculty of Arts and Sciences at Harvard College, leading to an A.B.
Covers first-year applicants and transfer applicants; Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match applicants are handled within the first-year cycle
official.degree_award: Full undergraduate degree at Harvard College (A.B.). The award is need-based financial aid attached to enrolment; it is not a standalone short-term award.
official.deadline_note: Harvard publishes the same deadline for the CSS Profile, the FAFSA and the IDOC Packet, for the 2027-2028 school year: November 1 for Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match, February 1 for Regular Decision, and March 1 for Transfer. The November 1, 2026 date is carried here as the next binding institutional deadline as at the 2026-10-01 verification date. Harvard also states it will accept a late application, but may not be able to respond as quickly.
official.application_cycle: Annual, by admissions plan. Instructions are published for the 2027-2028 school year. Harvard's goal is to give a financial aid decision at the time of admission: an estimate of financial aid in mid-December for Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match applicants, and a financial aid decision around April 1 for both Restrictive Early Action and Regular Decision. Current Harvard students reapply every year and are automatically emailed reapplication instructions.
official.funding_label: Entirely need-based. "Because Harvard is committed to affordability, our scholarships are designed to cover 100% of your demonstrated financial need." The process: "First we determine your award by establishing your parent contribution. Then we factor in student employment and any outside awards you've received. Your remaining need will be covered by scholarship funds which are grant-based and never need to be repaid." International students are eligible for exactly the same aid as American students. Harvard publishes no fixed award figure â€” each package is individualized.
official.living_cost_coverage: Housing and food are part of Harvard's published cost of attendance and are covered through the need-based package, since Harvard meets 100% of demonstrated need. For 2026-27: Housing $14,250 and Food $8,942. On top of that, "If you are eligible for aid, you may also receive an additional allowance for travel and personal expenses." Students are also expected to meet a standard student contribution, usually by working around 10 to 12 hours per week during the semester.
official.travel_coverage: "If you are eligible for aid, you may also receive an additional allowance for travel and personal expenses." Harvard's published cost of attendance includes estimated transportation costs of $0-$5,000 for 2026-27, and an aid-eligible student may receive an additional allowance for travel and personal expenses on top. The specific travel allowance for an international student is not itemised on the pages read.
official.tuition_rule: Tuition is part of Harvard's published cost of attendance and is covered by the need-based package up to demonstrated need. For 2026-27, Tuition is $62,226 and the subtotal of billed costs (tuition, fees, housing, food) is $91,634, with total billed and unbilled costs of $95,134-$100,134. Harvard states it meets 100% of demonstrated financial need, and that for families with incomes up to $200,000 financial aid will cover at least the full cost of tuition.
official.host_institution_fee: Fees are a billed component of Harvard's cost of attendance and are included in the need-based calculation. For 2026-27, Fees are $6,216 (2025-26: $5,476; 2024-25: $5,126).
covered_expenses: The full cost of attendance up to demonstrated need, for 2026-27: Tuition $62,226; Fees $6,216; Housing $14,250; Food $8,942; Subtotal of billed costs $91,634; Estimated personal expenses $2,500; Estimated books $1,000; Estimated transportation costs $0-$5,000; Total billed and unbilled costs $95,134-$100,134
The remaining need after parent contribution, student employment and outside awards, covered by grant-based scholarship funds that never need to be repaid
An additional allowance for travel and personal expenses for students eligible for aid

Scholarship funds drawn from Harvard endowment funds, gifts from alumni, general tuition revenues, and federal and state grants; the Faculty of Arts and Sciences Scholarship program includes more than 2,000 individual endowment and gift funds, including a $150 million gift from Ken Griffin '89
Federal Work-Study Program eligibility for students whose package indicates it (subsidises wages for term-time and summer employment)
Federal Pell Grant or SEOP/SEOG, and the Massachusetts Gilbert Grant, where the student is a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or Massachusetts resident respectively
not_covered_or_excluded: The parent contribution: Harvard determines parent contribution from family income, assets and circumstances. For families with annual incomes below $100,000 the expected parent contribution is zero; families with significant assets are asked to pay more. Typical home equity and retirement assets are not considered.

The student contribution: "As the primary beneficiary of a Harvard education, all students are expected to contribute to their college expenses. Your financial aid award will include a standard expected contribution from your own earnings." If you have savings or other assets, you are expected to contribute a small portion as well.

Health insurance: "In addition, health insurance is required at a cost of $4,954 (for 2026-27) unless you are covered under your family's health plan." This is stated as a cost in addition to the total billed and unbilled costs, and Harvard does not publish on these pages whether it sits inside the demonstrated-need calculation.

International airfare to the United States is not a published line item: Harvard's cost of attendance lists only "Estimated transportation costs $0-$5,000" with a separate, unquantified statement about an additional travel allowance for aid-eligible students.

Any cost above demonstrated financial need, and any cost arising where the student's family withdraws financial support or has incurred large consumer debts: Harvard states "we can't provide extra aid for students whose parents withdraw financial support. Similarly, we can't provide additional aid for families that have incurred large consumer debts."

Aid is never merit-based and there are no preferential policies: "Financial aid is completely need-based and considers many factors... There are no merit-based awards, and we have no preferential policies that give some students more attractive awards than others."

Federal Direct Loans and Pell/SEOG are not available to international students: federal loans require the applicant to "be a US citizen, permanent resident or other eligible noncitizen", and federal grants require U.S. citizenship or permanent residency.

Loans are never part of the required package: "Loans are never required, but are available to interested families." Parents may borrow to meet the parent contribution, but Harvard's grant aid does not require it.
benefits: Grant-based scholarship funds that never need to be repaid, covering the remainder of demonstrated need after parent contribution, student employment and outside awards.
Need-blind admissions: the aid application and demonstrated need never affect the chance of admission.

Harvard's published affordability statistics: 25% of Harvard families pay nothing to attend; 55% of students receive need-based Harvard scholarships; 1 in 4 pays nothing; the average parent contribution is $13K.
An additional allowance for travel and personal expenses for students eligible for aid.

The Harvard Student Loan, available to all need-based aid recipients regardless of citizenship or federal aid eligibility: up to $3,500 for the academic year or up to $1,750 per semester, fixed interest rate of 4.0 percent (5.0% for loans disbursed before 07/01/2016), 10 years to repay, and no origination or insurance fees. Interest is paid by Harvard during enrolment, grace and deferment.
Automatic annual reapplication instructions for current students.
eligibility: "The process to apply for financial aid is essentially the same for all prospective students. Regardless of your citizenship or when you are applying, you will need to submit a CSS Profile and an IDOC Packet."
"US Citizens and Permanent Residents will also need to submit the FAFSA, the Free Application for Federal Student Aid."
"International students are eligible for the same amount of aid as US students."
"Applying for financial aid at the same time as you apply for admission" is encouraged, and Harvard states that "applying for financial aid will in no way jeopardize your chances of admission."
"Our goal is to provide you with a decision about financial aid at the time that you are admitted."

Harvard will consider unusual or changed financial circumstances: "You will be asked to provide information about your family income and assets, outside awards, and any unusual or changed financial circumstances."
general_eligibility: Apply for admission to Harvard College, indicating interest in financial aid at the same time as the admission application.
File the CSS Profile for the relevant school year via the College Board, listing Harvard as a recipient using code 3434.
Submit the IDOC Packet with the required tax and income documents through the College Board IDOC Service.

Where the applicant is a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or other eligible non-citizen, also file the FAFSA using Harvard's code E00468. International students who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents do not file the FAFSA.
Submit the required income documentation for both parents, or the Tax Non-Filer Statement where parents do not file tax returns, plus business, trust or estate documents where applicable.
Report any outside awards, which must be applied toward college expenses and are factored into the aid package.
ineligibility_conditions: Applicants who do not submit a CSS Profile: Harvard states "you cannot access IDOC until you have completed the CSS Profile", so the whole financial aid file cannot be completed without it.
Applicants who send draft or estimated taxes: "Please do not send draft or estimated taxes. We need the actual 2025 tax return as filed with the government."
Applicants who email their documents: "No. Email is not a secure method for sending financial aid information. Please submit everything as described in our instructions."
Applicants who send only part of a tax return: all pages and schedules are required, including schedules such as Schedule 1, Schedule A and Schedule B.

Applicants whose parents do not file tax returns and who submit neither a Tax Non-Filer Statement nor income documentation: Harvard requires the Tax Non-Filer Statement plus whatever documentation exists, such as a wage statement, salary certificate, or letter from the employer stating annual income.
Students whose parents withdraw financial support: Harvard cannot provide extra aid in that situation.
Families that have incurred large consumer debts: Harvard cannot provide additional aid for them.
Applicants relying on federal aid (Direct Loans, Pell, SEOG) who are not U.S. citizens, permanent residents or other eligible non-citizens.
Applicants who do not report outside awards: outside awards must be reported and applied toward college expenses, and outside awards cannot be used to replace the parent contribution.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship restriction. Harvard states plainly that "International students are eligible for the same amount of aid as US students" and that the application process is "essentially the same for all prospective students. Regardless of your citizenship or when you are applying, you will need to submit a CSS Profile and an IDOC Packet." Only the FAFSA, the federal loans and the federal and Massachusetts grants are citizenship-conditional.
official.international_eligibility: International applicants are eligible for exactly the same need-based aid as American students. Their specific documentation route is published: "International students are eligible for the same amount of aid as US students. If your parents file an income tax document in their country, you will submit that as part of the financial aid process. Make sure to translate the document to English. official.selection_notes: There is no aid selection committee, essay or separate award decision to prepare for. Harvard's stated process is: establish the parent contribution; factor in student employment and outside awards; cover the remaining need with grant-based scholarship funds. Aid is need-based and completely international-blind, with no merit component and no preferential policies. The award arrives with the admission decision: an estimate of financial aid in mid-December for Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match applicants, and a financial aid decision around April 1 for both Restrictive Early Action and Regular Decision. Individual review is possible for complex or uncommon circumstances: "We are happy to work with you on an individual basis if you have complex, uncommon, or challenging financial circumstances that are not easily described in the standard aid application." Harvard also publishes explicit limits on that discretion â€” no extra aid where parents withdraw support, and none for families carrying large consumer debts. Harvard states it does not track financial aid materials until after admissions decisions have been made, and that if something is missing after admission the applicant will be notified; applicants should monitor their College Board account in the meantime.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply to Harvard College and indicate interest in financial aid in the same submission â€” Harvard wants you to know you can afford to come the moment you are admitted.
Pick your plan: Restrictive Early Action / QuestBridge Match (November 1), Regular Decision (February 1), or Transfer (March 1). The CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC all share that date.
Register for the CSS Profile and list Harvard with code 3434.
Decide the parent-profile structure: one profile if your parents are married or live together; one each if they are separated or divorced.
Prepare both parents' 2025 income tax document with every page and schedule, or a Tax Non-Filer Statement plus employer letters if they do not file.
Prepare your own 2025 income tax document (signed) or a Tax Non-Filer Statement plus any W-2 Forms.
Translate any non-English document into English yourself if needed â€” Harvard says an official translation is not required and students usually write the translation on the document.

Handle the CSS Profile fee problem early if it applies to you: if you cannot afford it or the College Board cannot process payment from your country, use Harvard's alternate application for financial aid instructions.
Skip the FAFSA if you are not a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or other eligible non-citizen.
Complete the CSS Profile before you try to open IDOC â€” Harvard states you cannot access IDOC until the CSS Profile is done.
Upload everything through IDOC. Do not email documents to Harvard under any circumstances.
Add business, trust or estate documents, and a letter on unusual circumstances, if they apply to you.
Note the aid decision timing: mid-December for Restrictive Early Action and QuestBridge Match, around April 1 for Restrictive Early Action and Regular Decision.
important_advice_for_students: Applying for aid does not hurt your admission chances. Harvard states need-blind admissions explicitly: your financial need and your aid application will never affect your chance of being admitted. There is no reason to apply without indicating aid.
You get exactly the same aid as an American student. Harvard states this twice and in strong terms. Do not assume international status reduces the package.
Aid is 100% need-based with no merit component and no preferential policies. There is nothing to win with extra talents or activities at the aid stage.

Budget for the student contribution, not just the scholarship. Harvard's aid includes a standard expected contribution from your own earnings, usually met by working around 10 to 12 hours a week. Harvard also publishes an average parent contribution of $13K.

You are not required to take any loan. Harvard states loans are never required and that most students graduate debt-free, even though the Harvard Student Loan is open to international students on the same terms as everyone else.

Airfare is the gap to plan for. Harvard's cost of attendance lists only $0-$5,000 for transportation and mentions an unquantified additional travel allowance for aid-eligible students. Confirm the actual treatment of international airfare with the Financial Aid Office before you commit.

Health insurance is a separate required cost: $4,954 for 2026-27 unless you are covered under your family's health plan. Harvard lists this as an addition to the total billed and unbilled costs, so check whether it sits inside your demonstrated need.

You cannot substitute an outside scholarship for Harvard's money. Outside awards first replace the term-time job expectation and then replace an equal amount of Harvard scholarship â€” they never reduce the parent contribution. Win external awards only as much as your need.
Report outside awards or you risk an aid reduction later. They must be reported and applied toward college expenses.

Late is fine, late is slower. Harvard will accept a late application, and a late tax filing does not affect eligibility â€” it only pushes back your decision. That is a genuine benefit of Harvard's process.

Do not send draft or estimated taxes. Harvard requires the actual return as filed with the government. Estimates on the CSS Profile itself are fine, because Harvard updates the profile when the real return reaches IDOC.
A single missing schedule can cost you time. Harvard flags sending one or two pages and omitting schedules like Schedule 1, Schedule A and Schedule B as a common mistake.
If you have an unusual circumstance, say so in writing. Harvard reviews complex cases individually but will not compensate for parents withdrawing support or for large consumer debts.

Watch your College Board account, not Harvard's portal, until admissions decisions are made. Harvard does not track financial aid materials until after decisions, but will notify you if something is missing after admission.
common_rejection_risks: Not indicating financial aid interest on the admission application.
Missing the applicable CSS Profile, FAFSA or IDOC deadline (November 1 Restrictive Early Action/QuestBridge, February 1 Regular Decision, March 1 Transfer).
Trying to access IDOC before completing the CSS Profile.
Sending draft or estimated tax returns instead of the actual return as filed.
Sending only part of a tax return and omitting the schedules.
Emailing documents instead of using IDOC â€” Harvard states explicitly that email is not secure and it will not be accepted.
Parents who do not file tax returns submitting nothing, or neither a Tax Non-Filer Statement nor alternative income documentation.
Failing to translate non-English documents.
Not adding Harvard's CSS Profile code (3434) or FAFSA code (E00468), so Harvard never receives the form.
Failing to report outside awards.
Canadian students submitting the wrong forms â€” Harvard specifies the T-1 General Form for the personal return and the T-2 Corporate Return for the corporate return.
Relying on the FAFSA's 20-school limit and leaving Harvard off the list without adding it back once admitted.
A student contribution shortfall: if you cannot save enough to meet your expected contribution, the Harvard Loan may be needed, and Harvard Grant eligibility is required to use it.
Expecting Harvard to cover a gap created by parents withdrawing support or by family consumer debt â€” Harvard rules both out.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The parent contribution, determined from family income, assets and circumstances. Zero for families with annual income below $100,000; families with significant assets are asked to pay more.
The student contribution, a standard expected contribution from your own earnings, usually met by working around 10 to 12 hours per week.
Health insurance of $4,954 for 2026-27, required unless you are covered under your family's health plan, and published as a cost in addition to the total billed and unbilled costs.
International airfare and visa costs, where the additional travel allowance for aid-eligible students does not reach them â€” Harvard publishes no itemised international travel figure.
Any cost above demonstrated financial need.
Expenses arising from parents withdrawing financial support or from family consumer debt, which Harvard explicitly will not cover with additional aid.
Money borrowed by parents to meet the parent contribution, if the family chooses not to fund it from savings or current income.
Term-time work earnings used to meet the student contribution, offset by outside awards if you hold any.

Harvard's published limits on discretion: no extra aid where parents withdraw financial support, and none for families with large consumer debts; individual review is available for complex or uncommon circumstances

official.description: The Aga Khan Foundation's International Scholarship Programme (AKF ISP), established in 1969 by Prince Karim Aga Khan IV, is an opportunity for outstanding scholars from selected countries who have no other means of financing their studies to pursue postgraduate education. It has supported more than 1,500 students. Awards are structured as half grant and half loan, so 50 percent of the award must be repaid, and they cover tuition and student living expenses. Priority goes to Master's programmes; PhD students receive funding for the first two years only. The 2026-2027 cycle is closed and the next cycle opens in early 2027.

Use the eligibility tool on the AKDN International Scholarships page to verify eligibility and get your local team contact.
Apply through the AKF contact in your country â€” there is no central portal.
Price the award honestly: 50 percent must be repaid plus a service charge, so model the loan half before you accept.
important_advice_for_students: This is not a gift. Half of every AKF ISP award is a loan you repay, with a service charge on top. Repayment starts six months after you graduate, terminate your studies, or lose support for falling below academic standards.
You need a guarantor. Someone has to co-sign the award agreement. Do not apply without one lined up.

The AKF wants you to arrive with other funding. It says plainly to consider the ISP "a resource of last resort" and to secure multiple sources to reduce what you request. Applying with a thin funding plan is itself an eligibility failure.
If you are a PhD applicant, understand the cliff. You get two years and then you are "expected to find funding from alternative sources". Only Master's students get the full duration of the course.
Your country of origin and your destination country both matter. You must be from a listed country, and you cannot study in the UK or Russia even if your country is eligible.
First year only. Already enrolled means already ineligible. Do not accept an offer and then apply.
Age matters as a preference, not a rule: preference is given to young professionals under 30. If you are over 30, you are not barred, but you are competing against a stated preference.

Distance learning is allowed but conditional. Local, regional and distance-learning programmes are fundable "only if the quality of the course is maintained", so expect to be asked to justify quality.
The award does not pay for your flight, your clothes, your furniture or your family. Those four exclusions are stated explicitly, so budget them yourself.
You must keep demonstrating need and academic standing for the whole programme. Improving your finances is not neutral â€” ongoing financial need is part of maintaining the award.
Timing: the 2026-2027 cycle is closed and the next opens in early 2027. There is no published day-level deadline, so watch the AKDN page and your local AKF contact rather than a calendar date.
Use the AKF's own list of alternative scholarships. The Foundation publishes a long 'starter' list of other scholarships and assistance programmes precisely because it expects you to fund the rest.
common_rejection_risks: Having already enrolled in, or commenced, postgraduate study.
Applying to a part-time programme or a short-term course.
Planning to study in the United Kingdom or Russia.
Applying from a country not on the list, without being originally from a listed country.
Having no admission to a reputable postgraduate institution.
Demonstrating no genuine financial need.
Presenting no multi-source funding plan that covers all years of study.
Being unable to name a guarantor to co-sign the award agreement.
Applying to a low-quality local, regional or distance-learning programme without being able to demonstrate that quality is maintained.
Being over 30 â€” not a hard bar, but the AKF states a preference for young professionals under 30.
Applying to a PhD without funding secured for years three onward.
Expecting the award to cover airfare, clothing, furniture or family living expenses.
Falling below the academic standards expected of ISP students during the programme, which withdraws support and starts the repayment clock.
estimated_uncovered_costs: International travel costs â€” explicitly not covered.
Clothing â€” explicitly not covered.
Furniture â€” explicitly not covered.
Living expenses for family members â€” explicitly not covered.
Repayment of 50 percent of the award amount, plus the service charge on the loan component, beginning six months after graduation, termination of studies, or withdrawal of support.
For PhD students: all funding from year three onward, since the award covers only the first two years.
Any other costs arising from the multi-source funding plan you were required to build â€” the AKF expects you to cover the balance yourself.
Costs of the guarantor arrangement, if any, which the AKF requires but does not describe.
document_audit: The Aga Khan Foundation does not publish a document list for the AKF ISP on its official page. documents is therefore recorded as an empty list rather than filled from assumption.

Evidence you will need in substance, from the published eligibility criteria: academic records; a Bachelor's degree or equivalent training/professional experience; documentation of genuine financial need; a thoughtful, reliable, multi-source funding plan covering all years of study; admission to the postgraduate institution; first-year status; and evidence of leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular and/or entrepreneurial achievements, and volunteer contributions.
Guarantor arrangement: a guarantor is required to co-sign the award agreement. The AKF does not publish the guarantor's documentation requirements, financial thresholds or eligibility.

Publication check: no file size limits, accepted file extensions, translation or certification rules are published for this programme. Confirm the actual document requirements with the AKF contact in your country, since the process runs through them.

official_fields_confirmed: Programme identity and origin: the Aga Khan Foundation's International Scholarship Programme (AKF ISP), established in 1969 by Prince Karim Aga Khan IV, which has supported more than 1,500 students to date
Purpose: an opportunity for outstanding scholars from selected countries who have no other means of financing their studies, to pursue postgraduate education
Selection process: global, annual and competitive, with a limited number of new awards in each cycle
Cycle status: the 2026-2027 application cycle is now closed and the next cycle will open in early 2027
Eligible origin countries: Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, the Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania and Uganda
Diaspora provision: in countries such as Canada, Portugal and the USA, applications are accepted from those originally from one of the countries listed above
Destination restriction: "At this time, the AKF ISP is not available to students who wish to study in the United Kingdom or Russia."

All seven eligibility criteria verbatim: excellent academic records; a Bachelor's degree or equivalent training/professional experience; genuine financial need; a thoughtful, reliable, multi-source funding plan that covers all years of study; admission to a reputable postgraduate institution; starting the first year of the programme; and strong leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular and/or entrepreneurial achievements, and volunteer contributions
Age preference: "preference is given to young professionals under 30 years of age"

Resource-of-last-resort framing: "Awards are provided according to need, but please consider the AKF ISP a resource of last resort and secure multiple sources of funding to reduce the amount you request"
Programme mix: priority to Master's programmes, PhD studies also considered

Mode rules: local/regional universities and distance learning programmes acceptable only if course quality is maintained; applications for part-time programmes and short-term courses are not considered
First-year rule: applicants must be entering their first year; students who have already enrolled in or commenced postgraduate studies are not eligible
Award structure: half grant and half loan, with 50 percent of the award amount repayable

Duration: Master's scholarships granted for the entire duration of the degree course; PhD scholarships awarded for the first two years, after which the student is expected to find funding from alternative sources
Coverage: "The award covers tuition expenses and student living expenses"
Explicit exclusions: "It does not cover, for example, the cost of international travel, clothing, furniture, or living expenses for family members."
Maintenance condition: good academic standing plus ongoing financial need must be demonstrated during the programme
Guarantor: a guarantor is required to co-sign the award agreement

Repayment trigger and timing: repayment of the loan component, which includes a service charge, begins six months after the first of graduation, termination of studies, or withdrawal of support following failure to meet the academic standards expected of ISP students
Application route: "Applications are handled by contacts in countries where AKF ISP is available", with an eligibility tool used "to verify your eligibility and learn how to contact our local team"
AKF publishes a long curated 'starter' list of other scholarships and financial assistance programmes for applicants who are told to secure multiple funding sources

official.description: The Rotary Foundation awards up to 50 fellowships a year for master's degrees and up to 120 for certificate studies at Rotary Peace Centers hosted by partner universities. Rotary states that the fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses.
purpose: Develop the capacity of peace and development professionals to become effective catalysts for peace
Support dedicated leaders from around the world through academic training, practice, and global networking opportunities
Train peace and development leaders who are committed to community and international service and the pursuit of peace
Build networks of academics, peace workers and Rotary members, and keep alumni connected to their regional peace fellow community
study_type: Full-time master's degree study at a Rotary Peace Center host university
Blended-learning postgraduate professional development certificate for working professionals
official.degree_award: Two tracks: a full master's degree at a Rotary Peace Center host university, or a postgraduate professional development certificate (no degree). Rotary states the fellowships may not be used for doctoral study.
official.duration: Master's programs last 15 to 24 months and include a two- to three-month field study designed by the participant. The professional development certificate program is one year of blended learning with 11 weeks of on-site participation (a two-week preliminary online course, a ten-week on-site course with field studies, a nine-month social change initiative with interactive online sessions, and a one-week on-site capstone seminar).
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle named by academic-year span (for example 2027-28, 2028-29). Applications are submitted between February and 15 May, and selected candidates are notified in November.
official.deadline_central_display: Submit your application between February and 15 May
official.deadline_note: Rotary publishes only a month-and-day closing date (15 May) with a February opening; no calendar year is published for the close, so deadline_date cannot be set from official sources.
official.funding_label: Rotary Peace Fellowship - up to 50 master's fellowships and up to 120 certificate fellowships awarded by The Rotary Foundation each year
official.tuition_coverage: Fully covered. Rotary states the fellowships cover tuition and fees.
official.living_cost_coverage: Fully covered. Rotary states the fellowships cover room and board.
official.travel_coverage: Fully covered. Rotary states the fellowships cover round-trip transportation.
official.tuition_rule: The Rotary Foundation fellowship pays the host Rotary Peace Center university directly for tuition and fees; being selected for the fellowship does not mean you have been admitted to the university, so the fellow must separately apply for admission to the university where the Peace Center is located.
covered_expenses: Tuition and fees
Room and board
Round-trip transportation
Internship and field-study expenses
benefits: Membership of a global network of peace fellows, academics, peace workers and Rotary members
Workshop series developing professional skills in peacebuilding and development
Networking opportunities with Rotary members and districts
A nine-month social change initiative with interactive online sessions (certificate program)
Reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities
eligibility: Be proficient in English
Have a bachelor's degree
Have a strong commitment to cross-cultural understanding and peace as shown through professional and academic achievements and personal or community service
Have the potential for leadership (master's program)
Demonstrate leadership skills (certificate program)
Have at least three years of full-time relevant experience in peace or development work (master's program)
Have at least five years of full-time relevant experience in peace or development work (certificate program)
Be able to explain how their plan to promote peace aligns with Rotary's mission (certificate program)

For Makerere University certificate candidates: either be from Africa, have worked in Africa, work with African communities or initiatives outside the continent, or demonstrate a compelling interest in learning about peacebuilding approaches within the region

For Bahçeşehir University certificate candidates: either be from the Middle East or North Africa, have worked in the region, work elsewhere around the world with communities or initiatives related to the Middle East or North Africa, or demonstrate a compelling interest in learning about peacebuilding approaches within the region

For Symbiosis International University certificate candidates: either be from Asia, have worked in Asia, work with communities or initiatives outside Asia, or demonstrate a compelling interest in learning about peacebuilding approaches within the region
general_eligibility: Be proficient in English
Have a bachelor's degree
Have a strong commitment to cross-cultural understanding and peace as shown through professional and academic achievements and personal or community service
People with disabilities and people from other diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply
ineligibility_conditions: Rotary Peace Fellowships may not be used for doctoral study
Active Rotary members, or Rotaract members who are also Rotary members, are not eligible
Employees of a Rotary club or district, Rotary International, or other Rotary entity are not eligible

Spouses, lineal descendants (children or grandchildren by blood or legal adoption), spouses of lineal descendants, or ancestors (parents or grandparents by blood) of any living person in these categories are not eligible
Former Rotary members and their relatives as described above, within 36 months of their resignation, are not eligible
Candidates currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program, or who will be enrolled in the upcoming academic year, are not eligible to apply
Candidates must have at least three years between the completion of their most recent academic degree program (undergraduate or graduate degree) and their intended start date for the fellowship

Rotary Peace Fellows who have completed the certificate program, master's program, or a Global Grant Scholarship must wait three years between the end date of that program and their intended start date for the fellowship

Request university transcripts now if you are applying to the master's program
Book IELTS or TOEFL if your program requires an English language proficiency test score
Identify academic and/or professional referees who will submit recommendations

Research the curriculum and programs at each Rotary Peace Center and, for the master's program, decide your ranked pair
important_advice_for_students: Submit original and authentic content based on your personal experience, knowledge and motivation. Rotary states that use of generative AI content is highly discouraged and that plagiarism will disqualify an application

Do not apply to more than you can genuinely complete: all applications are considered final upon submission

Do not stop at the Rotary stage. Being selected for the fellowship does not mean you have been admitted to the university, and you must apply separately for admission to the university where your Peace Center is located
For the master's program you will be asked to rank two Rotary Peace Centers; research the curriculum at each before you rank them

For the certificate program, come with a social change initiative to promote peace and development within the program region; the feasibility and impact of that initiative is a published selection criterion
All materials must be in English, so budget for certified translation of anything not already in English
Do not wait for a Rotary club to appear: build the peace and development experience and the leadership evidence first, since that is what the published selection criteria weigh

A spouse, child, grandchild, spouse of a lineal descendant, parent or grandparent in an excluded Rotary category

Still enrolled in, or about to enrol in, an undergraduate or graduate programme in the coming academic year

Applying for doctoral study, which Rotary states the fellowships may not be used for
Recommenders not entered before submission, leaving the application with missing or unverified recommendations
Plagiarism, or reliance on generative AI content, which Rotary says will disqualify an application
Certificate applicants who do not meet the published regional criterion for their chosen center

Visa application and issuance fees are not mentioned in the published coverage list
Personal belongings, laptop and electronics costs are not mentioned in the published coverage list
Any costs arising from a change of Rotary Peace Center after the November notification are not addressed in the published coverage list
Confirm directly with Rotary which additional expenses, if any, remain the fellow's responsibility before accepting

Master's fellows complete a self-designed two- to three-month field experience and present their master's research in a final seminar
Certificate fellows complete field studies, a preliminary online course, a ten-week on-site course, and a one-week on-site capstone seminar that overlaps with the incoming cohort
Certificate fellows design and carry out a nine-month social change initiative with interactive online sessions
Both tracks: after the program, share your own work and experience, stay in touch with peace fellows in your region and maintain strong connections with Rotary members

official.deadline_central_display: Online applications must be submitted by the candidate between 20th April 2026 and 11th May 2026 at 6:00pm Italian time.
official.deadline_note: The central IYT scholarship application window closed at 6:00pm Italian time on 11 May 2026 for the 2026-2027 edition. Separately, applicants must submit a pre-admission application to the chosen university under that university's own procedures and admission deadlines, and scholarship eligibility is conditional on admission within the deadlines set by the IYT Technical Committee with the universities. Renewal applications for the 2026-2027 cohort were due by 20 July 2027.
official.status_note: Article 5.2 of the official current call sets the 2026 application window as 20 April to 11 May 2026 at 6:00pm Italian time, which closed before today's date of 1 October 2026.

Article 11.1 sets the annual scholarship at EUR 10,800, paid quarterly as EUR 4,800 then EUR 3,000 and EUR 3,000.
official.funding_label: EUR 10,800 annual scholarship plus exemption from enrolment fees and university contributions, for 9 months from 1 October 2026
benefits: Annual scholarship of EUR 10,800 paid quarterly into an Italian bank account in the recipient's name
Exemption from enrolment fees and university contributions (with named exceptions)
Compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association as part of the course
eligibility: Be a citizen of one of the listed eligible countries and permanently resident there
Hold an academic qualification valid for enrolment in a Master's/Postgraduate degree programme at the chosen institution; students who are about to graduate are not eligible
Not be currently studying at an Italian university and not have obtained an Italian university degree

Students currently studying at an Italian university and those who have obtained an Italian university degree are not eligible.

official.description: Invest Your Talent in Italy (IYT), now in its 11th edition, is a scholarship programme of the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia for citizens of 23 listed countries to attend a higher education course in Italy at Master's or Postgraduate level. Winners receive an annual scholarship of EUR 10,800 paid quarterly over a 9-month period starting 1 October 2026, plus exemption from enrolment fees and university contributions, with certain named exceptions. Applications for the 2026-2027 edition ran from 20 April to 11 May 2026 at 6:00pm Italian time and included a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association.

official.description: The University of Padova offers up to 76 Padua International Excellence Scholarships to brilliant international students enrolling in an English-taught first-cycle (Bachelor's) or master's degree course. Each award is EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year plus exemption from student fees, and beneficiaries remain liable for the regional fee and the revenue stamp.
purpose: Support brilliant international students who wish to attend an English-taught first-cycle/Bachelor's degree course or master's degree at the University of Padova
Attract highly talented prospective students to degree programmes completely held in English
Recognise academic excellence in the field of study and the quality and results of a candidate's previous academic career
study_type: Enrolment in a degree programme completely held in English at the University of Padova
official.degree_award: Full degree. The scholarship is attached to enrolment in a first-cycle/Bachelor's, single-cycle or master's degree programme and is discontinued once the stated maximum duration is reached.
official.duration: Maximum 2 years for master's degree programmes; maximum 3 years for bachelor's and/or single-cycle degree programmes. At the end of that period beneficiaries are required to pay the student tuition fees due until graduation.
official.application_cycle: Annual. The application for the degree course of your interest automatically makes you eligible to compete for the award; the scholarship results are published according to the deadlines specified in the Admission Notice.
official.deadline_central_display: Apply to an English-taught degree at the University of Padova within the deadline; scholarship results will be published according to the deadlines specified in the Admission Notice. More information will be available in the Calls for Application published in November 2026.
official.deadline_note: The University states that candidates must apply within the deadline of the degree course Admission Notice and that full Call for Application detail will be published in November 2026. No specific calendar date is published on this page, so deadline_date is left null.
official.funding_label: Padua International Excellence Scholarship - up to 76 scholarships, EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year plus exemption from student fees
official.funding_period: per academic year, paid in 2 (two) installments of EUR 4,000.00 gross each
official.tuition_coverage: Exemption from student fees is included in the award, but beneficiaries are only required to pay the regional fee and the revenue stamp per academic year. After the maximum scholarship duration, beneficiaries pay the student tuition fees due until graduation.
official.tuition_rule: The University of Padova grants exemption from student fees as part of the award; the beneficiary is not exempt from the regional fee or the revenue stamp, which must be paid each academic year. At the end of the maximum scholarship duration the beneficiary must pay the student tuition fees due until graduation.
official.host_institution_fee: Beneficiaries are only required to pay the regional fee and the revenue stamp per academic year.

Exemption from student fees for each academic year
not_covered_or_excluded: Regional tuition fee, payable by the beneficiary each academic year

official.description: The Bicocca International Scholarship Programme (BISP) is reserved for international students resident abroad, holding a foreign qualification and admitted to one of seventeen named English-taught degree programmes at the University of Milano-Bicocca. Each scholarship consists of EUR 10,000 per academic year (gross amount) and includes exemption from tuition fees; beneficiaries are not exempt from paying the administrative fee and the regional tax.
purpose: Provide financial support to talented international students and encourage access to degree programmes at the University of Milano-Bicocca
Reward academic excellence and global potential among the best students from all over the world
Support the University's growing international community, with five scholarships dedicated to each international course to ensure a wide and fair opportunity for top-tier candidates
degree_levels: Single-cycle degree (Laurea Magistrale a Ciclo Unico)
study_type: Full-time enrolment in one of the seventeen English-taught degree programmes listed in Article 1 of the call
official.degree_award: Full degree. The scholarship attaches to admission to a named Bachelor's, single-cycle or Master's degree programme and is renewable for up to 3 years for Bachelor and single-cycle degrees and 2 years for Master degrees.
official.duration: Renewable for a maximum of 3 years for Bachelor (Laurea) programmes and single-cycle degree programmes (Laurea Magistrale a Ciclo Unico), and 2 years for Master degree programmes (Laurea Magistrale).
official.application_cycle: Annual, named by academic year. The call read is the Call for Applications for the Bicocca International Scholarship Programme A.Y. 2026/27, published January 2026 and last updated 16/07/2026.
official.deadline_central_display: For free entrance (open access) courses: be admitted and have confirmed the admission offer by 15 March 2026 at the latest. Priority is given to candidates who have applied to the first Call for Admission. Each limited access course has its own admission deadlines, to be found on apply.unimib.it.
official.deadline_institutional: Limited access programmes run to their own course deadlines, published on apply.unimib.it; scholarship results for limited access programmes are published following the publication of the admission ranking list.
official.deadline_note: The only hard date published for the scholarship itself is 15 March 2026, and it applies to free access (open access) courses. Limited access courses use their own admission deadlines.
official.funding_label: Bicocca International Scholarship Programme (BISP) - EUR 10,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from tuition fees; five scholarships per eligible course, 100 in total
official.funding_period: per academic year, paid in two instalments in the first year
official.tuition_coverage: Tuition fees are exempted for the scholarship holder. Beneficiaries are not exempt from paying the administrative fee and the regional tax. A withdrawing student retains the tuition fee exemptions for the academic year of reference but must refund the amounts received.
official.tuition_rule: The scholarship includes exemption from tuition fees at the University of Milano-Bicocca for the awarded degree programme. The University pays the tuition exemption directly and requires the beneficiary to enrol for renewal years by paying only the administrative fee. Beneficiaries remain liable for the administrative fee and the regional tax.
official.host_institution_fee: Beneficiaries are not exempt from paying the administrative fee and the regional tax. For renewal years, enrolment is possible by paying only the administrative fee.
official.tax_status: Bicocca International Scholarships are considered as a form of income by the current Italian tax regulation and are subject to the tax regulations in force. The award is published as a gross amount.

Exemption from tuition fees

important_advice_for_students: Do not look for a BISP application form. The University states applicants are not required to send or fill out any application form other than applying to the relevant Bachelor's or Master's programme

Do not confuse the scholarship with a fee waiver. You get EUR 10,000 gross per year plus tuition exemption, but you still pay the administrative fee and the regional tax, and the call says nothing about accommodation, food or travel
Budget for the tax. The call states the scholarship is considered income under current Italian tax regulation and is subject to the tax regulations in force, and the amount is published as gross
Bank your first exam. The second instalment depends on passing at least one exam in the first semester, and credits recognised from previous studies are not counted towards it

Do not accept DSU benefits in parallel. The scholarship cannot be combined with the DSU regional scholarship or with DSU-connected benefits such as the meal card, housing or extraordinary grant; if you are offered an incompatible award you must choose within ten days of the most recent awarding

official.description: The ISU Bocconi Scholarship supports students with financial need at Bocconi who also meet a published merit requirement, using the Italian national income statement or its non-resident equivalent. For a.y. 2026-2027 the published benefits are a free daily meal valued at 829 euros, a second free daily meal, preferential restaurant and cafe rates, a 200-hour work-study opportunity at 14 euros per hour and a 3,000 euro cash contribution for high-merit applicants. Applications run in session-specific windows for a.y. 2027-2028, from 12 November 2026 for first year BSc and law international candidates through 25 June 2027 for PhD and later-year students, and must be submitted every year of enrolment.
official.program_type: University need-based scholarship with merit requirement (student fees, grants and bursaries category)
official.coverage: Published benefits for a.y. 2026-2027 cover a daily meal, preferential dining rates, a work-study placement and a possible 3,000 euro cash contribution, with no stated tuition fee waiver and no stated coverage of travel, so fully_funded is false.
official.funding: Need-based (partial to full) — economic thresholds set annually by the Lombardy Region (a.y. 2026-27 reference values: ISEE/ISEEU Parificato no higher than €26,887.93; ISPE/ISPEU Parificato no higher than €58,452.06), plus free daily meal worth €829.00 (2026-27 figure), a 200-hour work-study programme, cash stipend and a possible 50% tuition-fee reduction. The a.y. 2027-28 economic thresholds are not yet published.

Sign every document with a handwritten signature matching your ID document signature
Submit only in your own session window, as only one application per session is allowed
Have your non-resident status documents ready, as these are uploaded after the main application

Submitting incomplete or inconsistent documentation, which results in no benefit at all
Submitting an ISEEU Parificato certificate later than the 11 January 2027 correction deadline for Early session international candidates
Ignoring the notification messages, which Bocconi sends only through the Notifications area of MyApplication
Combining the scholarship with the ISU reduction for low-income households, which is not permitted
Relying on dates shown inside the online procedure, which are standard system dates, not the real deadlines

official.description: Sapienza University of Rome announces a call for applications for admission to 94 PhD Programmes of the 42nd cycle, based on qualifications and examinations, or examinations only. A PhD programme is the third cycle of studies and the highest level of university education in the Italian system, lasts three years, and entry is granted through a competitive selection process. Sapienza PhD scholarships are entirely financed by Sapienza at a published annual gross amount of EUR 16,243.00, plus a research budget equal to 10% of the scholarship.
purpose: Enable candidates to develop the skills required to carry out highly qualified research activities
Train researchers through the third cycle of studies, the highest level of university education within the Italian academic system
Allocate Sapienza PhD scholarships to the individual courses following resolution No. 108/2026 of the Academic Senate dated 15/05/2026
Attract and support doctoral candidates including through joint and inter-university PhD programmes agreed with funding bodies and companies
study_type: Research doctoral study based on qualifications and examinations, or examinations only
Full-time doctoral research, with a self-designed or supervisor-guided project developed within a doctoral school
official.degree_award: Full PhD degree (Doctor of Philosophy), third cycle. Admission requires a second-cycle degree. Some programmes are joint degrees, for example Astronomy with the University of Rome Tor Vergata, where a joint degree is awarded on completion of the cycle.
official.duration: The duration of a PhD programme is three years. The duration of the scholarship is equal to the legal duration of the programme.
official.application_cycle: Annual, named by academic year and cycle number (Academic Year 2026/2027 - 42nd Cycle, issued by Rectoral Decree No. 998/2026 of 15/05/2026, Prot. n. 68062/2026). A separate pre-selection call exists for citizens of the People's Republic of China under the Sapienza-CSC agreement.
official.deadline_central_display: Applications must be submitted by 17 June 2026 at 14:00 (local time - CET) without any exception. The application fee must be paid through the PagoPA system no later than 17 June 2026 at 14:00 (local time - CET).
official.deadline_institutional: Each individual PhD programme publishes its own admission procedures and evaluation criteria on its programme web page under the 'Call for application (42nd cycle)' section, and holds its examination dates separately. Candidates who anticipate completing their master's degree by 31 October 2026 must also have obtained the required degree by that date, or are admitted with reserve.
official.deadline_note: A separate published deadline exists for the China Scholarship Council pre-selection: 24 February 2026 at 14:00 (local time - CET) for Chinese candidates applying under the Sapienza-CSC agreement for the 42nd cycle.
official.funding_label: Sapienza PhD scholarship (scholarships entirely financed by Sapienza, plus scholarships financed by Departments, Departments of Excellence, public or private bodies, other Universities, or the Italian Science Fund FIS)
official.funding_period: per year gross of statutory withholdings, paid on a monthly basis, for the legal duration of the programme
official.living_cost_coverage: No tuition applies to a PhD programme as such, but all admitted candidates must pay a stamp duty of EUR 16.00 and a regional tax of EUR 140.00 on enrolment.
official.travel_coverage: The scholarship amount is increased up to 50% for authorised periods abroad up to 12 months (extendable to a total of 18 months for joint PhDs with international institutions). Every PhD student, with or without scholarship, has a budget for research activities in Italy and abroad corresponding to 10% of the amount of the scholarship.
official.tuition_rule: PhD programmes at Sapienza do not carry tuition fees. All admitted candidates must instead pay a stamp duty of EUR 16.00 and a regional tax of EUR 140.00 on enrolment. Admitted candidates with a recognised disability of at least 66% or a disability recognised under Article 3, paragraph 3 or paragraph 1 of Law No. 104 of 05/02/1992 are exempt from paying the regional tax and must evidence their status by emailing ufficio.dottorato@uniroma1.it.
official.host_institution_fee: Stamp duty of EUR 16.00 plus regional tax of EUR 140.00 payable by all admitted candidates on enrolment, with a regional tax exemption for recognised disabled candidates.
official.tax_status: The annual amount of the scholarship is EUR 16,243.00 gross of statutory withholdings to be paid by students, pursuant to Ministerial Decree No. 247/2022. For international students, payment of the scholarship may in any case be made only after obtaining a tax identification number (codice fiscale) issued by the competent authority or institution. The EUR 19,800.00 top-up is described as gross of welfare charges borne by the recipient.
covered_expenses: Annual PhD scholarship of EUR 16,243.00 gross paid monthly for the legal duration of the programme
Research activity budget in Italy and abroad equal to 10% of the scholarship amount, for every PhD student with or without scholarship
Scholarship increase of up to 50% for authorised periods abroad up to 12 months, extendable to 18 months for joint PhDs with international institutions
Top-up to EUR 19,800.00 for the first potential winner in the final rankings who holds a degree obtained abroad and resides abroad (maximum one per PhD programme)
Equivalent 50% allowance for PhD students without a scholarship for authorised periods of study or research abroad, maximum 12 months
not_covered_or_excluded: Stamp duty of EUR 16.00 payable by all admitted candidates
Regional tax of EUR 140.00 payable by all admitted candidates, unless exempt for recognised disability
The non-refundable participation/application fee for admission, payable through PagoPA (the amount is not stated in the call text read)

PhD scholarships cannot be combined with research fellowships or other scholarships awarded for any reason, except grants from national or foreign institutions intended to integrate the training or research activities of scholarship holders through stays abroad, and funding from the Fondo Giovani MUR
Positions without scholarship, for which it is not possible to compete directly; non-funded positions are allocated only after completion of the acceptance process for funded positions
Scholarship for any PhD programme that is not accredited under Ministerial Decree No. 226/2021 will not be activated for the 42nd cycle
Third-party funded scholarships are conditional on confirmation of the funding commitment through a specific agreement, and payment is conditional on the funder disbursing the money to Sapienza
benefits: Monthly payment of a EUR 16,243.00 gross annual scholarship for the legal duration of the programme
Research activity budget in Italy and abroad equal to 10% of the scholarship amount
Scholarship increase of up to 50% for authorised periods abroad, up to 12 months or 18 months for joint PhDs with international institutions
Possible top-up to EUR 19,800.00 for the first-ranked candidate holding a foreign degree and residing abroad
Regional tax exemption on enrolment for candidates with a recognised disability
eligibility: Access to the PhD programme is open to individuals of any age and nationality

By 31 October 2026, hold a degree from the pre-Ministerial Decree 509/99 system (so-called 'old system'), or laurea specialistica and/or magistrale (Ministerial Decree No. 509/99, Ministerial Decree No. 270/2004)
Hold a second-level academic qualification issued by institutions belonging to the AFAM sector (Higher Education for Art, Music and Dance)

Hold an official foreign degree corresponding to the second cycle according to the Bologna Process qualifications framework and level 7 according to the European Qualifications Framework, which allows access to the PhD programme at academic institutions in the country where it was issued and is recognized as suitable for access to the PhD programme in Italy (Master's degree or equivalent title, in any case with a written final thesis), with no 'substantial difference' according to the Lisbon Convention principles and the CIMEA national methodology
Pay the application fee through the PagoPA system integrated into the online application form by the deadline
Declare the scholarship(s) they intend to compete for, indicating potential preferences in order of priority
Self-declare possession of the admission requirements pursuant to Article 76 of Presidential Decree No. 445/2000
general_eligibility: Open to individuals of any age and nationality
Requires a second-cycle degree (Master's, specialist, single-cycle degree, or an equivalent foreign qualification), with a written final thesis in the case of a foreign qualification
Candidates who obtain the required degree between the date of submission of the application and 31 October 2026 are admitted 'with reserve' until they obtain it
ineligibility_conditions: Those who have already benefited, even partially, from a scholarship awarded for attending a PhD or equivalent programme at this University or another university in Italy cannot benefit from another PhD scholarship; on admission they must forgo the awarded scholarship if positions without scholarship are available
Those who have already benefited from a PhD scholarship, even partially, cannot receive a second one for the same qualification
Simultaneous enrolment in more than one PhD programme, or in both a PhD programme and a first- or second-level Master's programme, for the same academic year is not allowed
Enrolment and registration for the second year of a PhD programme is incompatible with entering into a research contract pursuant to Article 22 of Law No. 240 of 30/12/2010

The annual gross personal taxable income limit to be eligible for the PhD scholarship is set at EUR 16,243.00, excluding the scholarship itself; on reaching the limit the PhD student must reimburse all scholarship instalments unduly received in the relevant tax year (1 January - 31 December of each year)

PhD scholarships cannot be combined with research fellowships or other scholarships awarded for any reason, except grants from national or foreign institutions for stays abroad and Fondo Giovani MUR funding; in case of subsequent incompatibility any unduly received instalment must be reimbursed

It is not possible to compete for non-scholarship positions; a candidate may renounce a scholarship only within the limit of the number of non-scholarship positions announced in the call, according to ranking order

Falsity in the self-certifications leads to exclusion from the competitive tests, or forfeiture if already enrolled as a winner, without prejudice to criminal sanctions under Article 76 of Presidential Decree No. 445/2000
For PhD programmes not accredited under Ministerial Decree No. 226/2021, activation for the 42nd cycle will not proceed
In written examinations, use of a different ink pen, use of pencil unless required, signature, or correction fluids are reasons for exclusion
official.citizenship_residency: Open to individuals of any age and nationality. Non-EU citizens requiring an entry visa for long-term stays in Italy must hold a visa for 'post-graduate studies' and provide the Receipt of First Residence Permit Request for study purposes.
official.international_eligibility: Foreign qualifications are admitted where they correspond to the second cycle in the Bologna Process framework and level 7 EQF, allow PhD access in the country of issue, are recognised as suitable for access in Italy, and present no 'substantial difference' under the Lisbon Convention and CIMEA methodology. Applicants holding a degree obtained abroad and residing abroad who are the first potential winner in the final rankings (maximum one per PhD programme) receive an increased scholarship of EUR 19,800.00. A separate pre-selection call is published for citizens of the People's Republic of China under the Sapienza-CSC agreement.

masters: Admission requires a second-cycle degree (laurea specialistica/magistrale, or equivalent foreign second-cycle/level 7 EQF qualification with a written final thesis)
Candidates who complete the required degree between application submission and 31 October 2026 are admitted with reserve

phd: The PhD is the third cycle of studies and lasts three years

Those who already obtained a PhD degree without a scholarship may apply provided the predominant research topics and scientific-disciplinary sectors of the aspired PhD programme differ from those of the PhD programme for which the title was obtained
For PhD programmes with multiple curricula there is a single competition with a single Selection Committee, and a unified ranking list

host_requirements: The PhD programme must be one of the 94 programmes listed in Annex A, which is an integral part of the call, and belong to the Doctoral School indicated there where established
Enrolment must be completed by the deadline specified in the notification sent after publication of the final rankings, or the candidate is considered to have withdrawn

Foreign degree holders must additionally provide, for enrolment, the certificate of the academic qualification, the transcript of records, and a CIMEA statement of comparability or a Declaration of Value or a Diploma Supplement, all translated into Italian or English and authenticated with an Apostille or legalized by the Italian Diplomatic Representation

All candidates must provide a passport or, for EU citizens, a valid Identity Card, a tax identification number (codice fiscale), and, where applicable, a visa for 'post-graduate studies' and residence permit documents

Candidates requiring a visa for postgraduate studies must access the UNIVERSITALY portal and complete the 'pre-enrolment application', which must be validated by the University PhD Offices and then submitted to the diplomatic or consular representation in their country of residence
PhD programmes subject to accreditation under Ministerial Decree No. 226/2021 only; unaccredited programmes are not activated for the 42nd cycle
requirements: Submit the application online through INFOSTUD: log in, click on the 'PhD Programmes' section, select 'Submit a new application', fill out the online form in all its parts, upload the required documents, close and submit

documents: For candidates with a qualification obtained in a country of the European Union: a self-certification of the academic qualification with list of exams and related grades in Italian or English, pursuant to Article 3 of the call

Valid ID for sitting the examinations

For enrolment of foreign degree holders: transcript of records (ToR) translated into Italian or English with Apostille or legalisation

Passport or, for EU citizens, a valid Identity Card

Valid Residence Permit (only for non-EU citizens regularly living in Italy); if expired, the Receipt of Renewal Request

document_format_rules: Qualification documentation must be in Italian or English

SLD certification must be detailed and clear, indicating nosological codes and an explicit reference to the specific type of SLD (reading and/or writing and/or calculation); if it does not state that the issuer is accredited, a note providing evidence of such accreditation must be added
Disability and SLD support requests must be submitted strictly by the deadline of the call and must specify the type of support required
In written examinations candidates must only use a black ink biro pen; the paper provided must not be signed or made recognisable in any way, under penalty of exclusion
The application must be submitted through the INFOSTUD online form by uploading the required documents; once submitted it can no longer be modified or resubmitted
No file type, file size or page limit is published in the call
selection_criteria: The purpose of the admission test is to guarantee an adequate comparative evaluation of the candidates
All testing modalities and the grids containing the evaluation criteria are published on the web page of each individual PhD programme under the 'Call for application (42nd cycle)' section
A foreign language test may be required, as reported on the individual PhD Programme web pages
Tie-break for a position covered by scholarship: the candidate with the less favourable economic condition prevails, pursuant to Prime Ministerial Decree No. 159, Article 8, paragraph 4 of 05/12/2013

Tie-break for a position without scholarship, in order: higher graduation mark for the title giving access to the PhD; then higher average mark; then achievement of the degree in the shortest possible time considering the legal duration of the programme; then the younger candidate prevails

For PhD programmes with multiple curricula there is a single competition and a single Selection Committee; the examinations are the same for all curricula, though a separate set of written questions may be set for each curriculum
official.selection_notes: Selection Committees are appointed pursuant to the Sapienza PhD Regulations; for third-party or Department-funded scholarships the Selection Committees may be supplemented by a scientific expert from the funded projects. Candidates must attend examinations at the stated date, time and venue without waiting for further convocation and provide valid ID. Oral tests may be held via videoconference if specified on the programme web page, or may be requested on documented valid grounds at the absolute discretion of the Selection Committee. Results for each completed examination are published on the individual PhD programme web page, identifying candidates by matricola, and are also made available on the candidate's personal application page. Final rankings are published exclusively on https://www.uniroma1.it/it/pagina/elenco-dei-corsi-di-dottorato, indicating total score, any curriculum selected or assigned, and scholarships awarded, and candidates are admitted in descending order of merit until all announced positions are filled. Successful candidates are notified by email to the address given in the application; failure to complete enrolment within the specified timeframe is treated as withdrawal and the position passes to the next candidate. Any renunciation of the PhD programme or of the scholarship is irrevocable, and no further offers are made in the event of subsequent reassignments.

application_readiness_checklist: Open Annex A of the call and confirm your PhD programme is one of the 94 listed, and read that programme's own web page under 'Call for application (42nd cycle)' for its specific procedures, criteria, testing modality and examination dates
Confirm you will hold a second-cycle degree by 31 October 2026; if you complete it later you are admitted only 'with reserve'

Check the EUR 16,243.00 gross personal taxable income limit, excluding the scholarship; going over it means repaying the year's instalments
Confirm you have never held, even partially, a PhD scholarship for the same qualification at any Italian university
Confirm you are not enrolling in another PhD programme or a first- or second-level Master's programme in the same academic year
Confirm you are not entering a research contract under Article 22 of Law 240/2010 while registering for the second PhD year

Prepare valid ID for the examination, and a black ink biro if there is a written test
