important_advice_for_students: Start early and finish early. The call states that complaints about system malfunctions near the deadline are not accepted and that the participation fee is non-refundable under any circumstances, so there is no upside to submitting in the last hour

Read your own programme's web page, not just the general call. The testing modality, the evaluation-criteria grids, the examination dates, whether a foreign language test is required and whether oral tests can be by videoconference are all published per programme, and Annex A links to each one
Do not sign the examination paper. Signing it, using anything other than a black ink biro, or using correction fluids is a stated ground for exclusion
Do not apply to a programme you cannot finish financially. You pay a EUR 16.00 stamp duty and a EUR 140.00 regional tax on enrolment, and the scholarship is the only recurring income published

Track your income carefully. The eligibility limit is EUR 16,243.00 gross personal taxable income excluding the scholarship itself, and exceeding it means repaying all instalments received in that tax year

Do not accept a second PhD scholarship. Holding one already, even partially, for the same qualification, disqualifies you, and if you are admitted you must forgo the awarded scholarship if non-scholarship positions are available
You cannot compete directly for a non-scholarship position. Non-funded positions are allocated only after all funded positions are accepted, in ranking order

If you are ranked but not funded, do not assume you are out. The rankings also record eligibility assessments for specific scholarships, and a funded awardee who renounces or fails to enrol causes reassignment in ranking order to the first eligible candidate
Renunciation is irreversible. The call states that no further offers of positions or scholarships are made in the event of subsequent reassignments

If you are already enrolled in a previous year on a non-scholarship position and win again, you must formally withdraw from the previous enrolment and notify the PhD Office - Programmes and Careers before completing the new enrolment
Check that your programme is accredited under Ministerial Decree No. 226/2021; activation for the 42nd cycle does not proceed for unaccredited programmes
For Chinese applicants there is a separate, earlier route: the Sapienza-CSC pre-selection call, with its own 24 February 2026 deadline and a restricted list of programmes in the Appendix

Budget the abroad uplift correctly. Authorised periods abroad raise the scholarship by up to 50% for up to 12 months, extendable to 18 months for joint PhDs with international institutions, and non-scholarship students get an equivalent 50% allowance

Beware the incompatibility. The scholarship cannot be combined with research fellowships or other scholarships, except stays-abroad integration grants and Fondo Giovani MUR funding, and later incompatibility means repaying what you received
common_rejection_risks: A non-EU qualification that is not translated into Italian or English, or not authenticated with an Apostille or legalized by the Italian Diplomatic Representation
A foreign qualification presenting a 'substantial difference' under the Lisbon Convention and CIMEA methodology, or one that does not allow PhD access in the country where it was issued
No written final thesis in the case of a foreign qualification
Not holding the required second-cycle degree by 31 October 2026
Failing to close and submit the application in INFOSTUD, or failing to pay the application fee through PagoPA by 17 June 2026 at 14:00 CET
Paying outside the integrated PagoPA system, for example an unsolicited PagoPA payment, which the call states will not be accepted
Falsity in the self-certification, which leads to exclusion or forfeiture plus criminal sanctions under Article 76 of Presidential Decree No. 445/2000
Signing or marking the written examination paper, using a pen other than black ink, using pencil when not required, or using correction fluids
Not attending at the stated date, time and venue without waiting for further convocation, or arriving without valid ID
Exceeding the EUR 16,243.00 gross personal taxable income limit, which requires repayment of that year's instalments
Having already held, even partially, a PhD scholarship for the same qualification
Enrolling in more than one PhD programme, or in a PhD plus a first- or second-level Master's programme, in the same academic year
Entering a research contract under Article 22 of Law 240/2010 while registering for the second PhD year
Applying to a PhD programme that is not accredited under Ministerial Decree No. 226/2021
Missing the enrolment deadline in the notification, which is treated as withdrawal
Missing the disability or SLD support request deadline, or submitting certification that does not name nosological codes and the specific type of SLD
Missing the 5-day documentation deadline for industrial PhD reserved positions or for supernumerary foreign state scholarship positions
estimated_uncovered_costs: Stamp duty of EUR 16.00 payable by every admitted candidate on enrolment
Regional tax of EUR 140.00 payable by every admitted candidate on enrolment, unless exempt for a recognised disability
The non-refundable participation/application fee for admission, payable through PagoPA; the call requires it but does not state the amount in the text read
Living costs in Rome, which the scholarship amount is not itemised against and the research budget of 10% is for research activities rather than subsistence
Books, equipment, conference travel and consumables beyond the 10% research activity budget in Italy and abroad
Costs of obtaining the Apostille or legalisation of qualification documents, and of sworn translations
UNIVERSITALY pre-enrolment and visa application and issuance costs for non-EU citizens requiring a visa for 'post-graduate studies'
First residence permit costs for non-EU citizens
Any fees or income loss arising from a suspension of the PhD programme, during which the scholarship is suspended for up to six months

official.description: IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: the official Taiwan scholarship sources read on 2026-10-01 do not describe a programme called the 'Elite Scholarship for University Lecturers from South & Southeast Asia'. What they describe is the Taiwan Scholarship system, run jointly by the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Science and Technology, and divided into three named programmes - the MOE Scholarship, the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship and the MOFA Scholarship. Everything recorded below is published for that system and is labelled with the programme it belongs to. The framework that is well established is: every application goes to the local Taiwan Representative Office (ROC overseas mission), the applicant must also apply separately to a university in Taiwan, tuition and miscellaneous expenses are capped at NTD 40,000 per semester under the MOE Scholarship with the student paying the excess, living allowances run from NTD 15,000 to NTD 33,000 per month depending on programme and degree level, and no award may exceed five years in total. The lecturer-specific scholarship named in this record's title is not among the three programmes published, so its amount, quota, eligibility and deadline are deliberately null.
purpose: The Ministry of Education (MOE) Taiwan Scholarship Program provides tuition and miscellaneous expenses of up to NTD 40,000 each semester and a monthly living allowance of NTD 15,000 or NTD 20,000 (published MOE programme description).

The published qualification test for the system is academic and personal: international students who must be foreign nationals with a secondary school graduation diploma or a post-secondary degree, who have shown excellent academic performance, and who are of good moral character (published Scholarship Comparison Table).
All scholarship applications must be submitted to the local Taiwan Representative Office, and applicants must apply separately to a university or college in Taiwan for admission (published).
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or development-goal requirement is published for the MOE, Huayu Enrichment or MOFA scholarships. The published qualifying test is individual: excellent academic performance and good moral character.

The only published objective with a geographic dimension is the country condition - eligibility is tied to countries that have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, or have been recognised as friendly relations with Taiwan by MOFA - which is a diplomatic criterion, not a development goal.
No published rule addresses lecturers as an occupational group, so no lecturer-specific targeting could be established.
study_type: Degree study in Taiwan at a university or college, or Language Enhancement Program study
On-campus study at a participating Taiwanese institution; the published scholarship period runs from 1 September to 31 August of the following year, with summer classes excepted in principle
official.degree_award: A degree awarded by the Taiwanese university or college the recipient attends. The scholarship itself confers no qualification, and no published rule permits the award to be held while not enrolled.
official.duration: Bachelor 4 years; Master 2 years; Doctoral 4 years (MOE Scholarship). LEP 1 year (MOE and MOFA Scholarships). The Huayu Enrichment Scholarship is granted in blocks of 2 months (summer term), 3, 6, 9 months or 1 year (12 months). No award may exceed a total of five years in any programme, and award periods must be continuous with no breaks.
official.application_cycle: Annual, routed through diplomatic missions. All scholarship applications must be submitted to the local Taiwan Representative Office, and the applicant must apply separately to a university or college in Taiwan for admission. Cycle dates are set by the overseas mission and are published on the mission's own materials, not on the central scholarship site; the central site publishes guidelines and forms, not a global deadline.
official.deadline_central_display: No central deadline is published. The scholarship site publishes guidelines, forms and comparison tables, and directs every applicant to their local Taiwan Representative Office, which owns the application timing.
official.deadline_institutional: Two deadlines apply and neither is central: the deadline set by the local Taiwan Representative Office for the scholarship application, and the separate admission deadline of the Taiwanese university or college the applicant applies to. Both are mission- and university-specific and are published only by those bodies.
official.funding_label: Three published programmes with different structures. MOE Scholarship: up to NTD 40,000 each semester towards approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses, with any excess payable by the student, plus a monthly living allowance of NTD 28,000 (Bachelor) or NTD 15,000 (LEP) per month. MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship: no tuition or miscellaneous contribution; living allowance NTD 20,000 (Master/Doctoral) or NTD 28,000 (LEP) per month. MOFA Scholarship: no tuition or miscellaneous contribution; living allowance NTD 28,000 (Master/Doctoral) or NTD 33,000 (LEP) per month, plus one-way economy-class plane tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan, with recipients responsible for all other expenses and MOFA providing no other subsidy.
official.funding_period: per month for the living allowance; per semester for the tuition and miscellaneous expense cap
official.tuition_coverage: Only under the MOE Scholarship, and only as a cap. The MOE will pay up to NTD 40,000 each semester for each recipient's approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses; if those exceed a total of NTD 40,000, the remaining amount must be paid to the university or college by the student. The MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship and the MOFA Scholarship publish 'N/A' for tuition and miscellaneous expenses, so those two programmes pay nothing toward fees.
official.living_cost_coverage: Yes, as a published monthly living allowance, but the rate varies by programme and by degree level: NTD 28,000 per month for a Bachelor under the MOE Scholarship, NTD 15,000 per month for an LEP under the MOE Scholarship, NTD 20,000 (Master/Doctoral) and NTD 28,000 (LEP) per month under the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship, and NTD 28,000 (Master/Doctoral) and NTD 33,000 (LEP) per month under the MOFA Scholarship.
official.travel_coverage: Only under the MOFA Scholarship, and only one way: MOFA will provide recipients with one-way economy-class plane tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan. Recipients are responsible for all expenses during their stay in Taiwan, and MOFA will not provide any other subsidies. No travel component is published for the MOE Scholarship or the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship.
official.tuition_rule: Capped, not full. Under the MOE Scholarship the MOE pays up to NTD 40,000 each semester for approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses, and the published rule is explicit that 'If these exceed a total amount of NTD40,000, the remaining amount must be paid to the university/college by the student.' The published exclusions also allow a university to subsidise the outstanding amount, and that subsidy is expressly permitted to coexist with the scholarship. The Huayu Enrichment and MOFA scholarships pay nothing toward fees at all.
official.home_tuition_rule: Not published. The published tuition rule addresses only fees payable to the Taiwanese university or college, and the Huayu Enrichment and MOFA tuition lines are published as 'N/A'. Nothing addresses fees owed to, or by, an institution outside Taiwan.
official.host_institution_fee: Not published as a host fee. The only host-related published figures are the NTD 40,000 per semester cap the MOE pays towards approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses, the excess of which the student must pay to the university or college, and the separate published list of universities and colleges that give Taiwan Scholarship recipients a discount on tuition and/or miscellaneous expenses - a discount that is separate from, and additional to, the scholarship cap.
official.tax_status: Not published. None of the pages read states any tax treatment of the living allowance, the tuition and miscellaneous expense payments or the MOFA airfare.
covered_expenses: MOE Scholarship: up to NTD 40,000 each semester towards approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses, with the excess payable by the student
MOE Scholarship: monthly living allowance of NTD 28,000 (Bachelor degree) or NTD 15,000 (LEP)
MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship: monthly living allowance of NTD 20,000 (Master/Doctoral) or NTD 28,000 (LEP); no tuition or miscellaneous expenses
MOFA Scholarship: monthly living allowance of NTD 28,000 (Master/Doctoral) or NTD 33,000 (LEP); no tuition or miscellaneous expenses
MOFA Scholarship only: one-way economy-class plane tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan
not_covered_or_excluded: Tuition and miscellaneous expenses above NTD 40,000 per semester under the MOE Scholarship - the excess 'must be paid to the university/college by the student'
All tuition and miscellaneous expenses under the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship and the MOFA Scholarship (published as N/A)
All living costs beyond the published monthly allowance

Return travel and any travel other than MOFA's one-way economy-class direct flights - under the MOFA Scholarship, 'Recipients are responsible for all expenses during their stay in Taiwan. MOFA will not provide any other subsidies'
Any total award period beyond five years, for any programme
Broken or gapped award periods - under the MOFA Scholarship, 'Scholarship award periods must be continuous, with no breaks'

A concurrent Taiwan Scholarship, MOE scholarship, MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship or MOFA Scholarship: a person who has received any other scholarship or subsidy from any Taiwan Government agency or any education institution in Taiwan is ineligible, with the single exception of a university subsidy covering the outstanding amount of tuition and other fees where the total exceeds the maximum the scholarship pays
Employment beyond the published limit: a working permit is capped at a maximum of 20 hours per week and a maximum validity of six months per semester
Employment for Huayu Enrichment Scholarship recipients unless they take language courses for six months or more
benefits: A published monthly living allowance in one of five bands depending on programme and degree level, from NTD 15,000 to NTD 33,000 per month
Under the MOE Scholarship, up to NTD 40,000 per semester towards approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses
Under the MOFA Scholarship, one-way economy-class airfare for direct flights to and from Taiwan - the only airfare component published in any of the three programmes
Permission to apply for a working permit during the award, capped at 20 hours per week and six months per semester
Access to a published list of universities and colleges that offer Taiwan Scholarship recipients a tuition and/or miscellaneous-expense discount, on top of the scholarship itself
Defined maximum durations that suit long research degrees: 4 years for a Bachelor or a Doctoral degree and 2 years for a Master's degree under the MOE Scholarship
eligibility: Be a foreign national holding at least a secondary school graduation diploma, or holding a post-secondary degree, and have shown excellent academic performance and be of good moral character
Be a national of a country that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan, or that has been recognised as friendly relations with Taiwan by MOFA (MOE Scholarship and MOFA Scholarship qualification test)
Not be a Mainland China, Hong Kong or Macao student studying under a Special Administrative Region arrangement
Not be an ROC national or an overseas Chinese student

Not already hold continuing student status at any university or tertiary college in Taiwan, and not already be registered to begin study there - except a student who will complete a degree and graduate that year, who may apply for a higher degree
Not have already studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level as the one intended
Not be an exchange student or a dual/joint degree student admitted under an academic cooperation agreement with an overseas university
Not have held a Taiwan Scholarship for a total of five years
Never have had a Taiwan Scholarship or MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship revoked

Not have received any other scholarship or subsidy from any Taiwan Government agency or any education institution in Taiwan, except a university subsidy covering the outstanding amount of tuition and other fees where that total exceeds the maximum paid by the scholarship

For a programme not completely taught in English, submit a TOCFL result or certificate at Level 3 or above - or, where the local Taiwan Representative Office does not organise TOCFL testing, take the test at Level 3 or above at your own expense by the end of the first semester after arrival and submit the result to your university or college
Apply for admission separately to a university or college in Taiwan, and submit the scholarship application to the local Taiwan Representative Office
general_eligibility: International students who must be foreign nationals with a secondary school graduation diploma or a post-secondary degree, who have shown excellent academic performance, and who are of good moral character. Mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao SAE students are not eligible (published qualification test for the MOE and MOFA Scholarships).
Nationals of countries that have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, or that have been recognised as friendly relations with Taiwan by MOFA (published qualification test).
ineligibility_conditions: An ROC national or an overseas Chinese student

A person who already has and is continuing to maintain student status at any university or tertiary college in Taiwan, or who has already registered to begin studies at a university or college in Taiwan - this restriction does not apply to a student who will complete a degree and graduate that year, who may apply to pursue a higher degree
A person who has already studied in Taiwan for a degree at the same level as the one in which they intend to enrol
An exchange student or a dual/joint degree student admitted to a university or college in Taiwan under an academic cooperation agreement with an overseas university or college
A person who has held a Taiwan Scholarship for a total of five years
A person who has ever had a Taiwan Scholarship or MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship revoked

A person who has received any other scholarship or subsidy from any Taiwan Government agency or any education institution in Taiwan - the single published exception being a subsidy provided by a university or college to cover the outstanding amount of tuition and other fees where the total exceeds the maximum amount paid by the scholarship
official.citizenship_residency: Foreign nationals only, and from an eligible country. Applicants must be foreign nationals, and under the MOE and MOFA Scholarships they must come from a country that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan or that MOFA has recognised as friendly relations with Taiwan. ROC nationals, overseas Chinese students, and Mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao SAE students are all excluded. No individual country quota and no residence-permission condition are published on the pages read.
official.international_eligibility: Open to foreign nationals from Taiwan's diplomatic partners and MOFA-recognised friendly countries, at degree level from Bachelor to Doctoral and in the Language Enhancement Program, subject to an excellent academic record, good moral character, and a set of seven published disqualifiers. There is no lecturer-specific, research-fellow or visiting-lecturer stream in the three programmes published, and the specific scholarship named in this record's title is not among them.
host_requirements: Enrol at a university or college in Taiwan - the applicant must apply separately for admission, and the award is attached to that enrolment

For the MOE Scholarship, the recipient's approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses must be at or below the NTD 40,000 per semester cap, or the student must pay the excess to the university or college
The award period must be continuous, with no breaks (published for the MOFA Scholarship as a general condition)

Language conditions attach to the host's programme: where the programme is not completely taught in English, a TOCFL Level 3 result or certificate is required, and a nine-month-or-longer recipient should participate in TOCFL at Level 3 (Band B1) or above
requirements: Hold at least a secondary school graduation diploma, or a post-secondary degree
Have an excellent academic record and be of good moral character
Be a foreign national from a country with diplomatic relations with Taiwan, or recognised as friendly by MOFA

Not fall into any of the seven published ineligible categories (ROC national or overseas Chinese; already studying or already registered in Taiwan; already studied in Taiwan at the same level; exchange or dual/joint degree under a cooperation agreement; five years of Taiwan Scholarship already; prior revocation; other Taiwan government or Taiwanese institutional scholarship or subsidy)
Submit the scholarship application to the local Taiwan Representative Office
Apply separately to a university or college in Taiwan for admission

For a programme not completely taught in English, submit a TOCFL Level 3 or above result or certificate, or sit the test at your own expense by the end of the first semester after arrival and submit the result to your university or college
For a nine-month-or-longer award, participate in TOCFL at Level 3 (Band B1) or above

Accept the work conditions if you intend to work: a working permit is capped at 20 hours per week with a maximum validity of six months per semester, and Huayu Enrichment Scholarship recipients may work only if they take language courses for six months or more
documents: The central site publishes the official document set as downloadable attachments, not as a checklist: MOE Scholarship Guidelines (Chinese and English PDFs), MOE Scholarship Application Form (PDF), MOE Scholarship Terms of Agreement (PDF), Scholarship Application Process (PDF), Items Required for Health Certificate - Form B (PDF), a List of MOE Overseas Offices (PDF), a list of universities and colleges offering degree programmes taught in English, and a list of universities and colleges that give Taiwan Scholarship recipients a tuition and/or miscellaneous-expense discount

The same attachment set is published for the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (Guidelines, application form, terms of agreement, Mandarin Language Centers in Taiwan list, health certificate Form B, list of MOE overseas offices) and for the MOFA Scholarship (Guidelines, application form, assessment form, recommendation form, terms of agreement, recipient form, English Programme of Taiwan Scholarship, Plane Ticket Application Form in PDF/DOC/ODT, health certificate Form B).
Language evidence is a published document requirement: a copy of the results or a certificate of TOCFL at Level 3 or above for programmes not completely taught in English.
Health documentation: a health certificate is part of the published process, with the required items set out in Items Required for Health Certificate (Form B).
The scholarship guidelines and their attachments are legally constituted documents; the page records the guideline update date of 10 February 2026 and reference number 臺教文（五）字第1152500420A號令.
document_format_rules: No file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule or signature rule is published as text on the scholarship guidelines page.

The binding format source is the published MOE Scholarship Guidelines themselves, which are issued as dated, numbered legal instruments (update date 10 February 2026, reference 臺教文（五）字第1152500420A號令) and are retrievable through the MOE Laws and Regulations Retrieving System, with the page recording the Guidelines themselves as updated on 8 May 2026.

The published attachments are the format carriers: a prescribed application form (PDF), prescribed terms of agreement (PDF), a prescribed health certificate form (Form B) and a prescribed plane ticket application form for MOFA recipients. Health certificate items are enumerated in Form B rather than left to the applicant's judgement.

Documents that are photocopies are specified as such - for example, TOCFL transcripts and certificates are required as photocopies at Level 2 or above for Chinese-taught degree programmes - so the accepted form is named even where no other rule is stated.
selection_criteria: Published qualifying test: foreign nationality, a secondary school graduation diploma or a post-secondary degree, excellent academic performance, and good moral character
Published country test (MOE and MOFA Scholarships): the applicant's country must have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, or be recognised as friendly by MOFA
Published exclusion test: the seven ineligible categories act as hard screens before any merit consideration

Language readiness is a published criterion, with TOCFL Level 3 or above required for programmes not completely taught in English, and TOCFL participation at Level 3 (Band B1) or above expected of recipients with nine months or more of award

No published assessment rubric, interview process, panel, weighting or pass mark appears on the pages read. The published process document is a separate attachment (Scholarship Application Process PDF) and the MOFA scheme adds a published assessment form and recommendation form for representative offices, which indicates where assessment happens without publishing the criteria.
official.selection_notes: No official source was found, so no selection method, assessment weighting, panel, interview stage or notification timing is recorded. Nothing has been inferred from how other Taiwan MOE scholarship schemes select candidates, because this scheme's own rules were never read.
application_method: Identify the programme you are applying to. Three are published with different money: MOE Scholarship (tuition cap plus living allowance), MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship (living allowance only), MOFA Scholarship (living allowance plus one-way airfare).

Prepare the prescribed application materials from the published attachments: the relevant Guidelines in English or Chinese, the relevant Application Form, the Terms of Agreement, the health certificate Form B, and for MOFA recipients the Plane Ticket Application Form.

Submit the scholarship application to the local Taiwan Representative Office. The published rule is absolute: 'All scholarship applications must be submitted to the local Taiwan Representative Office.' Find the mission through the MOFA overseas office list or the List of MOE Overseas Offices.

Apply separately for admission to a university or college in Taiwan. The scholarship and the admission application are two distinct submissions, and the published MOE description is explicit that applicants 'must apply separately to a university or college in Taiwan for admission'.

If your programme is not completely taught in English, arrange a TOCFL test at Level 3 or above before applying, or be ready to sit it at your own expense by the end of the first semester after arrival and submit the result to your university or college.
Check the published list of universities and colleges offering degree programmes taught in English, and the separate list of institutions that offer Taiwan Scholarship recipients a tuition discount.
Sign the prescribed Terms of Agreement, which are part of the published document set for each programme.
application_steps: 1. Choose the programme (MOE, MOE Huayu Enrichment, or MOFA) and read its Guidelines in English or Chinese, noting the living-allowance band for your degree level.

2. Self-screen against the seven published ineligible categories, including the five-year cumulative cap, the same-level prior study bar, and the bar on any other Taiwan government or Taiwanese institutional scholarship or subsidy.
3. Confirm your country qualifies - diplomatic relations with Taiwan, or recognition as friendly by MOFA.
4. Locate your local Taiwan Representative Office using the MOFA overseas office list or the List of MOE Overseas Offices, and obtain its own deadline, which the central site does not publish.

5. Complete the prescribed Application Form, arrange the health certificate using Items Required for Health Certificate (Form B), and obtain a TOCFL Level 3 or above result if your programme is not completely taught in English.
6. Submit the scholarship application to the Representative Office by its deadline. Do not send it to the central office.
7. Apply separately for admission to a Taiwanese university or college, using the institution's own process and deadline.
8. Sign and return the prescribed Terms of Agreement once selected, and note the continuous award-period requirement and the five-year cumulative cap before accepting.
applicant_submission_route: Applicant -> local Taiwan Representative Office (ROC overseas mission). The published rule: 'All scholarship applications must be submitted to the local Taiwan Representative Office.'
Applicant -> Taiwanese university or college, separately, for admission. These are two independent applications and neither substitutes for the other.
Taiwan Representative Office -> central scholarship office (the Office of the Taiwan Scholarship and Huayu Enrichment Scholarship Program) for the selection decision under the published Guidelines.
official.application_portal: No central online application portal is published. Applications are lodged with the local Taiwan Representative Office, and the central site publishes downloadable forms and guidelines as PDF attachments rather than a submission system. The central scholarship office is contactable by email at taiwanscholarship@mail.moe.gov.tw and by the published office telephone numbers, and the published overseas-office lists are the routing mechanism for finding the correct mission.
award_holder_conditions: Enrol and remain enrolled at the Taiwanese university or college for which you were awarded, since the award is attached to that enrolment
Keep the award period continuous - published as an express condition, with breaks not permitted and a maximum total of five years
Where the tuition cap applies, pay the student share of tuition and miscellaneous expenses to the university or college where approved costs exceed NTD 40,000 per semester

Meet the language condition: for programmes not completely taught in English, produce the TOCFL Level 3 or above result or certificate, and where the mission does not organise testing, sit the test at your own expense by the end of the first semester after arrival and submit the result to your university or college
Participate in TOCFL at Level 3 (Band B1) or above if your award runs for nine months or more

If working, hold a working permit limited to a maximum of 20 hours per week with a maximum validity of six months per semester, obtained through the Workforce Development Agency; Huayu Enrichment Scholarship recipients may work only if they take language courses for six months or more

For the MOFA Scholarship specifically, note that the airfare benefit is one-way economy class on direct flights to and from Taiwan only, and that you are responsible for all other expenses during your stay

Do not accept a second Taiwan government or Taiwanese institutional scholarship, save the published exception of a university subsidy covering the outstanding amount of fees above the scholarship maximum
Sign and abide by the programme's Terms of Agreement, which are a published part of the document set
arrival_rules: No arrival date, arrival deadline or pre-arrival condition is published centrally. Arrival timing is set by the university and the mission, not by the scholarship office.

The only published travel provision is under the MOFA Scholarship: one-way economy-class plane tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan. The words 'direct flights' are part of the published benefit, so a non-direct routing is not covered as published.

Arrival formalities after a scholarship is awarded are governed by the published TOCFL fallback - where the local mission does not organise testing, the recipient must sit the TOCFL test at their own expense by the end of the first semester after arrival in Taiwan and submit the result to the university or college.

The MOFA Scholarship award period starts on 1 August of the first year of study in Taiwan and ends when the award expires, on graduation, on suspension or withdrawal, or on termination of the scholarship. That start point is the closest thing to an arrival rule that is published.
timeline_rules: MOE Scholarship period: begins on 1 September and ends on 31 August of the following year, with summer classes excepted in principle. Graduates who cannot graduate by June of the year can keep the scholarship until August of that year.
MOE Scholarship total cap: the scholarship period must not exceed a total of five years.
MOE Scholarship durations: Bachelor 4 years, Master 2 years, Doctoral 4 years, LEP 1 year.
MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship: award blocks of 2 months (summer term), 3 months, 6 months, 9 months or 1 year (12 months), with a maximum total of five years.

MOFA Scholarship: the award period starts on 1 August of the first year of study in Taiwan and ends when the award period expires, on graduation, on suspension or withdrawal, or on termination; award periods must be continuous with no breaks and must not exceed a total of five years.

Language deadline: where the local Taiwan Representative Office does not organise TOCFL testing, the recipient must sit the test at Level 3 or above at their own expense by the end of the first semester after arrival and submit the result to the university or college.

Guideline currency: the scholarship comparison page carries a publication date of 2026-06-10, an update date of 10 February 2026 and reference number 臺教文（五）字第1152500420A號令, so the money figures in this record are current to the 2026 guideline cycle and should be re-checked each cycle.
official_application_route: Scholarship application: to the local Taiwan Representative Office. The published requirement is that all scholarship applications must be submitted there.
Admission application: separately, to a university or college in Taiwan. The MOE states applicants must apply separately to a university or college in Taiwan for admission.

Guidelines and legal basis: the MOE Taiwan Scholarship Program Directions, published on the MOE Laws and Regulations Retrieving System at https://edu.law.moe.gov.tw/EngLawContent.aspx?lan=E&id=250, and the scholarship guidelines page at https://taiwanscholarship.moe.gov.tw/web/pages.aspx?p=7.
official.program_type: Government scholarship administered jointly by the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Science and Technology of Taiwan (Republic of China). Published programmes: the MOE Scholarship, the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship and the MOFA Scholarship, all applied for through Taiwan's overseas missions with separate university admission. NOT CONFIRMED: a programme titled 'Elite Scholarship for University Lecturers from South & Southeast Asia' does not appear in the published comparison table or guidelines read on 2026-10-01.
coverage: MOE Scholarship: up to NTD 40,000 per semester towards approved tuition and miscellaneous expenses, excess payable by the student
MOE Scholarship: monthly living allowance of NTD 28,000 (Bachelor) or NTD 15,000 (LEP)
MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship: monthly living allowance of NTD 20,000 (Master/Doctoral) or NTD 28,000 (LEP); no tuition contribution
MOFA Scholarship: monthly living allowance of NTD 28,000 (Master/Doctoral) or NTD 33,000 (LEP); no tuition contribution
MOFA Scholarship only: one-way economy-class plane tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan
official.deadline_note: No deadline date is published centrally. LSE-style central deadlines do not exist in this system: the scholarship site states that 'All scholarship applications must be submitted to the local Taiwan Representative Office', and the MOE page states that applications 'must be submitted to a Republic of China (ROC) overseas mission'. deadline_central is deliberately null. Deadlines are published per mission and per university, and they differ.

undergraduate: Bachelor degree: 4 years under the MOE Scholarship, with a living allowance of NTD 28,000 per month
masters: Master degree: 2 years under the MOE Scholarship
Master/Doctoral level living allowance: NTD 20,000 per month under the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship; NTD 28,000 per month under the MOFA Scholarship

official.region: Taiwan (Republic of China) - host. Applicants must be foreign nationals from countries that have diplomatic relations with Taiwan or that MOFA has recognised as friendly relations with Taiwan. No lecturer-specific or South and Southeast Asia-specific country list is published on the pages read.
official.funding: Partial

important_advice_for_students: This record could not be verified and must not be relied on for an application. No official page describing this scholarship was found, so nothing about its eligibility, money, deadlines or process is established here.

Check the operative official source yourself before spending any time on this: the Taiwan Scholarship and Huayu Enrichment Scholarship Program site (https://taiwanscholarship.moe.gov.tw/) publishes the Ministry of Education's Taiwan Scholarship programmes, and its Scholarship Guidelines page carries a comparison table of the MOE Scholarship, the MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship and the MOFA Scholarship. No scholarship for university lecturers from South and Southeast Asia appears there.

If you were told about this scholarship by a university or an agent, ask them to name the official guideline document and the administering office. Taiwan MOE scholarship rules are published as numbered administrative rules, so a citable document should exist.

application_readiness_checklist: Establish first that the programme in this record exists as named. The official comparison table and guidelines read on 1 October 2026 list three programmes - MOE Scholarship, MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship and MOFA Scholarship - and no 'Elite Scholarship for University Lecturers from South & Southeast Asia'. Confirm the correct programme with your mission before investing effort.
Check your country's status: it must have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, or be recognised as friendly by MOFA.

Check the seven hard screens before anything else: ROC national or overseas Chinese student; already studying or already registered in Taiwan; already studied in Taiwan at the same level; exchange or dual/joint degree under a cooperation agreement; five years of Taiwan Scholarship already held; a prior revocation; or any other scholarship or subsidy from a Taiwan government agency or a Taiwanese institution.

Note the one permitted exception to the other-scholarship bar: a Taiwanese university may subsidise the outstanding amount of your tuition and other fees where that total exceeds the maximum the scholarship pays.
Find your local Taiwan Representative Office through the MOFA overseas office list or the List of MOE Overseas Offices, and get its deadline. The central site publishes no deadline.

Choose your programme on the money, not the name: MOE Scholarship pays a tuition cap of NTD 40,000 per semester plus a living allowance; Huayu Enrichment and MOFA pay no tuition and differ mainly in allowance level, duration block and - for MOFA - one-way airfare.
Budget the tuition gap. Even under the richest programme the MOE pays only up to NTD 40,000 per semester, and the published rule is that you pay the excess to the university.

If your programme is not completely taught in English, arrange a TOCFL Level 3 or above result now; if your mission does not run the test, you must sit it at your own expense by the end of your first semester after arrival.
Get the prescribed document set ready: the relevant Guidelines, the Application Form, the Terms of Agreement, and the health certificate using Items Required for Health Certificate (Form B).
Remember the two-application problem: the scholarship goes to your mission, the admission application goes to the university, and neither replaces the other.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme that does not exist under that name. The record's title is not one of the three published programmes, so the most likely failure is aiming at a scholarship stream that is not open.
Nationality screen: not a foreign national, an overseas Chinese student, or from a country without diplomatic relations with Taiwan or without MOFA friendly recognition.
Already studying, or already registered to study, in Taiwan - the published exception is only for someone completing a degree and graduating that year who is moving to a higher degree.
Having already studied in Taiwan at the same level as the degree intended - this is a separate bar and it is easy to overlook.
Being admitted as an exchange or dual/joint degree student under a cooperation agreement, which is an explicit exclusion.
Holding a Taiwan Scholarship for five years in total, or having had a Taiwan Scholarship or MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship revoked at any point.

Holding any other scholarship or subsidy from a Taiwan government agency or a Taiwanese institution - the commonest practical trap, because Taiwanese university scholarships often come as automatic add-ons.
Missing the TOCFL requirement, or sitting the test late where the mission does not organise it: the published deadline is the end of the first semester after arrival, at your own expense.
Assuming tuition is fully covered. NTD 40,000 per semester is a cap, and the excess is your liability.
Missing the mission's own deadline, because the central site publishes none and applicants naturally look there.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and miscellaneous expenses above NTD 40,000 per semester under the MOE Scholarship - the published rule puts the excess on the student
All tuition and miscellaneous expenses if you hold the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship or the MOFA Scholarship, both of which publish N/A for fees
The gap between a NTD 15,000 and NTD 33,000 monthly allowance and the actual cost of living and studying in Taiwan, which the award does not benchmark to any published cost of living
Return airfare, and any airfare at all unless you hold the MOFA Scholarship - and even then only one-way economy class on direct flights
All other expenses during your stay in Taiwan under the MOFA Scholarship, which states that recipients are responsible for them and that MOFA provides no other subsidies
TOCFL test fees, which the published rule places on the applicant where the mission does not organise testing
Books, equipment, insurance and personal costs - no published component covers them
Any cost of a second scholarship you were relying on, if the other-scholarship bar applies

Language evidence: a TOCFL result or certificate at Level 3 or above is required for programmes not completely taught in English, and Chinese-taught degree programmes require a photocopy of a TOCFL transcript or certificate at Level 2 or above. submission_workflow: 1. Confirm the correct programme name and money against the published scholarship comparison table, and confirm that the scholarship you have in mind is one of the three open programmes.
2. Self-screen against the seven published ineligible categories and the country condition.
3. Locate your local Taiwan Representative Office via the MOFA overseas office list or the List of MOE Overseas Offices, and obtain its application deadline and any local additional requirements.
4. Download the current Guidelines (EN), Application Form, Terms of Agreement and Items Required for Health Certificate (Form B) for your programme, checking the update date and reference number.

5. Obtain a TOCFL Level 3 or above result or certificate if your intended programme is not completely taught in English; use the list of universities and colleges offering English-taught degree programmes to check first.
6. Complete the prescribed application form and health certificate, and submit to the Representative Office by its deadline. Do not send the application to the central office.
7. Apply separately for admission to the Taiwanese university or college, by that institution's own deadline and process.
8. If selected, sign and return the Terms of Agreement, and note the continuous award-period rule, the five-year cumulative cap, and the tuition excess you must pay yourself.

official.description: Webster Vienna Private University offers the WVPU New Student Scholarship, a partial tuition award in three tiered levels for newly admitted bachelor's and master's degree students, on the basis of both academic achievement and financial need. Up to 20 awards are made per year at EUR 12,000/7,000/4,000 per academic year for bachelor's degrees and EUR 8,000/5,000/3,000 for master's degrees. official.description: IPOET (International Programme Office for Education and Training) offers 75% tuition fee waivers funded by the Government of Sweden and administered by Chalmers, and Chalmers awarded approximately 33 IPOET scholarships in 2026. The scholarship is a partial tuition-fee reduction of 75% across the four semesters of a two-year programme, rising to 85% in the second and final year for students who excel in their first year, and no funds are transferred to the scholarship laureates.
purpose: Reduce the tuition burden on prospective fee-paying students from non-EU/EEA countries who hold outstanding academic records

study_type: First year of a two-year (four-semester) Master's programme at Chalmers University of Technology
official.degree_award: Full Master's degree. The scholarship is a tuition-fee reduction attached to a place on a Chalmers Master's programme; it is not a degree or a short-term award.
official.duration: Scholarship offers are valid for two years of study (4 semesters, a 2-year programme) under certain conditions set out in the Scholarship Regulations for fee paying students. The tuition reduction may increase to 85% during the second and final year for students who excel during their first year of studies.
official.application_cycle: Annual. The scholarship application period for Master's programmes opens in late November and closes in mid-January, in parallel with the national master's admission round. The key dates page read gives the cycle as late November 2026 to mid-January 2027 for admission in autumn 2027.
official.deadline_central_display: The application period for scholarships administered by Chalmers is open from late November 2026 until mid-January 2027. Chalmers states the scholarship deadline aligns with the programme application deadline, not the deadline for submitting supporting documentation. All deadlines are at midnight CET on the date indicated.
official.deadline_institutional: 1 February 2027 for both paying the application fee or proving fee-exempt status, and for submitting supporting documentation. Scholarship award notifications are sent by e-mail between mid-March and late April 2027, and the first semester's tuition fees must be received by 1 May 2027.
official.deadline_note: Chalmers publishes the closing date only as 'mid-January' without a specific day on the scholarship page; the key dates page places the master's programme application deadline at 15 January 2027, which is the date used for deadline_central because Chalmers states the scholarship deadline aligns with the programme application deadline.

official.tuition_rule: The IPOET waiver is applied by Chalmers directly as a reduction of the tuition fees charged by the University; no funds are transferred to the scholar. official.host_institution_fee: The scholar pays the remaining share of the Chalmers tuition fee that the 75% reduction does not cover, plus the non-refundable application fee to universityadmissions.se.

official.selection_notes: Selection is based on the applicants' relative academic excellence, which primarily includes a weighted average grade of at least 80% but also the home university's stature including position on global ranking lists and the priority order of the application for Chalmers Master's programmes. The ranking of the applied-for Master's programmes is crucial for the assessment of the scholarship application, and Chalmers advises selecting a Chalmers Master's programme as number one (1) priority to maximise the chance of a scholarship. Fields of study are unrestricted. Chalmers admissions (scholarship committee) cannot give any preliminary notifications; all applicants for scholarships administered by Chalmers are notified by e-mail when the selection is completed, between mid-March and late April.

Do not be discouraged by waiting. Chalmers states there is no correlation between how early you submit and the likelihood of receiving a scholarship, although applying early expedites the assessment
Do not chase preliminary news. Chalmers admissions (scholarship committee) cannot give any preliminary notifications, so any agent or contact claiming to know early is not speaking for Chalmers

Ignore anyone asking you to pay to apply. Chalmers states explicitly that applying for Chalmers scholarships is free of charge and that you must not follow other links or pay fees in respect of applying

Do not be confused by other Cholarships. The Swedish Institute (SI) scholarships for Global Professionals are not administered by Chalmers and have their own timeline and process. The Avancez, US Friends of Chalmers, Adlerbert Study, COLFUTURO, FIDERH, FUNED, Alfred Ots, WeMakeScholars, LPDP and SI Pioneering Women in STEM awards are separate schemes

A genuine advantage: being granted alternative or complementary funding from an external patron does not affect your eligibility, because Chalmers states an applicant's financial status is not taken into account during the nomination process

Start your residence permit planning around the tuition payment. Chalmers states you cannot start the residence permit application process until you have paid the tuition fees, and the process can take a long time

Already being a current student at Chalmers, since these scholarships are for prospective students only and must be submitted before the start of the first academic year

Not fulfilling the eligibility requirements for the Master's programme applied for, which removes the applicant from scholarship consideration regardless of the scholarship application itself
Data in the scholarship form that cannot be verified against the universityadmissions.se documents
Using a different e-mail address from the one registered on universityadmissions.se, so the verification code and notifications do not arrive
Missing the verification code because it went to junk mail
Not ranking the Chalmers programme as number one priority
Failing to confirm acceptance by the deadline in the award notification, which forfeits the offer

100% of living costs, accommodation and subsistence in Gothenburg - no funds are transferred to scholarship laureates, so this is entirely unfunded
Travel and relocation costs, not mentioned in the published description
The non-refundable application fee payable to universityadmissions.se
Books, equipment, course materials and project costs
Swedish residence permit application and issuance fees, and the processing time lost because the process cannot start until tuition is paid

document_audit: All required supporting documents uploaded on your universityadmissions.se account. Proof of application fee payment, or documentation of EU/EEA citizenship, by 1 February 2027

referee_tracking.instructions: Chalmers publishes no referee, recommendation or reference-letter requirement for the IPOET Scholarships. Selection is made on the published academic and ranking criteria by the Chalmers scholarship committee, and no interview is described on the pages read. Do not spend effort arranging referees for IPOET itself. The only third-party input that matters is the prestige of your home university, which Chalmers assesses from its position on global ranking lists rather than from a referee.

alerts.message: The master's programme application period opens on 16 October 2026. Do the universityadmissions.se application first, since the scholarship application depends on its 8-digit number.
The Chalmers scholarship application period opens. You may apply before completing your programme documentation, but the scholarship is only processed once the programme application is complete.
Prepare the application fee and the supporting documents now. Missing either on 1 February 2027 removes the application from consideration.

Two hard deadlines on the same day: application fee paid or fee-exempt status proven, and all supporting documents uploaded. Chalmers states your scholarship application will not be considered if either is missed.
The scholarship portal closes. The scholarship deadline aligns with the programme application deadline, not the documentation deadline. After this point you cannot change the application.
Check your junk e-mail folder for the verification code, which is sent within a few minutes to the address registered at universityadmissions.se.
All applicants are notified by e-mail, whether awarded or not. Chalmers cannot give preliminary notifications, so no news before then is meaningful.
Confirm acceptance by the deadline specified in the notification, following the instructions in it. Failing to confirm forfeits the offer.
First semester tuition balance due to Chalmers. Only after paying can you start the residence permit application, which takes a long time.
Mandatory enrolment in Ladok. Studies begin.

submission_workflow: Confirm you are a non-EU/EEA citizen liable to pay Swedish tuition fees and a first-time Master's applicant
Check your weighted average grade is at least 80% and consider how your home university ranks globally
Submit your Master's programme application at universityadmissions.se between 16 October 2026 and 15 January 2027
Rank your Chalmers Master's programme as number one of a maximum four choices
Pay the application fee or prove fee-exempt status by 1 February 2027
Upload all required supporting documents on your universityadmissions.se account by 1 February 2027
Read the IPOET requirements and the requirements of every other Cholarship you intend to apply for
Open https://scholarship.portal.chalmers.se/ with the same e-mail address as your universityadmissions.se account
Enter your 8-digit application number and the emailed verification code, checking junk mail
Complete and submit the scholarship application by mid-January 2027, verifying that every entry matches your uploaded documents
Amend the application any time before the deadline if needed
Await the e-mail notification between mid-March and late April 2027
If awarded, accept by the deadline in the notification
Pay the remaining first-semester tuition by 1 May 2027 and start the residence permit application
Enrol by 30 August 2027
post_award_requirements: Confirm acceptance of the scholarship offer by the deadline specified in the notification
Pay the remaining share of the tuition fees, with the first semester due by 1 May 2027
Enrol by 30 August 2027; enrolment is a mandatory step
Remain enrolled and studying at Chalmers for the two years covered by the offer, under the conditions in the Scholarship Regulations for fee paying students
Aim to excel in the first year of studies, since the reduction may then increase from 75% to 85% of tuition fees in the second and final year
Start the residence permit application only after paying tuition fees, and allow for a long processing time
No published return-home, deferral, clinical or repayment obligation exists for this award; none is recorded. No funds were transferred to you in the first place

official.description: The LiU International Scholarship is aimed at supporting international master's degree students with significant academic potential who are required to pay tuition fees. LiU states the tuition fees for a student awarded a LiU International Scholarship are normally reduced by 50%, offers a limited number of these scholarships to new students, and reserves the right to determine year by year how many scholarships are offered and what percentage is given. The scholarship may cover the total tuition fee or part of it, and the student must pay any remainder by the payment deadline.
purpose: Support international master's degree students with significant academic potential who are required to pay tuition fees at Linköping University
Recruit outstanding new students to master's programmes at Linköping University by reducing their tuition fees
Provide a tuition-fee reduction rather than a living-cost grant, with the scholarship covering the total tuition fee or part of it
study_type: Master's degree study at Linköping University as a new student, normally at a workload of 30 credits per semester with courses included in the programme
official.degree_award: Full Master's degree. The scholarship is a tuition-fee award attached to a master's programme place, not a degree or a short-term award.
official.duration: The scholarship offer is only valid for the specific year and master's programme stated in the Notification of Selection Results. For a master's programme the scholarship or fee normally covers a workload of 30 credits per semester as long as the courses are included in the programme. LiU International Scholarship holders must pass at least 75% of their courses during the first academic year in order to receive the scholarship for the following academic year.
official.application_cycle: Annual. The application period for LiU Scholarships opens each year on the day students receive the Notification of Selection Results and is only open for a short window. For 2026 the window ran from 26 March to 30 March, closing at 23:59 CET, with recipients published on 10 April.
official.deadline_central_display: In 2026, the application period was open from 26 March and closed at 23:59 CET on 30 March. LiU states the application period for LiU Scholarships opens each year on the day students receive the Notification of Selection Results and is only open for a short window. No dates are published for the next cycle.
official.deadline_institutional: Eligible students must already have applied by the deadline for the first admission round, submitted all required documents by the deadline, chosen a Linköping University master's programme as first priority (ranked number 1 of 4), and have been admitted to their first choice in the First Notification of Selection Results, which is usually at the end of March.
official.deadline_note: The only dates published are for the 2026 cycle: opening 26 March, closing 30 March at 23:59 CET, and recipients published 10 April. LiU publishes the rule that the window opens on the day of the Notification of Selection Results, usually end of March, but no calendar dates for the next cycle are published, so no forward-looking deadline_date can be set from official sources.
official.funding_label: LiU International Scholarship - tuition fees normally reduced by 50%, or the total tuition fee; limited number of scholarships for new students, with the percentage and volume determined year by year
official.funding_period: Tuition-fee reduction for the specific year and master's programme stated in the Notification of Selection Results, normally covering a workload of 30 credits per semester
official.tuition_coverage: The tuition fees for an awarded student are normally reduced by 50%. LiU states the scholarship covers the total tuition fee or part of the tuition fee, and that if it covers part of the fee the student must pay the remainder no later than the payment deadline. LiU reserves the right to determine internally, year by year, what percentage will be offered.
official.tuition_rule: Linköping University applies the reduction to the tuition fees it charges. The offer is valid only for the specific year and master's programme stated in the Notification of Selection Results, and normally covers a workload of 30 credits per semester as long as the courses are included in the programme. For any additional courses beyond 30 credits there will be an additional fee. If the scholarship covers only part of the tuition fee, the student must pay the remainder no later than the payment deadline.
official.host_institution_fee: Any tuition fee not covered by the scholarship must be paid by the student no later than the payment deadline, and an additional fee applies for any courses beyond 30 credits per semester. Citizens from countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland must pay application and tuition fees for higher education in Sweden.

Assume your money must cover everything except half the tuition. There is no published living-cost allowance, no travel coverage and no stipend. Gothenburg or Linköping rent, food, insurance and travel are on you

Treat the 75% course-pass rule as a hard deadline, not a target. LiU assesses only results registered on 1 July of the regular academic year, and explains that studying 60 credits a year means you need 45 completed credits from your programme by 1 July or you lose the scholarship. Over-examining in a later semester does not help

Do not stack the Swedish Institute scholarship with this one. LiU states that applicants awarded a scholarship by the Swedish Institute will subsequently have their Linköping University scholarship rescinded. If the SI is your better route, take the SI

Do not skip the residence permit. LiU states applicants unable to acquire a permit from the Swedish Migration Board in time for the start of studies or the registration deadline will have the scholarship rescinded
Watch your fee-paying status. If your status changes to that of a non-fee-payer the scholarship is no longer valid, and LiU requires you to inform the University in writing

Be realistic about volume. LiU states it offers a limited number of scholarships and reserves the right to decide year by year how many are offered, what percentage, and the merit process itself where more eligible applicants than places exist
Do not overshoot 30 credits a semester without budgeting. LiU states the scholarship or fee normally covers 30 credits per semester and that additional courses beyond that carry an additional fee
Expect the result on the university page, not by email. LiU publishes the list of recipients on the scholarships page, and for 2026 the published date was 10 April

official.description: The Adelaide Academic Excellence Scholarship offers a 50% tuition fee reduction and is a prestigious, highly competitive award with limited places for students with a high distinction average. It recognises international students commencing undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degrees who have achieved outstanding academic performance in their previous studies. Applications open on Monday 24 August 2026, and applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with scholarship offers made throughout the recruitment cycle until all allocations have been exhausted.

Apply early even though no priority is published. Because review is rolling and offers stop when allocations are exhausted, a complete application in the first weeks of the cycle is strictly better than the same application in the last

For postgraduate applicants, note the ATAR 99 route does not apply to you. The undergraduate-only ATAR 99 threshold and the GPA threshold are listed separately, and only the GPA or comparable score applies to you

Get your comparable score argument in order. A minimum overall GPA of 6.7 on a 7.0 scale, or a comparable score, must be demonstrated in the qualification used as the basis of admission. Prepare the evidence of that comparison rather than assuming it is self-evident

Protect the award from day one. The continuation condition is a Program Term GPA of 5.5 on a 7.0 scale in each compulsory Study Period. A single term below can suspend the scholarship, and the suspension mechanism is not simply a make-up opportunity

Note the recovery rule, which is unusual and worth understanding. If your overall GPA falls below the minimum, the scholarship is not applied to the next invoice; if your GPA returns to the minimum or above, it recommences and is applied to the next invoice. So a dip is not necessarily permanent, but you will pay the intervening invoice
Use the free academic support. The University points to the Student Academic Learning Support team and its free academic support services, which is directly relevant to holding the 5.5 GPA

official.description: The UQ International Excellence Scholarship is funded by The University of Queensland and is a tuition fee reduction of 25% per annum for the duration of the enrolled coursework program. It is for high achieving international students commencing a relevant full-time undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program of at least 16 units at UQ in 2027. There is no separate scholarship application: applicants are assessed automatically when they apply to study a program at UQ.

official.description: The ANU University Research Scholarship supports high-achieving higher degree by research students whose research aligns with the University's strategic directions, offered through two annual central scholarship rounds that also include the Research Training Program and other centrally managed scholarships. It provides a stipend of $40,475 per annum (full-time base stipend rate 2027) paid fortnightly, plus travel and removal allowances, a thesis allowance, a dependant child allowance for international students and paid medical, maternity and parental leave. No separate application is needed: eligible candidates are considered through their HDR admission application by selecting 'Australia: ANU - Other Scholarship', with international Round 1 applicants required to apply for admission by 31 August.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your course appears on the List of eligible courses before you apply â€” applying to an ineligible program removes you from consideration.
Submit one application for an Approved course; there is no separate scholarship form, so missing the scholarship step is not possible but also gives you no way to strengthen the case.
Have your ATAR equivalent (undergraduate) or WAM (postgraduate coursework) ready, because the offer percentage is set from it: 60-74.9 = 20%, 75+ = 25%.
Be a full fee-paying, non-sponsored student â€” a sponsored place disqualifies you.
Complete and pass the Genuine Student assessment, including the financial checks, before you can be considered; this can take time, so start it early.
Be ready to pay the reduced acceptance deposit by the deadline in your Letter of Offer â€” this is what confirms the scholarship.
Plan to enrol full-time at a La Trobe campus in Australia and maintain satisfactory academic progress.
important_advice_for_students: There is nothing to fill in for this scholarship separately â€” the University assesses you automatically from your course application, so do not waste time hunting for a scholarship form.
Do not defer. The scholarship may not be deferred to future intakes or years, and if you cannot secure a student visa for that intake the scholarship offer may be revoked.
Budget separately: this is a tuition discount only. There is no published living allowance, no travel cover, and the remaining 75-80% of tuition is yours to fund.
If you are stacking value, note this scholarship can be combined with the Early Acceptance Grant to form a discount on first-year tuition fees, but only if all conditions for both offers are met.
Paying the reduced deposit on time is what converts the scholarship in the Letter of Offer into a confirmed award; a late or missed deposit can withdraw it.
Scholarship enquiries go through the online enquiry form on the scholarship page (separate routes for prospective and current students) rather than a published email address.

Failing to meet the conditions in the Letter of Offer or missing the reduced-deposit payment deadline.
Deferring the offer to a later intake, or being unable to secure a student visa for the intake.

official.description: doc.funds.connect is an Austrian Science Fund (FWF) programme, run in cooperation with the Christian Doppler Research Association (CDG), that funds joint doctoral training programmes at Austrian universities and Austrian universities of applied sciences. It pays the personnel costs of 5 to 8 doctoral candidate positions plus training costs of up to â‚¬5,000 per doctoral candidate position per year, for a maximum of 48 months. The applicant is a multi-institutional consortium of researchers, not an individual: individual doctoral candidates never apply to the FWF and are recruited by the funded consortium under its own admission and selection procedures.
purpose: Attractive career opportunities for doctoral students help them gain a foothold in promising research fields â€” doc.funds.connect grants fund joint doctoral training programs at universities and universities of applied sciences.

The program facilitates cooperation between institutions, strengthens the research competence of universities of applied sciences, and offers doctoral students additional opportunities for career development.

The main goal of the program is to fund the establishment and expansion of structured doctoral programs based on international standards, developed and organized jointly by universities and universities of applied sciences. These cooperative training and research structures are intended to help provide doctoral students with an excellent education in the long term.

At the same time, the funding also supports the development of research staff at universities of applied sciences according to the Universities of Applied Sciences Studies Act (FHG) and strengthens the cooperation between universities of applied sciences and universities.
Long term, the program aims to interlink basic and applied research and help establish application-oriented basic research.

Selected degree programmes must meet minimum Design/Projects ECTS thresholds (45 CP of 120, 34 CP of 90, or 23 CP of 60). Other DAAD scholarship programmes exist for applicants from the field of History of Architecture or applicants with a scientific project. Study visits abroad within a funded programme are only possible under narrow conditions.

If you already have an admission from a desired degree programme, complete the form anyway and upload it. Do not upload work samples or portfolios to the DAAD portal itself. The portal closes at 24.00 hrs CET/CEST on the last application day.

German-language architecture programmes generally expect at least B2, usually C1; for those, proof of German at a completed B1 level per the European Framework or TestDaF must be submitted.

A German language course before the scholarship period is compulsory if the language of instruction or working language at the German host institution is German.

Individual fees, dorm damage, parking tickets, library charges and similar are your responsibility

official.description: The Chinese Government Scholarship Type B is the Tsinghua route for international, that is non-PRC-citizen, master's and doctoral students who have been admitted to or recommended for a Tsinghua programme. Full coverage includes tuition fee, free dormitory or an accommodation subsidy, a stipend and comprehensive medical insurance, for 1 to 3 academic years at master's level and 4 to 5 at doctoral level. Applicants must be under 35 for a master's or under 40 for a doctoral programme, must not hold another Tsinghua scholarship or a CSC nomination, and are nominated by their Tsinghua programme and apply through the CSC system. Holders undergo an annual review.
official.program_type: Government-funded scholarship (Chinese Scholarship Council, delivered through a host university)

The specific stipend amount is set by the Chinese Scholarship Council and is not published on Tsinghua's page, so funding_amount is null. Travel is not stated as covered, so fully_funded is false.
official.funding: Fully Funded

official.description: Entrusted by the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China, the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences recruits outstanding young graduate students from around the world and provides full scholarships through the 2026 Chinese Government Scholarship call. Successful Master's students are exempted from RMB 30,000/year tuition and successful PhD students from RMB 40,000/year, receive monthly stipends of RMB 3,500 and RMB 5,000 respectively, free UCAS Beijing campus accommodation or a housing subsidy of up to RMB 700-1,000/month, and RMB 800 medical insurance, for 36 months. Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens, hold an equivalent degree, be within the age limits of 35 (Master's) or 40 (PhD), be proficient in English or Mandarin, and submit the same information to both the CSC Online Application System (UCAS agency number 80001) and UCAS's own admission system by 31 January 2026 Beijing Time.
