The published student offer is explicit about access and merit: 'Apply for an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master. Students from all over the world are welcome. You will study at several universities in Europe and beyond. Full scholarships are available for the best students' (published).
Almost 50,000 students have taken part in Erasmus Mundus since 2004 (published).
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or development-goal requirement is published for Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters. The published selection frame is academic merit - scholarships are available to 'the best-ranked students worldwide' - and mobility and transnational delivery through a consortium of at least three institutions in at least three countries.
Individual joint masters may pursue their own thematic aims, and the consortium's own website is the authority for those; no scheme-level development-goal condition is published.
study_type: International joint master's programme with mobility across the consortium: 'You will study at several universities in Europe and beyond'
Typically comprising periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence
A joint degree programme governed by a study agreement signed with the relevant Erasmus Mundus Joint Master at the beginning of your studies
official.degree_award: Either a joint degree - one single degree certificate issued on behalf of at least two higher education institutions - or multiple degrees, meaning at least two degree certificates issued by two higher education institutions of the consortium. Which one applies is defined in detail when you sign the study agreement with the relevant Erasmus Mundus Joint Master at the beginning of your studies.
official.tuition_rule: The scholarship is the funding mechanism rather than a fee remission, and it is not automatic. The published position is that 'Masters may also offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide' - note the two operative words, 'may' and 'offer' - and that each master's website publishes 'all the steps of the application process (with and without scholarship)'. So a student on a self-funded place pays the consortium's fees, and a scholarship place is won on ranking. No fee amount, no fee-waiver mechanism and no published rule on fees at a Portuguese institution or at any other consortium member is published on this page.
official.home_tuition_rule: Not published. The scheme concerns fees at the participating European institutions. Nothing addresses fees payable to, or by, an institution in the applicant's home country, and no published rule requires an applicant to disengage from, or pay fees at, a home institution.
official.host_institution_fee: No host fee is published. The published institutional side of the scheme is separate and is for institutions, not students: 'Erasmus+ also offers grants to higher education institutions to run EMJM programmes', and the application route for that grant is published separately. No fee payable to a Portuguese or other consortium institution is described.
official.tax_status: Not published. The page states that scholarships 'contribute to' travel, visa and a living allowance but gives no statement on tax treatment, and Erasmus+ publishes no tax guidance for scholarship holders on this page. Tax treatment of an Erasmus Mundus scholarship varies by country of residence and of payment and must be checked with the awarding institution and the relevant national tax authority.

host_requirements: The programme must be an accredited Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, meaning a consortium of at least 3 institutions from at least 3 different countries plus multiple associated partners from the academic and non-academic world
The consortium must jointly design and deliver the master, typically including periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence

document_format_rules: No file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule, date-of-issue rule, certification rule or signature rule is published centrally by Erasmus+ for this action.
The binding format source is the specific joint master's own application process, published on that programme's website, and it can differ from one Erasmus Mundus Joint Master to another.

One published rule has a practical format consequence: a bachelor's-equivalent level of learning must be 'officially recognised, according to national legislation and practices, in the degree awarding country', so the evidence of equivalence is a formal recognition document issued in the country where the qualification was awarded, not a self-assessment.
official.selection_notes: There is no central Erasmus+ selection. Applications go to the individual joint master, and the published scheme-level facts are that each programme sets its own entry requirements and its own application process with and without a scholarship, that a new batch of programmes is selected each year, and that scholarships go to the best-ranked students worldwide. The practical consequence is that the same student faces a different competition in each programme, and 'best-ranked' is a relative statement within a programme rather than a threshold that can be checked in advance. No published appeals process, notification date or feedback mechanism exists at scheme level.
application_steps: 1. Search the Erasmus Mundus course catalogue for the programmes on offer, and identify the joint master you want.
2. Check the programme's own website for the course of study, the list of participating universities, the entry requirements, and the full application process both with and without a scholarship.
3. Confirm you meet the entry requirement: a bachelor's degree, or the last year of one graduating before the master's starts, or an officially recognised bachelor's-equivalent level of learning.
4. Assemble the documents that programme's own website requires. Erasmus+ publishes no central list.
5. Apply directly to the institution running the programme, within that programme's own window - in most cases between October and January for a course starting the following academic year.
6. If shortlisted, expect the programme's own selection, and note that scholarship places are awarded on ranking to the best-ranked students worldwide.
7. If awarded, sign the study agreement with the relevant Erasmus Mundus Joint Master at the beginning of your studies, which is where the joint or multiple degree structure is defined in detail.
applicant_submission_route: Student -> the institution running the chosen Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, directly. The published rule: 'Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme.'
There is no central Erasmus+ application, no central student portal and no central selection body. Each master's website publishes the process for its own programme.
Institution running the programme -> Erasmus+ institutional grant route, which is a separate published application that institutions make to run EMJM programmes.
official.application_portal: No central application portal for students. The published route is direct application to the institution running the chosen programme, with the programme's own website carrying the process and the forms. The two central published tools are the Erasmus Mundus course catalogue, which is for searching programmes, and the Erasmus Mundus Association's applicant resources, which provide course contacts, events with national volunteer representatives and stories from successful applicants. Neither is an application submission system.
arrival_rules: No arrival rule, arrival deadline, visa support or relocation support is published centrally for Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters.
The published mobility element that touches travel is a scholarship contribution towards travel costs and towards visa costs - a contribution, not a full funding, and no amount is published.

Because the degree is completed across several institutions, arrivals and departures are structured by the consortium's mobility pattern, which is defined in the study agreement signed at the beginning of studies. No central rule, minimum or maximum stay per country is published.
For a Portuguese-coordinated programme, the Portuguese institution is one mobility stop among at least three institutions in at least three countries, not a sole host.
timeline_rules: A new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year.
Published application timing: in most cases applications are submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.
Master's duration: 1 to 2 academic years, expressed as 60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits.
The study agreement with the relevant Erasmus Mundus Joint Master is signed at the beginning of studies, and is where the joint or multiple degree structure is defined in detail.
The programme's own application steps are published on the master's website and set the operative dates, including any separate scholarship and non-scholarship deadlines.
official_application_route: Student -> the institution running the chosen Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, directly, using that programme's own published application process (with and without scholarship).
Programme discovery -> the Erasmus Mundus course catalogue.
Programme detail, entry requirements, participating universities and all application steps -> the individual master's website.
Institutional side, published separately: Erasmus+ offers grants to higher education institutions to run EMJM programmes, and institutions apply on that separate route.

Applicant support -> the Erasmus Mundus Association, which publishes course contacts, events with national volunteer representatives, and stories from successful applicants. Scheme questions -> Europe Direct or the published Erasmus+ contact points.

important_advice_for_students: You apply to the university, not to Brussels. Erasmus+ publishes no central application; the institution running the programme runs its own process, and that is where your ranking is decided.

The scholarship is not automatic and is not the programme. Every joint master publishes a process 'with and without scholarship', so a self-funded place is a real option and a real cost. Decide which route you are applying on before you invest effort.
'Best-ranked' is relative. The same transcript wins in a weak cohort and loses in a strong one, so choose cohorts by the supervisor and project rather than by brand.

Timing is narrow: in most cases applications go in between October and January for the following academic year. Miss it and the programme is simply closed to you for that cycle, and a new batch of programmes is added each year rather than the same one re-opening.

Confirm the degree title carefully. You will get either a joint degree or multiple degrees, and the detail is fixed in the study agreement you sign at the start - ask what exactly is on the certificate before you accept.

Weigh the money honestly: the published benefits are participation costs plus contributions to travel, visa and a living allowance, with no rates published. Get the actual figures for the specific programme and the specific scholarship route from the institution.
If you rely on a bachelor's-equivalent level of learning, get it officially recognised under the legislation of the country where you earned it. Self-assessment will not satisfy the published rule.

referee_tracking.instructions: Erasmus+ publishes no central referee requirement for Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters. Any reference requirement belongs to the specific programme, whose website is the published authority for entry requirements and the application process. Approach referees only after reading that programme's own checklist, because a reference prepared for one Erasmus Mundus Joint Master will rarely fit another.

post_award_requirements: Sign the study agreement with the relevant Erasmus Mundus Joint Master at the beginning of your studies, which is where the joint or multiple degree structure is defined in detail.
Follow the programme's published pattern of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence across the consortium's institutions.
Meet the specific financial terms of your scholarship route, which the programme publishes rather than Erasmus+.

If on a scholarship, note that it is awarded on ranking and that the published scheme provides no renewal mechanism; there is no published route to extend an EMJM scholarship beyond the programme's own duration of 1 to 2 academic years.

Complete the requirements of the degree itself in at least two institutions, since the published award is either a joint degree on behalf of at least two higher education institutions or multiple degrees from at least two of them.
questions_to_ask_host: Is this programme a currently selected Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, and in which year's batch was it selected?
Which institutions are in the consortium, which countries, and where in the pattern does the Portuguese institution sit?
Will I receive a joint degree or multiple degrees, and exactly what appears on the certificate or certificates?
How many scholarships are available, how many applicants were there last cycle, and what does 'best-ranked' mean operationally here?
For the scholarship route, what are the actual amounts for participation costs, travel, visa and the living allowance, and are they paid in monthly instalments?
What is the exact application deadline, and is there a separate earlier deadline for scholarship consideration?
What is the exact breakdown of the published October-to-January application window, and are there interviews?
Are there language requirements, and does the programme waive or reduce tuition fees for self-funded students as well?
What happens to the scholarship if I defer, if I fail a module, or if the consortium changes my mobility country?

verification.source_conflict_rule: The European Commission's Erasmus+ page is the scheme-level authority and is the only source read in this pass. verification.source_freshness_rule: The page carries a 'Last updated: 26 June 2025' stamp, so all scheme-level statements are current to that date. On the merit strand specifically: 'Nova SBE believes in distinguishing its students' academic merit. Thus, the School offers merit scholarships to students who present a high academic performance' (published).

Nova SBE also publishes a separate purpose for partner-funded awards: 'Nova SBE, in partnership with different national and international entities, annually rewards the students' academic achievements' (published).

document_format_rules: Language: all Social Mobility Scholarship documentation must be in Portuguese or English. If written in another language it must be translated by a certified translation agency or translator, and must include the entire document - 'partial or autonomous translations are not accepted'.

For the Continuity Scholarship and the André Sousa Bessa, Banco Primus and NOS routes, the published rule is that documents must be originals or copies accompanied by a sworn translation into English or Portuguese if written in any other language.

File packaging: the Social Mobility Scholarship requires all documentation in a single PDF submitted in the designated field. The Accenture, António Serrenho, Deloitte and KPMG applications each require a single PDF document containing the listed items.
Certification: the IRS Model 3 must be complete and fully identified, which is a content requirement on the tax document itself.
Video submissions: Banco Primus, NOS and Explorer Excellence each require a three-minute video in English answering published questions.
No file-size limit and no signature rule are published on this page. The regulations, which are published in Portuguese, are the likely source of any further format rule and were not read.
official.selection_notes: Selection works in published tiers. The Merit Scholarship is for high academic performance, with retention checked at the end of the first year. The Social Mobility Scholarship is need-based and evidence-led, resting on the IRS Model 3 or an equivalent foreign household tax return. The partner-funded 100% awards each publish their own criteria and, in several cases, a second stage: the Women in Finance Scholarship ranks candidates on 'the final score resulting from the weighting of two factors' - the application score and the positioning of the applicant's Bachelor's programme institution in international rankings - while Banco Primus, NOS and Explorer Excellence add a three-minute video in English and a final interview, and André Sousa Bessa adds a final interview with a representative of the family. The published portfolio-level admission rule is decisive and is easy to miss: 'Scholarships are awarded on a rolling basis to applicants, which means that the budget available for scholarships may be used before the end of the Master's admission cycle. Due to the high volume of deserving candidates and the limited funding available for scholarships, we strongly recommend that you apply as early as possible.' No published quota, no published assessment weighting beyond the Women in Finance factors, and no appeals process.
application_steps: 1. Apply to a Nova SBE Master's programme. The scholarship mechanism is a designated field in that application form, so there is no separate scholarship form for the Merit, Social Mobility or Continuity Scholarships.

2. When you apply, show interest in the relevant scholarship in the designated field of the Master's application form. This cannot be done afterwards: applications 'cannot be considered after the application to the Master's program has been submitted'.

3. For the Social Mobility or Continuity Scholarship, submit your most recent household tax return - IRS Model 3 for the previous fiscal year in Portugal, or a governmental or certified authority household tax return for the most recent fiscal year from other territories - properly identified, in Portuguese or English, or fully certified-translated into one of those languages, as a single PDF in the designated field.
4. Apply early. Awards are made on a rolling basis and the budget can be exhausted before the end of the Master's admission cycle.
5. Monitor your email, including spam and the trash folder, throughout - the page states candidates are responsible for checking their emails regularly during this process.

6. For a partner-funded 100% award, watch the published window of 13 November 2025 to 23 March 2026 and note that accepted students must pay the first instalment of tuition as the enrolment fee to secure their place and be considered for the scholarship.

7. If shortlisted for a second-stage award, respond to the emailed request: a three-minute video in English for Banco Primus, NOS and Explorer Excellence, the published document list for Accenture, António Serrenho, Deloitte, KPMG, McKinsey First Generation and McKinsey Women in Leadership, or an interview for André Sousa Bessa.

8. If you want Portuguese nationality, Portuguese residence, a disability rating, or an award open to students from a specific region, check that award's own published conditions - several awards are nationality-restricted, and the Accenture, KPMG and Deloitte awards give priority to candidates with a disability rating of 60% or higher, or to disabled and displaced students.

9. For the CEMS awards, note the separate clock: the application period starts in November of CEMS Year 1, and the BNP Paribas award's € 9,200 yearly global amount can be split between up to three students.
applicant_submission_route: Master's applicant -> Nova SBE Master's programme application form, using the designated scholarship field. This is the single submission point for the Merit, Social Mobility and Continuity Scholarships.
Awarded student -> designated field in the portal for the Social Mobility Scholarship tax documentation, as a single PDF.

Enrolled student -> separate scholarship application form shared with students by Nova SBE for the Accenture, António Serrenho, Banco Primus, Deloitte, KPMG, McKinsey, NOS and Explorer Excellence awards, within the published 13 November 2025 to 23 March 2026 window.
Shortlisted candidate -> email response to Nova SBE, submitting a three-minute video in English, a document pack, or attending a final interview with the partner.
official.application_portal: The operative route is the Nova SBE Master's programme application form, which contains a designated field for the scholarship of interest. There is no separate scholarship portal for the Merit, Social Mobility or Continuity Scholarships. For the partner-funded awards, Nova SBE shares a separate application form with students and then communicates by email, and the published instruction is that candidates are responsible for checking their emails regularly, including spam and the trash folder. The CEMS awards are applied for within the CEMS Year 1 period starting in November. The DGES Scholarship is administered by the Direção Geral do Ensino Superior, whose applications for the 2026/27 academic year open on 14 August.
arrival_rules: No arrival rule, arrival deadline, visa support, relocation support or settling-in support is published for any Nova SBE scholarship. Every published award is a percentage of the tuition fee value, and the recurring exclusion list contains no travel item.

The published timing rule that matters on arrival is financial: the first instalment of tuition, paid as the enrolment fee, must be paid to secure the place, and that amount is excluded from every scholarship including the 100% awards.

Nothing is published on visa sponsorship, Portuguese residence requirements, or arrival formalities. Note that several awards are nationality- or residence-restricted - Portuguese nationality for the António Serrenho, Banco Primus, Deloitte, McKinsey First Generation, McKinsey Women in Leadership and NOS awards, or three years' residence in Portugal for the two McKinsey awards - but none of these is an arrival condition, and none is tied to a visa.
timeline_rules: Partner-funded award applications: published window 13 November 2025 to 23 March 2026, Fall Intake only.

Merit, Social Mobility and Continuity Scholarships: interest must be shown at the time of the Master's application, and the application cannot be considered afterwards. The operative date is the Master's admissions deadline, which is not published on this page.

Awards are made on a rolling basis, and the published warning is that the scholarship budget may be used before the end of the Master's admission cycle, with limited funding and a high volume of deserving candidates - so early application is explicitly recommended.
Merit retention: to keep the Merit Scholarship and the Explorers, McKinsey and Women in Finance awards, students must check the merit criteria at the end of the first year of the Master's programme.

CEMS awards: the application period starts in November of CEMS Year 1; the CEMS Alumni Scholarship targets students with high financial need in CEMS MIM Year 1, and the BNP Paribas award's € 9,200 yearly global amount can be divided between up to three students.

important_advice_for_students: The scholarship decision is made in your Master's application, not after it. Interest must be shown in the designated field at the time you apply, and the page states applications cannot be considered after the Master's application has been submitted. This is the single most costly mistake available here.
Apply early - the school says so explicitly. Awards are made on a rolling basis and the budget can run out before the Master's admission cycle ends.
You will never be funded for the first instalment. Every award, including every 100% award, excludes the enrolment-fee instalment, and you must pay it to secure your place.
Know the 70% stacking ceiling before you chase the biggest number. Multiple Nova SBE awards together cannot exceed 70% of total tuition unless the whole package is a 100% social mobility scholarship.

The financial-need route is the strongest one. The Social Mobility Scholarship goes to 100%, and most partner-funded 100% awards require eligibility for a 100% Social Mobility or Continuity Scholarship - so the tax-return evidence is the gateway, not a side application.

Some of the best-funded awards are nationality-restricted. The António Serrenho, Banco Primus, Deloitte, McKinsey First Generation, McKinsey Women in Leadership and NOS awards require Portuguese nationality; the two McKinsey awards accept three years' residence in Portugal; the Explorer Excellence award is open to students of all nationalities but only in three named programmes.

Second stages are real. Banco Primus, NOS and Explorer Excellence want a three-minute video in English and add a final interview; several others want a specific document pack; André Sousa Bessa adds a family interview. Treat the email stage as part of the application.
Watch your spam folder. The page tells you twice that you are responsible for checking your email, including spam and trash, during the process.
The Portuguese-language regulations are the binding text and this English page is a summary. If a conflict matters to you, read the regulation linked for that specific award.

The McKinsey awards state that candidates 'may have a final interview with McKinsey'. These are partner interviews, not academic referees, and they are the published reason to prepare beyond the application form.

post_award_requirements: Pay the first instalment of tuition as the enrolment fee to secure your place - it is excluded from every award, including the 100% awards.
For the Nova SBE Merit Scholarship and the Explorers, McKinsey and Women in Finance awards, check the merit criteria at the end of the first year of the Master's programme to keep the award.

Stay within the stacking ceiling: funding across Nova SBE awards cannot exceed 70% of the total tuition fee unless the entire package comes from a 100% social mobility scholarship, and the Women in Finance Scholarship cannot be combined with the Merit Scholarship.
Remain enrolled in the specific programme for which the award was granted, and in the award's published intake.
Expect to be contacted by email for second stages, and to monitor spam and trash folders, throughout the process.
If you hold the CEMS awards, the funding applies to the CEMS Year 2 fee and runs from November of CEMS Year 1.

official.description: U.Porto states that it "promotes and/or sponsors a wide range of financial support for its students and researchers in order to ensure equal opportunity regarding access to our courses and to reward the merit of those students who have displayed exceptional academic achievement." These scholarships are a cash prize for students enrolled in Bachelor's, Master's and Integrated Master's programmes who display exceptional academic achievement, regardless of their socio-economic situation." selection_criteria: Academic excellence (weight 50%): as demonstrated by past academic results, transcripts, awards and distinctions. Indicators: academic record; scholarships and awards held; duration of previous studies; type of program and courses pursued; relative standing if available

Research potential (weight 30%): as demonstrated by research history, interest in discovery, the proposed research, its potential contribution to the advancement of knowledge in the field and any anticipated outcomes. Indicators: quality and originality of contributions to research and development; relevance of work experience and academic training to the field of proposed research; significance, feasibility and merit of proposed research; sound judgment and ability to think critically; ability to apply skills and knowledge; initiative and autonomy; research experience and achievements relative to expectations of someone with your academic experience

Personal characteristics and interpersonal skills (weight 20%): as demonstrated by past professional and relevant extracurricular interactions and collaborations. Indicators: work experience; leadership experience; project management including organizing conferences and meetings; ability or potential to communicate theoretical, technical or scientific concepts clearly and logically in written and oral formats; involvement in academic life; volunteerism and community outreach

official.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Master's (CGRS M) is one of three programs in the Canada Research Training Awards Suite, jointly administered by CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC, and it supports up to 3,298 students annually across all disciplines. The value is $27,000 for 12 months, and the merit review is conducted by the host institution against published weights of academic excellence 50%, research potential 30% and personal characteristics and interpersonal skills 20%. Applicants must be Canadian citizens, permanent residents or Protected Persons as of the deadline, and must have completed 0 to 12 months of full-time study in the program for which funding is requested. Applications go through the Research Portal to up to three institutions by 1 December before 8:00 pm ET, and offers are available in the portal from 1 April with alternate offers possible until 31 January of the following year.
official.program_type: Tri-agency government research training award (institutionally administered merit scholarship)
official.region: Canada (eligible Canadian institutions only, without exception)
official.coverage: A $27,000 stipend for 12 months with optional supplements; the published value contains no tuition-fee component, and the pages do not state that tuition, living costs and required expenses are covered, so it is not recorded as fully funded.
official.funding: Stipend: $27,000 for 1 year (page: 'Value and duration: $27,000 for 1 year')

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your status is Canadian citizenship, permanent residency or Protected Person as of 1 December - this is a hard gate
Identify up to three Canadian institutions that hold a CGRS M allocation in your field of research; applications to institutions without an allocation in your field will be re-labelled or refused
Contact the faculty of graduate studies at each institution for their internal admission deadline, which is earlier than the agency deadline
Count your completed months of full-time study in the program for which you are requesting funding as of 31 December, and confirm you fall in the 0-12 month or the 4-12 month window
Confirm you have not held a Master's-level CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC scholarship, or an Indigenous Scholars Award and/or Supplement
Confirm you are applying to only one CRTAS program this academic year
Ask your institution how it applies the first-class average requirement, since institutions may at their discretion accept applicants who have not obtained one
Start the Research Portal application early - the agencies warn of portal congestion near the deadline and require all 11 steps to be complete
common_rejection_risks: Missing the institutional admission deadline while hitting the 1 December agency deadline - the agencies require you to respect the internal deadline
Applying to more than three institutions, or to institutions with no allocation in your field of research
Being outside the 0-12 or 4-12 month study window as of 31 December, or miscounting part-time study (part-time is calculated proportionally by percentage of full-time course load)
Holding or currently holding another Master's-level tri-agency scholarship, which is disqualifying
Applying to more than one CRTAS program in the same academic year, where only the first eligible application is retained
Portal congestion causing a late submission on 1 December - the agencies state that late applications will not be accepted and that the burden is the applicant's
Missing the English or French submission option, or omitting certified translations of documents in another language
Forgetting to check the Research Portal for results from 1 April onward, with alternate offers possible until 31 January
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees - the $27,000 is a stipend with no published tuition component
Living costs above the $27,000 over 12 months
Bench fees, equipment, computing and fieldwork costs
Health insurance, where not provided by the province or institution
Conference and travel costs, unless you win the CRTAS Research Travel Supplements, which is the only concurrent award permitted

Research which Canadian institutions hold a CGRS M allocation in your field of research and shortlist up to three
Contact the faculty of graduate studies at each shortlisted institution for the internal admission deadline and the first-class average policy
Count your months of full-time study in the program for which you are requesting funding as of 31 December and confirm you are in the eligible window
Read the Tri-agency research training award holder's guide and the 11-step application instructions
Create your Research Portal account early and complete all 11 steps for each institution you are applying to
Arrange certified translations of any documents not in English or French
Submit all applications before 8:00 pm ET on 1 December 2026, allowing for portal congestion
From 1 April, check the Research Portal regularly for offers, and again for alternate offers until 31 January
On acceptance, confirm you hold no other tri-agency award, and comply with the award holder's guide

official.english_requirement_note: The PBEEE does not require an English language test. The program rules address only the language of forms and documents: 'Forms and documents must be completed in French. Documents written in a language other than French must be accompanied by a basic translation into French (Section 3.6 of the Common General Regulations).' The programme's official working language for applications is French, and no English score or level is published, so none is asserted here.
selection_criteria: The excellence of the applications presented will be assessed by multidisciplinary evaluation committees composed of professors and university researchers

Applications are evaluated according to the evaluation criteria and weighting published in the program rules, illustrated in the page image at https://frq.gouv.qc.ca/app/uploads/2025/08/capture-decran-2025-08-14-180258.png
official.duration: Component-dependent. VM: maximum 6 instalments, 2 years. Doctoral: up to 12 sessions, 3 years, with a reduced rate in sessions 10-12 if extended. Postdoctoral: not renewable, 3 instalments. Short-term: not renewable, maximum 4 instalments.
award_holder_conditions: Must comply with the scholarship holder's guide to the applicable rules
The start of the scholarship period must fall between 1 May 2026 and 15 January 2027; the scholarship is not retroactive and semesters prior to summer 2026 cannot be funded
Scholarship payments only begin once the FRQ receives a copy of the study permit for doctoral candidates, or the work permit for postdoctoral candidates
Must be dedicated full time to the research and to the research activities of the program

Must be physically present in Québec for the entire duration of the scholarship and attend the host university, except for the short-term component and research stays outside Québec authorised by the FRQ
Must comply with the scholarship terms and conditions regarding joint (cotutelle) degrees, concurrent scholarships, and part-time work with the supervisor's agreement
Open access is required: the thesis and peer-reviewed publications produced with scholarship support must be accessible without embargo
Must grant the MES and the FRQ a non-exclusive, irrevocable and non-transferable licence on the final report and research findings
Must acknowledge the financial support of the MES in partnership with the FRQ in publications, notices and interviews
supplements_or_initiatives: Component-specific supplementary scholarships for certain countries and institutions
Responsibility of the MES - the scholarship is financed by the Ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur and the Fonds de recherche du Québec

official.description: The PBEEE (Programme de bourses d'excellence pour les étudiants étrangers) is a merit scholarship from the Québec Ministry of Higher Education and the Fonds de recherche du Québec for foreign students doing full-time research study in Québec, awarded in 14 sub-components. Amounts and duration vary by component, from a $3,000 per month short-term award to a doctoral award totalling up to $87,000 over three years, and the MES adds an exemption from higher foreign-student tuition fees plus RAMQ medical insurance. The 2026-2027 round is marked out of competition and candidates must be preselected by a Québec university, the CCTT network or the China Scholarship Council.
official.program_type: Government research scholarship for foreign students (Québec)
official.coverage: Covers a component-dependent stipend for up to three years, a French-language university tuition-fee exemption for foreign students, and RAMQ medical insurance; it does not cover travel, family or relocation costs, and the physical-presence requirement means applicants must live in Québec throughout.

application_readiness_checklist: Establish your preselection route first - a Québec university, the CCTT network or the China Scholarship Council - because only preselected candidates can enter the competition
Apply to the university programme as a research master's, doctoral or postdoctoral study option; a professional master's, an essay or a literature review is ineligible
Check your country of citizenship against the component-specific bilateral agreements with Brazil, China, India, Israel and Wallonia before choosing a component
Confirm you are not a Canadian citizen or permanent resident and have not applied for Canadian permanent residence
Time your start between 1 May 2026 and 15 January 2027, since the award is not retroactive
Collect transcripts for every year of university study in chronological order, newest to oldest, with grading systems for non-North American institutions
Line up your supervisor early, since for some components the supervisor submits the acceptance letter through FRQnet, not you
Prepare all documents in French or with a French translation, as the forms and documents must be in French
common_rejection_risks: Not being preselected, which makes entry to the competition impossible regardless of academic strength
Applying to a professional master's or a non-research study option
Missing the earlier 23 October 2025 institutional nomination deadline, which is two months before the applicant deadline and is outside the applicant's control
Being a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or having applied for permanent residence
Already having received a PBEEE
Choosing a component whose bilateral agreement excludes your nationality
Starting the study period before 1 May 2026 or after 15 January 2027, which makes earlier or later months unfundable
Being a Québec, Wallonia or Maghreb candidate, who is ineligible, with Wallonia requiring prior study at a French-language Belgian institution
Not being able to be physically present in Québec for the whole scholarship period
estimated_uncovered_costs: Airfare to Québec and any travel, which the program does not list
Relocation and family costs
Room, board and everyday living costs beyond the stipend, which the program does not itemise
Research consumables and equipment not covered by the supervisor or institution
Any study costs before the 1 May 2026 start, which are explicitly unfundable
document_audit: Order transcripts newest to oldest as the rules specify, and include the grading system for any non-North-American transcript
Attach publisher acknowledgements for submitted articles and editor notices for accepted articles where the component requires them
If you have ever interrupted your studies, obtain both the official institutional attestation and a medical certificate, since either alone is insufficient
Confirm your supervisor has actually submitted the acceptance letter through FRQnet for components that require it
Include a justification and supporting documents for any exception measure, rather than assuming an exception will be granted

On award, begin the scholarship period between 1 May 2026 and 15 January 2027 and apply for your study or work permit
Accept the open access, licensing and acknowledgement conditions

official.description: The Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED) program is a short-term exchange offered by Global Affairs Canada, enabling students from ASEAN member states to conduct study or research at a Canadian post-secondary institution in areas that contribute to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It provides 10,200 CAD for four months or one academic term, funding eligible expenses including airfare, health insurance, living expenses, ground transportation and books. Canadian institutions apply on behalf of candidates through My EduCanada, and the 2025 application period is closed.
official.coverage: Covers 10,200 CAD for four months or one academic term, applicable to visa or permit fees, airfare, health insurance, living expenses, ground transportation, and books and supplies; college and undergraduate tuition fees are waived through a required student exchange agreement, and graduate study does not require an agreement.

official.description: The UCAS Scholarship for International Students offers non-Chinese students funding to study at the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences or a CAS institute. The Full Scholarship bundles a tuition waiver (PhD RMB 40,000/year, Master's RMB 30,000/year), a monthly stipend (PhD RMB 2,500, Master's RMB 2,000, topped up by host assistantship to at least RMB 3,500 and RMB 3,000 respectively), basic accommodation, RMB 800/year medical insurance and a RMB 600 application fee waiver, for up to 36 months without extension; a Partial Scholarship covers tuition, insurance and the fee waiver only. PhD and Master's applications closed on 31 January 2026, while visiting student categories are open-ended.

official.coverage: Covers tuition exemption, a monthly living stipend, basic accommodation, medical insurance and the application fee; it does not state any travel, settlement or repatriation component, and the stipend is a contribution rather than a full cost-of-living guarantee.

purpose: The University of Helsinki Doctoral School (UHDS) provides annual funding for doctoral researcher positions in the University's doctoral programmes. The University-funded doctoral researcher positions covered by this record - the salaried doctoral researcher posts referred to on the University pages as university-funded doctoral researcher positions - are the same employment scheme: annual funding, one application round, and a position designated as full-time work.
The positions are designated as full-time work, not study (published: 'These doctoral researcher positions are designated as full-time work').

application_steps: 1. Identify the doctoral programme you want to apply to. The University directs applicants to the doctoral programme's own webpage for programme information, research plans, supervisors and contact details.

2. Read both the general application instructions and the doctoral programme specific instructions in the Studies Service. The University states that both should be read carefully, and the programme-specific instructions can add to the general ones.

3. Contact the doctoral programme directly if you have questions about the programme, your research plan or potential supervisors - the University explicitly routes these questions to the programme rather than answering them centrally.
4. Prepare your application against the instructions you have read, including the programme's own requirements.
5. Submit within the single annual application period, which for the next salaried round is 24 August to 7 September 2026.
6. If awarded, take up the position as full-time work, with the employee rights published for university-funded doctoral researchers.

important_advice_for_students: This is a job, not a grant. The position is designated as full-time work, so plan for employment realities - tax, pension, contract terms - rather than for a student stipend.

official.description: Tampere University offers a highly selective Tampere University tuition fee scholarship awarded at admission, covering 50% of the tuition fees for the programme duration for a limited number of the best-performing applicants. A separate early bird offer gives a EUR 2,000 reduction on the first year of tuition fees to all fee-paying students who are not awarded the tuition fee scholarship, and a Graduation Scholarship of EUR 2,000 is available to Bachelor's graduates who graduate within three academic years. The scholarship application is made as part of the admission application through Studyinfo.fi.
purpose: To support fee-paying students at Tampere University: 'Tampere University offers a limited number of partial scholarships as well as an early bird discount to support fee-paying students.'
The tuition fee scholarship is 'an exclusive opportunity awarded to a limited number of the best-performing applicants'.
The early bird offer incentivises rapid acceptance of an admission offer and payment of the reduced first-year fee.
The Graduation Scholarship rewards Bachelor's graduates who complete their degree within three academic years and continue to a Master's degree at Tampere University.

official.degree_award: Not an award in its own right: these are tuition-fee reductions attached to admission to a Tampere University bachelor's or master's degree programme. No separate credential is awarded.
official.duration: The tuition fee scholarship covers 50% of the tuition fees for the programme duration. 'The total duration of any Tampere University scholarships may not be longer than the normative duration of studies for the degree to be completed' - three academic years for a Bachelor's degree and two academic years for a Master's degree, calculated on the basis of semesters enrolled as attending. The early bird offer is valid only for the first year of studies.
official.application_cycle: Awarded at admission. The scholarship must be applied for as part of the application for admission, during the relevant admission application period, using the same online application used to apply for admission at Studyinfo.fi. Tampere University describes the offers as 'Scholarships available at admission in 2027'.
official.deadline_central_display: No scholarship deadline is published on the official page; the scholarship is applied for within the admission application period at Studyinfo.fi, whose dates vary by admission round and start term.

The early bird offer has its own operational deadline: the student must accept the study place and pay the reduced first-year tuition fee within three weeks (21 days) after receiving the admission information. Scholarships are not available in the open university route or transfer applications.

official.tuition_coverage_note: The tuition fee scholarship covers 50% of tuition fees for the programme duration (EUR 10,000 per academic year in all Bachelor's programmes and EUR 12,000 in all Master's programmes for students admitted in 2027, so roughly EUR 5,000-6,000 per academic year remains payable). The early bird offer reduces the first-year fee by EUR 2,000 and the Graduation Scholarship reduces the first year of Master's tuition by EUR 2,000; these are separate from the 50% scholarship.
official.tuition_rule: Tampere University waives 50% of the tuition fee itself for the holders of the tuition fee scholarship, awarded at admission to a limited number of applicants. Tuition fees are payable by students who are citizens of countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland studying in a bachelor's or master's programme taught in English; the fee is not charged to EU/EEA/Swiss citizens or other fee-exempt students, so those students cannot hold the fee-paying scholarship. Joint programmes may have different fees.
official.host_institution_fee: The Student Union TREY membership fee and the student healthcare fee are explicitly not covered by the tuition fee, and the tuition fee itself does not cover personal study-related costs such as study materials, books, computers or printers.

official.description: The Nokia Scholarship is a one-off grant of up to EUR 7,500 for individuals pursuing a doctoral degree in Information and Communications Technologies (ICT) or in areas supporting the development of ICT. official.description: The Fulbright-Nokia Distinguished Chair in Information and Communications Technologies is a 3-6 month research, teaching and guest-lecturing appointment for a U.S. scholar or specialist at a Finnish higher education institution of the scholar's own choosing. official.description: The France-South Africa Scholarship Programme of the French Embassy to South Africa awards France Excellence scholarship holder status to students with South African, Lesotho or Malawian citizenship studying a Master's degree or PhD in France, with the 2027 call running from 21 July 2026 to 8 October 2026 for September 2027 entry. official.description: Dublin City University offers a family of partial, merit-based tuition-fee scholarships for 2027-28 that applicants who apply as non-EU students are automatically considered for; there is no separate scholarship application. Awards are faculty and level specific, ranging from a EUR 1,850 fee reduction (Humanities and Social Sciences undergraduate) to EUR 6,100 (Faculty of Science and Health undergraduate), and the reduction is applied directly to the student's account. Only successful recipients are notified by email, and a recipient of one DCU International scholarship cannot also be considered for another DCU scholarship such as the DCU Merit Scholarship.

The purpose is a partial reduction of the full-time 2027-28 Non-EU tuition fee; DCU states generally that its scholarships 'are intended to cover full or partial payment of tuition fees or living costs', though these awards are fee reductions only.

official.description: This record covers the University of Bologna's Study grants and subsidies hub for a.y. 2026/27, whose main international instrument is the reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax) for citizens of particularly poor and developing countries or non-OECD countries who declare that their family holds income and assets only outside Italy. For a.y. 2026/27 that fixed fee is EUR 500 to EUR 700 plus the mandatory EUR 157.04 first instalment for first and single cycle programmes, and EUR 600 to EUR 1,400 plus EUR 157.04 for second cycle programmes, depending on country category and credit attainment. The page also covers ER.GO regional study grants, which give full tax exemption leaving only EUR 157.04 payable, plus merit, disability, parental, family-member and refugee fee reductions.
purpose: 'You can count on financial support at every stage of your studies. Discover opportunities tailored to your needs.'
The fee reduction mechanism exists because 'Studying at the University of Bologna is an achievable goal regardless of your financial situation: fees are lower for those with lower incomes'.

The reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax) is described as 'an important aid for those who are citizens of a particularly poor and developing country or one that is not member of the European Union and the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development'.
The ER.GO regional study grant scheme exists so that 'The Region bears the cost of your academic studies'.
Where several exemptions apply simultaneously, the University states it 'will apply the most advantageous one for you'.

official.deadline_note: Multiple distinct deadlines apply and none of them is a scholarship deadline. (1) Income documentation (ISEE, or documents for foreign income) must be uploaded by 30 October 2026 at 18:00, or 16 November 2026 at 18:00 with a EUR 100 late submission fee; failing to upload means no exemption and the full programme amount is payable. (2) Fee payment deadlines for open-access programmes with no entrance exam: 24 September 2026 for Bachelor's and single cycle degrees, 29 October 2026 for second cycle/two-year Master's degrees, with a final late window to 19 November 2026 for the first instalment with a late payment fee. (3) Second instalment by 18 December 2026 and third instalment by 15 March 2027. (4) Amounts of the second and third instalments only become visible after 23 November 2026. (5) The reduced fixed fee declaration itself is made through the ER.GO portal; if the form is not completed, the reduction is applied automatically but the University then requires a separate declaration of foreign-only family income and assets by the deadline given in a Student Contributions Office email, and failure to reply means being charged the maximum tuition fee.
official.funding_label: Reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax) for citizens of particularly poor and developing countries or non-OECD countries, a.y. 2026/27: EUR 500-700 (first/single cycle) or EUR 600-1,400 (second cycle) plus the mandatory EUR 157.04 first instalment; ER.GO scholarship recipients pay only EUR 157.04
official.funding_period: per academic year; a.y. 2026/27 amounts published
official.tuition_coverage_note: Partial tuition coverage only, and it varies by category. Reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax) for a.y. 2026/27: citizens of particularly poor and developing countries pay EUR 500 + EUR 157.04 on first or single cycle programmes and EUR 600 + EUR 157.04 on second cycle programmes if a freshman or holding the minimum credits, or EUR 600 + EUR 157.04 and EUR 700 + EUR 157.04 respectively if the minimum credits are not held. Nationals of non-OECD countries pay EUR 1,000 + EUR 157.04 and EUR 1,200 + EUR 157.04 respectively if a freshman or holding the minimum credits, or EUR 1,200 + EUR 157.04 and EUR 1,400 + EUR 157.04 without them. ER.GO scholarship recipients get full tax exemption and pay only the EUR 157.04 first instalment. Full exemption of the variable part (paying only EUR 157.04) also applies where the family economic indicator is at or below EUR 27,000.
official.tuition_rule: The University of Bologna itself reduces the tuition contribution. The fee has two parts: a fixed instalment of EUR 157.04 that is always due, and a variable part depending on the programme and calculated on the family unit's economic situation. The reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax) replaces the variable part with a published flat amount for citizens of listed particularly poor or developing countries and of non-OECD countries; the flat fee is a fixed-amount tax rather than an income-assessed contribution. Where the student does not qualify, the maximum all-inclusive contribution for the programme is payable.
official.home_tuition_rule: The requirement that the applicant's family hold income and assets only outside Italy is the mirror image of home-country fee treatment: the fee status is assessed on the family unit's Italian and foreign income, with ISEE for income in Italy and separate documentation for foreign income and assets.
official.host_institution_fee: The first instalment of EUR 157.04 is 'not a university fee, but an amount that you must always pay, regardless of your financial status, even in the case of total exemption'. It comprises the regional right to higher education tax of EUR 140, EUR 16 stamp duty and EUR 1.04 for the accident insurance premium. It cannot be refunded: on withdrawal, only EUR 17.04 of stamp duty and insurance is deducted, and only the EUR 140 regional tax can be reclaimed from ER.GO.
official.tax_status: Three distinct tax regimes are published. (1) Reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax): a fixed-amount tax for international students who meet the stated requirements. (2) Total or partial exemption (No Tax Area): a fee reduced on the basis of the family's economic status, requiring the relevant documentation and specific merit requirements (CFU and year of enrolment). (3) Full exemption for ER.GO scholarship recipients. The University states these are incompatible where it matters: 'reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax) and total or partial exemption (No Tax Area) are incompatible'.
covered_expenses: Reduced fixed fee for citizens of particularly poor and developing countries: EUR 500 + EUR 157.04 (first or single cycle) and EUR 600 + EUR 157.04 (second cycle) for a freshman or a student holding the minimum credits; EUR 600 + EUR 157.04 and EUR 700 + EUR 157.04 without the minimum credits

Reduced fixed fee for nationals of non-OECD countries: EUR 1,000 + EUR 157.04 (first or single cycle) and EUR 1,200 + EUR 157.04 (second cycle) for a freshman or a student holding the minimum credits; EUR 1,200 + EUR 157.04 and EUR 1,400 + EUR 157.04 without the minimum credits
Full exemption of the variable part where the family economic indicator is at or below EUR 27,000, leaving only EUR 157.04 payable

Full exemption of the variable part for first-year second cycle students who graduated on time and with top marks under the merit-based incentive, for students at the Collegio Superiore, permanent members of religious orders, students with a civil disability certificate of 66% or more or an L. 104 certificate, students with a parent receiving a disability pension under L. 118/1971, and students who become parents during the year with an indicator at or below EUR 40,000
Full exemption for ER.GO scholarship recipients, leaving only the EUR 157.04 first instalment

Partial exemption where the indicator is above EUR 27,000, where other family members attend the University of Bologna and the indicator is below EUR 60,000, and where the applicant is a citizen of a particularly poor or developing country or a non-OECD country with family income and assets only outside Italy
20% fee reduction for students with other family members enrolled at the University of Bologna

Fee reduction for graduating students who only have to sit the final examination: EUR 500 if graduating by 30 September 2027 (or 30 November 2027 for healthcare professions programmes) and EUR 1,000 if graduating by 31 December 2027

Canteen discounts, discounted public transport passes in Bologna, Cesena, Forli, Ravenna and Rimini, cinema, museum, theatre and sports discounts, and free licences for Matlab, Prezi, Stata SE, Microsoft 365 and Mathematica
University halls of residence accommodation and rent grants through published calls for applications
not_covered_or_excluded: The mandatory first instalment of EUR 157.04 (regional right to higher education tax EUR 140, EUR 16 stamp duty, EUR 1.04 accident insurance), payable regardless of financial status and even under total exemption
Living costs, accommodation and travel are not covered by the fee reduction itself; hall of residence places and rent grants are separate, competitive calls for applications

Reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax) and total or partial exemption (No Tax Area) are incompatible: applying for No Tax Area means submitting foreign-income documentation that ER.GO checks, and incomplete or incorrect documentation removes Flat Tax eligibility and results in the maximum programme fee
Reduced-fee entitlement is lost if the applicant has been enrolled for more years than the standard duration of the programme plus one, calculated from the academic year of first matriculation

Reduced-fee entitlement requires the family to hold income and assets only outside Italy; with dual citizenship the applicant must specify where the family's income and assets are and may only accept the reduced fee if those are exclusively in a particularly poor or non-OECD country

If the Flat Tax form is not completed, the reduction is applied automatically but the applicant must still make the foreign-income declaration within the deadline given by the Student Contributions Office email, and failure to reply results in being charged the maximum tuition fee amount
Benefit is revoked on a negative ER.GO outcome, for example documentation with missing or incorrect data

Non-EEA nationals who are not naturalised, and those without permission to remain in the State or holding only short-term or temporary permission such as work permits or study visas, are not eligible for Irish-style state fee support; the analogous published rule here is that free-fee-style concessions are governed by the University's own criteria and merit requirements
Minimum credit attainment is required: 10 CFU from 11 August 2025 to 10 August 2026 to enrol in the second year, and 25 CFU to enrol in years after the second

Late payment triggers a block on the student career - the student cannot sit exams or carry out procedures such as withdrawal or transfer until the fees and late payment fee are paid (EUR 30 for delays up to thirty days, EUR 150 for longer)
benefits: Where more than one exemption situation applies, the applicant may submit an application for each and the University states it 'will apply the most advantageous one for you'
An exemption application and a scholarship application can be made before the programme is chosen or before enrolment is completed, so deadlines are not missed
The Flat Tax route requires no documentary evidence of the family's economic situation: 'You do not have to attach any documentation on your family's economic situation'
ER.GO benefits extend beyond fees to accommodation in university residences, catering contributions and season transport tickets

Separate calls on the same hub cover 150-hour collaboration grants, peer tutoring grants, international mobility scholarships, degree and doctoral awards, research scholarships, and scholarships for students from countries where access to university education is prevented or severely limited by conflict or discriminatory policies
eligibility: For the reduced fixed fee: hold citizenship in one of the published particularly poor or developing countries, or in one of the published non-OECD countries

documents: ISEE (family economic indicator) where the family's income is in Italy

Merit-based total exemption for first-year second cycle students who 'graduated on time and with top marks'

official.program_type: Public university tuition-fee reduction and regional right-to-higher-education study grant scheme
official.coverage: Covers part or all of the variable tuition contribution, never the EUR 157.04 fixed first instalment. application_readiness_checklist: Check your country against the two published 2026 lists (particularly poor/developing countries, and non-OECD countries) - this is the gate to the Flat Tax route

Count your years of enrolment from the academic year of first matriculation, including years at another university or on another programme, and confirm you are within the standard duration plus one year
Confirm your family holds income and assets only outside Italy; if it holds any in Italy, the Flat Tax route does not apply and you need the ISEE-based exemption route
Gather the ISEE or foreign income and asset documentation, ready to upload in Studenti Online by 30 October 2026 at 18:00
Set the 16 November 2026 at 18:00 fallback in your calendar with the EUR 100 late submission fee budgeted
Budget the EUR 157.04 first instalment, which is due whatever your status
Check your CFU attainment between 11 August 2025 and 10 August 2026: you need 10 CFU for second year and 25 CFU for later years to keep the income-based exemption
If you have dual citizenship, be ready to state where the family's income and assets are on the form
If you want ER.GO or Unibo benefits on top, tick the economic-status submission in the same ER.GO portal form rather than using the Flat Tax-only route
Set a PagoPA payment for each instalment and check Studenti Online after 23 November 2026 for the later instalment amounts
important_advice_for_students: Do not ignore the 30 October documentation deadline - missing it means no exemption at all and the maximum programme fee, not a smaller fee
Do not submit the wrong route: Flat Tax and No Tax Area are incompatible, and an incomplete foreign-income submission through the No Tax Area route actually destroys your Flat Tax eligibility
Do not assume the fee is zero; EUR 157.04 is always payable, and it is a tax plus stamp duty plus insurance, not a university fee
Do not treat the reduced fee as permanent - it must be claimed again every academic year, and the credit window (11 August to 10 August) is what decides your next-year fee

Do not assume your Flat Tax declaration is complete just because the form was optional; if you skip it the reduction is applied automatically but you must still answer the Student Contributions Office email within its stated deadline or the maximum fee is charged
Do not rely on reminders from the University - it states it does not send automatic notifications
Do not wait for the second and third instalment amounts to appear before 23 November 2026; they will not be visible earlier

Do consider the ER.GO study grant route if your situation allows it, since a successful ER.GO scholarship reduces you to paying only EUR 157.04 and can be combined with hall of residence and catering support
Do not ignore the restricted-entry programmes: if yours has an entrance exam, the payment deadline is in that programme's call, not the university-wide date
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 30 October 2026 at 18:00 documentation deadline, or paying the EUR 100 late fee after 16 November 2026 at 18:00 and then also missing payment
Applying for No Tax Area with incomplete or incorrect foreign-income documentation, which removes Flat Tax eligibility and results in the maximum fee
Being enrolled beyond the standard duration of the programme plus one year
Missing the credit thresholds (10 CFU for second year, 25 CFU for later years) in the 11 August 2025 to 10 August 2026 window
Failing to declare that family income and assets are solely abroad when the Student Contributions Office asks, which results in the maximum fee
A negative ER.GO verification outcome, which revokes benefits already obtained
Not paying the EUR 157.04 first instalment by the deadline, which blocks the student career
Assuming the university-wide 24 September deadline applies to a restricted-entry programme with an entrance exam
estimated_uncovered_costs: The mandatory first instalment of EUR 157.04 every year (EUR 140 regional tax, EUR 16 stamp duty, EUR 1.04 accident insurance)
Living costs and rent in Bologna, which the fee schemes do not cover
Housing in university halls of residence unless a separate competitive call is won
Food beyond discounted canteen prices
Travel, visa and immigration costs
Books, materials, equipment and printing
The difference between the reduced fixed fee and the programme's maximum all-inclusive contribution, which is what a non-qualifying student would pay
PagoPA late payment fees: EUR 30 for delays up to thirty days, EUR 150 for longer, and a EUR 100 late submission fee for late income documentation
A EUR 150 late enrolment fee if you enrol in a.y. 2026/27 after deciding not to and then changing your mind
document_audit: Flat Tax route: no economic documentation is required at all - 'You do not have to attach any documentation on your family's economic situation'. Keep a copy of the submitted declaration showing that you accepted the flat-rate fee

Income-based route: ISEE where income is in Italy, or the required foreign income and asset documentation, uploaded in Studenti Online by 30 October 2026 at 18:00 (or 16 November 2026 at 18:00 with the EUR 100 late fee)
Dual citizenship: the form must state where the family's income and assets are, and you may only accept the reduced fee if those are exclusively in a particularly poor or non-OECD country
Country eligibility: verify against the two published PDF lists (Elenco Paesi Particolarmente Poveri 2026, Elenco Paesi NON OCSE 2026)
Credit evidence: proof of 10 CFU (second year) or 25 CFU (later years) attained between 11 August 2025 and 10 August 2026
Disability evidence: civil disability certificate of 66% or more, or L. 104 certificate, where claimed; parental disability pension documentation under L. 118/1971 where claimed
Fee position: check Studenti Online 'Fee Situation - enrolment' to confirm the fee applied, and keep the payment confirmation, remembering the update may take up to two days
Graduating-student reduction: proof that all ECTS except the final examination are complete, plus a family indicator at or below EUR 40,000, when applying to the notice issued around January 2027

referee_tracking.instructions: The official pages name no referees and no recommendation letters for the fee reductions or the Flat Tax route, which are entitlement-based on published criteria. official.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT, Monbukagakusho) Scholarship for Research Students funds graduate-level study at a Japanese university through either embassy recommendation or university recommendation. For research students the scholarship pays a monthly stipend of JPY 143,000 to 145,000, exempts tuition in full, and provides a round-trip airfare travel allowance. Under embassy recommendation the term is within two years for an irregular course or the standard school year for a regular course, with six months of preliminary Japanese language training added where needed; under university recommendation the duration depends on each university's quota, up to a standard school year. Applicants must be under 35 and eligible for admission to a master's or doctoral programme at a Japanese graduate school.
purpose: One of seven types of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship programme, whose stated scope is study in Japan for students from overseas.

Research students study a 'Major in field of specialty at a graduate school etc.' - the programme's field of study is the applicant's graduate-school specialisation rather than a general scholarship theme.

The programme has two application routes so that candidates can be recruited either by a Japanese diplomatic mission in their own country or by a Japanese university with an MEXT-approved recommendation quota.

The page states that detailed requirements are set in the application guidelines and that 'If the application qualifications differ from the application guidelines, the contents of the guidelines should be followed.'
study_type: Graduate school research studies
Preliminary training of Japanese etc. (six months) where required
official.degree_award: Not a separate award: it is a scholarship attached to study in a Japanese graduate school programme, leading to the qualification of that programme. No additional credential is conferred by the scholarship itself.
official.duration: [Embassy recommendation] Irregular course: within 2 years; Regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added). [University recommendation] Duration depends on each school's quota (up to a standard school year). Preliminary training of Japanese etc.: 6 months, only for those who need this training.
official.application_cycle: Annual, run in two cycles: embassy recommendation (candidates are recruited and initially screened by a Japanese embassy or consulate general in their own country) and university recommendation (Japanese universities recruit candidates under student-exchange agreements and then recommend them to MEXT). The page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission in their country for openings.
official.deadline_central_display: No central deadline is published. Applications for embassy recommendation are made through the Japanese embassy or other diplomatic mission in the applicant's own country, and the type and field of application vary from country to country; university-recommendation applicants apply to a Japanese university that holds an MEXT recommendation quota, where 'Application requirements and academic standards vary depending on the accepting university'.
official.deadline_institutional: For university recommendation, no institutional deadline is published on this page; deadlines and requirements are set by each accepting Japanese university and differ by university. For embassy recommendation, deadlines are set nationally by each Japanese embassy or diplomatic mission and are not published centrally.

official.description: The NL Scholarship (formerly the Holland Scholarship) is a Dutch government and university-funded award for international students from outside the European Economic Area who want to do a bachelor's or master's in the Netherlands. It pays a single amount of EUR 5,000, disbursed in the first year of studies, and the official page states explicitly that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. Applicants apply to one of the participating Dutch research universities or universities of applied sciences, which publish their own closing dates and fields of study; the programme is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with those participating institutions.
purpose: 'The NL Scholarship (formerly known as Holland Scholarship) is meant for international students from outside the European Economic Area (EEA) who want to do their bachelor's or master's in the Netherlands.'

The scholarship is financed by 'the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science as well as several Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences', so it serves both as a Dutch government instrument for attracting international students and as an institutional recruitment tool.

Its explicit design limit is stated on the page: 'The scholarship amounts to € 5,000. You will receive this in the first year of your studies. Please note that this is not a full-tuition scholarship.'

Integrity is part of the programme's purpose: Nuffic may not be involved in activities involving unacceptable behaviour, and Nuffic operates an Integrity Code of Conduct applying to those who handle individual NL Scholarships.

verification.source_conflict_rule: The Study in NL page governs the programme's purpose, amount, the four general criteria, the participating institution lists and the opening date. The participating institution's own page governs its closing dates, eligible fields, specific requirements and documents. Nuffic's Integrity Code of Conduct governs unacceptable conduct. Where the institution's requirements are stricter than the four general criteria, the institution's requirements apply.
verification.source_freshness_rule: The participating institution list and all institution-specific closing dates and fields change every academic year. Anything tied to a previous academic year's list or deadline is treated as stale; the record is re-verified when the new academic year's lists are published, which historically happens around November.

official.description: The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship at NIAS lets researchers and policymakers work on applied monetary economics, macroeconomics and public finance for five to ten months. It is open to prominent mid- to late-career researchers and to promising early-career talents from the Netherlands or abroad, with a minimum of three years of post-PhD experience required, and the Foundation gives particular priority to researchers with an outstanding record in those fields. Fellows receive a personal stipend, or a Dutch University Grant if affiliated with a Dutch university or research institute, plus subsidised housing where eligible or reimbursement of local public transport. The 2027-2028 call ran from 15 January to 13 April 2026 and has closed.

official.description: The Tilburg University Waiver is a Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) tuition-fee waiver that halves the institutional tuition fee for one-year (non-Research) Master's programmes starting in September 2027. It awards 21 waivers a year, allocated by School: six each to Tilburg School of Economics and Management, Tilburg Law School and Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences, two to Tilburg School of Social and Behavioral Sciences, and one to Tilburg School of Catholic Theology. Eligibility requires a non-EEA nationality, a most recent degree completed in one of 63 designated countries, direct admission to a regular one-year Master's, and no other tuition-fee funding; when there are more eligible applicants than waivers, recipients are chosen by random lottery and results are issued by 1 June 2027.
purpose: 'Created as part of Tilburg University's commitment to Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI), this waiver recognizes the structural barriers that can limit access to postgraduate education.'
'By reducing tuition by half, the waiver empowers talented graduates from under-represented regions to contribute, collaborate, and lead within our global academic community.'
The award exists 'to support talented students worldwide to pursue their graduate studies at Tilburg University and join our diverse academic community'.

It is explicitly aimed at 'exceptional international master's applicants who hold a non-EEA nationality and completed their previous degree in an eligible country', so the country list is the operational expression of the DEI aim.
study_type: Full-time Master's study (regular, non-Research one-year programmes; two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence also eligible)
official.degree_award: Not a degree and not a separate credential: it is a 50% reduction of the institutional tuition fee attached to admission to a Tilburg University Master's programme.
official.duration: Applies to all regular one-year Master's programmes starting in September 2027, i.e. the 2027-2028 academic year. The two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence is explicitly included as an exception. Waivers are not available for the February intake. No renewal or multi-year continuation of the waiver is described.
official.application_cycle: Annual for the 2027-2028 academic year (September intake). 21 waivers are available for that year, divided by School: Tilburg School of Economics and Management 6, Tilburg Law School 6, Tilburg School of Social and Behavioral Sciences 2, Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences 6, Tilburg School of Catholic Theology 1. Applicants are informed of the outcome by 1 June 2027.

official.deadline_institutional: For admission itself: 'For detailed admission deadlines and instructions, please visit the webpage of your chosen Master's program', so individual Master's programmes may publish additional admission deadlines before 1 April 2027.
official.deadline_note: A single waiver deadline governs the award: 1 April 2027 for both the Master's programme application and the waiver webform. Two further dates are published: results are issued by 1 June 2027, and reserve allocation requires the waiver form submitted before 1 April 2027 plus conditional or unconditional admission held by 1 June 2027. Admission deadlines are set by each individual Master's programme page and may be earlier.
