official.description: Tulī Takes Flight is a New Zealand Government scholarship for Pacific people to start or continue tertiary study or vocational training, administered through the Pacific Education Foundation. For the 2027 round it funds study at New Zealand tertiary providers at NZQA levels 4-10, paying $12,500 each year for vocational (levels 4-7 non-degree) and undergraduate study and $17,500 each year for postgraduate study, for awards of one, two or three years. The money can be used for full-time course costs such as tuition fees, materials and equipment, and for living costs such as accommodation, transport and childcare. Eligibility is limited to New Zealand citizens or permanent residents of indigenous Pacific cultural heritage who have lived in New Zealand for the last three years and are studying full-time.
purpose: The Tulī Takes Flight scholarship is 'part of the gesture of goodwill and reconciliation to Aotearoa Pacific families and communities that followed the Government's 2021 apology for the Dawn Raids that occurred in the 1970s'.
'The Tulī scholarship acknowledges the ongoing importance of education for Aotearoa Pacific families and communities.'
It is 'intended to support Pacific people to reach their potential by reducing some of the financial barriers towards study or training'.

A quarter of the scholarships awarded are targeted to priority pathways: science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM); health and allied health; digital, data and AI; engineering and skilled trades; training, research and the education workforce; and green, climate and sustainability fields.
The remaining scholarships support the full breadth of Pacific community study needs, 'including: social services, construction, Pacific languages, Pacific customs and culture'.
For the published round the Pacific Education Foundation are supporting Pacific learners moving into future-focussed fields 'while still funding the breadth of study Pacific communities need'.

official.description: The Rhodes Scholarship for New Zealand is a postgraduate award supporting outstanding all-round New Zealand students to study at the University of Oxford, funded by the Rhodes Trust with the Robertson Foundation and administered in New Zealand by Universities New Zealand – Te Pōkai Tara. Up to three scholars are elected from New Zealand each year. The scholarship's fees are paid directly by the Trust to the Oxford college and University, while the overall value of the award is set by the Rhodes Trust and is not published on the Universities New Zealand page. Candidates must hold New Zealand citizenship or a New Zealand Permanent Resident Visa, have spent at least five of the previous ten years in New Zealand, have graduated with a GPA of 7.50/9.00, and fall within the published age bands.
purpose: 'Rhodes Scholarships are postgraduate awards supporting outstanding all-round students at the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom and providing transformative opportunities for exceptional individuals.'
'Established in 1903 under the will of Cecil Rhodes, the Rhodes is the oldest and perhaps most prestigious international graduate scholarship programme in the world.'

'Rhodes's vision in founding the Scholarship was to develop outstanding leaders who would be motivated to "fight the world's fight", to "esteem the performance of public duties as their highest aim" and to promote international understanding and peace.'
'The Rhodes Trust provides the Rhodes Scholarship in partnership with the Second Century Founder, John McCall McBain, and other generous benefactors.'
In New Zealand the application and selection process is administered by Universities New Zealand – Te Pōkai Tara, on a partnership basis between the Rhodes Trust and the Robertson Foundation.
Rhodes Scholarship Advisers at each New Zealand university have the role of encouraging and supporting applications for the scholarship in New Zealand.
degree_levels: Doctoral (Oxford graduate study; the page describes the award as a postgraduate award without restricting it to taught master's)
study_type: Postgraduate study at the University of Oxford, United Kingdom

official.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International Excellence Scholarship (prior to 2023 named the University of Waikato International Excellence Scholarship) was established in 2015 to "promote educational opportunities, foster internationalisation and support talented international applicants who are enrolling as new students into undergraduate or postgraduate programmes at the University of Waikato." The regulations state: "The scholarships are tuition fees credits paid in NZD, have a value of up to $15,000 for undergraduate study and up to $10,000 for postgraduate study. Scholarships are awarded to applicants who have demonstrated excellent academic achievement. Successful applicants may be called upon to become global ambassadors for the University of Waikato." The regulations are explicit that the award is partial: "The total value offered is a contribution towards tuition fees only, and all remaining tuition fees and other costs must be met through other means."

official.application_cycle: Rolling annual cycle. "Applications can be submitted at any time and decisions will normally be made within 3 to 4 weeks of the time of application." Applications are not considered if received within four weeks of the start of each of the university's three main trimesters (A, B and C Trimesters) or H Trimester of a limited number of qualifications. official.description: The University of Otago International Master's Research Scholarship supports international students undertaking a thesis-based Master's degree at the University of Otago. It pays a stipend of NZ$18,204 per annum plus a tuition fee waiver for one year capped at NZ$35,000, covering the thesis component of a Master's Research degree for up to one year of full-time enrolment. Four scholarships are offered each year, normally one per Academic Division. Applications are accepted at any time and reviewed four times a year - 1 March, 1 June, 1 September and 1 November. Selection is based predominantly on academic merit and the applicant's potential for research.
purpose: 'The University of Otago International Research Master's Scholarship provides funding to support international Master's students studying at the University of Otago.'
The scholarship's stated design is research-focused: 'Selection is based predominantly on academic merit and the applicant's potential for research.'

It is deliberately scoped to the research element of postgraduate study: 'This Scholarship will only provide support for the thesis component of a Master's Research degree for up to 1 year full-time enrolment.'
It targets the transition into postgraduate research by international students: applicants 'must be obtaining their first Master's qualification' and 'undertaking a thesis-based Master's'.

Full-time enrolment

official.degree_award: Not an award in its own right: it is a funding award attached to enrolment in a thesis-based Master's degree at the University of Otago, leading to the Master's qualification of that programme. No separate credential is conferred.
official.duration: One year of support: the tuition fee waiver runs for 1 year, and 'This Scholarship will only provide support for the thesis component of a Master's Research degree for up to 1 year full-time enrolment.' The stipend is paid per annum.
official.application_cycle: Continuous intake with periodic assessment. 'Applicants can apply anytime but applications will be reviewed four times a year (1 March, 1 June, 1 September and 1 November).' Four scholarships are offered each year, normally one per Academic Division.
official.deadline_central_display: No closing date. Applicants can apply at any time, and applications are reviewed four times a year: 1 March, 1 June, 1 September and 1 November.
official.deadline_institutional: Applications are reviewed on four fixed review dates each year - 1 March, 1 June, 1 September and 1 November - so in practical terms an applicant must have a complete application in by the relevant review date.
official.deadline_note: This is a rolling application rather than a deadline-based scheme, so deadline_central is deliberately null and no precision can be asserted. The operative dates are the four published review dates, which determine when a complete application will next be considered.
official.funding_label: University of Otago International Master's Research Scholarship: NZ$18,204 stipend per annum plus a tuition fee waiver for 1 year capped at NZ$35,000, excluding student services fee and insurance

official.tuition_coverage_note: Partial and capped. The scholarship provides 'a tuition fee waiver for 1 year capped at NZ$35,000 for Master's study'. The University warns: 'Depending on your programme of study, the scholarship may only partially cover the cost of your tuition fees... You will be responsible for payment of any remaining tuition fees charge above the NZ$35,000 waiver.' The waiver is for the thesis component only, and explicitly excludes the student services fee and insurance.
official.tuition_rule: The University of Otago grants a tuition fee waiver itself, capped at NZ$35,000 for one year of the thesis component of a Master's Research degree. The waiver does not extend to the student services fee or insurance, and any tuition charged above NZ$35,000 remains payable by the student. The University directs students to check with its International Office for tuition fee rates.
official.host_institution_fee: The student services fee and insurance are expressly excluded from the value of the scholarship, and tuition above the NZ$35,000 waiver cap remains payable.

official.description: The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship supports doctoral students at the University of Otago, both domestic and international, and is open to candidates for the Doctor of Philosophy and for professional doctorates (DClinDent, DMA, DBA, EDd). It pays a stipend of NZ$34,128 per annum plus a tuition fee waiver for 36 months - a domestic tuition fees waiver for the PhD, and for professional doctorates a waiver capped at the domestic rate. Up to 153 scholarships are offered annually. Applications are accepted at any time and considered at quarterly rounds in March, June, September and November, with submissions made through eVision together with a completed departmental assessment by the first day of each round month. Selection rests predominantly on academic merit and research potential. The University is currently reviewing the strategic direction of its doctoral scholarship programme.
purpose: 'The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship provides funding to support doctoral students studying at the University of Otago.'
It is open to both domestic and international students: 'The Scholarship is available to both domestic and international students.'
It is deliberately broad across doctoral qualification types: 'Candidates for professional doctorates, as well as the PhD, are welcome to apply.'
Selection is research-led: 'Selection is based predominantly on academic merit and the applicant's potential for research.'

The University states it is 'reviewing the strategic direction of its doctoral scholarships' and directs applicants to check the page for future information, so the award's design is under active reconsideration rather than settled.

official.description: The Ulam Programme, run by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA), aims at increasing the internationalisation of Polish universities and scientific institutions. It allows outstanding scientists who hold at least a doctoral degree to strengthen the scientific potential of Polish higher education and research institutions by joining in their research activities, particularly research projects and didactic activity. Researchers may be invited from abroad regardless of age, discipline or country of origin, including Polish scientists working permanently abroad, for a period of 6 to 24 months. Funding under the Programme includes remuneration for the Principal Investigator and the Inviting Person. Applications are submitted by the inviting institutions, not by the individual researchers.
purpose: 'The programme aims at increasing the internationalisation of Polish universities and scientific institutions.'

'The programme will allow outstanding scientists with at least a doctoral degree to strengthen the scientific potential of Polish higher education and research institutions by joining in their research activities, particularly research projects and didactic activity.'
'The programme provides opportunity to invite researchers from abroad, regardless of their age, discipline or country of origin, including Polish scientists working permanently abroad.'

'Universities, scientific and research institutes and other authorized entities will be able to invite to Poland specialists in their priority fields, who will significantly develop the scientific research conducted by a given institution, strengthen didactic activities, or support the institution in preparing applications for research grants.'

It serves both research and teaching capacity: invited researchers contribute to 'research projects and didactic activity', and can 'support the institution in preparing applications for research grants'.

A Special Track exists for scientists already recognised by European initiatives, so that applicants who hold a Seal of Excellence under the MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships - European Fellowships programme or an Accolade of Excellence under MSCA4Ukraine are not bound by the remaining requirements for the Principal Investigator.
degree_levels: Doctoral degree or equivalent (minimum for the invited researcher)
Doctorate, PhD or equivalent held abroad (Principal Investigator requirement in the Special Track)
study_type: Research activity in a research project or programme
Didactic activity (teaching)
Support for preparing research grant applications
Research employment (fellowship) rather than enrolment in a degree
official.degree_award: Not a degree and not a degree-granting. The programme funds a period of employment and research activity in Poland for an invited researcher; it confers no academic credential.
official.duration: 'The programme provides opportunity to employ foreign researchers for a period from 6 to 24 months.'
official.application_cycle: Annual call cycle administered by NAWA. The current published call is Call no. 9/2026 of 13 February 2026. NAWA publishes closed calls with their own documents and results for each prior year (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025), confirming an annual cadence.

application_readiness_checklist: Understand first that you cannot apply yourself - 'the applications in the Programme are submitted by the inviting institutions', so your first task is finding a host, not filling in a form

Target Polish universities, scientific and research institutes or other authorized entities whose priority fields match your specialisation, since institutions invite specialists in their priority fields
Confirm you can commit to between 6 and 24 months in Poland, since the programme funds employment for that period

Check whether you qualify for the Special Track: you need a Seal of Excellence under MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships - European Fellowships or an Accolade of Excellence under MSCA4Ukraine, plus a Principal Investigator holding at least a PhD or equivalent obtained abroad

important_advice_for_students: Do not look for an individual application portal for this programme - there is not one; NAWA states applications are submitted by the inviting institutions

Do not confuse this with a degree scholarship; it funds research employment and didactic activity for 6 to 24 months and confers no academic credential
Do note that age, discipline and country of origin are all expressly not barriers - 'regardless of their age, discipline or country of origin', including Polish scientists permanently abroad

Do exploit the Special Track if you hold a Seal of Excellence or MSCA4Ukraine Accolade of Excellence, because NAWA treats those European certificates as binding verification of application quality and exempts such applications from the remaining Principal Investigator requirements
Do make sure your institution has both a Principal Investigator and an Inviting Person identified, since funding includes remuneration for both roles
Do not delay on the institution side; because the institution is the applicant, their internal deadline comes before NAWA's and is not published
Do read the Regulations of Institutional Programmes for Researchers (Appendix 1) and the Beneficiary Agreement template (Appendix 2), which govern the funding relationship

verification.source_conflict_rule: The call announcement PDF for the current call governs the deadline, award numbers, funding amounts and binding requirements, and the Regulations of Institutional Programmes for Researchers (Appendix 1) govern the award. The programme description page governs the programme's purpose, scope, duration and Special Track rules. Where the description page and a call document differ, the current call document governs that call. NAWA's archived closed calls are historical evidence only and never override the current call.
verification.source_freshness_rule: This is a call-based programme: each annual call republishes its own announcement, regulations, templates and forms under a versioned asset path (Ulam_2026 for this cycle), and NAWA archives prior calls. Only the current call's documents may be relied on; anything drawn from the 2020-2025 closed calls is stale, and the record must be re-verified when call no. 10/2026 or the next cycle is published.

official.description: The Poland My First Choice NAWA programme, run by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA), encourages young talented people from a published list of 44 countries and territories to study at Polish university-type higher education institutions. It offers a scholarship during the statutory period of full-time second-cycle (Master's) studies at academic institutions, both public and non-public, supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education, and in addition provides an exemption from tuition fees at public universities. Applicants choose the university and field of study themselves from the offer of universities listed in the call, and must apply for admission to that university themselves and independently of their application to NAWA, because NAWA does not act as an intermediary in admission.
purpose: 'The Poland My First Choice NAWA programme aims to encourage young talented people from the countries listed below to pursue studies at the Polish university-type higher education institutions (HEIs).'

The scholarship covers 'the statutory period of full-time second-cycle studies at academic HEIs (both public and non-public) supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education', so its stated aim is the complete funded Master's cycle rather than a partial period.
It removes a second cost barrier for public universities: 'In addition, the Programme provides an exemption from tuition fees at public universities.'

It is deliberately institution-neutral: 'Applicants select the university and the field of study at which they want to study independently, based on the offer of universities listed in the call for applications.'
Its scope is bounded by Polish higher education governance: 'The Programme does not provide for a call for applications for fields of study offered by the HEIs supervised by other ministries.'

official.description: Erasmus+ supports student and doctoral candidate exchanges for study abroad, both within countries fully part of the Erasmus+ programme and to and from countries associated to Erasmus+. It is administered through institutions rather than centrally: there is no central application form, and the applicant must approach the international or Erasmus+ office of their own university, whose selection is obliged to be fair and transparent. The grant is a contribution to travel and daily living costs, awarded through a participant grant agreement signed with the sending or receiving institution, and the grant amount varies with living-cost differences, applicant numbers, distance and the availability of other grants. As an Erasmus+ student the recipient is exempt from tuition, registration and examination fees and from laboratory and library access charges at the receiving institution, though small insurance or student union fees may still apply.
purpose: 'Studying abroad is a central part of Erasmus+ and has been shown to have a positive effect on later job prospects. It is also an opportunity to improve language skills, gain self-confidence and independence and immerse yourself in a new culture.'
'Erasmus+ also offers the chance to combine studying abroad with a traineeship.'

The published benefits are framed as employability and skills: 'improve your communication, language and inter-cultural skills', 'gain soft skills highly valued by employers', and to 'combine with a traineeship abroad to gain work experience'.
It operates in both directions of mobility: exchanges happen 'within countries fully part of the Erasmus+ programme' and 'to and from countries associated to Erasmus+'.

The mobility must be academically purposeful: your study period abroad must be 'relevant for your degree-related learning and personal development needs' and 'part of the study programme that you are following'.
Recognition is a core programme commitment, not a courtesy: the sending institution 'must recognise the credits ... and count them towards your degree, without any other requirements'.
study_type: Full-time study abroad
Long-term mobility (blended mobilities may include a virtual component)
Short-term blended mobility
Combined study abroad with a traineeship
official.degree_award: Not a degree and not a degree-granting award: it is mobility funding that attaches to a study period abroad within the applicant's existing degree programme. The qualification awarded is the one of the home institution's programme.
official.duration: Long-term mobility: minimum of 2 months to a maximum of 12 months abroad, including blended mobilities with a virtual component. Short-term mobility: between 5 and 30 days abroad, and these must be blended mobilities; only doctoral candidates can do a short-term mobility without a virtual component. Maximum total duration: 12 months within one study cycle, with more than one exchange possible within that limit. For 'one-cycle' courses such as medicine or architecture, Erasmus+ mobility abroad can last up to 24 months. 'Cycle' refers to the level of study as defined by the European Qualifications Framework (EQF).
official.application_cycle: Continuous and institutional rather than central: 'There's no central application form to study abroad with Erasmus+. You can reach out to the international or Erasmus+ office of your university or higher education institution to start the process.' Funding is applied for by the sending or receiving institution on behalf of its students each year under the Erasmus+ annual call.
official.deadline_central_display: No central deadline. Erasmus+ publishes no application date: 'There's no central application form to study abroad with Erasmus+. You can reach out to the international or Erasmus+ office of your university or higher education institution to start the process.'
official.deadline_institutional: Set by your own sending institution. Erasmus+ publishes no institutional date, so the operative deadline is the internal call your university or its Erasmus+ office sets, which follows the national Erasmus+ call in which the institution applies for funding.
official.deadline_note: Deliberate null for deadline_central. The programme is institution-administered and the Commission publishes no application dates at all; the only timing information published concerns mobility duration. Applicants must obtain their institution's internal deadline directly.
official.funding_label: Erasmus+ student mobility grant: a contribution to travel and daily living costs, amount varying by living-cost differences, applicant numbers, distance and availability of other grants, plus fee exemption at the receiving institution
official.funding_period: per mobility period, which may be a long-term mobility of 2 to 12 months, a short-term blended mobility of 5 to 30 days, or up to 24 months for one-cycle courses
official.tuition_coverage_note: Fee exemption rather than a cash payment: 'As an Erasmus+ student, you are exempt from fees for tuition, registration, examinations, and charges for access to laboratories or libraries at the receiving institution. Small fees for insurance or student union membership may still apply.'
official.tuition_rule: Erasmus+ operates by exemption at the receiving institution rather than by fee payment: the student is 'exempt from fees for tuition, registration, examinations, and charges for access to laboratories or libraries at the receiving institution'. The exemption is not absolute, because 'Small fees for insurance or student union membership may still apply.'
official.home_tuition_rule: The applicant remains enrolled at their home institution throughout: the sending institution must recognise the credits earned abroad and 'count them towards your degree, without any other requirements', so the home programme and its fees continue while the mobility takes place.
official.host_institution_fee: No tuition, registration, examination, laboratory or library access charges at the receiving institution, with small insurance or student union membership fees still possible.
covered_expenses: A grant contribution to travel costs
A grant contribution to daily living costs
Exemption from tuition fees at the receiving institution

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are registered at a higher education institution that participates in the Erasmus+ programme, and check the Commission's published ECHE 2021-2027 list for your institution
Confirm you are enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree or tertiary-level qualification
Find a receiving institution connected to yours by an inter-institutional agreement, since mobility without one cannot proceed

Confirm the Erasmus Charter position on both sides: both institutions must hold the Charter if in EU Member States or associated third countries, and a non-associated third-country institution must commit to the Charter principles when signing
Frame the mobility so it is part of your study programme and relevant to your degree-related learning and personal development needs, because both are stated requirements
Contact the international or Erasmus+ office of your own institution for the internal route and deadline, because there is no central Erasmus+ application or deadline
Choose your mobility length deliberately: 2 to 12 months long-term, or 5 to 30 days short-term blended, or up to 24 months for one-cycle courses such as medicine and architecture
If you are not a doctoral candidate, plan a blended short-term mobility with a virtual component, since only doctoral candidates can omit it
Budget on the assumption that the grant is only a contribution to travel and daily living costs, and that small insurance or student union fees may still apply
If you have a physical, mental or health-related condition, ask the Erasmus+ coordinator at your sending institution about additional funding before you apply
important_advice_for_students: Do not look for a central Erasmus+ application form; there isn't one, so your first action is your own university's Erasmus+ or international office
Do not assume a fixed grant amount; the Commission publishes no scale, and the amount depends on living-cost differences, how many students apply, distance and other available grants
Do not treat the grant as full funding - it is 'a contribution to your travel and daily living costs'

Do not forget the fee exemption is broad: tuition, registration, examinations and laboratory or library access charges are all exempt, but small insurance or student union membership fees may still apply
Do secure the learning agreement for studies before you travel; it defines how your work will be recognised and sets everyone's rights and responsibilities
Do rely on the recognition guarantee: your sending institution must count your credits towards your degree 'without any other requirements'
Do plan your mobility duration against the 12-month-per-study-cycle cap, remembering you may do more than one exchange within it and up to 24 months for one-cycle courses
Do check that your mobility sits inside your own study programme, since relevance to your degree-related learning and personal development needs is a stated eligibility condition
Do use Erasmus+ Online Language Support and read the Erasmus+ Student Charter once you are accepted

Do remember that doctoral candidates have options the others do not, including short-term mobility without a virtual component, and should also consider the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions for research periods abroad

tuition_coverage is recorded as true but specifically as a fee exemption at the receiving institution, not as a cash tuition payment, and the published carve-out for small insurance and student union membership fees is preserved rather than smoothed over.
deferrable, return_home_required and clinical_restriction are left null because the Commission publishes no such conditions; they are not assumed to be false.

verification.source_conflict_rule: The Commission's Studying abroad page governs eligibility, duration, grant purpose, fee exemption and recognition requirements. The sending or receiving institution governs selection, internal deadlines and the specific grant amount, and its rules govern where the Commission's page is silent. The Commission's ECHE 2021-2027 institution list governs which institutions can participate. Where national agency guidance and the Commission page differ on process, the institutional and national agency route governs, because the Commission explicitly delegates the process to institutions.
verification.source_freshness_rule: Erasmus+ is a rolling programme rather than an annual scholarship with a fixed application round, and institutional participation, the ECHE list and the annual call all change each year. Both pages read carry explicit last-updated dates. Anything not confirmed against the current ECHE 2021-2027 list and the current annual call should be treated as stale, and the record should be re-verified when the next programme cycle publishes new guidance.

official.description: The Fulbright Program in Poland, initiated in 1959 and administered by the Polish-U.S. Fulbright Commission, is a merit-based exchange programme jointly funded by the governments of Poland and the United States. It runs distinct awards in both directions: grants to Poland for US citizens (Scholar, Student, English Teaching Assistant, Specialist, Schuman) and grants to the USA for Polish citizens (Graduate Student up to USD 47,000 for a first year, Junior Research, Polish Scholar, Polish Studies, STEM Impact). Benefits include a stipend, J-1 visa and SEVIS support, medical insurance, a travel allowance and additional allowances for host institution fees, relocation, research and family support, with application windows published as month ranges per award.
official.program_type: Government-funded bilateral academic and cultural exchange programme (US Department of State and Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education)
official.coverage: Covers a living stipend, J-1 visa and SEVIS fees, medical insurance, round-trip travel and additional allowances for host institution fees, relocation, research, conferences and family support, with amounts and duration varying by award; tuition is not stated to be fully covered across all awards.

official.description: CEEPUS, the Central European Exchange Programme for University Studies, is a multilateral exchange programme with Central and Eastern Europe that unites universities from 16 countries within networks of at least three institutions from at least two different contractual countries. Within a network, incoming students are exempted from tuition fees and receive a comprehensive grant from the host country set according to local living costs, with exchanges lasting 3 to 10 months. For the 2027/28 round the central deadline for network applications is 30 November 2026 at 23:59 CET, with an extended deadline of 15 December 2026 for signed letters, and individual mobility decisions rest with the host National CEEPUS Office.

official.description: The National Science Scholarship (PhD) develops top researchers for Singapore by funding up to five years of PhD study at top international institutions, with a compulsory one-year research attachment at an A*STAR research institute before the PhD begins. Support covers full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance of SGD 4,500 for Singapore Citizens or SGD 4,100 for Permanent Residents, a monthly overseas living allowance, annual return airfare and several other allowances. Applicants apply in one of two annual cycles closing 1 April and 1 October, and scholars serve a four-year work-back commitment in Singapore, reduced to three years if the PhD is completed in a non-anglophone country.

official.description: The Temasek Undergraduate Overseas Scholarship "is awarded to exceptional polytechnic graduates who demonstrate academic excellence, outstanding extracurricular involvement, and a strong passion for STEM fields." Scholars "will have the opportunity to pursue further education at top overseas universities, and are expected to contribute to Singapore's innovation and growth upon graduation." The award is comprehensive: it covers tuition and other compulsory fees over the course of study, pays a monthly living allowance, and adds a one-time relocation allowance including return airfare, a one-time pre-studies allowance, and reimbursement of application fees to up to five overseas universities and visa processing fees. It is bonded: scholars must serve a 4-year bond in a STEM-related role in Singapore or with a Singapore-headquartered company after graduation.

official.selection_notes: A four-stage assessment is used. Shortlisted applicants complete "a series of assessments designed to evaluate his or her general abilities, motivations, interests, and values": an online psychometric and personality assessment, and a remote on-demand video interview. official.description: The Temasek Undergraduate Local Scholarship is delivered through the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) as a bond-free donated award. SIT describes it as "a merit-based scholarship established to nurture and recognise talented students pursuing a full-time Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) undergraduate degree programme at the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT)." Each Scholarship "is valued up to S$18,030 per annum, including an annual stipend of S$7,200", plus a one-time laptop allowance of S$2,000 in the first year of study and, if eligible and if the scholar chooses it, an additional one-time Global Mobility Grant of S$10,000 for a University-conducted global exposure programme. Temasek describes the award as funding "the full cost of their studies e.g., course fees, allowance, and where needed, accommodation and flights." The scholarship is bond-free and forms part of Temasek's S$150 million "T-Spring" community gift marking its 50th anniversary in 2024.

official.description: The Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) Scholarship is described by SUSS as "a premier scheme aimed at providing high calibre students the opportunity to develop their full potential in their chosen discipline." The award "covers 100% of course fee (inclusive of government subsidy) for recipient's remaining candidature of study. It includes course materials, examination fee and other compulsory fees, as well as Miscellaneous Fees. There is no bond attached to the scholarship." The scholarship is restricted to part-time undergraduate programmes, is open only to Singapore citizens and permanent residents, and is not available for students applying to the Law programmes. Applications run in two windows each year: 1 August to 15 September for the January Semester and 1 February to 15 March for the July Semester.

official.application_cycle: EPFL Bachelor admission cycle for students in their final year of secondary school; the official pages publish the day and month only, not the year
official.deadline_central_display: students in their final year of high school must check the corresponding box on their Bachelor's application form before April 30th and provide the requested application file; selections are shortlisted once Bachelor registrations close on 30 April
official.deadline_note: The official pages publish 'before April 30th' and state that Bachelor registrations end on 30 April, but they do not publish a calendar year, so no ISO date can be asserted. There is no separate scholarship deadline: the fellowship is applied for inside the regular EPFL Bachelor application. Negative decisions are communicated no later than the end of June and positive decisions are transmitted at the end of June, subject to a final average matching the published criteria.
official.status_note: The application is embedded in the EPFL Bachelor admission cycle, which closes on 30 April each year with shortlisting after registrations end and decisions at the end of June. No explicit open/closed statement is published.

official.funding_duration: 6 semesters (3 years)
official.tuition_coverage_note: The official pages describe the fellowship as a financial support of CHF 10,000 paid in instalments, a reservation of a room in an EPFL partner student residence on request and at your own cost, and an excellence certificate. They make no statement about tuition fees, so tuition coverage is not recorded. The English page confirms the housing request is 'to be filled in the registration form' and the French page specifies 'sur demande et a vos frais'.

official.citizenship_residency: Swiss nationals and C-permit holders, refugees and stateless persons resident in Switzerland, holders of a certificate under art. 1 of the EPFL admission ordinance, and anyone who obtained the Swiss secondary II diploma while domiciled in Switzerland. The scholarship is therefore limited to candidates meeting a Swiss status or Swiss-schooling condition; there is no open route for unqualified foreign applicants.
official.international_eligibility: Not stated as an open international route. Eligibility is defined by Swiss residence status or by having completed Swiss secondary II schooling while domiciled in Switzerland.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open regardless of the field of study chosen. The fellowships are part of the 'Attract Talent' pillar of EPFL's Student Support Program and are funded by a named list of donors and foundations.
official.application_method: Tick the corresponding box on the EPFL Bachelor application form before 30 April and provide the requested application file. Where the applicant is eligible, an ad hoc form is issued and the listed documents are requested. Each section then pre-selects the best applications for a presentation of the maturity project (or another subject, if not applicable) before a jury made up in part of EPFL academic staff, in a short five-minute presentation followed by questions. The applications retained are then examined by the Central Committee for Bachelor Excellence Fellowships, which awards the fellowships.

official.description: EPFL's Bachelor Excellence Fellowships are offered to holders of a Swiss high-school maturity diploma and holders of a Swiss vocational maturity diploma undertaking the CMS, and to any applicant to an EPFL Bachelor programme who meets one of four published status or schooling conditions. The fellowship is worth CHF 10,000 spread over three years, paid as six semester instalments, and comes with a guaranteed room reservation in an EPFL partner residence on request and at the student's own cost, plus an excellence certificate. Applications are made by ticking a box on the Bachelor application form before 30 April, followed by section pre-selection, a five-minute jury presentation of the maturity project, and a decision by the Central Committee for Bachelor Excellence Fellowships at the end of June.

official.coverage: Provides CHF 10,000 in cash instalments over three years plus a residence room reservation that the student pays for, and does not state that tuition or all living costs are covered.

official.description: The SNSF Starting Grants are the SNSF's highest level of career funding, enabling researchers to carry out their own independent project and lead a research team in Switzerland. Applicants can request a budget of up to 1 million francs for project funding over five years and can additionally apply for funds to cover their own salary. Eligibility requires a doctorate (or equivalent or medical degree), falling within the eligibility window, not yet having achieved the objective of the call, and a Swiss link of at least two years of research at an average of at least 80% worktime. Evaluation is a two-phase, competition-based procedure with external peer review and interviews.
official.program_type: Career-stage research grant (highest level of SNSF career funding), including the applicant's own salary
official.coverage: Funds an independent research project and team leadership in Switzerland: up to CHF 1 million project funding over five years plus, on request, the applicant's own salary. It is a research grant rather than a student funding package, so tuition and personal living costs are not items it covers.

official.description: The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program, administered by the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs with the Institute of International Education, provides 10 months of professional enrichment and non-degree graduate-level study in the United States for accomplished mid-level professionals from designated countries. Fellows are nominated by U.S. Embassies or Fulbright Commissions based on their potential for leadership and a demonstrated commitment to public service, and are placed in groups by professional field at selected U.S. universities offering specially designed programmes of study and training. Eligibility requires an undergraduate degree, at least five years of full-time professional experience, limited or no prior experience in the United States, demonstrated leadership, a record of public service, and English language ability. Application deadlines vary by country, and final selections are approved by the J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board, with awards announced in the spring for fellowships beginning in the fall.
purpose: 'The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program provides 10 months of professional enrichment and non-degree graduate-level study in the United States for accomplished mid-level professionals from designated countries.'
The programme targets public-service leadership specifically: fellows are nominated 'based on their potential for leadership and a demonstrated commitment to public service'.
It is deliberately non-degree professional enrichment rather than degree study, combined with academic study: 'professional enrichment and non-degree graduate-level study'.

The academic component is professionally designed and field-based: fellows 'are placed in groups by professional field at selected U.S. universities offering specially designed programs of study and training'.

It serves as a national selection mechanism: U.S. Embassies and Fulbright Commissions conduct an initial review and nominate candidates, and final selections are approved by the J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board.

verification.source_conflict_rule: The U.S. Department of State Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs programme page governs the programme's purpose, length, eligibility conditions, selection process and country-specific routing. The Institute of International Education governs the programme's administration, the eligible-country list and the benefit package, since it is the published administrator. Each US embassy or Fulbright commission governs its own national application details and deadline. Where any of these differ, the national mission governs its own deadline and documents, and the Department of State and IIE pages govern the programme itself.
verification.source_freshness_rule: The programme runs on an annual cycle with country-specific deadlines, so the effective deadline changes by country and year even though the programme definition is stable. The eligible-country list, benefit package and participating countries are republished by the Institute of International Education each cycle. Anything not confirmed against the current IIE eligible-country list and the applicant's own current embassy announcement is stale, and the record must be re-verified each cycle.

official.description: The Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship is a program of the US Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, funded by the US Government and implemented by the Institute of International Education, that supports Pell Grant-receiving US undergraduates for credit-bearing study abroad or internships abroad. Awards are up to $5,000, with the option of an additional Critical Need Language Award of up to $3,000 and/or STEM Supplemental Award of up to $1,000, and the final amount is set by financial need, program length, overall program cost and the strength of the application. official.description: Harvard College states: "You can afford Harvard. We know that paying for college is a big concern for many families, and we're committed to making a Harvard education - and the opportunities that come with it - possible for more students than ever." Its stated goal is "to bring the most promising students to Harvard-period", and its financial aid officers "create a comprehensive financial aid package that accounts for the full cost of attendance". Need is assessed on family income, assets and overall circumstances; Harvard states "You'll never be required to take on loans" and that financial circumstances will not affect admission chances. For 2027-2028 the aid application consists of a CSS Profile for everyone, plus IDOC document submission, plus the FAFSA for US citizens, permanent residents and other eligible non-citizens. Harvard publishes three income bands: families at or below $100,000 with typical assets receive aid covering all billed expenses plus extras; at or below $200,000 receive Free Tuition Plus; above $200,000 receive tailored aid. Students are expected to cover $3,500 in personal expenses per academic year, usually through work-study hours.

official.description: The University of Texas at Austin's International Student and Scholar Services (ISSS) states that "Certain scholarship opportunities are open to international students who meet eligibility criteria", and that "Scholarship applications are open twice a year: once in the Fall for the spring and summer terms and once in the Spring for the upcoming fall term and academic year." Applications for Spring 2027 and Summer 2027 scholarships are accepted 1 October 2026 to 1 November 2026, and applications for Fall 2027 and the 2027-2028 academic year are accepted 1 February 2027 to 1 March 2027. Applications are submitted through LASSO, the university-wide scholarship system. ISSS states plainly that "scholarships are one-time awards, and recipients are not guaranteed to receive the scholarship in subsequent years." The portfolio runs from fixed-value tuition scholarships (for example the $3,500 SIAWE and $4,800 STEM awards) to competitive need-based cash aid (General ISSS Financial Aid), a nonresident tuition waiver (TAMS), a fee scholarship established by student referendum (IEFS), and a Western Hemisphere tuition exemption (Good Neighbor Scholarship).
purpose: Provide scholarship assistance to international students who meet the published eligibility criteria
Support students who can demonstrate financial need through competitive General ISSS Financial Aid
Recognise students from specific communities and academic pipelines through named endowed scholarships
study_type: Full-time

official.degree_award: A financial award attached to an existing UT Austin enrolment (tuition scholarship, tuition waiver, fee scholarship, tuition exemption or cash award). No award in this portfolio confers a degree.
official.duration: Awards are semester or academic-year specific. Most are one-time awards: ISSS states "scholarships are one-time awards, and recipients are not guaranteed to receive the scholarship in subsequent years."
official.application_cycle: Two cycles a year. Spring/Summer Term Scholarships: applications accepted 1 October to 1 November. Fall Term and Academic Year Scholarships: applications accepted 1 February to 1 March. The general timeline is published as Fall/Academic Year Scholarships February 1 - March 1 and Spring/Summer Term Scholarships October 1 - November 1. ISSS adds: "Application deadlines are subject to change. Begin researching scholarships well in advance, and always check the criteria and due dates in the application."

official.funding_period: Varies by award: one-time semester awards (for example the $4,800 STEM Scholarship for the fall semester, the $5,000 Carlos and Clara Quintanilla spring tuition scholarship, the $2,000 Dr. David Nilsson spring tuition scholarship, the $3,500 SIAWE spring tuition scholarship) and academic-year awards (for example the $5,000 African Leadership Bridge academic year award, split $2,500 fall and $2,500 spring). General ISSS Financial Aid amounts are not published and depend on competitive allotments.
official.tuition_coverage: Partial and award-specific. The STEM Scholarship is a $4,800 tuition award; the SIAWE, Nilsson and Quintanilla scholarships are spring tuition scholarships; TAMS waives the nonresident portion of tuition; the African Leadership Bridge award combines a $5,000 academic year award with a waiver of the nonresident tuition portion; the Good Neighbor Scholarship provides an exemption of one year's tuition (fall, spring and summer). General ISSS Financial Aid is cash and "does not provide a waiver of the nonresident portion of a student's tuition & fee bill."
official.travel_coverage: Limited and award-specific: the portfolio includes Travel Grants and the Viva Travel Grant (complimentary flights for faculty and students travelling to Mexico). No living-cost component is published for any award in the portfolio.
official.tuition_rule: Awards are applied by UT Austin, not paid to the student as an unrestricted sum: "All cash awards will automatically apply to any outstanding UT debts upon disbursement. Award amount[s] in excess of debts will be distributed to the student's direct deposit account." General ISSS Financial Aid is cash only and "does not provide a waiver of the nonresident portion of a student's tuition & fee bill."

official.description: The University of Chicago states that "Nearly $20 million in need-based financial aid has been offered to international students at UChicago over the past four years, and a recent gift of $35 million for international financial aid has strengthened the University's commitment to enrolling a diverse and talented student body from around the world." Its commitment is explicit: "We are committed to meeting 100% of your demonstrated need with a loan-free financial aid package if you are admitted and applied for funding." Packages "are based on an estimate of the full costs of enrolling at the University of Chicago, including tuition, housing, health insurance, a meal plan, and estimates for additional costs like books and personal expenses." International students must apply for funding during the admissions process; they are not eligible afterwards or during their four years in the College. Separately, UChicago offers partial-tuition merit scholarships - single lump-sum or renewable annual - which are considered independently of financial situation and for which all first-year applicants are automatically considered.

official.degree_award: A need-based financial aid package attached to an admission offer, plus separately awarded partial-tuition merit scholarships. No award confers a degree.
official.duration: Need-based aid is set for the duration of study. For merit scholarships, UChicago states they "may be a single lump-sum award, or a renewable annual award". International transfer applicants receive no financial aid at all.
official.application_cycle: Aid is applied for at the same time as admission, once per admissions cycle. Admission is offered for entrance in the Autumn Quarter only (except prospective students-at-large). Merit scholarship winners are notified "on a rolling basis through the end of April".
official.deadline_central_display: Early Decision I and Early Action: Nov 2, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision: Jan 4, 2027
official.deadline_institutional: The financial aid application shares the admission application deadline in each plan. official.deadline_note: UChicago publishes no separate financial aid deadline; the Student Financial Aid Worksheet and supporting documentation must be in with the admission application by the plan deadline (Nov 2, 2026 for ED I/EA; Jan 4, 2027 for ED II/RD).

official.description: Study in Latvia, the official portal of the State Education Development Agency (VIAA), publishes the Latvian state scholarship for studies: "Citizens of 39 eligible countries are welcome to apply for Latvian State scholarship for studies in Latvian higher education institutions." The award is a monthly stipend of EUR 500 for Bachelor's and Master's students and EUR 700 for PhD students, granted for up to 10 months (Bachelor's and Master's) or up to 11 months (PhD), with a maximum of two terms within one study cycle. VIAA is explicit about the limits: "A scholarship do not fully cover all the expenses related to your studies. Some expenses related to tuition fees, living costs, and other expenses must be covered personally", travel from the home country to and from Latvia is not covered, insurance must be arranged personally, no scholarship is paid for presence in Latvia of under 15 calendar days, and the award cannot be held concurrently with other grants. Applications are open annually from 1 February to 1 April through the VIAA electronic application system, with the decision notified by e-mail in June.

official.description: The French Community of Belgium offers the government of Quebec a pool of 60 monthly scholarships per academic year, which the Quebec side may split into short, medium or long terms, for candidates from Quebec pursuing specialised Master's-level or postgraduate studies in the French-speaking Community of Belgium. Each award pays a monthly stipend of EUR 789.71 for second cycle or EUR 963.29 for third cycle programmes, university registration fees, a EUR 24.79 per month materials or travel allowance, and one-off thesis or dissertation printing payments on programme completion. Fields prioritised but not exclusive are life sciences, environmental sciences and new social issues.

official.description: This is a programme information page rather than an open scholarship, published by the Czech Development Agency (Důzm zahraniční spolupráce, DZS). It states: "The fourth programme period of the EEA Grants (2021-2028) builds on previous cooperation in the field of education while responding to the current challenges of the Czech education system and to the priorities arising from the Memorandum of Understanding between the Czech Republic and the donor states (Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein), approved by the Government of the Czech Republic in November 2025." The total allocation is "EUR 24.117 million (EUR 20.5 million from the EEA Grants and EUR 3.617 million from national co-financing)", and "Mandatory cooperation with a partner from a donor state is a key element of the programme." The 'Projects and grants' sub-page adds that the programme "will focus on supporting and developing civic and pedagogical competences and on strengthening the quality of initial teacher education as well as teachers' continuing professional development", and that DZS is "currently preparing" it. "The Programme Agreement is expected to be signed in 2026, followed by the launch of the first calls for proposals at the turn of 2026/2027."

official.description: The Ernst Mach Grant programme, financed by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Women, Science and Research (BMFWF), is named after the Austrian physicist and philosopher Ernst Mach (1838-1916) and invites "Students and young researchers from foreign universities ... to come to Austria for a research or a study stay." The ASEA-UNINET strand "is open to undergraduates, graduates, postgraduates and postdocs from Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Philippines or Vietnam in all fields of study who want to study or do a research project in Austria." It runs within the ASEAN-European Academic University Network (ASEA-UNINET) and closes for applications on 1 March, with age limits of 35 for undergraduates, graduates and postgraduates and 45 for postdocs at the time of application, and durations of 9 months for undergraduates and graduates, 4 to 9 months for postdocs, and up to 36 months for postgraduates. A separate Ernst Mach-ASEA-UNINET Short-term Research Grant for postdocs and lecturers has ongoing applications.

Support doctoral/PhD study either at an ASEA-UNINET member university in Southeast Asia or in Austria

Support short-term research stays in Austria for postdocs and lecturers at ASEA-UNINET member institutions

official.description: The assigned page no longer exists. portalvs.sk returns HTTP 404 for '/aktuality/ponuky-a-podmienky/applied-informatics-fpv-umb'; Portal VS now runs its national scholarship scheme on a dedicated site, scholarships.portalvs.sk, which operates the Slovak national programme 'Scholarships for talented students from abroad'. That programme is "designed for all international students worldwide, including Slovaks living abroad, who plan to pursue higher education in Slovakia" and grants "up to EUR 15,000", paid at "EUR 500 per month" for ten months each academic year (September to June), over three academic years for Bachelor's or combined Bachelor's and Master's study, or two academic years for a Master's. Critically for this record, the scheme is "exclusively designated for full-time bachelor's, full-time combined bachelor's and master's studies, and full-time master's studies at a selected public or state Slovak higher education institution (HEI)", and applicants must choose one of the selected public HEIs offering a programme under the Smart Specialisation Strategy (SK RIS 3 2021+). The Faculty of Business Management (FPV) at UMB, the institution named in this record, is a private university and therefore falls outside the scheme's published eligibility.

official.funding_label: National scholarship scheme for talented foreign students studying in the Slovak Republic, co-financed by the European Union under the Slovakia Programme (ESIF) and by the state budget
official.funding_period: EUR 500 per month, paid over ten months each academic year (September to June); the programme states an overall value of "up to EUR 15,000" over three academic years (Bachelor's or combined Bachelor's and Master's) or two academic years (Master's). "The academic year in Slovakia starts on September 1st and ends on August 31st of the following year."
official.tuition_coverage: Possible but not guaranteed. "Based on the current legislation, scholarship recipients accepted into this scholarship scheme and enrolled and entered to a full-time study programme taught in foreign language to a public HEI may have their tuition fees waived in accordance with Section 96, Para 15 of Act No. 300/2025 Coll. on Higher Education, however waiving the tuition fees is exclusively on HEIs decision."
official.living_cost_coverage: Partial: a monthly stipend of EUR 500. The programme publishes no living-cost calculation and no statement that living costs are met in full.
official.tuition_rule: Tuition may be waived under Section 96 paragraph 15 of Act No. 300/2025 Coll. on Higher Education for recipients enrolled in a full-time foreign-language study programme at a public HEI, but "waiving the tuition fees is exclusively on HEIs decision", so it cannot be relied upon.
official.host_institution_fee: The host institution is a selected public or state Slovak HEI offering a programme under SK RIS 3 2021+. The fee level is set by the HEI, and any tuition waiver is at the HEI's discretion.
covered_expenses: Monthly scholarship payment of EUR 500, for ten months each academic year from September to June
Overall value of up to EUR 15,000 over the supported period

selection_criteria: "The order of applicants in the respective category will be determined on the basis of the results of a standardised test."
SAT test: a minimum total score of 1100 points, equivalent to percentile 63
SCIO tests: a minimum average percentile of 63, calculated as the average of the percentiles obtained in the Mathematics and General Academic Prerequisites tests
"The result of the chosen standardised test will be the only criterion for the selection of successful applicants."
"Both tests are evaluated according to the same percentile scale, ensuring equal opportunities for all applicants regardless of which test they took."

official.selection_notes: Selection is purely test-score based. During evaluation, applicants are divided into five geographical groups: Europe; USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Oceania; South America; Central America and Africa; Asia. The complete list of countries by category is published as a link. There are 170 first-level places annually (110 ESIF-funded for public HEIs outside the Bratislava region, 60 state-budget-funded for public HEIs in the Bratislava region) and 55 master's places (35 ESIF-funded outside Bratislava, 20 state-budget-funded in Bratislava). "The Ministry may adjust the number of scholarships awarded as needed." Evaluation takes place after applicants are officially enrolled in their selected study programmes, followed by a preliminary list and then a final list, with the HEIs and applicants informed. "Your overall rank among all accepted applicants will also be important. The rank is determined based on the point ranking of each applicant."

alerts.message: Take the SAT or SCIO test. The test result is the only selection criterion, and the minimum threshold is SAT 1100 or SCIO average percentile 63.
Only selected public or state HEIs on the SK RIS 3 2021+ programme list are eligible - private institutions such as UMB are not.
You must be officially enrolled and have commenced the programme by then, because evaluation happens after enrolment.
Bring all original documents to your HEI. Altered or false documents mean withdrawal and repayment.
Changing HEI is not permitted, and switching to part-time study stops payment for that period.
Payment stops during the interruption and only resumes if the total interruption is 180 days or less.
Monitor scholarships.portalvs.sk for the official opening date; no next-cycle date is published yet.

official.description: The Staff Exchanges action of the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions "funds short-term international and inter-sectoral exchanges of staff members involved in research and innovation activities of participating organisations", with the aim of developing "sustainable collaborative projects between different organisations from the academic and non-academic sectors (in particular SMEs), based in Europe and beyond." Exchanged staff benefit from new knowledge, skills and career development perspectives while participating organisations increase their research and innovation capacities. Grants are awarded to international consortia, not to individuals: a consortium "needs to include at least three organisations in three different countries, two of which need to be located in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country", must include both academic and non-academic sectors, and "participation of organisations from non-associated third countries is strongly encouraged". Projects can last up to four years and fund secondments of one month to one year. Seconded staff receive "a top-up allowance (for travel, accommodation, subsistence costs), which is on top of the salary paid by their organisation", plus a special needs allowance where applicable, alongside funding for research, training and networking activities and for management and indirect costs. The current call is closed; the 2027 call opens on 15 December 2026.

official.application_cycle: Call-based. "Applications to MSCA Staff Exchanges can be submitted at any time from the opening date of the chosen call. The completed proposal, including all annexes, should be submitted by the specified submission deadline of the chosen call." The 2027 call opens on 15 December 2026; the current call is closed.

official.description: The Japan Student Services Organization (JASSO) states: "JASSO offers scholarship for qualified international students who are accepted by a Japanese university, graduate school, junior college, college of technology or professional training college (hereinafter referred to as 'Japanese school') under a student exchange agreement or other student exchange arrangement on a short-term basis from 8 days to one year between Japanese school and their home higher educational institution outside Japan (hereinafter referred to as 'home school')." The award is a monthly stipend of 80,000 JPY. Critically, "Applications for the scholarship will be accepted only from Japanese school": JASSO screens the application documents submitted by the Japanese school, decides which programmes to support, and notifies the result. Students cannot apply directly, and JASSO notes that "the selection method of scholarship recipients is different from each school and each program", directing students to ask their home school.

official.description: The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation states that its PhD scholarship "supports students with an excellent academic record who are engaged in humanities and social sciences research that contributes to the advancement of Canada and society." Scholars receive "Up to $50,000 per year for three years", plus "Up to $20,000 per year for research and travel", along with mentorship and experiential learning, an engaged multidisciplinary community, and a network of more than 500 alumni. Applications are assessed on academic excellence, alignment of the research project with the Foundation's mission and four founding themes, the rigour of the research proposal, and the ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society. The 2027 competition runs from 1 September to 6 November 2026, with a mandatory eligibility verification step that must be completed first.
purpose: Support doctoral students with an excellent academic record engaged in humanities and social sciences research that contributes to the advancement of Canada and society

Develop engaged doctoral scholars who can share knowledge for the benefit of society and create impact beyond academia
official.degree_award: A funded doctoral programme of study. The award attaches to the candidate's PhD registration, in Canada or abroad for Canadian citizens, and does not itself confer a degree.
official.duration: Three years: "Up to $50,000 per year for three years." Scholars may suspend the Scholarship for up to one year for parental, medical, personal or professional leave.
official.application_cycle: Annual competition. "The application process for the 2027 Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship will begin on September 1, 2026, with the opening of the eligibility verification form." New Scholars join the cohort in April.
official.deadline_central_display: November 6, 2026, at 5 p.m. ET - deadline to submit the complete application
official.deadline_institutional: October 2, 2026 - deadline to submit an eligibility verification request. October 30, 2026, at 9 a.m. ET - deadline for references to be received. The Scholarship is self-applied and is not university-nominated, so no institutional deadline applies; the Foundation's own deadlines are the two above plus the final submission date.
official.deadline_note: The 2027 competition has three published dates: the eligibility verification form opens 1 September 2026; the eligibility verification request must be submitted by 2 October 2026; references must be received by 30 October 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET; and the complete application must be submitted by 6 November 2026 at 5 p.m. ET. "You cannot submit your application if the references letters are not attached to your file."

official.living_cost_coverage: Partial: the award is an annual stipend of up to $50,000. No living-cost calculation or separate accommodation component is published.
official.travel_coverage: Partly, through a separate annual allowance: "Up to $20,000 per year for research and travel". The Foundation also states that travel costs to attend the in-person interview in Montréal are covered by the Foundation.
official.tuition_rule: No tuition-fee rule is published. The award is described as a stipend plus a research and travel allowance, with no statement that tuition fees are paid or waived, and the value is the same whether the Scholar studies in Canada or abroad: "The location of study does not affect the Scholarship amount."

official.selection_notes: "Only applications that meet the program's eligibility criteria will be assessed." A two-step process is used: the Foundation reviews the eligibility form, and only confirmed applicants receive access to the full application. After submission you receive a confirmation e-mail; applicants selected to move forward are notified by e-mail, and "All other applicants will be informed at the end of the application review period." Selection involves group meetings and individual interviews, conducted in French or English depending on the applicant's preference, with an in-person interview in Montréal preferred and virtual interviews permitted where the candidate cannot travel. "The Foundation understands excellence holistically." Members of the selection committees are named in the Foundation's Annual Reports following the selection processes. Once approved by the Board of Directors and once the funding agreement is signed and required documentation submitted, funding begins.

coverage: Annual stipend of up to $50,000 for three years

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are in the first or second year of your PhD at the time of application - third year and later is ineligible

Confirm your eligibility category: Canadian student at a Canadian university, Canadian student at a university outside Canada, or international student at a Canadian university. International students outside Canada or at non-Canadian universities are ineligible

Check that your field is broadly humanities or social sciences and that your research maps to at least one of the four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment
Submit the eligibility verification form by 2 October 2026 - you cannot access the full application until the Foundation confirms you
Secure exactly three referees: your PhD supervisor, another academic referee, and one outside academia. No family members, and no more or fewer than three
Choose a supervisor or former supervisor if your thesis supervisor has not been chosen or does not know you well, and explain it in the 'Special Circumstances' section
Brief your referees early: they must complete their reference material inside the application file by 30 October 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET, and letters cannot be sent to the Foundation directly
Verify before you submit that the reference letters are attached to your file - the Foundation will not accept an application without them
Submit the complete application by 6 November 2026 at 5 p.m. ET and keep the confirmation e-mail
Prepare to be interviewed in French or English, in person in Montreal, with travel costs covered
important_advice_for_students: Do this in order: the eligibility form comes first and the full application is only unlocked after the Foundation confirms you, so missing 2 October closes the door for the whole cycle
Do not plan on tuition being covered - the published benefits are a stipend of up to $50,000 per year and a research and travel allowance of up to $20,000 per year, and nothing else

Do not worry about the amount if you plan to study abroad: the Foundation states the amount is the same wherever you study, though it does convert foreign external funding into Canadian dollars when assessing value
Do use the fourth language rule: you need effective communication in French or English, not both
Keep letters to three to four pages - there is no word limit but the Foundation's own guidance is that a letter should not exceed that, and quality trumps quantity
If you are writing in French, you get 20% more room on any page limit
Part-time work up to 20 hours per week is explicitly allowed and does not reduce the award, including RA, TA and lecturer roles

If you need a parental, medical, personal or professional leave, you can suspend the Scholarship for up to one year, but know that payments pause until you re-enrol full-time and that there is no paid parental leave
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 2 October eligibility verification deadline, which makes the whole application impossible
Being in the third or later year of the PhD at the time of application
Being an international student who resides outside Canada or is enrolled at a non-Canadian university
A field outside the broad humanities and social sciences, or research not aligned with any of the four themes
Submitting without the three reference letters attached, which the platform will not permit
Missing the 30 October 9:00 a.m. ET reference deadline
Using more or fewer than exactly three referees, or a family member as a referee
Submitting reference letters directly to the Foundation instead of through the application file
A proposal that is strong academically but not clearly linked to a Foundation theme, since theme alignment is an explicit assessment criterion
A letter from a referee chosen mainly for convenience rather than one who can speak to academic leadership and community contribution
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees - no tuition coverage is published
Living costs above the up-to-$50,000 annual stipend; no living-cost breakdown is published
Health insurance and mandatory student fees
Anything outside the up-to-$20,000 annual research and travel allowance, including conference and fieldwork costs beyond it
Relocation and immigration costs for international students moving to Canada
Income lost during a leave, since payments pause and no paid parental leave is provided

Format rules: no word limit but a letter should not exceed three to four pages; French documents get 20% extra length on any page limit; referees may write in either official language regardless of the applicant's application language; the application form is removed from the portal after the competition ends; the Foundation may translate documents and does not use AI-assisted translation

referee_tracking.instructions: One letter from your PhD supervisor. If your supervisor has not yet been chosen or does not know you well, you may ask a former supervisor or another professor, and the Foundation strongly recommends explaining this in the 'Special Circumstances' section of your application.

One letter from another academic referee. The Foundation defines this as "anyone who can vouch for your academic progress... someone who knows you as a student, academic, or researcher." Choose someone who can demonstrate your academic leadership in your research area and your contribution to graduate students and the community.

One letter from outside academia: "someone who knows you outside of academia and can speak to your character, commitment or commitment and engagement in non-academic settings." Family members cannot act as referees. Referees may live outside Canada.

Exactly three referees, no more and no less. Reference letters cannot be sent directly to the Foundation; they must be completed through the specific mechanism provided inside the application file. Deadline for references to be received: 30 October 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET. The application cannot be submitted if the reference letters are not attached to the file. Referees may respond in either French or English.

official.description: The University of Waterloo International Student Entrance Scholarship awards $10,000 to international fee-paying students admitted to full-time first-year degree studies, with no application required because eligible students are granted it automatically. The award is paid in two instalments of $5,000, available in late July for first-term tuition and in late November for second-term tuition, and can be received in addition to other Waterloo entrance scholarships. It applies to the first year only and is conditional on full-time enrolment and continuing international fee-paying status, with exclusions for certain health sciences and professional programmes, transfer students, deferred offers and 2+2 programmes.

official.description: The President's Graduate Fellowship (PGF) is awarded by NUS to PhD research candidates who show exceptional promise or accomplishment in research, with a number of PhD students selected each semester. It provides a full tuition fee waiver at the University plus a monthly stipend of SGD 4,800 for Singapore Citizens, SGD 4,400 for Permanent Residents and SGD 3,900 for international students, with CPF contributions on top for Citizens. Applicants must be nominated by their Faculty or Department and apply through GradApp, and the Fellowship is tenable for one year initially, renewable each semester up to a maximum of four years.
