official.description: The Alfred Werner Scholarship Program of the Swiss Chemical Society (SCS) Foundation supports highly talented international students who obtained their BSc from a university outside Switzerland and want to pursue a Master of Science in Chemistry, Biochemistry or the Pharmaceutical Sciences at a Swiss university or one of the Swiss Federal Institutes of Technology. The scholarship is a single figure of CHF 36'000 (previously CHF 30'000); the official page publishes no itemised split between tuition, living costs and travel. Students are admitted to their MSc place first and are then nominated by the admitting academic institution â€” the SCS Foundation does not accept direct applications from individual candidates.
purpose: Connecting outstanding talent with Switzerland: to bring talented Master students to Switzerland and facilitate their next career steps

To support highly talented international students who obtained their BSc degree from a university outside Switzerland to pursue MSc studies in Chemistry, Biochemistry or the Pharmaceutical Sciences at a Swiss university or one of the Swiss Federal Institutes of Technology
Program history states the aim is to invite young scientists to perform their Master studies in Switzerland and become part of the next generation of Swiss chemists
Build a robust pipeline of future scientists for the Swiss chemical and pharmaceutical industry and enable industry to offer scholars internships or training positions early

official.description: The University of Basel operates its own hardship fund for students with very limited resources and from low-income families. Its scholarship funds are awarded primarily as partial scholarships in the final degree phase of a Bachelor's or Master's programme, and the page states the amounts only as ranges (CHF 200-600 per person per month). The scheme is therefore a partial, supplementary award rather than full funding, and the university states that funding studies is essentially the responsibility of the parents and the scholarship office in the parents' canton of residence.
purpose: The University of Basel has its own fund to aid students with very limited resources and from low-income families.
Essentially, the parents and the scholarship office in the parents' canton of residence are responsible for funding studies.
Scholarships from the university are granted by the scholarship committee of the Senate in addition to any cantonal education contributions.
International students should find out what scholarships they are eligible for in their home country.
The student welfare office provides additional information and assistance with submission of applications.
degree_levels: Bachelor's (BA) - awards are made primarily during the final degree phase of the BA
Master's (MA) - awards are made primarily during the final degree phase of the MA
Medicine / nursing (BA and MA level) - only via the Margarete and Walter Lichtenstein Foundation, restricted to Swiss citizens
study_type: Full-time study (no separate part-time funding route is published)
Final degree phase of a Bachelor or Master programme is the main target of the scholarship funds
Degree programmes in biology with a focal area in zoology/botany (Legat Grobe)
official.degree_award: Not an award in itself - it is financial aid attached to an existing Bachelor or Master degree programme at the University of Basel; no separate certificate is awarded.
official.application_cycle: Semester-based: applications for the fall semester and applications for the spring semester, each with its own cut-off. Two rounds per academic year.
official.deadline_central_display: Application for the fall semester: until June 15. Application for the spring semester: until January 15.
official.deadline_institutional: Same as central - the university itself is the awarding body, so there is no separate institutional deadline.
official.deadline_note: The official deadlines page prints an asterisk next to both dates (Until June 15 (*), Until January 15 (*)) but the corresponding footnote text is not published on either the deadlines page or the funding page, so the asterisk's meaning could not be established. No year is attached to the dates, so no YYYY-MM-DD deadline could be derived.
official.status: OPEN - the fall-semester cut-off (15 June) has passed, and the next published cut-off is 15 January for the spring semester.
official.funding_label: Scholarship funds from the university (partial scholarships); Solidarity fund (Solifonds); Legat Grobe; Margarete and Walter Lichtenstein Foundation; Health and Accident Fund
official.funding_period: Scholarship funds and Legat Grobe: per person, per month. Solidarity fund (Solifonds): per person, per semester.
official.living_cost_coverage: Partial only. The award is a monthly or per-semester cash amount, not a tuition waiver; the page publishes no statement that it covers housing, food or transport.
official.tuition_rule: No tuition waiver is published on either the Scholarships page or the Funding from the University of Basel page. The university states that the parents and the scholarship office in the parents' canton of residence are essentially responsible for funding studies, and that its own scholarships are granted in addition to (not instead of) any cantonal education contributions.
covered_expenses: Supplementary partial scholarships for enrolled students, primarily in the final degree phase of a BA or MA
Scholarship funds from the university: CHF 200 to 600 per person, per month
Solidarity fund (Solifonds) from the student body: CHF 500 to 1000 per person, per semester
Legat Grobe: CHF 200 to 600 per person, per month, for biology degree programmes with a focal area in zoology/botany
Margarete and Walter Lichtenstein Foundation medical-department funds, for medical students with Swiss citizenship
Health and Accident Fund: costs incurred in the event of illness or accident that are not covered by health insurance, on submission of a cost estimate
not_covered_or_excluded: Tuition fees are not listed among the uses of any of the five funds - no tuition waiver is published
Living costs are not listed as a covered expense line; the awards are fixed cash amounts, not cost-based reimbursement
Travel costs are not listed as a covered expense
The Margarete and Walter Lichtenstein Foundation funds are restricted to students with Swiss citizenship, so non-Swiss applicants are excluded from that fund
The Legat Grobe is restricted to students completing a BA or MA in biology with a focal area in zoology/botany

important_advice_for_students: Do not treat this as a full scholarship: the largest published figure is CHF 600 per month from the university scholarship funds. Build a full living-cost budget around that number, not around tuition being waived.
No tuition waiver is published on either page, so assume you still pay University of Basel tuition fees unless Social Services tells you otherwise in writing.

The university itself says that funding studies is essentially the responsibility of the parents and the scholarship office in the parents' canton of residence, and that its awards come in addition to cantonal education contributions. Do not stop applying for cantonal or home-country aid on the strength of a Basel award.
International applicants are told by the university to check what they qualify for in their home country - the Basel funds are not a substitute for home-country or cantonal support.
If you are claiming illness or accident costs, apply before treatment and attach a cost estimate; the page states this as the expected procedure.
Because no document list or format rules are published online, ask the student welfare office for the required attachments rather than guessing.

Applying to the Legat Grobe from a degree programme other than biology with a zoology/botany focus.
Missing the semester cut-off: 15 January for spring, 15 June for fall. Late applications are not described as accepted.
Submitting a Health and Accident Fund claim only after the treatment has already happened, or without a cost estimate.
Expecting the award to cover tuition, housing or travel - none of those cost lines are published as covered.
Assuming the award replaces cantonal education contributions - the page says the university grants scholarships in addition to them.
estimated_uncovered_costs: University of Basel tuition fees - no tuition waiver is published on this page.
The large majority of living costs: the published award is CHF 200-600 per month (university funds) or CHF 500-1000 per semester (Solifonds), against Basel living costs.
Housing, food and local transport - none listed as covered.
Travel to and from Switzerland - not listed as covered.
Health insurance premiums and any illness/accident costs not covered by insurance, unless the Health and Accident Fund is granted.
Any shortfall between the award and the parents' or cantonal contribution the university says is still expected.

official.description: This is JASSO's reservation route into the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students, for students who secure admission to Japan from overseas. The published benefit is a monthly stipend of 48,000 yen, for 12 months if you enrol in April and 6 months if you enrol in September or October. Applications are never made to JASSO directly: the applicant must complete the procedure through the school they plan to enrol in, and only schools on JASSO's reservation-category list can nominate students.
purpose: The objectives of the reservation program are to contribute to ease their financial concerns about arrival and studies in Japan, promote pre-arrival admission and improve the level of learning.

The underlying scholarship is awarded to privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who have received pre-arrival admission in a graduate school, undergraduate school, junior college, college of technology (3rd year or above) or specialized course in a specialized training college in Japan and are facing financial difficulties.

Pre-arrival admission is defined as a programme through which international students can directly apply for admission from overseas; selection is carried out and permission for admission is granted without requiring candidates to come to Japan even once before enrollment.
study_type: Full-time enrolment only, as defined by the programme
Pre-arrival admission (application from overseas, no prior visit to Japan required)
April (spring) enrolment or September/October (autumn) enrolment
official.degree_award: Not a degree - a scholarship attached to an existing enrolment in a Japanese educational institution.
official.duration: 12 months (from April in the year of enrollment to next March) for students enrolled in April; 6 months (from October in the year of enrollment to next March) for students enrolled in September or October.
official.application_cycle: Two enrolment intakes are described: April (spring) enrolment and September/October (autumn) enrolment. JASSO publishes separate eligible-school lists for each, and the autumn list is based on the school list as of 1 April 2026 while the spring list is based on the list as of 1 October 2025.
official.deadline_note: No application deadline is published on the official English reservation-programme page. The page states only 'Please ask school you plan to enroll in. We do not accept applications directly from students', and 'To receive the scholarship, the applicant must complete the procedure through your school', so the operative date is set by the nominating school.

eligibility: Graduate level: a privately-financed international student who plans to enrol as a full-time student in a graduate school in Japan in April (September or October for autumn enrollment) using pre-arrival admission.

EJU exam or English courses: a privately-financed international student who plans to enrol as a full-time student in an undergraduate school, junior college, college of technology (3rd grade or upper) or specialized course in specialized training college in Japan in April (September or October for autumn enrollment) using pre-arrival admission.

Under this programme 'full-time student' does not include research students, trainees, non-degree students, advanced course students, special course students, auditing students and special students, among others.
To receive the scholarship, the candidate must complete the procedure through the school.

Conditions published on the parent scholarship page (Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students), which governs the award this reservation grants: the candidate must meet the grading criteria in the application guidelines; must meet the Japanese or English language condition (JLPT N2 or higher, EJU Japanese 200 points or more, or a JASSO-recognised level; or CEFR B2 or above), except for candidates at a preparatory Japanese language programme, a university preparatory course or a Japanese language institute; must agree after the grant to cooperate in the JASSO career path survey; any allowance received (excluding enrollment fee, tuition fee, etc.) must not exceed an average of 90,000 yen per month; if the candidate has a financial supporter in Japan, that supporter's annual income must be less than 5 million yen; the candidate must not be receiving a scholarship that cannot be combined with the Honors Scholarships; and the candidate must not be receiving support under JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program.

application_steps: 1. Identify your reservation category: Graduate level, EJU exam, or English courses.

2. Check the published JASSO eligible-school list for that category and for your intake (spring, or September/October) - the page warns the JASSO EJU list is a snapshot as of 1 October 2025 for spring and 1 April 2026 for September/October enrolment.
3. Obtain pre-arrival admission from that school, selecting admission from overseas without travelling to Japan first.
4. Ask the school how to apply; JASSO will not accept your application directly.
5. Complete the procedure through the school so that the school can nominate you.
6. Enrol as a full-time student in April, or in September/October for autumn enrolment.
7. After the grant, sign the JASSO-designated sheet every month at the international students' office of your school, and cooperate with the JASSO career path survey.

application_readiness_checklist: Pick your reservation category first - Graduate level, EJU exam, or English courses - because each has its own eligible-school list and the categories are not interchangeable.
Confirm your target school is on the JASSO list for that category and for your intake. JASSO warns the EJU list is a snapshot (1 October 2025 for spring, 1 April 2026 for September/October).
Get pre-arrival admission from that school, applying from overseas without travelling to Japan.
Ask the school's international office, in writing, for the nomination route and its internal deadline - JASSO publishes none.

Check the grant conditions published on the parent scholarship page: allowance (excluding enrolment fee and tuition) must average 90,000 yen or less per month, and if you are supported in Japan your supporter's annual income must be under 5 million yen.
Check the language condition (published on the parent page): JLPT N2+, EJU Japanese 200+, a JASSO-recognised level, or CEFR B2+.
Make sure you will enrol as a full-time student - research students, trainees, non-degree, advanced-course, special-course, auditing and special students are excluded.
Plan for the published duration only: 12 months from an April enrolment, 6 months from a September/October enrolment.
important_advice_for_students: Do not send anything to JASSO. Every JASSO page for this scholarship says applications go through your school, and a direct application will simply be ignored.

Budget on 48,000 yen per month. That is a stipend, not a tuition waiver, and the parent page's allowance test explicitly excludes enrolment fee and tuition fee, so you still pay tuition and enrolment fees in full.

Do not assume your school can nominate you: on the parent scholarship page JASSO states that the number of students an educational institution can recommend depends on the number of international students enrolled in it, and that depending on your institution you may not be able to apply.
Start with the reservation list, not with the scholarship. If your school is not on the list for your category and intake, there is no route into this scholarship through that school.
Pre-arrival admission and the scholarship are two separate selections. Holding pre-arrival admission does not give you the scholarship; the school's nomination does.
Once awarded, you must sign the JASSO sheet every month at your school's international students' office, and cooperate with the JASSO career path survey.
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to JASSO instead of through the school.
School not on the JASSO reservation list for the relevant category and intake.
Graduate school applicant trying to use the 'EJU exam' category, which explicitly excludes graduate schools.
English-courses applicant whose school's course is not conducted only in English, or does not offer pre-arrival admission for that course.
Enrolling in a study type that is not 'full-time' (research student, trainee, non-degree, advanced course, special course, auditing, special student).
Already holding the Japanese Government (MEXT) Monbukagakusho Scholarship or a Foreign Government Scholarship, which makes the student not privately-financed.
Allowance from other sources (excluding enrolment fee and tuition) averaging more than 90,000 yen per month (parent page condition).
A financial supporter in Japan with annual income of 5 million yen or more (parent page condition).
Holding support under JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program, or a scholarship that cannot be combined with the Honors Scholarships (parent page conditions).

Failing to meet the published Japanese or English language condition, except for candidates at a preparatory Japanese language programme, university preparatory course or Japanese language institute (parent page condition).
Failing the grading criteria in the application guidelines (parent page condition).
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees at your school - no tuition waiver is published and the parent page's allowance test excludes tuition fee.
The enrolment/admission fee - also excluded from the allowance definition and not covered.
Housing, food and daily transport - the 48,000 yen monthly stipend is not described as a living-cost payment.
Books, materials and course-related costs.
Medical insurance premiums and health costs - the reservation page does not list insurance among the benefits, unlike the GKS row elsewhere on JASSO pages.
Airfare to Japan, visa and relocation costs - travel coverage is not published.
Everything after the published scholarship period ends (12 months from April, or 6 months from a September/October enrolment).
document_audit: The official reservation-programme page publishes no document list at all, so there is nothing to audit against on the page itself.

The one document the parent scholarship page names is the JASSO-designated sheet that the recipient must sign every month at the international students' office - it is a post-award obligation, not an application attachment.

Prerequisites you will need in practice, though not listed as a document list: evidence of pre-arrival admission, proof of privately-financed status, evidence of your allowance level, and proof of your supporter's income if you are supported in Japan.
No file type, file size, translation, signature or date rules are published for any document in this programme.
Practical consequence: get the exact attachment list, language and format from your nominating school's international office in writing, because JASSO publishes none.

2. Verify the school is on the JASSO list for that category and intake.
3. Apply for and receive pre-arrival admission from the school, from overseas.

official.description: Global Scholarships is University of Galway's international Non-EU scholarship programme, described by the university as designed to attract and support outstanding students from around the world and to recognise academic excellence while fostering a diverse, global community of learners. The award takes the form of a partial fee waiver that is deducted from annual tuition fees for the 2027/28 academic year and is valid for Autumn 2027 entry only. Amounts vary by college, programme and award type, ranging from a 15% tuition discount to 50% of tuition fees, with Merit and Excellence cash-equivalent awards published in euro per year. It is explicitly not full funding: scholarship students must still pay 50% of the total tuition fee before registration, and no living-cost or travel support is published.

Its published value is approximately NZD $35,000 over a three-year tenure, structured rather than as a single payment: year one is paid as a fee waiver for accommodation in a University-owned or affiliated residential college (around $19,000, up to the standard room rate, and nothing if the recipient does not stay in such a college), and years two and three pay $7,000 each towards tuition and student services fees, conditional on satisfactory academic performance â€” normally a GPA of 7.0 (A-) or better in the preceding year. It is therefore not full funding: tuition in year one, living costs beyond the college room rate, and travel are not covered. Applications open 1 May in the year prior to study, and the closing date is two weeks after the applicant is invited to apply following an Offer of Place.

official.description: Danish universities each year receive a limited number of government scholarships to fund highly qualified full-degree students from countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland. The scholarship is administered by the universities themselves, which select the students, so the amount and the precise form of the award are set institution by institution. Study in Denmark states that the government scholarship consists of two parts and can be given as full or partial tuition fee waivers and/or grants towards covering living costs, and it directs applicants to the admission details of the higher education institution of their choice for the real terms.

Non-EU students who cannot get SU should look at the SU equal-status application on the same page - it is a separate route that this page explicitly points to.

The family-permit exclusion is easy to miss: if your residence permit came from a parent under sections 9c(1)/9m of the Aliens Consolidation Act and you are from a non-EU/EEA country, you are barred from this scholarship.

Not eligible if you have a legal claim to the rights of Danish citizens, are eligible for a grant under Danish law regarding the State Educational Grant and Loan Scheme (SU), or were granted a residence permit at the time of admission under the Danish Aliens Consolidations Act section 9c subsection 1 as the child of a foreign citizen holding a permit under section 9m and are a citizen of a country not acceded to the EU or covered by the EEA agreement.

official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Administered by the University of Copenhagen under the Danish Government Scholarship programme. Availability is faculty-specific and tightly capped: the Faculty of Social Sciences generally offers 2-3 per year and only with the September intake, the Faculty of Theology generally fewer than 4 per year, and the Faculties of Science and Health and Medical Sciences describe their numbers as very limited.
official.application_method: No separate scholarship application exists. "All non-EU/EEA applicants to the University of Copenhagen's MA/MSc degree programmes will automatically be considered for the Danish Government Scholarship, provided they are eligible. Therefore, you do not submit an individual application. Nominated students receive information directly through the application portal. If you are offered a scholarship, but do not accept it within the specified deadline, the scholarship offer will be revoked, and offered to another applicant." The Faculty of Social Sciences states that the admission offer itself will either confirm a scholarship award or require tuition payment, and that being told to pay tuition means no scholarship was granted.

official.description: The University of Copenhagen offers a limited number of tuition waivers and grants through the Danish Government Scholarship programme for highly talented students with outstanding academic records from non-EU/EEA countries. There is no individual scholarship application: all non-EU/EEA applicants to MA/MSc programmes are automatically considered as part of the academic assessment, and awards are made solely on academic achievement, with financial need explicitly not taken into consideration. The scholarship takes the form of full or partial tuition fee waivers and/or an amount covering basic living expenses, with faculty-specific caps: the Faculty of Science funds tuition plus 22 months of living expenses for applicants above a 90% bachelor's GPA admitted to their first-priority programme, Health and Medical Sciences and Humanities run smaller automatic schemes, Social Sciences offers roughly 2-3 per year only on the September intake, and Theology grants partial tuition waivers only.
official.program_type: Government-funded university tuition waiver and living-expense grant, decided automatically with admission
official.coverage: Full or partial tuition fee waiver and/or an amount covering basic living expenses, depending on faculty; travel is not covered and living-cost support is described only as basic living expenses.
official.funding: Partial to Full - 'granted either as full or partial tuition fee waivers and/or as an amount that covers basic living expenses'

official.description: The BI International Baccalaureate Scholarship is awarded to applicants who graduate with the top grades from the International Baccalaureate programme and covers 100% of tuition fees for up to three years, subject to academic progression. BI states that scholarships are awarded on academic excellence and not on financial need, with a minimum of 33 IB points for consideration, and only candidates admitted to the Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Data Science for Business or Bachelor of Digital Business commencing Autumn 2026 are considered. Applicants must apply for the scholarship at the same time as admission, uploading a combined one-page PDF of CV and scholarship letter into the Scholarship section, and decisions are made in two rounds at the end of April and in July.

official.selection_weighting: Explicitly published out of 100 points: quality of the applicant's motivation 30 points; previous study results in the transcript of records 30 points; reasons for recommending the applicant in recommendation letter 1 10 points; the same in recommendation letter 2 10 points; motivation for submission by the host institution 10 points; top talent profile of the applicant 10 points.
official.duration: One academic year for a 60 ECTS master's programme, or two academic years for a 120 ECTS master's programme. For a one-year programme, the final instalment of EUR 1,525 is not awarded if the master's degree is not obtained by July or September 2027. For a two-year programme, at least 54 ECTS must be obtained in the first academic year by July or September 2027 to receive the final instalment of EUR 1,525 of year one and to be entitled to the scholarship for the second year. Exceptions can only be granted by VLUHR in agreement with the hosting institution and the Department of Education and Training.

Must obtain the master's degree within the award period, or 54 ECTS in year one for a two-year programme, to receive the final EUR 1,525 instalment

At least half of the master's programme credits must be obtained at the Flemish host institution
On completion of the mobility, must submit an essay in the provided format and complete a short questionnaire about the mobility
If the scholarship is lost, must pay the full tuition fee to continue the programme

official.description: Master Mind Scholarships are granted by the Flemish government to excellent students who want to follow a master's programme at a Flemish higher education institution, to promote Flemish higher education as a top study destination for international talent. The total budget for 2026-2027 is EUR 480,000 and an estimated 30 international students can benefit, with a maximum award of EUR 10,225 per academic year for one year (60 ECTS) or two years (120 ECTS). Applicants must have a GPA of 3.5 out of 4.0 and the stated English proficiency, be nominated by a single host institution, and have their file submitted through Mobility-Online by 27 April 2026 at 23h59 GMT+1.
official.coverage: Provides a maximum of EUR 10,225 per academic year as a cash award, with the host institution permitted to charge a tuition fee of EUR 136.50 for 2026-2027, but does not cover tuition fees, accommodation, living costs beyond the award, or travel.

application_readiness_checklist: Convert your GPA to a 3.5 out of 4.0 scale using the published method on the last obtained bachelor's or master's degree
Take IELTS or TOEFL no more than 3 years before the April application processing date, at 7.0/94/C1 for a standard programme or 6.5/90/B2 for a School of Arts programme
Apply to the chosen Flemish host institution by its own deadline, which precedes the central 27 April date
Ensure only one Flemish institution nominates you
Get certified translations of any transcript or diploma not in Dutch, French, German or English
Ask your referees for two signed English recommendation letters
Plan the credit split so at least half the master's credits are earned at the Flemish host institution
Do not hold an Erasmus+, Erasmus Mundus, BAEF, Fullbright or other Flemish Government scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Missing the host institution's internal deadline, which is earlier than 27 April
Not being nominated, or being nominated by more than one institution
GPA below 3.5 out of 4.0
English test older than 3 years at the April processing date, or below the required band
Failing the host institution's academic check or not being accepted
Enrolling in a preparatory, bridging or distance learning programme
Not being accepted by the host institution even if selected, since acceptance is a condition
Failing to obtain the degree or 54 ECTS and thereby losing the final EUR 1,525
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees beyond the EUR 136.50 the host institution may charge
Accommodation
Living costs beyond EUR 10,225 per academic year
Travel to and from Belgium
Visa and immigration costs
document_audit: Verify your GPA conversion follows the published American GPA calculation annex
Check every document is in Dutch, French, German or English or has a certified translation attached
Confirm both recommendation letters are signed and written in English
Ensure the CV includes your GPA out of 4.0 and any publications, awards or previous scholarships
Check the English test date is within 3 years of the April processing date
Confirm your passport or national ID copy is legible

Begin the mobility in September 2026
Achieve the credits and degree required to keep the final instalment
Submit the completion essay and mobility questionnaire

official.description: This is not a single award but the Charles University overview page for the institutional and governmental scholarship schemes available to applicants and students of the University. It routes prospective students to the Czech Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport schemes (developing-country scholarships, general international scholarships, International Visegrad Fund Scholarships), the Václav Havel Bursary, the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies scholarships for foundation programme students, and faculty-level schemes (Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, Faculty of Science STARS for PhD students, Faculty of Social Sciences 'FSV UK SCHOLARS' and a GI Bill for U.S. veterans only). Separately, full-time doctoral students receive a guaranteed doctoral study income of at least 1.2 times the Czech minimum wage for the standard length of study (4 years), and students in emergencies can obtain bursaries, loans of technical aids and counselling from the Carolina Centre. No single award amount is published, because amounts are set by the internal regulations of each awarding body or faculty.
purpose: Present an overview of every institutional and governmental scholarship scheme available to applicants and students of Charles University.
Point international applicants to the correct awarding body: the University rectorate, the individual faculty, or an external funder such as the Czech Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport.
Guarantee doctoral study income for full-time doctoral students at a minimum of 1.2 times the minimum wage in Czechia during the standard length of studies.
Offer emergency support for students in emergency or otherwise difficult financial situations.
study_type: Foundation programme
Degree programme (bachelor's and master's)
Doctoral (PhD) study
official.degree_award: Not an award in itself — the listed schemes support study towards Charles University degrees and foundation programmes; the Václav Havel Bursary applies to students of both foundation and degree programmes
official.duration: Full-time doctoral students receive doctoral study income during the standard length of their studies (4 years); other schemes run for the academic year or the period specified in the awarding body's rules
official.deadline_note: No application deadline is published on this overview page. The University states that the exact amounts are always set by the internal regulations of the respective faculty and advises contacting the faculty's Admission Office directly; each national or external scheme (MEYS, Václav Havel Bursary, faculty schemes) runs its own timetable on its own official page.
official.funding_label: Institutional and governmental scholarship and bursary schemes for international applicants and students (overview directory, no single award)
official.funding_period: Published as ranges by bursary type, not as one figure: scholarship for outstanding academic achievement totals CZK 10,000–50,000 per academic year; scholarship for outstanding RDI/artistic/creative achievement up to CZK 100,000 per academic year; scholarship for RDI activities under special legislation up to CZK 360,000 per academic year; bursary to support study abroad up to CZK 180,000 per academic year; doctoral bursary CZK 10,500–25,000 per month. Scholarship paid from sources other than the state Contribution/Subsidy is not subject to these caps.
official.tuition_coverage: Most faculties offer merit-based scholarships for outstanding students and various forms of tuition fee waivers or reductions. The overview page publishes no university-wide tuition waiver and no university-wide tuition amount; waivers are set by each faculty's internal regulations.
official.living_cost_coverage: No scheme on this page is published as covering living costs in full. Partial, targeted support exists in the form of the accommodation bursary (basic accommodation bursary awarded by the Rector to all eligible students upon application, plus an increased accommodation bursary awarded at two rates based on an assessment of the household's social situation) and the bursary for students in a difficult social situation.
official.tuition_rule: Tuition-fee waivers or reductions are granted by the individual faculty, not centrally; the University states that the exact amounts are always set by the internal regulations of the respective faculty and directs students to the faculty's Admission Office. No tuition waiver condition is published for international students on this page.
covered_expenses: Periodic payments of a single amount or a lump sum, credited as a non-cash payment to the student's account, for any of the grounds in Article 3(1) of the Scholarship and Bursary Rules: outstanding academic achievement; outstanding RDI, artistic or other creative achievement contributing to greater knowledge; RDI activities under special legislation; a student in a difficult social situation (including accommodation bursary); cases worthy of special consideration; support for study abroad; support for study in the Czech Republic; support for doctoral students

Doctoral study income for full-time doctoral students, at a guaranteed minimum of 1.2 times the minimum wage in Czechia for the standard length of study (4 years), made up of a doctoral scholarship, a salary or wage for creative activities directly related to the preparation of the dissertation, or a combination of both
Emergency assistance via the Carolina Centre: bursaries, loans of technical aids, and counselling services
not_covered_or_excluded: No scheme on this page is published as full funding: none is stated to cover tuition, living costs and required expenses together
The overview page publishes no travel, airfare, health-insurance or relocation funding
Scholarship for outstanding academic achievement may not be awarded to doctoral students (Article 4(6))

Where a bursary to support study abroad was paid and its purpose cannot be fulfilled or was not fulfilled with respect to the award conditions, the student is required to return the bursary (Article 10(3))

Scholarships paid from other sources are not covered by the University caps in Articles 4–10, but conversely the state Contribution/Subsidy schemes carry no entitlement to any amount beyond those caps
benefits: Guaranteed minimum doctoral study income of 1.2 times the Czech minimum wage during the standard length of doctoral study, which is often supplemented by research-project participation awards and remuneration for teaching undergraduates
Emergency financial support through the Carolina Centre, including loans of technical aids and counselling services
Continued access to further support after the first year of studies: most faculties offer merit-based scholarships for outstanding students
eligibility: A scholarship or bursary may be awarded to a student in accordance with section 91 of the Higher Education Act on one of eight published grounds: (a) outstanding academic achievement; (b) outstanding RDI, artistic or other creative achievement contributing to greater knowledge; (c) RDI activities in accordance with special legislation; (d) the student is in a difficult social situation, including an accommodation bursary; (e) cases worthy of special consideration; (f) to support study abroad; (g) to support study in the Czech Republic; (h) to doctoral students
A doctoral bursary is awarded to all students enrolled in a full-time doctoral programme whose study does not exceed the standard length of study of the given programme

A basic accommodation bursary is awarded by the Rector to all students upon application, unless subject to an obstacle under Article 13, and except for students to whom the increased accommodation bursary has already been awarded and students permanently residing in the district where they study or permanently residing in Prague if they study in Prague

The Václav Havel Bursary provides a scholarship to international students whose studies are hindered or prevented by repression under totalitarian, authoritarian or other non-democratic regimes anywhere in the world; it applies to students of both foundation and degree programmes
The Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies offers scholarships to selected students of Charles University foundation programmes
Faculty of Science STARS scholarship is for talented PhD students
general_eligibility: Applicants and students of Charles University; each scheme applies to a specific set of programmes (foundation, bachelor's, master's, doctoral) set by the awarding body
For a bursary to support study in the Czech Republic, the University states only that foreigners may be awarded it, with criteria and amount determined by the Rector or a dean
ineligibility_conditions: A scholarship or bursary may not be awarded or paid where the actual length of study in a bachelor's or master's programme exceeds the standard length of this programme by more than two years (Article 13(1))
A doctoral bursary may not be awarded where the aggregate of completed study exceeds the standard length of study in the programme in which the student is pursuing his studies (Article 13(2))
A doctoral bursary may not be paid where the Subject-Area Board concludes that the student failed to fulfil the requirements of the individual curriculum (Article 13(3))

An accommodation bursary may not be awarded or paid where: the student is pursuing studies otherwise than as a full-time student; the student is enrolled in a programme taught in a foreign language; previous studies at public higher education institutions were, more than twice, terminated rather than successfully completed; or the actual length of study in one of simultaneously pursued programmes exceeded its standard length by more than one year (Article 13(4))
A bursary for a student in a difficult social situation may not be awarded or paid where the actual length of study exceeded the standard length of study in the programme (Article 13(5))

A scholarship for outstanding academic achievement may not be awarded or paid where the actual length of study exceeded the standard length of study in the programme by more than one year (Article 13(6))

Where the assessment of a doctoral student indicates failure to fulfil study requirements, the dean may reduce the doctoral bursary or award it at up to 50% of the normal amount; failure to fulfil the individual curriculum leads to withdrawal of the bursary (Article 12(5)–(6))
official.citizenship_residency: Open to international applicants and students of Charles University. Individual schemes are restricted by origin: the Faculty of Social Sciences' GI Bill participation is for U.S. veterans only; the Václav Havel Bursary is for students whose studies are hindered or prevented by repression under totalitarian, authoritarian or other non-democratic regimes anywhere in the world.
official.international_eligibility: The Czech Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport offers three distinct scholarship opportunities for international students: scholarships for applicants from developing countries, general scholarships for international students, and International Visegrad Fund Scholarships. Charles University also directs international applicants to the Study in Czechia and Study in Prague scholarship portals and to educational organisations, private beneficiaries and international foundations.

undergraduate: Foundation programmes: the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies offers scholarships to selected students of foundation programmes; the Václav Havel Bursary applies to foundation programme students

Bachelor's programmes: scholarship for outstanding academic achievement may, where the Faculty Internal Regulation provides for it, be awarded in the first unit of study of a post-bachelor's programme for excellent results in the previous bachelor's programme
masters: A scholarship for outstanding academic achievement is awarded to students retroactively for excellent academic results in the previous unit of study; where the Faculty Internal Regulation treats the unit as a semester, results from the previous two units within the same academic year may be used

The number of students awarded a scholarship for outstanding academic achievement represents at least 10% of students of a faculty, a programme of study or a unit of study, or a programme of study and a unit of study, in all cases where no obstacle under Article 13 has arisen; this number does not include students in the first unit of study, and unless the Faculty Internal Regulation provides otherwise does not include students in the first unit of study of a post-bachelor's programme
phd: A doctoral bursary is awarded to all students enrolled in a full-time doctoral programme whose study does not exceed the standard length of study
A scholarship for outstanding academic achievement may not be awarded to doctoral students

After passing the state doctoral examination, the doctoral bursary is increased by CZK 2,000 per month from the following calendar month; a Faculty Internal Regulation may provide a further increase not exceeding CZK 10,000 per month in total
An additional bursary not exceeding the health insurance premium paid by a full-time doctoral student may be awarded, paid twice a year

host_requirements: The student must be enrolled in a study programme at Charles University; a dean awards scholarships and bursaries in the faculty in which the student is enrolled
Scholarships under Article 3(1)(b) and (c) may also be awarded by the dean of the faculty which offers the relevant programme of study and where the student is not enrolled
Awards paid from the state budget Contribution or Subsidy are decided in first instance by a dean or the Rector; the Rector is the appeal body
Where a scholarship is awarded by the Rector, the form and dates of payment are set in a Rector's directive; otherwise in a dean's directive
requirements: The student must indicate in the application: name and surname, as well as other names and the maiden name where appropriate, date of birth, the address of permanent residence, and the address for delivery of mail if it differs and cannot be delivered electronically
The application must state the subject matter of the application
The application must state what is being requested
The application must bear the student's signature
For an accommodation bursary, an application for assessment of the social situation of the student's household is required, in accordance with applicable legislation

The form, formal elements and dates for submission of applications, the processing time limits and payment conditions are set by a Rector's directive; unless the Rector's directive provides otherwise, the bursary application is submitted in electronic form
documents: Signed written application stating identity, date of birth, addresses, subject matter and what is requested
Application for assessment of the social situation of the student's household (for the increased accommodation bursary)
Faculty-specific supporting documents for faculty schemes, set by the relevant Faculty Internal Regulation (not enumerated on this overview page)
document_format_rules: Unless otherwise provided in a Rector's directive, the bursary application is submitted in electronic form
A postal appeal is deemed filed on time if the letter was submitted to the postal service operator on the last day of the deadline
No file-size limit, accepted file type or translation rule is published on this overview page; these are set by the relevant Rector's or dean's directive
selection_criteria: Scholarship for outstanding academic achievement: the basic criterion is the average grade or weighted average grade, or other similar indicator, from examinations and other graded study requirements over the previous unit of study, determined in accordance with Article 8(13) of the University's Code of Study and Examination; awarded to a set number of students with the best indicator
Scholarship for outstanding RDI, artistic or other creative achievement and scholarship for RDI activities: award criteria are set out in the Faculty Internal Regulation
Bursary to support study abroad: criteria are set out in the Faculty Internal Regulation

Bursary for a student in a difficult social situation: awarded based on the student's social situation in accordance with section 91(3) of the Higher Education Act, in the amount determined in that provision

Bursaries in cases worthy of special consideration: criteria include participation in teaching and research activities, work in laboratories, contributions to the development of information technologies, international cooperation, excellent sports achievements, representation and promotion of the University, or laudable citizen acts
official.selection_notes: The award is decided in first instance by a dean or by the Rector; the Rector is the appeal body. A dean awards, of his own motion, the scholarships for outstanding academic achievement and for doctoral students, and may award, of his own motion, the scholarships for RDI activities, cases worthy of special consideration and those from the Scholarships and Bursaries Fund or other sources. The Rector may award, upon application, the bursary for students in a difficult social situation and the bursary to support study in the Czech Republic. In the absence of special provisions of the Higher Education Act, the Administrative Procedure Code applies. A decision is issued in writing with a statement part, reasoning and notice of the right of appeal, stamped with the official stamp and signed by a person in authority. An appeal may be filed within thirty days of the date of notification of the decision; an appeal filed only against the reasoning is impermissible; new facts and new evidence are taken into account only if they could not have been presented earlier.
application_method: Submit the application to the dean of the faculty in which you are enrolled, or to the Rector, depending on the scheme
For an increased accommodation bursary, submit an application for assessment of the social situation of the student's household
Where a scheme is run by an external funder (MEYS, Václav Havel Bursary), follow that body's own application route on its official page
application_steps: Identify which scheme you are eligible for on this overview page (rectorate, faculty, or external funder).
Meet the admission requirement of the relevant programme: obtain admission to a Charles University foundation or degree programme first where required.

Prepare the application with the mandatory content: name and surname and other names/maiden name, date of birth, address of permanent residence, mail-delivery address if different, subject matter of the application, what is being requested, and the signature.
For an increased accommodation bursary, prepare the household social situation assessment required by the Rector's directive.

Submit the application electronically through the University's information system unless the Rector's directive for your bursary provides otherwise, or in writing, before the deadline set in the relevant Rector's or dean's directive.
Track processing: first-instance proceedings commence on the day the dean or Rector received the application.
If refused or reduced, note the 30-day appeal period from notification of the decision, and that the Rector decides the appeal.
applicant_submission_route: Student submits directly to the dean of the faculty in which the student is enrolled, or to the Rector for rectorate-level bursaries
Scholarships under Article 3(1)(b) and (c) may be decided by the dean of the faculty offering the programme even where the student is not enrolled there
External schemes (MEYS, Václav Havel Bursary, faculty schemes) are applied for through that awarding body's own route
official.application_portal: No dedicated university scholarship portal is published on this page. Applications are handled through the faculty in which the student is enrolled or the Rector's Office, using the University's electronic information system unless the relevant Rector's directive provides otherwise.
award_holder_conditions: Awards from the state Contribution or Subsidy are subject to the obstacles to granting in Article 13

Where a bursary to support study abroad was paid to a student who should not have received it, or its purpose cannot be or was not fulfilled with respect to the award conditions, the student is required to return the bursary; the person who decided on the award decides on return of his own motion, stipulating the deadline, manner and procedure

A doctoral bursary may be reduced or withdrawn if the annual assessment of the doctoral student indicates failure to fulfil study requirements or the individual curriculum; a reduced bursary or one at up to 50% lasts no longer than until the end of the academic year following the assessed year, and may be reinstated on a subsequent positive assessment
Where a student is eligible for only part of a calendar month, the amount paid is proportionate to the number of days of eligibility

Where the student is enrolled in several programmes, the accommodation bursary, the difficult-social-situation bursary and the doctoral bursary may each be awarded and paid only once for the given period
Scholarships paid from other sources are not subject to the maximum amounts in the Scholarship and Bursary Rules
timeline_rules: The doctoral bursary is paid retroactively for the whole year of study as monthly periodic payments of the same amount, or as a lump sum

The accommodation bursary is paid retroactively as a periodic, usually quarterly, payment of the same amount; it is paid over ten months in an academic year to a student enrolled in a bachelor's or master's programme, and during the whole academic year to a doctoral student
The bursary for a student in a difficult social situation is paid retroactively, usually quarterly, by the Rector's Office over ten months in an academic year
The additional doctoral bursary for health insurance premium is paid twice a year

application_readiness_checklist: Decide which specific scheme you are applying for on the Charles University overview page — rectorate, faculty-level, or an external funder (MEYS, Václav Havel Bursary). The page is a directory, not an application form.

Secure or apply for admission to the relevant Charles University programme first where the scheme is tied to enrolment; several scholarships are awarded by the dean of the faculty in which you are enrolled.
Check the English-language teaching question carefully: the basic accommodation bursary is explicitly not available to students enrolled in a programme taught in a foreign language.

Check the standard length of study for your programme. More than two years over standard length in a bachelor's or master's programme blocks all scholarships and bursaries; more than one year over blocks the scholarship for outstanding academic achievement.

Collect the mandatory application content before you start: name and surname and any other names/maiden name, date of birth, address of permanent residence, a separate mail-delivery address if different, the subject matter, what is being requested, and your signature.
For an increased accommodation bursary, prepare the household social situation assessment in the form required by the Rector's directive.
Read the Faculty Internal Regulation 'Rules for Awarding Scholarships and Bursaries at the Faculty' for your faculty — the faculty sets the actual award amount and, in many cases, the deadline.
important_advice_for_students: Do not treat this page as an application portal. It carries no form, no amount and no deadline; it is a routing page.
Do not assume a full scholarship. Nothing here is published as covering tuition, living costs and required expenses together.
Do rely on the guaranteed doctoral study income as a real entitlement for full-time doctoral students: at least 1.2 times the Czech minimum wage for the standard length of study (4 years).

Contact the faculty Admission Office directly rather than the central rectorate for the specific amount and deadline of a faculty scheme — the University states amounts are always set by faculty internal regulations.
Note that most faculty merit scholarships are awarded retroactively for the previous unit of study, so they are awarded after your results exist, not at the start of the year.
Use the Carolina Centre route if you are in an emergency financial situation rather than waiting for a scholarship round.
common_rejection_risks: Actual length of study in a bachelor's or master's programme exceeding the standard length by more than two years — an absolute bar to any scholarship or bursary.
Actual length of study exceeding standard length by more than one year — bars the scholarship for outstanding academic achievement.
Enrolment in a programme taught in a foreign language — bars the accommodation bursary.
Not being a full-time student — bars the accommodation bursary and the doctoral bursary.
Previous studies at public higher education institutions terminated rather than successfully completed more than twice — bars the accommodation bursary.
Aggregate of completed study exceeding the standard length of the doctoral programme — bars the doctoral bursary.
Failure to fulfil the individual curriculum as judged by the Subject-Area Board — bars or withdraws the doctoral bursary.

Missing mandatory application content (identity, addresses, subject matter, request, signature) — the dean or Rector must invite you to cure deficiencies within a reasonable time, which is the most common delay cause.
Applying to a bursary to support study abroad and then not fulfilling the purpose for which it was awarded — the bursary must be returned.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs beyond the published bursary ranges: no scheme on this page is published as covering living costs in full
Tuition fees for programmes taught in English, unless your faculty grants a waiver or reduction under its own internal regulations
Airfare, travel and relocation: no travel funding is published anywhere on this page
Health insurance: only a bursary not exceeding the premium actually paid by a full-time doctoral student is described, and only for doctoral students
Books, equipment and course-specific costs: not addressed on this page
The gap between a bursary award and actual cost of living in Prague, which the University publishes separately on its 'Costs of Living' page rather than covering here
document_audit: Signed application — the signature is a prescribed requirement, not optional.
Name and surname, other names and maiden name where appropriate, and date of birth — all mandatory identifying data points.
Address of permanent residence, plus a mail-delivery address if different and not deliverable electronically.
Subject matter of the application and a clear statement of what is being requested — both mandatory.
Submission form: electronic by default, unless the relevant Rector's directive provides otherwise. Check the directive for your bursary type.
For an increased accommodation bursary: the household social situation assessment document required by the Rector's directive.
No file-size limits, accepted file types or translation rules are published on this page; they are set in the applicable Rector's or dean's directive, which you must obtain.

referee_tracking.instructions: No referee or reference requirement is published on this overview page. The published selection route is the grade-based indicator from examinations and graded study requirements of the previous unit of study, assessed by the dean or Rector; where a faculty Internal Regulation requires references, it is set there, not here.

alerts.trigger: You are planning to study at Charles University and need money
alerts.message: Start with the faculty, not the rectorate: faculty scholarship amounts and deadlines are set in the faculty's internal regulations, and the University explicitly directs students to the faculty Admission Office.

alerts.trigger: You are enrolling in a programme taught in a foreign language
alerts.message: You are excluded from the basic accommodation bursary under Article 13(4)(b). Plan accommodation costs accordingly.

alerts.trigger: You are a full-time doctoral student
alerts.message: Your doctoral bursary is an entitlement during the standard length of study, but it is reduced or withdrawn if the annual Subject-Area Board assessment finds you did not fulfil your individual curriculum.

alerts.trigger: You received a bursary to support study abroad
alerts.message: You are contractually required to return it if its purpose cannot be or was not fulfilled; the deciding dean or Rector sets the return deadline, manner and procedure.

alerts.trigger: You received a decision you disagree with
alerts.message: The appeal period is 30 days from notification; an appeal against the reasoning alone is impermissible. Missing or defective notification of the right of appeal extends the outer limit to 90 days.

submission_workflow: Choose the specific scheme and identify the deciding authority: dean of the faculty where you are enrolled, or the Rector.
Obtain the applicable Faculty Internal Regulation or Rector's directive for that scheme — it fixes the amount, the deadline and the submission form.
Assemble the mandatory application content, including your signature.
Submit electronically through the University's information system unless the Rector's directive for that bursary provides otherwise.
Retain proof of submission; proceedings commence on the day the dean or Rector received the application.
If the application is deficient, cure it within the reasonable time period given, or ask the dean or Rector's office to help you correct it.
If refused or reduced, decide within 30 days of notification whether to appeal, and file with the dean or the Rector as the notice specifies.
post_award_requirements: Hold the award for its stated purpose; a bursary to support study abroad must be returned if the purpose is not fulfilled.
Accept that bursary payments are proportionate to days of eligibility if you become eligible part-way through a month.

For doctoral students, undergo the annual assessment of the doctoral student by the Subject-Area Board; failure to fulfil study requirements leads to reduction of up to 50% or withdrawal of the doctoral bursary.

Do not enrol simultaneously in programmes in a way that would duplicate bursaries: the accommodation bursary, the difficult-social-situation bursary and the doctoral bursary may each be paid only once per period.
Watch your own length of study against the standard length, since exceeding it is the most common bar to payment.
Study in the Czech Republic bursary holders must comply with Article 23 of the Constitution of the University, which the criteria must also comply with.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the exact award amount of my faculty's scholarship or bursary for this academic year, and is it set in the Faculty Internal Regulation?
What is the application deadline for my faculty's scheme, and does the faculty accept electronic submission only?
Does my faculty grant any tuition-fee waiver or reduction for international students, and on what academic condition?
Am I in a programme taught in a foreign language, and does that exclude me from the accommodation bursary?
How does my standard length of study compare with my actual completed study, and does it put me within one or two years of the Article 13 bar?
Which Rector's directive governs the bursary type I want, and what does it require in terms of form, formal elements and submission dates?
For doctoral students: what does the annual Subject-Area Board assessment require of me to keep the doctoral bursary, and what happens to the CZK 2,000 post-examination increase?

official.funding_label: $5,000 per session for two or three consecutive sessions ($10,000 or $15,000 per year)

In all instances, the awarding graduate unit contributes to one-third the cost of the total award received by the student
The U of T program is jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and the University of Toronto
The Province allocates OGS awards to universities specifying the number each may offer annually

Automatic consideration for the SGS Inclusive Excellence Graduate Scholarship competition for students who are Black and/or Indigenous to Canada, with OGS awards valued at up to $15,000 per year and approximately 25 awards made annually
Refunds are issued for any award money left after tuition charges, by mailed cheque or direct deposit
eligibility: Be a Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident, or Protected Person under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (Canada) by the student deadline as determined by each graduate unit

International students studying or planning to study at the University of Toronto under a temporary resident visa (student study permit) are eligible for a set number of OGS awards, with valid study permits effective as of the graduate unit's OGS international application deadline

Be registered or intend to register in an eligible program on a full-time basis in 2026-2027, where an eligible program is a full-time program of two or three terms leading to a graduate degree, and a full-time student is one who is in at least 60% of a full course load (40% for students with a permanent disability) or as defined by their institution
Have not exceeded the lifetime maximum of government-funded support or maximum OGS/QEII support available for their current level of study

Have achieved at least A- (or equivalent) in each of the last two completed years of study (full-time equivalent), or, if the student has completed two years or more of graduate studies at the time of application, an overall average of at least A- (or equivalent) on all graduate courses completed

requirements: Submit an OGS application to your proposed graduate unit through the SGS centralized online OGS application by that unit's internal deadline
Submit a separate application to each graduate unit you are seeking admission to, since awards are not transferable between graduate units
Submit a separate application to each Ontario institution if applying to multiple universities, as each has its own unique OGS application and process
International students must hold a valid study permit effective as of the graduate unit's OGS international application deadline
Maintain an A- (or equivalent) average in each of the last two completed years of study
Meet the lifetime maximum of government-funded support for your current level of study
Demonstrate at least 60% of a full course load to count as full-time, or 40% with a permanent disability
Be in good standing with OSAP; any OSAP restriction must be cleared within 30 days of notification to accept and hold the award

Complete all components of the online application, since the application requires an OGS application form, transcripts, previous awards/publications/conference/research experience, a plan of study, and two academic references

Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, with unofficial and student-issued transcripts permitted, for example ACORN screenshots
Previous awards, publications, conference and research experience
Plan of study, maximum 2 pages: 1 page for the Plan of Study and 1 page for references/citations
Two academic references, with referees required to submit online

selection_criteria: Relevant experience and achievements obtained within and beyond academia, weighted up to 40% - assessed through transcripts, other academic accomplishments, prior scholarships and awards, publications and presentations, research and/or creative productivity, academic training and relevant work experience including co-op, and academic, professional and extracurricular activities such as teaching, mentoring, supervising or coaching, managing projects, science or research promotion, community outreach, volunteer work or civic engagement, chairing committees or organizing conferences

Plan of Study, weighted up to 30% - motivation, creativity, communication skills, feasibility, merit and significance; a course-based statement of intent or a research-based research proposal; connection or synergy with the programme of study; for research proposals, the focus and feasibility of the research question and objectives, the clarity of the proposed methodology, and the significance and expected contributions to research

Academic assessment reports, weighted up to 30% with 15% for each letter - ability to complete projects within an appropriate time period, contribution to research and development, critical thinking, application of skills and knowledge, judgment, originality, initiative, autonomy, enthusiasm, and ability to communicate clearly and logically in written and oral formats
Prior scholarships and awards may be used to confirm assessment based on other aspects of the file, but students should not be penalized for not having received other awards

At the graduate unit's discretion, exceptions may be made for highly meritorious applicants below the GPA minimum, for example applicants with documented medical issues or family care responsibilities, applicants who pursued alternative career paths, or mature students with professional experience
official.selection_weighting: Relevant experience and achievements up to 40%; Plan of Study up to 30%; academic assessment reports up to 30% (15% for each of the two letters). Must maintain accurate and current mailing and direct deposit information on ACORN
Award offers must be accepted by completing an SGS Award Payment Activation form through the SGS Forms Tool

May accept research assistantships, part-time teaching positions or other paid employment that does not affect full-time status and is commensurate with graduate unit policies; students in full-time paid employment are typically ineligible
Cannot hold an OGS in the same session or the same award year as a scholarship from SSHRC, NSERC, CIHR, QEII-GSST, or another OGS

Award holders who opt to apply for OSAP assistance should not report their OGS or QEII-GSST funding to OSAP, as SGS reports this on their behalf, and must report any other awards or fellowship funding

official.description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship encourages excellence in graduate studies at publicly-assisted universities in Ontario, and the U of T program is jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and the University of Toronto, which is allocated a fixed number of awards annually. The award is worth $5,000 per session, so $10,000 for two consecutive sessions or $15,000 for three, with the awarding graduate unit contributing one third of the total, and is tenable for one year. Applicants need an A- or equivalent in each of the last two completed years, must be registered full-time in an eligible two- or three-term programme, and are assessed on relevant experience and achievements (up to 40%), plan of study (up to 30%) and two academic assessment reports (up to 30%). Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons qualify, and international students on valid study permits compete for a set number of awards through a centralized adjudication of graduate unit nominations, with results in mid-July.

official.coverage: A value-based scholarship of $5,000 per session for two or three sessions ($10,000 or $15,000 per year), with the graduate unit contributing one third of the cost; it is not described as a tuition waiver, and any funds left after tuition charges are refunded.

official.description: This record covers Fudan University's announcement of the 2026 Shanghai Government Scholarship for International Students. The official announcement page is published by the University's International Cooperation Division with a publish time of 2025-10-31, but the page body is empty: it carries the title, publisher, date and site navigation only, with no eligibility rules, no benefit amount, no application steps and no deadline. Fudan's International Cooperation Division separately publishes a Scholarship documents section containing the SGS Annual Review Form, the Monthly Feedback form and the Absence from Scholarship Registration Request Form, which establish that holders of the scholarship are subject to recurring registration, feedback and annual review obligations. Nothing about the money itself is published on the pages that could be read.

application_readiness_checklist: Do not rely on this record for figures or dates. The official announcement page is empty, so contact the Fudan International Cooperation Division directly before you plan around any amount, deadline or condition.
Get the current cycle's SGS rules in writing from the International Cooperation Division - the 2026 announcement on the site has no body text.
Expect an ongoing obligation if you are awarded: the office publishes an SGS Annual Review Form, a Monthly Feedback form and an Absence from Scholarship Registration Request Form.
Note that the absence-from-registration form exists, which means missing a scholarship registration period is a formal process with a form, not an automatic lapse.
Keep your Fudan enrolment current, since the scheme is titled for international students of Fudan University.
Check whether the China Scholarship Council or the Shanghai municipal international services office has a parallel published call, since the announcement page links both.
important_advice_for_students: The published announcement contains no amount, no eligibility list and no deadline. Anyone quoting a figure or a closing date for this award from this page is not quoting the university.

Do not assume the award is a full scholarship. Nothing establishes tuition, living-cost or travel coverage, so fully_funded is false by default and you should budget as if you pay your own costs until the office confirms otherwise.
Treat the three published SGS forms as the clearest signal about what holding this scholarship involves: monthly feedback, annual review, and formal notification of any absence from registration.

The 2026 announcement was published on 2025-10-31 and has no visible content. Check the International Cooperation Division's notice pages and the Scholarship documents section for the live cycle rather than this archived stub.
If you are already a Fudan student, the absence-from-registration form is the item to keep - it is the only published mechanism for handling a gap in scholarship registration.
common_rejection_risks: Planning around a deadline or amount that is not actually published on the official page - the record is unpopulated for those fields.
Failing to complete the recurring obligations the office publishes forms for: monthly feedback and annual review.
Missing a scholarship registration period without submitting the Absence from Scholarship Registration Request Form.
Not holding current Fudan enrolment, since the award is titled for international students of Fudan University.
Assuming eligibility on the basis of nationality - no nationality rule is published, so the office's own list governs.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything, as far as the official pages establish - no tuition, living-cost, travel or any other expense is listed as covered on the pages that could be read.

All three are post-award or registration instruments rather than application attachments.
No file type, file size, translation, signature or date rules are published for any of these forms.

The Scholarship documents section (https://iso.fudan.edu.cn/isoenglish/51337/list.htm) holds only 8 records in total, and the most recent are dated 2020-04-20 and 2019-08-31, so the section itself is not a reliable guide to the current cycle.
Practical consequence: request the current cycle's application document list, formats and deadlines directly from the International Cooperation Division, in writing, before assembling anything.

official.description: A Charles University bursary for international students whose studies are hindered or prevented by repression under totalitarian, authoritarian or other non-democratic regimes anywhere in the world. The financial support is provided directly by Charles University. The bursary can only be awarded to a student who has already been admitted and enrolled in a degree programme at one of the faculties of Charles University through the standard admissions procedure, so admission comes first and the bursary decision comes later. Students may additionally apply for a contribution towards living expenses as part of preparation for studies in the Czech language. Applications are considered twice a year, by 31 March and 31 October, and the faculty — not the student — forwards the complete file digitally to the Chair of the Václav Havel Bursary Board.

official.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for up to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. The 2027 call opens on 1 January 2027 at 12:00 PM, closes on 15 April 2027 at 12:00 PM, and results are announced on 31 May 2027 at 12:00 PM. Applicants must hold a bachelor's or master's degree, come from a Visegrad or EaP/WB country different from the host institution's country, have completed previous study levels elsewhere, and be more than 150 km from the host. The award is EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester to the host institution.

official.region: Central and Eastern Europe (Visegrad countries and EaP/WB countries)
official.coverage: A fixed payment of EUR 3,500 per semester to the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester to the host institution, for 1 to 2 semesters; the page does not state that tuition fees, accommodation or travel are covered.
