official.description: The Aalto University Excellence Scholarship is a merit-based full tuition fee waiver awarded on a competitive basis to the highest-achieving applicants, made during the admission process for tuition-fee students. It is a tuition-only award: Aalto states plainly that it does not offer any university-wide scholarships to cover living costs in Finland and that students must cover all living expenses and other study-related costs from their own resources. The waiver runs for the target time of the degree programme (three years of full-time study for a bachelor's degree, two years for a master's degree) and is continued year by year only if study progress is confirmed.
purpose: The Aalto University Scholarship Programme seeks to recognize talented non-EU/non-EEA students across the world by awarding academic excellence.
Aalto University Excellence Scholarships are merit-based and they are granted on a competitive basis to the highest-achieving applicants based on the programme's evaluation criteria.
degree_levels: Bachelor's degree (English-language programmes; target time three years of full-time study)
Master's degree (two-year programmes; target time two years of full-time study)
study_type: Full-time study is required, and studying according to the approved personal study plan
English-language degree programmes at Aalto University, the group in which non-EU/non-EEA students are liable to pay tuition fees
Programme-specific variations apply in international double degree programmes, which follow their own tuition fee and scholarship regulations
official.degree_award: Not a separate award - the scholarship funds a full bachelor's or master's degree programme at Aalto University.
official.duration: The scholarship is granted for the target time of the degree programme: three years of full-time study for a bachelor's degree and two years of full-time study for a master's degree. It is continued to the second (or third, in a bachelor's) academic year subject to an annual study-progress check.
official.application_cycle: Annual, tied to the university admission round. Tuition-fee students may apply for the scholarship during the admission process, using the same application form. For master's programmes beginning in autumn 2027 the application period runs from 7 December 2026 to 5 January 2027, with an application document deadline of 12 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC +2).
official.deadline_central_display: Application period for two-year master's programmes beginning in autumn 2027: 7 December 2026 at 9.00 to 5 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC +2). The scholarship is applied for during this admission process, on the same application form.
official.deadline_institutional: Document deadline for the master's admission application: 12 January 2027 at 15.00 (UTC +2) - all application documents must be uploaded to and saved in the application form before this deadline. Evaluation by the study options January to March 2027; first-stage results in art, design and architecture 12 March 2027; admissions results published 30 March 2027.

The dates above are the published Aalto master's admission dates for autumn 2027 entry, which is the cycle in which the scholarship is applied for. Bachelor's (English) admission dates are published separately on Aalto's bachelor's admissions page and were not read.

official.funding_label: Aalto University Excellence Scholarship - 100% tuition fee waiver
official.tuition_coverage: Full. Aalto University Excellence Scholarships are awarded as tuition fee waivers, covering the full tuition fee, and they cover the full tuition fee during the target time of the programme. The waiver will be applied against the tuition fee; where the admission process had already granted a tuition-fee waiver, this is expressed as a 100% tuition fee waiver for the target time.
official.living_cost_coverage: None. 'Aalto University does not offer any university-wide scholarships to cover living costs in Finland. Students are expected to cover all their living expenses and other study-related costs from their own financial resources.'
official.tuition_rule: The scholarship is awarded as a 100% tuition fee waiver for the target time of the degree programme. In order for the scholarship to be valid, you must agree to the terms of the scholarship by the given deadline. The tuition-fee discontinuation (7th term of a bachelor's programme or 5th term of a master's programme) is a separate measure and is not part of this scholarship.
official.host_institution_fee: No additional host fee is payable in place of tuition, because the full tuition fee is the item covered. The university publishes the Finnish application fee of â‚¬100 for applicants who are not citizens of the EU, EEA member states or Switzerland, collected by the Finnish National Agency for Education in connection with the Studyinfo application form, and states that the fee is statutory and non-negotiable with no waivers available.
official.tax_status: The university is obliged by law to report all scholarships to the Finnish tax authority on annual basis. Scholarships in Finland are generally tax free up to the value of â‚¬26,269.46 per calendar year (in 2024; the exact amount changes annually); the amount exceeding the set limit is generally subject to tax. The set limit includes any combination of Aalto University's scholarships (including tuition fee waivers), travel grants, one-off payments and living-expense scholarships.

not_covered_or_excluded: Living costs - explicitly excluded: Aalto offers no university-wide scholarships to cover living costs in Finland

Automatic continuation for the standard duration of the degree programme, provided you do not fall within the discontinuation guidelines

For Aalto bachelor's graduates continuing into a master's programme under the original 3+2 right to study: a 100% tuition fee waiver for the master's target time (two years or four terms), conditional on a weighted average grade of at least 3.50 and completing the bachelor's degree within the target time
eligibility: You are liable to pay tuition fees at Aalto (the scholarship is for tuition-fee students).
The Aalto University Scholarship Programme seeks to recognize talented non-EU/non-EEA students, so the applicant group is non-EU/non-EEA students.
You apply during the admission process for your degree programme, on the same application form.

For the bachelor's-to-master's continuation route: you must have received the Aalto University Excellence Scholarship for your English-medium bachelor's programme, and completed the bachelor's degree within the target time period (three years or six terms) with a weighted average grade of at least 3.50.
general_eligibility: Liability to pay Aalto tuition fees.
Full-time study at the level of the degree programme (bachelor's or master's).
Application submitted in the national Studyinfo.fi service during the published application period.

ineligibility_conditions: Students who are not liable to pay tuition fees at Aalto.

Scholarships are automatically continued only unless: studies do not follow the personal study plan so that graduation is likely to be delayed by more than one term; studies progress so slowly that graduation is likely to be delayed by more than one term; studies progress below 45 ECTS credits per academic year leading to discontinuation of the residence permit; or the terms and conditions of the scholarship agreement are broken.
A student who does not agree to the scholarship terms by the given deadline does not obtain a valid scholarship.

For the bachelor's-to-master's continuation route: a bachelor's degree completed in more than the target time (three years or six terms), or with a weighted average grade below 3.50, disqualifies the applicant from the master's scholarship.

The master's continuation scholarship is available only for Aalto master's programmes to which you have a direct right to study, i.e. without applying through an external master's admissions procedure.
Aalto states that if the scholarship does not cover the whole duration of your studies, you cannot apply for Aalto's tuition fee waivers in the middle of your studies.
official.citizenship_residency: The scholarship programme is described as seeking to recognize talented non-EU/non-EEA students, because those are the students liable to pay tuition fees at Aalto. EU/EEA citizens are not liable to pay tuition fees and are not the target group.
official.international_eligibility: Non-EU/non-EEA students liable to pay Aalto tuition fees. Separate, country-specific partner awards published on the same page have their own nationality rules and amounts: the COLFUTURO partial discount (25% of tuition fees) for Colombian citizens, the FUNED partial discount (25% of tuition fees) for Mexican citizens, the Fulbright-Aalto University Graduate Award for United States citizens only, and the Pekka Mattila Excellence Scholarship, which is open regardless of age, nationality or gender but only to applicants liable to pay tuition fees in the School of Business Master's Programme in Marketing or International Management.

undergraduate: Target time: three years of full-time study for a bachelor's degree.
Continuation to the third academic year is subject to the same annual study-progress check as the second year.

Financial consequences of extending to the 7th term: if you received the Aalto University Excellence Scholarship for your bachelor's programme, extending to the 7th term means you will no longer meet the scholarship criteria for the Aalto University Excellence Scholarship for the master's programme under your original 3+2 right to study.
masters: Target time: two years of full-time study for a master's degree.

Continuation to the second academic year is conditional on progressing according to the approved personal study plan during the first academic year, and on having a goal-oriented and feasible study plan for the second year; study progress is checked during the spring term.

For bachelor's graduates continuing under the original 3+2 study right: 100% tuition fee waiver for the master's target time (two years or four terms), requiring the bachelor's Excellence Scholarship, graduation within target time, and a weighted average grade of at least 3.50.
phd: Not covered. The published target times are defined for bachelor's and master's degree programmes only, and the Excellence Scholarship is an admissions-stage tuition-fee waiver for degree students.

host_requirements: The applicant must be admitted to an Aalto University degree programme in which they are liable to pay the tuition fee directly to Aalto University; students in international joint programmes that have their own tuition fees and scholarship systems follow those specific regulations instead.

Study full-time and follow the approved personal study plan.

For the bachelor's-to-master's continuation: request the master's scholarship in Sisu when filling in the bachelor's degree graduation request, or contact the student services of your degree programme if eligible but not applied.
documents: Application form (in the Studyinfo.fi service)
Bachelor's degree certificate (PDF, named Degree-certificate-lastname-firstname)
Transcript of study records for the bachelor's degree (PDF, named Transcript-lastname-firstname), issued by the university's official authority and including all pages

Study-option-specific documents listed on the study option's webpage (these may include, for example, a motivation letter, and for the fields of art, design and architecture a portfolio and further work samples)
document_format_rules: File format: PDF only.

Upload each document as a separate file, to the correct attachment section of the application form; the applicant is responsible for uploading the correct documents to the correct sections, and incorrect uploads (e.g. a wrong file) may lead to rejection.
Scan each original document in the correct orientation so that a horizontal document is displayed horizontally and a vertical document vertically.
Ensure scans are high quality and the content of the documents is fully visible and legible.
Name files as instructed, e.g. Transcript-lastname-firstname and Degree-certificate-lastname-firstname.

At the application stage electronic copies of the original documents suffice; after admission results, admitted applicants must submit officially certified (attested) copies by the given deadline, and certified documents will be compared to the electronic documents uploaded at the application stage.
Official translations must be obtained where required before applying.

The degree certificate must include the student's name, the name of the degree, the name of the degree-awarding institution and the date the degree was awarded; a Diploma Supplement alone is not accepted, and a statement of completion of the studies is not sufficient.

The transcript must be issued by the university's official authority and be signed and, where applicable, stamped; an official digitally signed electronic transcript in PDF from the awarding university is also acceptable, but unofficial documents and screenshots from student information systems are not accepted.
If a required application document is missing after the document deadline, the application will be rejected as incomplete.
selection_criteria: Aalto University Excellence Scholarships are merit-based and are granted on a competitive basis to the highest-achieving applicants based on the programme's evaluation criteria.

Each study option evaluates and ranks applications that are complete and meet the general eligibility criteria, based on its own selection criteria, which may include the relevance of previous studies, academic performance, motivation and, in the fields of art, design and architecture, a portfolio.

The applications are compared to each other, and the highest-ranked applicants are admitted; since the number of study places is restricted, not all eligible applicants will receive an offer of admission, and study options are not required to fill all available places.
There is a very limited number of scholarships available, and programmes may also decide not to grant any scholarships.

For the bachelor's-to-master's continuation route: completion of the bachelor's degree within the target time period and a weighted average grade of at least 3.50, calculated from the completed degree in its entirety.
official.selection_notes: There is no separate scholarship selection round: the scholarship is decided as part of the admission process, using the programme's evaluation criteria. Evaluation is carried out by the study option during January to March 2027, and the admissions results are published on 30 March 2027 (first-stage results in the fields of art, design and architecture on 12 March 2027). In the fields of art, design and architecture a two-stage evaluation may apply, with selection committees evaluating the application documents and a second stage consisting of an interview, which may be conducted remotely.
application_method: Apply for the degree programme in the national Studyinfo.fi service during the published application period.
Request the Aalto University Excellence Scholarship on the same application form during the admission process.
Pay the â‚¬100 application fee if required, within seven days of submitting the application.
Upload and save all obligatory and study-option-specific documents by the document deadline.
After the scholarship decision, agree to the scholarship terms by the given deadline.
application_steps: 1. Read the application instructions, the general eligibility criteria and your study option's evaluation criteria, and prepare your documents in advance.

2. Complete the application form in the Studyinfo.fi service during the application period (7 December 2026 at 9.00 to 5 January 2027 at 15.00, UTC +2 for autumn 2027 master's entry). You may apply to a maximum of two study options and must rank them.
3. Request the Aalto University Excellence Scholarship on the same application form.

official.description: The Ramanujan Fellowship is a five-year, scientist-specific award created to reverse brain drain: it brings brilliant Indian and Indian-origin scientists and engineers working abroad back to take up scientific positions in India, across all areas of science. The support has three components - a consolidated personal fellowship of Rs.1,35,000 per month including an HRA component, a research grant of Rs.7.00 lakh per annum, and overhead charges of Rs.60,000 paid to the host institute. It is not a study scholarship: the fellow is not entitled to any salary from the institute, and taking a permanent, tenure-track or contractual position ends the fellowship in total.
purpose: The Ramanujan Fellowship is meant for brilliant Indian/Indian Origin scientists and engineers from all over the world to take up scientific positions in India and for those scientists who want to return to India from abroad.
The Fellowship is scientist-specific and very selective.
This fellowship is meant for working in new areas and laboratories in order to expand their research capabilities, other than the one where the candidate has obtained his/her doctorate degree.

Ramanujan Fellowship is meant for reverse brain drain i.e. inviting brilliant Indian/Indian Origin scientists and engineers who want to return to India from abroad to take up scientific positions in India.

important_advice_for_students: This is a research fellowship for a returning scientist, not a study scholarship. If you are a current student without a research career, you are the wrong applicant.

The Rs.1,35,000 per month already includes HRA - do not budget a separate housing allowance on top, because ANRF states it gives only the consolidated figure.
Only one international travel per year is available, so plan conferences and fieldwork around that limit.
Your grant is released year by year, not upfront for five years. Without the SE, UC and progress report, the following year's money does not arrive.

official.description: The University Research Fellowship is an eight-year, long-term research fellowship of the Royal Society for outstanding scientists in the early stages of their research career who have the potential to become leaders in their field. Applicants can request up to a maximum of Â£1,907,400 over eight years, which can cover their own salary contribution, indirect and estate costs, equipment and research expenses including consumables and travel, contributions to research assistance and staff costs, and relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants. It is a research employment fellowship, not a degree scholarship: the award is made to a person to build an independent research career at a UK university or research institution, or in the Republic of Ireland where awards are funded by Research Ireland.
purpose: The University Research Fellowship (URF) programme aims to support the next generation of research leaders to undertake cutting-edge research.

The stated objectives are to enable outstanding early career scientists with the potential to become leaders in their field to: build an independent research career at a UK university or research institution; gain the freedom, time, and long-term flexible support to pursue high-quality and innovative lines of scientific research; and develop as research leaders by offering tailored high-quality professional development, networking and engagement opportunities.

This scheme is for outstanding scientists who are in the early stages of their research career and have the potential to become leaders in their field. These long-term fellowships provide the opportunity and freedom to build an independent research career in the UK or Republic of Ireland and pursue cutting-edge scientific research.

The Royal Society recognises that diversity is essential for delivering excellence in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), and wants to encourage applications from the widest range of backgrounds, perspectives and experiences to maximise innovation and creativity in science for the benefit of humanity.

Not a degree programme. The grant may fund PhD studentships and technical support as staff costs within a fellow's award, but the fellowship itself is for the award holder's own research career.

Applications are assessed by one of five Research Appointment Panels according to research area: Ai - Astronomy, cosmology, physics, earth sciences, environmental physical sciences and geosciences; Aii - Chemistry and engineering; Aiii - Pure and applied mathematics, computer science, statistics, communications and computer engineering, and the mathematical aspects of astronomy, physics, cosmology, gravitation and theoretical physics; Bi - Molecular and cellular biology, zoology, plant sciences and physiology; Bii - Biomedical Sciences.
The aim of the interview is for the applicant to demonstrate the importance and scientific validity of their work and to describe how the award will lead to their scientific independence.

The Royal Society states that it regularly reviews and revises policies and processes to embed equity, diversity and inclusion principles in all aspects of grant making, so that all talented applicants have an equitable chance to succeed as per the assessment criteria.
official.selection_notes: The process is: apply through Flexi-GrantÂ®; eligibility checks; initial assessment by a minimum of two panel members with the most appropriate scientific expertise, with additional expertise co-opted where needed; a longlist is drawn up; longlisted applications undergo independent peer review; a shortlist for interview is drawn up with oversight from the Panel Chairs; shortlisted applicants are interviewed in person at the Royal Society; and at the end of the interview stage the Panels confirm the recommendations for funding. Applications crossing the remit of two Panels are assigned to a Primary Panel based on the primary subject area, with additional members seconded to the Review Panel for interdisciplinary applications. Published success rates are 7% (2022/23), 6.4% (2023/24), 6.8% (2024/25) and 6.3% (2025/26), based on eligible applications and offers made, and excluding upgraded reserves.

important_advice_for_students: This is not a scholarship for study. It is a research-employment fellowship for someone three to eight years past their PhD. If you are still a student or a fresh PhD, you are not eligible yet.

A second PhD, a master's or any taught programme will not be funded by this award. The published cost heads are salary, indirect and estate costs, equipment and research expenses, staff costs, and relocation/visa.

Plan for the mid-term review. Years six to eight are not guaranteed; they depend on satisfactory progress shown at a review at the start of year four, so the first four years determine whether the last three exist.

If you are near the eight-year boundary, the counting date is the round's closing date, not the interview date. If a career break affects your count, read the scheme notes, because the page says only that career breaks are excluded.

Do not rely on the grant cap being flexible beyond relocation and visa. The page says the cap may be exceeded for those costs where well justified, and says nothing about exceeding it for other reasons.

Take up the flexibility on offer. Part-time working, sabbaticals, secondments, parental and sick leave provision and childcare support for conferences are all published entitlements, and using them is not a penalty.
If you need a visa, mention it early: the Royal Society states visa costs are coverable and that a Global Talent Visa can be endorsed through a fast-track process.

referee_tracking.instructions: Longlisted applications are subject to independent peer review after the initial panel assessment. The Royal Society does not publish the number of referees, how they are nominated, or what they must include, so check the scheme notes.

Following eligibility checks, applications are initially assessed by a minimum of two panel members with the most appropriate scientific expertise, with additional expertise co-opted to the Panel where needed. Panel Chairs oversee the shortlist for interview, and the Panels confirm the funding recommendations at the end of the interview stage.

submission_workflow: 1. Verify eligibility against the research-experience window, the natural-sciences remit and all four disqualifiers.
2. Identify your primary subject area and Panel (Ai, Aii, Aiii, Bi or Bii).
3. Read the scheme notes, the Royal Society Funding Guidance, and the Republic of Ireland variants if relevant.
4. Request any adjustment from the Grants team, including a deadline extension or a different form format.
5. Build the budget against the Â£1,907,400 cap, justifying any relocation or visa costs that would take you over it.
6. Submit the application in Flexi-GrantÂ® before the published close date, writing pages 6-8 for external readers.
7. Await eligibility checks and initial assessment by at least two panel members.
8. If longlisted, respond promptly to independent peer review.
9. If shortlisted, prepare for and attend the in-person interview at the Royal Society.
10. On award, plan for the mid-fellowship review at the start of year four and the continuation of years six to eight.
post_award_requirements: Satisfy the mid-fellowship review at the start of year four, on which years six to eight depend.
Build an independent research career at a UK university or research institution, or in the Republic of Ireland.
Comply with the relevant conditions of award - the Research Ireland-specific conditions for Republic of Ireland-based fellows.
Use the fellowship within the published cost heads, with relocation and visa costs justified in the application.
Take up the published flexibility provisions where needed - part-time working, sabbaticals, secondments, parental and sick leave, and childcare support for conferences and research visits.
questions_to_ask_host: Is there a letter of support or heads-of-department agreement required from my institution, and at what stage?
What salary or salary increment will sit under the 'contribution to the award holder's salary' head at my institution, and what indirect and estate cost rates apply?
How does the mid-fellowship review at the start of year four work internally, and what evidence of progress will my department need to provide?
Are the funds portable if I move institution during the fellowship, and what would that require?
What are the PDRA and PhD studentship salary scales my institution would use for the staff-cost head?
If I am based in the Republic of Ireland, how do the Research Ireland-specific scheme notes and conditions of award differ from the UK terms?
What institutional commitments follow if I take a sabbatical or a secondment during the fellowship?

official.description: Sapienza's international scholarship portfolio is made up of several distinct schemes, of which the principal ones for graduates and students are the International Post-degree Scholarship and the International Thesis Scholarship. The International Post-degree Scholarship pays â‚¬1,290.00 per month for 6 to 12 months to support third-cycle study or postgraduate advanced training at an international university institution outside Italy, and is tax-exempt under Article 4 of Law 476/84; the International Thesis Scholarship pays â‚¬2,821.00 gross for a thesis-research placement abroad of at least two consecutive months. Both are competitive calls, and the post-degree call for 2026 closed on 16 September 2026, with a new call expected in April/May each year.
purpose: The International Post-degree Scholarship call, based on qualifications and exams, provides for the awarding of scholarships for courses or advanced training activities at international university institutions under Law No. 398 of 30 November 1989.

The selection will award 400 months of scholarships to support participation in third-cycle study programmes or postgraduate advanced training activities at international university-level institutions located outside Italy.

International Thesis Scholarships are financial benefits offered by Sapienza to students enrolled in degree programmes with the aim of promoting their international mobility for study abroad experiences.

International Thesis Scholarship are addressed to students who want to conduct part of their thesis research abroad and who are properly enrolled at least in the master's degree first year (two years duration) or in the last/second to last year of a single cycle degree.
degree_levels: Master's degree graduates and single-cycle master's degree (or equivalent integrated degree) holders from Sapienza - International Post-degree Scholarship
PhD students without a PhD scholarship (with faculty board authorisation to suspend doctoral studies) - International Post-degree Scholarship
PhD students with a PhD scholarship, who may benefit only by renouncing the PhD scholarship - International Post-degree Scholarship
Students enrolled in 'Scuole di specializzazione' (specialisation schools), with board authorisation - International Post-degree Scholarship
Master's degree first year students (two-year courses) and students in the last or second-to-last year of a single cycle degree - International Thesis Scholarship
study_type: Third-level studies or post-lauream specialization activities carried out in foreign or international university institutions located outside of Italy
For non-Italian citizens, the activities must be carried out in a foreign country different from the one of origin
Thesis research abroad at institutions, companies, foreign or community companies, supranational or international institutions of a higher scientific and cultural level
official.degree_award: Not a degree in itself. The post-degree scholarship funds attendance of courses or advanced training activities abroad; the thesis scholarship funds a period of thesis research abroad. Both can support progression into a third-cycle (PhD) programme.
official.duration: International Post-degree Scholarship: from a minimum of 6 months to a maximum of 12 months. International Thesis Scholarship: must be conducted for at least two consecutive months.
official.application_cycle: Annual. The International Post-degree Scholarship call is published every year in April/May; the published Call 2026 required applications by 16 September 2026. The International Thesis Scholarship is given by each faculty through its own Call, applied for at the faculty presidencies.
official.deadline_central_display: Call 2026 - deadline September 16, 2026. Applications must be submitted by September 16, 2026, under penalty of exclusion from the selection process.
official.deadline_institutional: For the International Thesis Scholarship, applications are made to the faculty presidencies under each faculty's own Call, so the operative deadline is the faculty's.
official.deadline_note: The 2026 call deadline of 16 September 2026 has passed as at the 2026-10-01 verification date, and the University states the call is published every year in April/May, so the next round is expected in 2027 with no date yet published. Scholarship payments are made throughout the year but are suspended in December and January due to Sapienza's year-end closing procedures.
official.status: UPCOMING - the published Call 2026 closed on 16 September 2026 and the page states the call is published every year in April/May, so the next call is expected but not yet dated.
official.funding_label: International Post-degree Scholarship: â‚¬1,290.00 per month for 6-12 months. International Thesis Scholarship: â‚¬2,821.00 gross for the whole internship.
official.funding_period: International Post-degree Scholarship: per month, for a minimum of 6 and a maximum of 12 months. International Thesis Scholarship: a single amount for the whole internship of at least two consecutive months.
official.living_cost_coverage: The post-degree scholarship is a monthly amount of â‚¬1,290.00 for the period of the activity abroad. The page does not state that the amount is calculated against living costs, and no separate accommodation, insurance or travel line is published.
official.tuition_rule: No tuition waiver is published. The post-degree scholarship covers attendance of courses or advanced training activities at a foreign institution, and the published benefits are the monthly amount, the tax exemption under Article 4 of Law 476/84 and - separately - the ability to exceed a stated income threshold. No fee payment at the host institution is described.
official.tax_status: Scholarships for attendance of courses or advanced training activities are exempt from Irpef treatment pursuant to Article 4 of Law 476/84. The International Thesis Scholarship amount of â‚¬2,821.00 is stated as gross with Regional Income Tax included, so that scheme is not tax-exempt on its face.

Total pool of 400 months of scholarships in the 2026 selection

Support for 6 to 12 months of third-cycle or postgraduate advanced training at an international institution

A separate thesis-research scholarship that can be applied for through the faculty presidencies while still enrolled in a degree programme
eligibility: All students under 29 who graduated from a master degree or single cycle degree programme, or any other equivalent degree, achieved at La Sapienza University of Rome within the last viable session of the academic year preceding the year of the announcement of the contest.
Candidates need to have graduated from Sapienza University of Rome.
They need to be 28 years old or younger by the announcement of the call.

They must obtain an official acceptance and/or invitation letter and/or a declaration of availability to admission from a hosting foreign institution or from a foreign supervisor, drafted on headed and certified paper.
The candidate's degree must fall within the CUN disciplinary area applied for, and the application will be rejected if it does not.
For the International Thesis Scholarship: properly enrolled at least in the master's degree first year (two years duration) or in the last/second to last year of a single cycle degree.
general_eligibility: Graduation from a Sapienza University of Rome degree programme within the last viable session of the academic year preceding the year of the call.
Age 28 or younger at the announcement of the call (the Q&A describes the eligible group as 'all students under 29').
A hosting foreign institution or foreign supervisor willing to issue an official acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document on headed and certified paper.
For non-Italian citizens, the host institution must be located in a country other than their country of origin.
The degree class must match the CUN disciplinary area chosen, and only one application may be submitted.
For the thesis scholarship, current enrolment in a Sapienza degree programme at the specified stage.
ineligibility_conditions: Not having graduated from Sapienza University of Rome.
Being 29 or older at the announcement of the call.
Applying to a CUN area for which you do not have the requested degree - the application will be rejected as incongruous or inconsistent with the area.
Submitting more than one application, or an application relating to more than one CUN disciplinary area.
For non-Italian citizens, choosing a host institution in their country of origin.
PhD students who hold a PhD scholarship and are unwilling to renounce it.
Specialisation school students who are winners of other scholarships, or who lack board authorisation.
Scholarship holders taking up any other scholarship during the period of the activity abroad, other than national or foreign institutional grants that integrate a foreign stay.
Scholarship holders whose income exceeds the published threshold for the major part of the calendar year in which they receive the scholarship.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to Sapienza graduates of any nationality. For non-Italian citizens the host institution must be located in a country other than their country of origin. Italian and international students are separately covered by the university's other schemes, such as the 'Scholarships for Meritorious Students from Italian and International Universities' and the 'Grants for international and Italian citizens living abroad awarded by the Italian government' listed on the same page.
official.international_eligibility: Graduates of Sapienza University of Rome, of any nationality, seeking to carry out third-cycle study or postgraduate advanced training at a foreign or international university institution outside Italy. Non-Italian citizens must place the activity outside their country of origin. The University publishes no list of hosting countries or institutions; the candidate must check academic catalogues and contact institutions directly.

undergraduate: Not covered by the two main international schemes. Undergraduates at Sapienza are instead covered by separate calls listed on the same page, including the 100 scholarships for students with care responsibilities or in vulnerable circumstances and the 2026-2027 call for reimbursement of study materials.
masters: International Post-degree Scholarship: open to holders of a Master's degree, single-cycle Master's degree or equivalent integrated degree awarded by Sapienza, graduated within the last viable session of the academic year preceding the year of the call, and aged 28 or younger at the announcement of the call.

International Thesis Scholarship: addressed to students properly enrolled at least in the master's degree first year (two years duration), for thesis research abroad of at least two consecutive months.
phd: PhD students can participate in the post-degree contest. A PhD student without a PhD scholarship will benefit from the scholarship if authorised by the PhD Faculty board to suspend doctoral studies for the specialisation activity abroad. A PhD student with a PhD scholarship can benefit only by renouncing the PhD scholarship.

host_requirements: The host must be a foreign or international university institution located outside Italy, and for non-Italian citizens outside their own country of origin.

The host institution (or a foreign supervisor) must issue an official acceptance and/or invitation letter and/or a declaration of availability to admission, drafted on headed and certified paper, with the institution's official signature and stamp.

The certification must contain the name of the course, its internal structure and respective duration (if it is a course of study), or the programme of the activities that will need to be completed (in case of a post-lauream specialization activity).

For the thesis scholarship, thesis research can be done at institutions, companies, foreign or community companies, supranational or international institutions of a higher scientific and cultural level.
There is no list of hosting countries or foreign institutions, and the candidate must contact institutions directly.
requirements: Graduate from Sapienza University of Rome within the last viable session of the academic year preceding the year of the call, with a degree class matching the chosen CUN area.
Be 28 or younger at the announcement of the call.

Obtain an official acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document from the hosting foreign institution or a foreign supervisor, on headed and certified paper with official signature and stamp.
Submit one application only, in PDF format using the model attached to the call, exclusively by certified and accredited personal electronic mail (PEC) to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it.
Attach the three required items to the application.
Indicate in the application the number of months you consider necessary for the scholarship, noting that this decision ultimately pertains to the Committee.
If shortlisted, attend the interview to verify your preparation in the selected disciplinary field and your knowledge of the language requested by the hosting foreign institution.
documents: The application, drafted in PDF format according to the model attached to the call

Official certification provided by the foreign institution or international university abroad for which the candidate wishes to apply (or a certified declaration provided by a professor of the same university) containing the acceptance or possible acceptability of the candidate to the chosen course of study or post-lauream specialization activity, drafted according to a certified format with the institution's official signature and stamp
Self-declaration of the candidate's publications and previously attained titles, drafted in PDF according to the format mentioned in the application model
Translation into Italian of the documentation released by the foreign or international institution, only if the document was initially released in a language other than English

After selection, a self-declaration reporting to possess the compulsory requirements stated in the call, with the obligation to maintain them during the period in which the candidate will receive the scholarship
After selection, a new certification released by the international institution indicating the starting and final date of the activity of specialization
document_format_rules: The application must be drafted in PDF format according to the model attached to the call.

The application must be sent exclusively by certified and accredited personal electronic mail (PEC) to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it - the University states 'exclusively', so other channels are not accepted.
The self-declaration of publications and previously attained titles must be drafted in PDF according to the format specified in the application model.

The host certification must be drafted according to a certified format, with the institution's official signature and stamp, and must state the name of the course, its internal structure and respective duration, or the programme of the activities to be completed.
An Italian translation of the host documentation is required only if the document was originally released in a language other than English; an English-language document needs no translation.
Candidates admitted to interview are informed via PEC, and the interview list is published on the Amministrazione trasparente portal, on this page, on the Sapienza website and on the call webpage.
The University publishes no file size limits and no page limits beyond what the attached application model may specify.
selection_criteria: The selection is based on curricular exams and on achieved titles.
A Selection Committee is nominated for each disciplinary area; the Committee attributes a score of up to 100 points for the evaluation of each candidate.
The Committee can give up to 50 points for the candidate's degree final grade, previously attained titles and publications.
The Committee can attribute up to 50 points for the interview.
A score under 35 points is considered not sufficient.

Once the applications are received, the Committee meets and establishes the selection criteria following the call guidelines and the regulation of the contest, and evaluates the consistency of the applications within the CUN field for which they were presented.
The Committee will officially report the reason for excluding any candidates.
official.selection_notes: Applications are scored out of 100 by a disciplinary-area Selection Committee: up to 50 points for the degree final grade, previously attained titles and publications, and up to 50 points for the interview. Suitable candidates are contacted for an interview to verify the level of preparation in the selected disciplinary field as well as knowledge in the language requested by the hosting foreign institution. A total score under 35 points is treated as insufficient. The list of candidates admitted to interview, with the date and place of interviews, is published on the Amministrazione trasparente portal, on this page, on the Sapienza website and on the call webpage, and candidates are notified by PEC.
application_method: Draft the application in PDF format using the model attached to the call, with the three required attachments.
Send the application exclusively by certified and accredited personal electronic mail (PEC) to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it.
For the International Thesis Scholarship, apply at the faculty presidencies under your faculty's own Call.
Await the interview list, which is published online and notified by PEC.
Attend the interview, and after selection produce the two post-selection documents.
application_steps: 1. Check eligibility: Sapienza graduate within the last viable session of the academic year preceding the call year, aged 28 or younger at the announcement of the call, with a degree class matching a CUN area.

2. Contact the foreign institution or a foreign supervisor yourself - there is no list of hosting countries or institutions - and obtain an official acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document on headed and certified paper with official signature and stamp.

3. Confirm the certification contains the course name, internal structure and duration, or the programme of activities, and that the host is outside Italy and, for non-Italian citizens, outside their country of origin.
4. Complete the application in PDF format using the model attached to the call, indicating the number of months you consider necessary.
5. Attach the host certification, the self-declaration of publications and titles, and - only if the host document is not in English - an Italian translation of it.
6. Send everything exclusively by PEC to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it before the deadline (16 September 2026 for the 2026 call).
7. Check the interview list on the Amministrazione trasparente portal, this page, the Sapienza website and the call webpage, and watch for the PEC notification.
8. Attend the interview, which tests preparation in your disciplinary field and your knowledge of the language required by the host.
9. If selected, produce the self-declaration of the compulsory requirements and a new host certification with the start and final dates.
10. Begin the activity from the day after the interview, and start it within the end of the calendar year after the one in which the contest was promulgated.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits directly by certified and accredited personal electronic mail (PEC) to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it, exclusively.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you graduated from Sapienza within the last viable session of the academic year preceding the call year - the post-degree scheme is for Sapienza graduates only.

Check your age against the published limits: the Q&A describes the eligible group as 'all students under 29' and the requirements section says candidates 'need to be 28 years old or younger by the announcement of the call'. If you are 28, confirm the reference date with the scholarship office rather than assuming.
Match your degree class to a CUN disciplinary area. An application to a CUN area for which you do not hold the degree is rejected outright.

Secure the host yourself - there is no list of hosting countries or institutions - and get an official acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document on headed and certified paper, with the institution's official signature and stamp, stating the course name, internal structure and duration or the programme of activities.
For non-Italian citizens, confirm the host is outside your country of origin as well as outside Italy.
Prepare the application in PDF using the model attached to the call, with the self-declaration of publications and titles in the same format.
If your host document is not in English, get it translated into Italian. An English document needs no translation.
Send everything by PEC to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it only. The University says 'exclusively', so email or in-person submission will not be accepted.
If you hold a PhD scholarship, decide now whether you are willing to renounce it - that is the only route to benefit.
Prepare for the interview to test both disciplinary preparation and the language your host requires.
important_advice_for_students: Do not assume a fee waiver. No tuition payment at the host is described anywhere; treat the â‚¬1,290.00 per month as your entire benefit and budget your own costs around it.

Start the host search immediately. There is no list of hosting countries or institutions and the University expects you to approach institutions yourself, which is normally the slowest part of this application.

Watch the income cap. The published rule is that a holder cannot possess, for the major part of the calendar year of the scholarship, an income superior to 'â‚¬ 7.750,000' - the figure is printed exactly that way on the official page. Get the intended threshold clarified with the scholarship office before you rely on it, because the notation is ambiguous.

Do not stack other scholarships. Holding any other scholarship during the period abroad is prohibited, with a narrow exception for national or foreign institutional grants that integrate a foreign stay.
For PhD students, the practical cost of this award is your PhD scholarship: you must renounce it, and you need faculty board authorisation to suspend doctoral studies.

Plan the timing carefully. You can only start receiving from the day after the interview, and the activity must begin within the end of the following calendar year, so a late decision can cost you months.

The two schemes are different. If you are still enrolled, the International Thesis Scholarship (â‚¬2,821.00 gross, at least two months, via your faculty) is the relevant one, not the post-degree monthly award.
Note the payment blackout: Sapienza scholarship payments are suspended in December and January because of year-end closing procedures, so do not assume a December instalment arrives.
common_rejection_risks: Not having graduated from Sapienza University of Rome.
Being outside the published age limit at the announcement of the call.
Applying to a CUN disciplinary area that does not match your degree class - the application is rejected as incongruous or inconsistent.
Submitting more than one application, or an application covering more than one CUN area.
Missing the published deadline - 16 September 2026 for the 2026 call, under penalty of exclusion.
Sending the application by ordinary email instead of PEC, which the University says must be used exclusively.
Submitting the application in the wrong format or without the model attached to the call.
Omitting the Italian translation when the host document is not in English - the translation is required in that case only.
A host certification missing the required content (course name, internal structure, duration, or programme of activities) or not on headed and certified paper with official signature and stamp.
For non-Italian citizens, a host institution in their own country of origin.
A total selection score under 35 points, which is stated to be insufficient.
PhD students unwilling to renounce an existing PhD scholarship, or lacking faculty board authorisation.
Specialisation school students who already hold another scholarship, or who are winners of a 'Scuola di specializzazione' scholarship.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition or enrolment fees at the host institution - not a published benefit of either scheme
Flights, travel and relocation to and from the host country
Accommodation at the host location
Health, medical and travel insurance
Books, materials, equipment and research costs for the thesis placement
Any income above the published threshold, which holders are not permitted to have for the major part of the award year
Anything arising from holding a second scholarship, which is prohibited during the award period

Submission channel: certified and accredited personal electronic mail (PEC) to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it, exclusively. Ordinary email, hand delivery and post are not accepted.

Attachment 2: self-declaration of the candidate's publications and previously attained titles, in PDF, in the format specified in the application model.
Attachment 3: translation into Italian of the documentation in Attachment 1, required only if that document was originally released in a language other than English.

referee_tracking.role: Selection Committee for the CUN disciplinary area
referee_tracking.instructions: A Selection Committee is nominated for each disciplinary area and scores the application out of 100, with up to 50 points for the degree final grade, previously attained titles and publications, and up to 50 points for the interview. No external referees or letters of reference are requested in the published application requirements; the Committee formally reports the reason for excluding any candidate.

Not a referee in the academic sense, but a mandatory signatory: they must issue an official acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document on headed and certified paper with the institution's official signature and stamp, containing the course name, internal structure and duration or the programme of activities. A certified declaration by a professor of the host university is accepted as an alternative.

submission_workflow: 1. Verify eligibility: Sapienza graduate within the last viable session of the preceding academic year, within the published age limit, with a degree class matching a CUN area.
2. Choose one CUN disciplinary area and one intended number of months, remembering the Committee decides the final number.

3. Approach a foreign host institution or supervisor yourself and obtain the official acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document on headed and certified paper with official signature and stamp, containing the course name, internal structure and duration or the programme of activities.
4. Confirm the host is outside Italy and, if you are a non-Italian citizen, outside your country of origin.
5. Download the call and the application model from the Amministrazione trasparente portal.
6. Complete the application in PDF using the model, and prepare the self-declaration of publications and titles in the same format.
7. Obtain an Italian translation of the host document if it is not in English.
8. Send the application and all three attachments by PEC to protocollosapienza@cert.uniroma1.it before the deadline.
9. Monitor the published interview list and your PEC inbox, then attend the interview.
10. If selected, submit the self-declaration of compulsory requirements and obtain the new host certification with the start and final dates.
post_award_requirements: Maintain the compulsory requirements stated in the call for the entire period of the scholarship, as confirmed by self-declaration.
Do not hold any other scholarship during the period of the activity abroad, except national or foreign institutional grants that integrate a foreign stay.
Keep income at or below the published threshold for the major part of the calendar year of the scholarship.
Ensure the host institution issues a new certification giving the starting and final date of the specialization activity.
Begin the activity from the day after the interview and no later than the end of the calendar year following the year in which the contest was promulgated.
For PhD students, maintain faculty board authorisation for the suspension of doctoral studies and remain without a PhD scholarship.
If you decide to renounce, notify the offices as soon as possible so the next candidates can be contacted, and return any first instalment already received.
questions_to_ask_host: Will the institution issue the acceptance, invitation or availability-of-admission document on headed and certified paper with its official signature and stamp, and does it state the course name, internal structure and duration?
Is the activity arranged as a course of study or as a post-lauream specialization activity, and does the host document reflect that distinction?
What are the start and end dates of the activity, and can the host confirm them in writing at the end so I can obtain the required post-selection certification?
What language will the activity be conducted in, so I can prepare for the interview on that language?
What additional costs will I face at the host - fees, accommodation, insurance - that the â‚¬1,290.00 per month will not cover?
For the International Thesis Scholarship, what is my faculty's Call deadline and which faculty presidency do I apply to?
What is the intended interpretation of the published income threshold, given the notation on the official page?

official.description: JASSO's Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students is a monthly stipend for privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who are enrolled in a Japanese educational institution and are facing financial difficulties. The published stipend is 48,000 yen per month at graduate and undergraduate level and 30,000 yen per month for Japanese language institute students, paid for 12 months (April to the following March) or 6 months (October to the following March). Applications are never made to JASSO directly: the applicant must ask the staff at the educational institution in which they are enrolled, and JASSO warns that the number of students an institution can recommend depends on how many international students it has enrolled, so some institutions may not be able to nominate anyone at all.
purpose: This is a scholarship program for privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who are enrolled in undergraduate schools, graduate schools, junior colleges, colleges of technology, specialized course in specialized training colleges, university preparatory courses or Japanese language institutes in Japan and are facing financial difficulties.

The programme exists to support privately-financed international students - that is, those not already funded by the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship or any Foreign Government Scholarship.

application_steps: 1. Confirm you are enrolled full-time in one of the six published categories of Japanese educational institution and hold 'Student' residence status.
2. Confirm you are privately financed - you are not a grantee of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship or any Foreign Government Scholarship.

3. Check your own eligibility against the allowance cap (90,000 yen average per month excluding enrolment fee and tuition) and, if supported in Japan, your supporter's income (under 5 million yen per year).
4. Check the language condition, unless you are at a preparatory Japanese language programme, a university preparatory course or a Japanese language institute.
5. Check that you do not hold JASSO Student Exchange Support Program support or a scholarship that cannot be combined with the Honors Scholarships.
6. Ask the staff at your educational institution how to apply and whether it can recommend you - the number of recommendations an institution can make depends on its enrolled international students.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are enrolled full-time in one of the six published categories of Japanese institution and hold 'Student' residence status.
Confirm you are privately financed - no Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship and no Foreign Government Scholarship.

Add up your own income from other sources. The total allowance excluding enrolment fee and tuition must average 90,000 yen or less per month, and if anyone supports you while you are in Japan their annual income must be under 5 million yen.

Check the language condition now: JLPT N2 or above, EJU Japanese 200 points or more, a JASSO-recognised level, or CEFR B2 or above - unless you are at a preparatory Japanese language programme, a university preparatory course or a Japanese language institute.
Make sure you are not on JASSO's Student Exchange Support Program and are not holding a scholarship that cannot be combined with the Honors Scholarships.

Ask your institution's international office immediately whether it can recommend you. JASSO states the number an institution can recommend depends on its enrolled international students, and that you may not be able to apply.
Ask for the application guidelines, because the grading criteria and the document list are set there and are not published on the JASSO page.
Note the enrolment month: the award runs April to March for a 12-month period, or October to March for 6 months.
important_advice_for_students: Do not apply to JASSO. The official instruction is to ask the staff at your educational institution, and there is no JASSO application portal for this scholarship.
Do not treat this as tuition funding. JASSO's own allowance rule is defined as 'excluding enrollment fee, tuition fee, etc.', so you still pay enrolment fee and tuition in full.
Budget on 48,000 yen per month (30,000 if you are at a Japanese language institute). That is the whole award, and it is capped at 12 or 6 months - there is no published renewal route.
Check your institution before you invest effort. JASSO explicitly warns that some institutions may not be able to recommend anyone, so your school's willingness is the first gate, not your grades.
Watch the 90,000 yen allowance ceiling. Family support, part-time work and small awards can push you over it, and the rule is an average per month across the year.
The monthly signing is not a formality. Failing to sign the JASSO-designated sheet each month at the international students' office is a breach of the published grant conditions.
Selection results are published in Japanese only on the JASSO page, so ask your institution how they will tell you.

official.description: The SMU Merit Scholarship is a bond-free undergraduate award from Singapore Management University, of which up to 35 are made each year. The published package is a full four-year tuition fee waiver - the waiver of annual subsidised tuition fees for regular terms (semesters 1 and 2) for up to four years, starting from Academic Year 2027-28 - plus a growth opportunities allowance of S$12,000 that the scholar can apply to overseas community service projects and global exposure opportunities such as exchanges, summer programmes and study missions, plus participation in development programmes run by SMU's Student Success Centre. It is a tuition waiver and an activity allowance only: no living-cost, accommodation or travel-to-Singapore support is published, so it is not full funding.

Our dedicated Student Success Centre implements and oversees development programmes for our scholars and is committed to guide and to develop the intellectual and holistic growth of our scholars.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a Singapore Citizen - this is the first eligibility criterion and international applicants are not eligible for this award.
Apply to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU; the scholarship is not available to other levels or to part-time study.

Tick the SMU Merit Scholarship in the Scholarship section of the online admission application. There is no separate scholarship form, so an application that omits this is not considered for the scholarship.
Write the scholarship personal essay as a distinct piece of work - it is completed and submitted online with the admission application and is the only scholarship-specific written component.
Nominate a tutor or principal as referee if you want a letter of recommendation, and give them enough time to submit it online. The letters are optional but SMU strongly encourages them.

important_advice_for_students: Do not assume this pays your living costs. The published package is a subsidised tuition fee waiver plus a S$12,000 activity allowance, so budget accommodation, food, transport and travel to Singapore yourself.

The waiver is described as subsidised tuition fees for regular terms (semesters 1 and 2). If your programme has compulsory ancillary or laboratory fees, ask SMU whether those are inside or outside the waiver before you compare offers.
The 'up to 4 years' wording matters. The waiver is not described as unconditional for four years, so ask what happens if you need a repeat year, a leave of absence, or a change of programme.
Scholarship timing lags the admission cycle. The package is stated to start from Academic Year 2027-28, so check carefully which intake's closing date applies to you.

Do not skip the referee. The letters are optional on paper, but SMU says applicants are strongly encouraged to obtain them, and shortlisting weighs the strength of non-academic records, so a tutor or principal letter is the cheapest way to strengthen that part.
Give referees real time. SMU specifically asks you to ensure your referee has sufficient time to submit the recommendation online, and a late nomination is a common self-inflicted loss.

The S$12,000 is a growth opportunities allowance, not a cash stipend. Plan it for the listed activities - overseas community service projects, exchanges, summer programmes and study missions - rather than treating it as spendable money.

official.description: The University of Zurich's hardship loan is an interest-free short-term loan for students who are enrolled at UZH and in an acute financial emergency without any debt, applied for without bureaucratic red tape and usually processed within a few working days. The maximum is CHF 6,000 per application, and it can be applied for at most once per semester with no application deadline. It is a repayable loan, not a grant: the applicant must be able to plausibly guarantee that the amount will be paid back within six months, and short-term loans that are not paid back on time are immediately sent to a debt collector.

Do not wait for a deadline, because there isn't one. There is no annual round; apply as soon as the crisis arises, because processing usually takes only a few working days.
Apply for the maximum only if you can actually repay it. Six months is short, and the guarantee is a condition of the award, not a formality.

If you are waiting on a cantonal scholarship, this loan is explicitly designed for that gap. official.description: MIT Student Financial Services treats students who are not eligible for federal student financial aid under the FAFSA - that is, everyone other than U.S. citizens, permanent residents and certain special cases - as 'international' for financial aid purposes, regardless of country of residence. International students go through exactly the same need-based process as domestic students, and MIT states it is committed to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need for international students, just as for domestic students. The award that results is primarily the MIT Scholarship, a non-repayable need-based grant covering the difference between the cost of attendance and the family's financial responsibility; MIT published a median MIT Scholarship of $73,666 for 2025-2026, awarded to about 58% of undergraduates. Applications require only two documents: the CSS Profile, using MIT's CSS Code 3514, and parental tax returns or income documentation submitted through the College Board's IDOC service.
purpose: International students are considered for aid using the same process that we use for all applicants. We are committed to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need for international students, just as we are for domestic students.

We are proud to be one of the very few institutions in the United States that are need blind and full need for all of our undergraduate students, domestic and international, and most MIT students receive need-based aid.

An MIT Scholarship is a grant we give you to help make up the difference between the COA and your family financial responsibility. It is the primary source of grant aid distributed by MIT, given solely on the basis of need, and does not need to be repaid.

If you receive need-based aid from MIT, you will have a section called 'Institution Grants' on your offer letter. These institutional grants are given to you by MIT on the basis of your financial need, and do not need to be paid back.
MIT works closely with all families who qualify for financial aid to develop an individual affordability plan tailored to their financial circumstances.
degree_levels: Undergraduate - MIT Student Financial Services' undergraduate aid pages apply to all MIT undergraduates, and the page states the need-blind, full-need commitment applies to 'all of our undergraduate students, domestic and international'.
study_type: Full-time undergraduate study at MIT is the frame for the published statistics on MIT Scholarships, including the share of full-time undergraduates receiving one.

Both prospective and continuing students are covered, with separate deadlines: prospective students applying Early Action, Regular Action or as transfers, and current students applying for the following academic year.

The award includes a term-time work amount as part of the financial aid offer, and MIT notes that students may choose to meet it with outside scholarships, the Pell Grant where eligible, or student loans.
official.degree_award: Not a degree. A need-based, non-repayable grant package attached to enrolment in an MIT undergraduate degree programme.
official.duration: Awarded annually. Recipients who are awarded an MIT Scholarship must fill out an annual Student Information Review Form between May 1 and July 1 so that MIT can match them with the right scholarship fund. Current students reapply for the following academic year with a February 15 deadline.
official.application_cycle: Annual, tied to MIT's admissions cycle. Prospective students must submit the CSS Profile and parental tax returns or income documentation through IDOC by the Early Action deadline (November 30, with offers released mid-January), the Regular Action deadline (February 15, with offers released mid-March), or the transfer deadline (February 15, with offers released after admission decisions). Current students apply for the following academic year by February 15 and receive their offer in late May or early June.
official.deadline_central_display: Prospective students - Early Action: application deadline November 30, offers released mid-January. Regular Action: application deadline February 15, offers released mid-March. Transfer: application deadline February 15, offers released after admission decisions. Current students: application deadline February 15 for the following academic year, with the offer received in late May or early June. Application deadlines are the same for both domestic and international students.
official.deadline_institutional: The same deadlines apply to international and domestic students, so there is no separate institutional deadline for international applicants. Aid documents can be managed and the offer accessed through the MIT Application Portal until mid-May.
official.deadline_note: Deadlines are published as month-and-day only, with no year attached, so no full ISO date can be derived for them from the official page. Late aid applications are permitted without penalty: MIT states there is no need to ask for an extension and no penalties for late applications, but financial aid applications must be received before the end of the academic year, which for most students is mid-May, and for those only attending in the fall, mid-December - and if the application is not completed by then, the student will not be eligible to receive either MIT or federal financial aid for that academic year.
official.status: OPEN - MIT states that applications can be submitted through the cycle's deadlines with no penalty for late applications, and that it is committed to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need for international students. The current prospective-student cycle runs on the published November 30 and February 15 deadlines, so applications are being accepted as at the 2026-10-01 verification date.
official.funding_label: MIT need-based financial aid for international students - principally the MIT Scholarship (non-repayable grant), plus the First Year Grant and the Health Insurance Grant
official.funding_period: Annual, awarded per academic year. The published MIT Scholarship amounts are annual medians by family income range for 2025-2026; the First Year Grant is a one-time $2,000 award split equally between the fall and spring semesters for first-year students only.
official.tuition_coverage: MIT is 'need blind' and 'full need' for all undergraduate students, domestic and international, meaning it is committed to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need. Beginning with the 2025-2026 academic year, students from families with an annual income under $200,000 - about the 80th percentile income for American families - typically attend MIT tuition-free, meaning total grant and scholarship aid covers at least the cost of MIT's tuition. This is family-income dependent: for families with income over $200,000 the published median MIT Scholarship of $37,750 covers 59% of tuition.
official.living_cost_coverage: The full-need commitment covers 100% of demonstrated financial need, which is assessed against the cost of attendance - including tuition, housing, dining, fees, and an allowance for books and personal expenses. For the 50% of American families with income below $100,000, parents can expect to pay nothing toward the full cost. The median annual price paid by an undergraduate who received an MIT Scholarship was $10,268 for 2024-2025, and the median net price is $0 for families in the $0-$100,000 income range.
official.tuition_rule: MIT is need blind and full need: it does not consider ability to pay in the admissions process, and it commits to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need with its aid, for all undergraduate students, domestic and international. Tuition coverage is family-income dependent rather than automatic - from the 2025-2026 academic year, families with annual income under $200,000 typically attend tuition-free, while the published median MIT Scholarship for families over $200,000 is $37,750, covering 59% of tuition. Students remain expected to contribute toward their own expenses from a summer savings contribution and student employment during the school year, and may offset the expected student contribution with an outside scholarship or a Federal Pell Grant if eligible.
official.home_tuition_rule: The CSS Profile and parental tax returns come from the student's family circumstances, and the award is need-based on those. If the parents live outside the U.S., MIT asks for the tax return from that country, along with a translation to English if applicable.
official.host_institution_fee: No host fee applies: the award is made directly to the student against MIT's cost of attendance, which includes tuition, housing, dining, fees, and an allowance for books and personal expenses. There is no separate mandatory fee payable by international students in place of tuition, and international students are considered for aid through the same process as domestic students.

application_readiness_checklist: Start with the classification test, not the paperwork: if you are not eligible for federal student financial aid under the FAFSA, you follow the international instructions regardless of where you live.

important_advice_for_students: MIT's need-blind, full-need commitment applies to international students exactly as to domestic students, and MIT says so explicitly. If you are admitted and your family cannot pay, that is not a reason to withdraw - it is what the aid package is for.

Expect to contribute something yourself. The median annual price paid by an undergraduate who received an MIT Scholarship was $10,268, and students are expected to contribute from summer savings and term-time work. Full need means MIT meets what it calculates to be your need, not that your family pays nothing.

Understand that tuition coverage is income-dependent. From 2025-2026 families under $200,000 typically attend tuition-free, but for families over $200,000 the published median MIT Scholarship is $37,750 and covers 59% of tuition. If your family income is above that band, start budgeting early.

Do not send anything to MIT. Parental tax documents go to the College Board's IDOC service, and MIT says it cannot accept documents sent directly to it. This is the single most common procedural failure point.
Budget two weeks for IDOC and 10 business days for the portal. MIT publishes both timings, and they are the reason late-feeling applications slip.

A professional translation is not required. Documents may be translated by you, your family or someone you know, which removes a real cost barrier - but they must be in English if the original is not.

There is no penalty for a late application, but there is a hard cut-off. MIT says just submit as soon as possible; the risk is not a penalty, it is missing mid-May (or mid-December for fall-only attendance) and losing the aid for the year entirely.

Do the Student Information Review Form between 1 May and 1 July. MIT uses it to match you to the right scholarship fund, and because donors often specify the kind of student they support, this is what connects you to the fund - and sometimes to an MIT alum donor.
Travel, visa and immigration costs are not addressed on these pages. They are not listed as covered expenses, so plan for flights and visa fees separately.

official.description: The Atomic Energy Scholarship (AES) Program of China is jointly initiated by the China Atomic Energy Authority (CAEA) and the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China (MOE) with the aim of fostering outstanding young talent working in the field of peaceful use of nuclear energy from developing countries. At Tsinghua University it funds master's and doctoral study only, in the Department of Engineering Physics or the Institute of Nuclear and New Energy Technology, covering tuition fees, free university dormitory or an accommodation subsidy, a stipend, and comprehensive medical insurance. The sibling 2026 Chinese Government Scholarship page on the same Tsinghua site states Type A applications, which is the category a bilateral programme such as this falls into, usually open between the last November and February with timelines varying by country, and recommends applying for Tsinghua pre-admission before mid-December; those dates belong to the CGS page, not to the Atomic Energy page.
